everything is looking really great and you can see the hours the team has put into this. Really great work everyone.

I have 3 suggestions for Shaman Talents: I will **Bold & Underline** what the suggested changes are

Earth's Grasp Talent - Increases the health of your Stoneclaw Totem by **50/75%** and the radius of your Earthbind Totem by 10/20%. **Earthshock now taunts your enemy to hit you and has its range reduced to melee range.**

Enhancing Totems - Stoneskin Totem now increases block amount by 15/30% and its flat damage reduction is increased by 15/30%, increases the effect of your Strength of Earth and Grace of Air totems by 8/15%, **Windwall Totem also now reduces Magical damage taken by 3/5% and its flat ranged damage reduction is increased by 15/30%** , and reduces the cooldown of your grounding totem by 1/2 sec.

Eye of the Storm - Gives you a **25/50/75%** chance to gain Focused Casting Effect that lasts for 6 sec after being the victim of a melee or ranged **--** strike **and reduces the chance you will be critically hit by melee and ranged attacks by 2/4/6%.** The Focused Casting effect prevents you from losing casting time when taking damage.

Please consider these to support a highly sought after playstyle, These talents are PERFECT for these additions(earths grasp, come on its right there!). I also want to highlight the Eye of the Storm change --> Remove CRITICALLY strike and change to just a strike but reduce the % for focused from 100 to 75% to still make it proc around the same. Adding in the Crit immunity will give shaman viability to tanks in raids. Im not talking about MT naxx, but lets let them tank ZG and OT in the big ones and what not.

FINAL suggestion.
Hordes Paladin Alliance Shaman please.

## Post 103228 by Shambakriger — 2024-10-16T23:33:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103228#p103228 | page 2 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Very interesting, some changes that I expected and some not so much (from a druid player)
Most impressed by the resto changes as they seem to flesh out the three existing playstyles without really altering them in any drastic way, very excited to play moonglow in the new patch!
For feral the changes to cat don't seem very significant compared to the nerf of losing MCP, I was sort of expecting an easy band-aid like claw weapon skill. But I'm interested to see how bleeds will work out now, even though this isn't the rotation i'd imagined for them.
Will the defense stat be seeing any kind of rework/added benefit for bears or should we count it as a somewhat dead stat? removing crit immunity from bears makes me skeptical about trying to push for dodge as a main stat, but I'm excited to try it out nonetheless.
For balance I'm honestly a bit dissapointed that we ended up going the later expansion of "literal balance" (switching between arcane and nature damage based on procs) route. I've come to kind of like this divide in the moonkin community between starfire and wrath enjoyers. It felt like a more vanilla way of balancing the spec, to have two differing playstyles within the same tree, much like moonglow/tree/regrowth in restoration
Anyways, I can't even begin to imagine the amount of work this must have taken and I am infinitely grateful that we are all able to enjoy this!<33

## Post 103255 by Harkonnan (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2024-10-17T01:38:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103255#p103255 | page 2 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

First off, great gamboza! that's allot of changes, and good ones!
Thank you dev's for putting all this work and effort into making this game so great. I have not been this excited to play WoW since original tbc release. Pat yourselves on the back.

So I haven't been able to go through all the changes, but As Paladin tends to be my main (along with druid), I only have one criticism (aside from waiting to see how numbers need to be tweaked).

It's this: Repentance is garbage. It just is. It always has been. It's not a Ret thing, it doesn't scream Retribution (putting someone to sleep in vengeance? sure....) and even with the changes it's still garbage for a capstone. a 60s CD for a skill that does a hundred or so damage ONLY if the mob is immune to sleep and ONLY if it's a humanoid, demon, yada yada.

It's supposed to be a spec changing thing! a Capstone ability! whoever designed this originally at blizz should be fired. It's like your mum making you wear a frilly sweater to school on picture day, everyone just looks at our "mighty" repentance and laughs.

For the love of Pete just make it baseline. It's already limited to PvP niche situations, NO ONE uses it in PvE, and I doubt people will suddenly start using it now. Just make it baseline for all specs and leave it in the garbage heap of semi-used skills where it belongs. And give us a proper capstone. here's a few ideas:

 1) Something that turns our judgements into a mini cleave and hits up to 3 targets.
 2) A speed boost. similar to rogues dash. Please no charger silly thing, I always hated that. But we could use a movement ability. the extra run speed of a mighty 8% is...um, nice? just give us a super fast 3ss run speed boost that increases the next holy damage skill by 20%. get us in melee for a big whallop, or get us out of the bad stuff.
 3) Divine Storm baby!
 4) A capstone that eliminates the taunt in our "taunt" ability, but does Holy damage instead (very much like the wrath taunt combined with the glyph). Having a range pulling ability on a low CD makes life so much easier.
 5) A capstone that reduces our Hammer of justice CD by 20 seconds and does holy damage when it's broken.
 6) An ability that, for 10 seconds, eliminates all mana costs and boosts holy damage by 20% or whatever.
 7) My druid has no idea what Diving storm even means, but she thinks my high elf paladin is cute in her frilly plate armor, so she supports it because my pally wants it.

Anything honestly would be better then the dumpsterfire that is Repentance. I GREATLY appreciate your recognition of it's lameness and your effort to make it viable, but you simply cannot polish poop. Give us something that people remember when they think Ret pally. And repentance isn't it.

EDIT: OK, so I thought about it, and I suppose that the fact that it goes for 30s makes it semi-OK? It still feels incredibly limited for a capstone. it still feels weird. It will only be useable in raids or on bosses immune to that stuff. It's a "too bad for open world play" kinda thing, it's still feels very one sided for a capstone. I would still prefer my other ideas, they are much more in the flavor of the Ret pally and make a generic capstone worth taking no matter what playstyle you are doing.

## Post 103264 by Lazarvs — 2024-10-17T02:37:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103264#p103264 | page 2 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Wow, this reminds me when the people cryed when a patch modifying pvp stuff came out on retail, there is an incoming river of complaints that would be enough to flood the entire planet! Let the TwowPocalypse begin ye Doomsayers!

But onward with the good news!

You've actually managed to refresh the purpose of vanilla, and bring a smile to a person that thinks as some might think aswell. You aligned some details of WC3 with wow, and made changes with that in consideration, i must say, im astonished with what you did here, and well, yeah, it takes alot of guts to put up with what is about to come.

As a dude that mostly plays 3 classes (although i played them all, with the exception of shamans) in this server, mainly because i like those 3 better. I have to speak mainly of what i saw in those.

Mage - I think you did a fantastic job here, Arcane tree is making me remind of all the good stuff that came late in TBC, making it a tree desirable to play, very mana consuming, but you can get mana now as a mage with the wand talent. Impressive i must say. Also, making the frost talent tree more fluid to play, with additional synergies, is a gush of fresh air! And fire just got a little tweak aswell!

Although i gotta say that putting ignite on 6 sec, might perpetuate the ignite damage to solo 1 player and that might be a terrible thing, you might want to rework that, or.. if you managed to spread the threat of the ignite to several mages adding charges to it, maybe you should also consider spreading the damage done, to all of them aswell. Just my 2 cents.

Warlock - AM I GLAD to see that affliction is up in the table, more strong than ever, and with exceptional taste! This will be a fun tree to explore now. Demonologist had a major breakthrough, to balance with the other Pet Class, the hunter. Now i can say that Demons will surely be more seen and used, this revamp surely has gotten warlocks thinking about going Demonologist, be it for pve, or pvp.

Destruction got a little bit less tweaks, but it's always gonna be there for whoever wants to play the "shadow mage". Overall, warlock was stripped out of a variety of dead talents, and i think you did an awesome job here, can't wait to play it!

Warrior - Well, what can i say.. Let's spot the facts first. In vanilla, raid setups were consistently balanced.. despite the fact that you had pure dps classes such as rogues, mages, and warlocks, making the bulk of the raid setup list, in between theese 3 classes, ending up usually having 3 to 4 groups, easily. With the time passing, and returning to 1.12, wow was massively known, and just before classic arrived, it was usual to see 14 to 18 warriors per raid. That meant that the raid setup was pretty much made in the idea that most of the classes would be there to support the warrior class as the main source of dps. This because we all knew that warrior was the top dps class ingame, just mostly gear dependant. And to top threat as a tank, you pretty much had to go fury-prot specc, doing most of the fight's with 2h weapon setup.

Well, seems that perk is about to come to an end here. And with some logic added to it, it seems.

Because i can't imagine a tank without a shield, in a aesthetic look, and it suits the change.

I prefer warrior as a tank, but i understand that many players play the class for it's dps projection and the majority of people will not be glad with theese changes, i believe. Nevertheless, the changes made to the Class enforce what must be enforced, a tank must wear a shield, and although i saw that it might have some initial issues with the traditional playstyle of tanking and generating threat, it might land in a nice place.

The time taken in the readjustment of the game will be massive perhaps, even to know of other classes mechanics, and how that will affect the raids, it's impossible to foresee.

As i saw written somewhere, theese changes might not be final, and the devs might reajust some to compensate some missing details or unbalancing changes.

I feel that your heart is in the right place, I praise you guys for such a bold patch. Hope it all comes to end well and in acceptance of the majority of the player base.

If not, the Unreal engine will fill up the vagues.

Let the games.. begin.

## Post 103279 by Mistermadigan — 2024-10-17T05:25:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103279#p103279 | page 3 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I'd still really want Druids to get a normal rez.
When you look at all the other healers they have a normal rez and a "gimmick".

Shaman have Ancestral Spirit and Reincarnation for a self-rez.

Priests have Resurrection and Spirit of Redemption (a gimmick to keep healing after they die).

Paladins have Redemption and Divine Intervention (a gimmick to prevent someone from dying).

In a way the Warlock's Soulstone spell is more useful as the targets of the spell have the option to immediately use it in combat, or wait for combat to end and then revive the party/raid.  Druids often have to run and reposition and then have the right rank and seed reagent in order to use their gimmick spell - making it less reliable than the Warlock spell.

All Druids have is the gimmick battle rez with such a long cooldown that makes them worthless in dungeon groups if there's no other class than can rez.  Just heal better so that nobody dies, get gud scrub.

Like, I'd be fine with a variation of the druid rez spell that consumes the seeds that can only be used out of combat with no cooldown.  This is just a bad joke at this point.  There's no good reason for Druids to not have a normal revive spell.

## Post 103284 by Anikedon — 2024-10-17T06:20:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103284#p103284 | page 3 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I appreciate the work that went into these changes, and am excited to see how some of my preferred classes - namely paladin, warrior, rogue, and hunter - perform, I question the idea behind turning Discipline into a pure DPS spec.

It seems like a half-implemented idea of what Blizz did originally in Legion, turning the spec into a dps/damage prevention hybrid. When that change was implemented, I swapped to Holy as that spec was much more straight forward, and reliable in the traditional healing sense. Discipline can also represent a disciplined mind, not just the castigation/flagellation of those who are deemed "impure" in the eyes of the priest. Thus it makes sense for the better mana regen/spell cost reduction as shown in the original version of the talent tree, and even moving into, the original, later versions of the game.

Referring back to the external disciplining mentioned in the notes, I also question the idea behind a button that damages (with the possibility of a crit) your allies in exchange for a buff. While that might make sense in the case of a Fury Warrior, I don't feel that real fits the theme of what you typically see amongst the priesthood represented in the game. The only real faction that would do something to that effect would be the Scarlet Crusade, which if that is the inspiration, perhaps someone spent too much time playing as Whitemane in HotS (I get it).

While I prefer melee, and tanking, overall, priest has always been my favourite clothie to play, and to see my favourite spec also be overhauled in such a way that basically forces you to have one heal spec rather than choosing between better heals, or better mana management and some good buffs (Inner Focus is a real nice clutch button to have), I felt compelled to let my opinion be written.

Again, I appreciate the work that has gone into the server, as the team clearly has passion.

## Post 103286 by Wolfheart1990 — 2024-10-17T07:03:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103286#p103286 | page 3 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Thank you for your hard work team.

While I appreciate the throwback to Warcraft III Priestess of the Moon, I am skeptical as to how functional using bows on a priest will be. Without attack power and physical hit/crit on gear, our bows will be like pea shooters compared to wands, which naturally have much higher base dps to reflect non-gear reliance, and also benefit from melee weaving and the improved Wand Specialization talent (+10% hit chance, chance to restore mana on hit). Searing arrows isn't enough to bridge this gap (adds up to 51-57 fire damange + 33% spellpower scaling on a 10 sec CD, SPENDS mana whereas using wand ranged attacks normally fills the role of dealing some damage while letting your mana regen for further spellcasting)

This, compared to the monumental new dwarf racial (Avatar. Turns your target into stone, increasing their armor by 25% and increasing all resistances by an amount equal to 150% of your level for 15 sec. (30 yard range, 1 Minute cooldown, 6% of your base mana as cost.), will only further cement dwarves a the Priest master race on Alliance, and cast Night Elves further into the shadows as a meme race.

Please consider re-balancing this change to make it at least in the same tier of usefulness as Avatar, or revoking it if the aforementioned is impossible.

As an alternative for another faithful throwback to Warcraft 3 in addition to / in place of the above, consider implementing Starfall in place of the currently weak Starshards. You could either make it a targetable AoE like Blizzard, or be much closer to the Wc3 rendition where it affects an area around the caster. This would distinguish Night Elves as the one priest race with access to an AOE while remaining faithful to our Warcraft 3 origins.

Edit: forgot to mention the added burden of sacrificing a bag slot's worth of inventory space for a quiver.

Okay, after reading everything (and understanding only a part as I don't play all classes :p), I still have a point I would like to understand. I won't get into what irritates me as a Night Elf Hunter (maybe we'll talk about this later, for the rage and the drama !).

Devs want to change things, but isn't there too much numbers upscaling ? I don't know how the balance of the new raid will be, but many specializations have free numbers boost in their talents, and not just weak playstyles which were lacking.

What I try to mean is, for the already existing content, wouldn't it making far easier to do it ? It's like a nerf of the difficulty when Blizzard wants you to go for the new content, but making the older raids or dungeons less challenging, if not boring and almost useless.

I could be wrong, but for example, Holy Priest's Spiritual Healing was giving 10% bonus to all their heals. Now 30%. That's quite a free bonus ! Protection Warrior is, at least in my opinion, a good tank. Now some talents which were improving his defensive stats are giving much more, for even less talent points.

And let's see the now Dwarf Priest racial. Okay, every priest has Fear Ward. Honestly, I think that's a good thing as it was a huge boost for some PvE encounter. But what happens when you put four Dwarves Priests in a raid ? As far as I can tell, that means they will rotate their racial to give a new bonus to the tank. A constant 25% increase in armor and 90 resistances to everything ! That is  quite a boost!

So yeah, I'm wondering where this is going about the power creeping of the classes and the content of the game.

This update is a heroic effort, just maybe needs another look over to make sure nobody's getting left out in the cold.

I have started to read each entries in depth. Since it's a huge wall of text, I won't be available to collect all my thoughts at the end, wanna give feedback as I go.
I think that racial changes are fair, specially if +3 (and more) weapon skill items get more frequent. Looking at you, Legacy. Alliance having some good PVP buttons to push is never bad for class balance. As a troll main (7 out of my 9 chars are trolls) berserking nerf hurts a bit but I find it absolutely fair. People usually don't know how broken it was.

Liking the way boomkin is moving. Instead of an either nature or arcane damage class it seems to be forced to combine the two. Flavorwise, good.
Slight concerns with feral, I'm afraid that things like barskin push them too much at PVP but since everything is getting stronger, this might be okay.
Liking resto changes but still no out of combat rez feels very weird.

BM hunter: same concern as with feral. Pet builds PVP as 2 vs 1 (almost). They might need a passive nerf which also damages them if the pet gets damaged or something. But we'll see, you did the balancing, not me.
MM seems perfect.
Survival: loving this, having a melee hunter. Putting down traps directly under the enemy during a fight might feel weird flavor-wise though. We'll see how it works out.

Arcane took a weird turn. You made them a mana-utility class sort of some years ago and now they are not really a utility class anymore, no more brilliance aura. It feels weird that all 3 mage builds race for the same caster DPS niche, just with different schools of magic. Would have preferred your 'rogue solution' to give variety to players and uniqueness to the trees.
Fire: totally fair but a bit boring. Fire mages coming back after changes and playing almost exactly the same while seeing everyone else having weird abilities might be a feels bad for them.
Frost: liking the PVP nerf and interested about the icycles.
My main regret with mages are that they are now 3 flavors of the same caster DPS niche. Arcane support concept from the past might have made the trees more diverse.

For palas: I totally agree that holy pala needed a unique identity. If additional taken damage is not a problem (they wear plate and a shield optimally after all) and they can fight of occasional AoE stuns and silences, this might be amazing. But reading this I immediately think about Strat UD's banshee and cases come to my mind where a healer relying mostly on melee-distance to work properly might feel like griefing. I hope it works out because I love the concept.
About prot: unsure. The idea of relying more on the prot tree is me gusta. They using the shield to deal damage is also cool. But can't judge neither them nor the retris atm.

Will check the others later.

## Post 103355 by aguric — 2024-10-17T11:22:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103355#p103355 | page 4 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I recently got into turtle wow and I've been enjoying the experience so far. I used to play tons of old vanilla when I was younger, probably over 2 years in /played. Turtle wow has brought back alot of nostalgia for me, It's been fun and all but this patch scares me...   maintenance_turtle

I've read through all the changes and although I respect the immense amount of effort you guys put into this and agree with many design philosophies, I'm afraid you're trying to fix too much at once and this will alienate much of the community who just wants a simple nostalgic classic+ experience.

Even stuff that's in a good spot you are trying to "make even better"; like warriors for instance; even though in your opening statement say that all 3 specs are in a good spot and fun to play.

Just as an example: I have a good friend who used to play warrior I can tell you what will happen if I convince him to come to turtle-wow for a classic+ experience after this patch drops:

1. At character starting screen he will ask why all signature Horde racials are nerfed.
2. At level 1 he will ask why his rage behaves differently.
3. At level 8, he will ask why his Hamstring has a 6 sec CD.
4. At level 10, he will ask why the talent tree is all scrambled.
5. At level 12, he will probably quit the game cuz this isn't the vanilla warrior he remembers. Why did they do this? Warriors were fine...
I hope you understand the issue here...

 **My general suggestions:**
- **Don't change too much at once - don't copy Blizzard patches please!**  scared_turtle
This is the same mistake Blizzard used to make. They never developed the game in a slow & steady pace with small changes with carefully gathered feedback from the community. Instead they remained largely absent and then they dropped these patch bombs out of the blue with revamped talent trees, new abilites for everyone, marketing team goes "Hey everyone! Your favorite class gets X and Y! Come play again!" and it's always a disorienting mess.

I'd much more appreciate if it all went in a slow and steady pace. Like give a patch for 1-2 classes seperately. Warriors for instance are fine already - there's no rush trying to make it even better in some mega class patch.

Warriors could be it's own patch: "The Warrior patch"  - everyone gets time to try out Warrior and give feedback of the changes. That would be great!

- **Please avoid trying to fix stuff that ain't broken.**
For example: Hamstring/Execute is a warrior core ability that's gone from no CD to several seconds CD.

Just don't give it a CD - it will be devastating for Warr when they parry/miss/dodge and it won't feel like classic wow at all. Balance around it instead.

- **Respect the old talent tree.**
Please try to avoid scrambling talents around between tiers - even though it's for a good cause, it will alienate people. If you want to make changes then try to be more subtle about it.

For example: Tactical Mastery is now tier 1 so that more specs have access to it.

Do this instead:
 - make the old effect baseline or similar.
 - make a new Tactical Mastery in the same old place in the Arms tree, now with some additional benefits to "Stance Dancing". It could for example be that you keep the positive effect of your old stance for 3 seconds after switching stance or something similar.

The important thing is to keep the talent in it's old place and that it buffs the effect. Keep it classic!

- **Don't go bananas on the racials.**
Nelf priests gets the hunter auto shot ability (as I understand it) which means they'll be able to move around and shoot at the same time. Yeah priestess of the moon is cool and all but this a crazy racial imbalance between priests - and doesn't it mess up loot?

Do this instead:
 - Allow nelf priests to equip bows.
 - Make bow transmog work with wands.
 - Rename Searing Arrow to Searing Shot and just give the wand/bow projective a burning effect.

This way it's balanced between priests, nelf can role-play as priestsess of the moon and they won't compete with other classes for bows but still prio wands. You also no longer need adding +healing +spell/dmg bows in the game for just 1 race-specific class.

... And please don't hate the Horde. We love our active racials :(

A thanks to you who read this   smiling_turtle_head

## Post 103357 by Akos1896 (Grandmaster of Forum PvP) — 2024-10-17T11:34:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103357#p103357 | page 4 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Priests. Baseline fearward is absolutely welcome.
Discipline is very interesting, I'm looking forward to playing it. 'Disciplining' own teammates by doing minor damage to reach a specific effect is extremely unique.
Holy is holy with a viable lightwell. I'm a bit disappointed that champion abilities didn't get a revamp but it is what it is. Also, encouraging renew cast for bigger heals feels unique.
I am really disappointed with shadow though. I understand that gear powercreep will reach levels where shadow priest recharge becomes too much. But these numbers just gut the shadow priest utility for early raiders (unless I really trust you and I believe that spell coefficient changes still make the reharge relevant even with weaker gear).
But most importantly. Randomly giving shadow priests the option to use holy nova is something I can't accept. Holy nova is a holy spell and allowing shadow priests to use 1 holy spell feels very bad design. Please just make an ability called shadow nova which is only castable in shadowform to prevent this design fail.
Including the night elf bows. I understand the lore background but as it stands, it will create many problems. There is a balance at Vanilla WOW: 3 relic classes, 3 bow classes, 3 wand classes. Tis was never changed or messed with. Allowing one race+class combination to use another item at that slot will spark debates. F.ex. 'I'm a troll shaman, dammit! I literally have bow specialization at every WOW expansion why the heck can't I use a bow on my relic slot if a dámn nelf can?'.
Also, if any bow can be equipped to that slot, the amount of salt when a random priest wins a really valuable bow over a warrior/hunter/rogue will be unbelievable.

Rogues I really liked. Will need to see this in action but I think you gave the trees perfect identity and interesting things to do. Specially loving subtlety as a utility tree. Rogue utility build... I need to get used to this expression.

Shamans.
Ele's elemental mastery change is fair. Ele's were too OP at PVP while had random threat spike issues at raiding too often. I welcome this change. Otherwise changes are minimal but good qol. Ele's trinity of problems for raiding was mana+threat+nat rez. Better clearcasting and water shield somewhat helps with mana. Electrify kinda helps with threat (but I'd still wanna see ele's being able to use grace of air at raids as it is supposed to). Nat rez was not addressed here, that's my main regret.
For enhancement, this is a complete overhaul, it is too early to tell. Does actually doing stuff instead of auto-attacking depletes mana too fast? Is it consequent enough? No idea, will need to see in action. Loving the shaman tanking option, though.
Resto... I mostly like it. Some people shout mana problems but I disagree, you just gave a bunch of meditation to a class which can easily get spirit if he goes after some specific items to do so.
My main problem is chain heal at raiding. Even spirit link rewards chain heal spam and you made 2 sec cast time available for everyone. things like tidal wave or undertow almost feel irrelevant at this point because based on how I see things based on a lot of resto experience, people will be just chain heal bot even more, it's even better now (unless you nerf chain heal scaling).

## Post 103390 by Wuiffi — 2024-10-17T14:00:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103390#p103390 | page 5 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Shadow Priest pve:
Instead of fixing one of the major problems of Shadow, which was fixed in WOTLK by Blizzard, you decided to stay on the same path.
What i mean by this is the scaling with different stats(spell, hit, crit and haste).
As we all know Shadow in classic, after you reach hitcap, what doesn't take long considering having 11% via talents and raidbuff, only properly scales with spelldamage and this has some severe downsides!
A list of issues that popped up experiencing it, on Turtle and blizz classic+TBC, playing the whole pve content:

 1. Spelldamage scales linear compared to haste, crit and hit.
For example a fictive cast with basedamage of 1000, 100% crit multiplier and a 100% spellcoefficient,
results in an average damage of 1010 having 1% crit.
Instead of having 1% crit, we increase the spelldamage by 10 resulting in 1010 damage each cast.
Now we already got 1000 spell(better gear) and the cast does 2000 damage at baseline.
We make the same comparison as before:
 1% crit results in an average damage of 2020, while 10 additional Spelldamage increase the damage to 2010.
At this point 1% crit is twice as powerful.

Because shadow is the only spec that mainly scales linearly, compared to other specs, it leads to deviations, resulting in over and underperforming at certain gearlevels.
For example: In TBC shadow during prebis or T4 was very strong. Especially after introducing haste in Sunwell that changed.
Some specs performance improved tremendously due to the new equipment, outperforming SP by an extra 1000 DPS. So while SP got an increase by about 500 DPS other improved by 1500 DPS.

Following points are especially troublesome in endgame content.
 2. The gear issue:
Every other stat on an equipment is a waste on you. So you are usually last, when it gets to loot distribution.

 3. The gear is worse:
Because usually there are stats on the gear you do not really scale with but these stats still taking up resources.
for example:
If u get an item with 50 spell and 2% crit a typical caster class may get an equivalent of 80 spell, assuming 1% crit is equivalent to 15 spell at a certain gear level. SP gets like 2 or 3 spell for 1% crit ending in 56 spell equivalent.

 4. Gear with multiple stats usually have higher stats in total, than gear only high in one stat.
for example:
If there is an Item with itemlevel 90, that gives 50 spell and 2% crit and there is an item for the same slot with itemlevel 90 only giving spell, it won't have 80 spell damage, it will be more likely in the 60s
Or an other option would be 42 spell, 1% hit, 1% crit, 1% haste.
The more stats a class scales with the stronger the items are for your class. SP is last on this list.

 5. This also effects PvP, while many people in BGs are casual geared, SP on similar gear level, outperforms many of them heavily. The closer you get to high end PvP, the more other classes close the gap or starting to outperform you.

My conclusion: You will never fix the problems surrounding shadow priest if you don't fix the scaling issue.
For pvp it would need a post twice as long as this.
But the results are way worse than in pve, it is an absolut and utter disaster.
Sry for my bad English, I hope it is understandable.

## Post 103417 by Bugranger — 2024-10-17T15:00:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103417#p103417 | page 5 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I like that you are not afraid to experiment, that's cool, keep it up!

But some decisions seem completely unplayable right now.

A few comments on "New Talent: Counterattack". Rooting a melee target after a parry for 3 seconds seems like a joke.

Because you can only parry melee targets that are fighting you. And rootingtargets that are already in melee doesn't seem like a priority for a warrior.

A warrior's priority is keeping a target in melee for as long as possible if the target is trying to escape. And there are only 2 such targets that are in melee with you, making attacks and planning to get out of melee range - Rogue and Hunter.

Both targets are trying to distance themselves from you with fewer attacks (this is obvious, since they both have CC with a fast recovery). And since the trigger is tied to a parry that can't be increased much, the chance to hold the target will be only 10% (and this is for a very small number of attacks).

I would like to suggest that this ability should not be tied to parrying the target's attack, but to when the target dodges your attack.

And this will sound logical, because the hamstring now has a cooldown and failures with it can become critical, and the new talent in some cases will "insure" these failures.

Looking forward to the patch, thanks! :)

## Post 103436 by Vainamoinen77 — 2024-10-17T16:46:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103436#p103436 | page 5 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

First off, I just wanted to say that I am very impressed by the scope of this patch. This being said, I would like to comment on some of the upcoming changes to the Priest class.

> First and foremost, Discipline was quite neglected in our first batch of changes, failing to give it tools that allows it to be functional and viable by itself instead of being just a secondary specialization you go into for a few tools.

I sympathize with your intents, I often found myself thinking that Discipline could stand having a more clearly designed identity. Unfortunately, there is one glaring problem: **Holy and Shadow are**, under normal circumstances, **mutually exclusive talent trees**. Yes, I am aware that some niche specs invest points in both, but generally speaking most Shadow Priests are sticking to Shadowform, and Holy priests are sticking to healing.

This means that both Holy and Shadow will turn towards Discipline as a secondary spec, and thus Discipline ought to offer talents that can be useful to both. I tried messing around with the talent calculator a bit from the perspective of a Shadow Priest, and I do notice that you reach a point when, quite simply, none of the options offered by Discipline seems appealing, or even useful at all.

More conerningly, the talent calculator states that **it is no longer possible to cast PW: Shield while in shadowform**. This change is not mentioned in the thread, despite the fact that depriving Shadow Priests of their main defensive spell is both a massive and an extremely questionable change, especially given how reliant Shadow Priests are on a channeled spell to deal damage. It would make doing solo content much, much less enjoyable.

Meanwhile, the Mana cost reduction to buffs is appreciated, reapplying buffs in between drinks is highly tedious.

> Fear Ward is now baseline, learned at level 20. Dwarf Priests are getting a new racial ability due to Fear Ward becoming baseline.

That's probably for the best, locking such a powerful utility behind a specific race was troublesome. The new Avatar spell for Dwarf Priests makes it seem that they will still be very happy with their choice anyway.

> Removed Elune's Grace, Night Elf Priests will now be able to use Bows with the ability to auto shoot and learn the ability Searing Shot.

This one is as cool as it is jarring. On the one hand, I find it lovely how true to WCIII this is. On the other, I struggle to imagine how this could ever play out nicely. Currently, Nelf Priests already have one special spell that is only there for lore reasons (starshards), which is otherwise not very useful. Elune's Grace was a very awkward defensive spell for a Priest, but it was useful in a pinch, so I guess it will be missed. I struggle to imagine ever wanting to be able to wield a bow instead of having a defensive cooldown, as unreliable as it may be, given that bows don't usually have useful stats for a Priest slapped onto them. I do think that it is a very flavourful change, but I fear that it is going to be either completely useless, or capable of causing problems down the line. I guess we'll see.
(Speaking of Nelves in general, what thought process led to the change to shadowmeld? It used to be a nice, if unimpressive, utility racial that allowed players to eat and drink in peace, but slightly empowering its capabilities as a tool for ambushes hardly seems to warrant such a longer cooldown.)

> Vampiric Embrace: Now has a 2 second cast time.

Alright, I'll be honest: I hate this change. Keeping VE up on regular mobs while in a dungeon was already a chore and a tax on your action economy that felt poorly thought and unnecessary; and this makes it that much worse. I understand the need to keep Spriest in check in a PvP environment, but I think that everything would feel smoother if VE was a passive buff with toned-down numbers instead of this.

> Holy Nova is now usable in Shadowform. Doing so will cause self-damage instead of self-healing.

Very cute. Unfortunately, picking up Holy Nova would steel require a Shadow Priest to do a deep dive into the Holy talent tree, which is hardly worth the investment. That is without mentioning that seeing a Shadow Priest spamming Holy Nova would simply look wrong, it would need a bit of a reskin for it to look natural.

## Post 103443 by Forthehorde — 2024-10-17T17:29:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103443#p103443 | page 5 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

*"People are resistent to change."*
I get that.

 *"You can't please all of the people all the time."*
I get that too.

But there are 3 fundamental issues at work here:
 1) Many changes alter the flavor of Vanilla, and Vanilla is why most (if not all) of us are here in the first place.
 2) Many changes seem PVP-related, which can potentially be a net-negative for a cross-faction PVE game.
 3) It's better to enhance what's lacking, than to nerf what's working.  This is originally what made TurtleWow great.

Personally, I was looking forward to class changes, but was expecting individual buffs to what was lacking, not an overhaul of entire systems. And certainly wasn't expecting nerfs, regardless of how many buffs balence them out. If something needs a buff, then elevate it to the same level of fun as everything else. Don't drag other stats down.

One of the pitfalls of overhauling a game system is that it's very easy to get into the mindset of balancing *numbers*.  This leads to the notion "well if I change this, I better change that"... which in turn leads to more changes, and soon the result becomes less recognizable.  By that time, you've put so much time and effort into it, you start to think "I can't go back now".

But that's exactly when you need to stop and ask these 2 questions:
 1) Does this *subtraction* make me want to play this charater MORE?
 2) Does this *addtion* make me want to play this charater MORE?

Because if the answer isn't "yes", then what's the point?  Otherwise, if you combine subtractions and additions then stand back and say it's *balanced*, then you're on the road to pleasing none of the people none of the time.

Helldivers 2 leanred this the hard way.

I'm not saying TurtleWow is going the direction of Helldivers 2, but many parts of this changelog have that feel.

*Last edited by Forthehorde on Thu Oct 17, 2024 6:08 pm, edited 7 times in total.*

## Post 103459 by Zulnam (Bug Report Enthusiast) — 2024-10-17T19:11:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103459#p103459 | page 6 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I am ready to open the portal to Outland and let the demons in.

Kidding. Some of these I really like, some of them I really don't. And the fact that it is a massive change across all classes means the meta will be altered drastically, for both pve and pvp.

With only numbers and words on a forum, it's a bit too early to tell but lets go over some of the ones that stood out to me.

This is primarily from a PvP player perspective as that is my favorite game mode.

 **Affliction Warlock** - i absolutely love it. It sounds great and Dark Harvest being a channeled ability, like so many others in the warlock toolkit, synergies very well with other talents. My only concern is that it will be too easily dispelled, nullifying it entirely. I would change **Resilient Shadows** to instead prevent a warlock's dots from being dispelled by the same percentage (10/20/30)

 **Hunter** - i feel like the Wingclip cooldown serves only to nerf hunter in pvp. No one was asking for this ability to do more damage, that was not it's intended purpose, but to help the player put some distance between them and their targets and escape the dead zone. Now with the cooldown, you better hope it doesn't get parried, dodged or misses entirely.

Also, I am not happy with Survival being turned into a melee spec. I still believe this is only to appease a small percentage of the players. Survival was meant to be a utility spec (hence why it had some melee abilities, because melee is utility for hunter). To add insult to injury, traps being placed in combat, a massive boost to hunters in pvp, is now a 31-point talent in Survival. A spec for melee hunters. That can now also fire their bow. And have Aimed Shot. And can put a frost trap in combat.

 **Shaman** - while I like the overall changes to the class, we should call a spade a spade: both Elemental and Enhancement were nerfed in PvP. Windfury, as you said, is a core identity of the enhancement shaman. It is also a proc. Which meant you could do 3 hits (on a slow weapon, 9+ seconds), without getting it. Now, that can be even longer. And it is guaranteed to be longer if you manage to get a proc.

Placing the option to change your Searing Totem's target behind a 21-point talent also seems like a poor choice to me.

 **Paladin** - overall i like the paladin changes quite a lot. Holy shock got nerfed as an offensive ability, but with the changes to Holy Strike and Crusader Strike it might not be as heavy as it originally seems. But the idea of a "melee healer" sounds very good in my head. Remains to be seen however if the changes will perform well enough in either pve or pvp to be a viable alternative to them sitting in the back, in cloth, and spamming flash of light.

I would love if repentance would also somehow affect targets in pvp, where it most often is castable. Perhaps after removal for any reason it does 50% of the damage meant for immune targets. This way the 31-point ret talent feels like more than just a light CC.

 **Rogue** - the main pvp spec has been completely evaporated I feel. But i do not main the class, so i am not sure how it will fare in the future, with Assassination now relying heavily on poisons and Subtlety on utility.

 **Night Elf Priest** - the addition of bows to the class will most likely do nothing to it but it is a very nice little flavor change that will certainly help with RP. I would love to see it expanded for more races (ie: orc mages and warlocks with axes? Why not?)

 **Frost Mage** - another slight nerf to one of vanilla wow's most iconic pvp specs, with an added new ability that, frankly, sounds bad for pvp. Not only do you lose mobility, but if an enemy player hits you they have a chance of taking out 30% of your health out in one swoop. And it doesn't even apply frost effects. This for a class and spec that relies on high mobility and control due to its low defense.

 **Overall notes**
 - Has PvP been tested with the new talent trees? I know WoW was never primarily about pvp, but now i feel like it is being overlooked altogether for the sake of pve with some of these changes.
 - with such a major overhaul of all talents, just be prepared to do 2-4 more balance changes next year, when the inevitable OP specs arise
 - another argument against changing so much in one go is the, lets be honest here, not stellar reception. The class balance was announced a long time ago (9 months?) and a lot of expectations where raised. It was inevitable that some would not be happy, but now a lot of people feel that their favorite toy will be tampered with just a little too much.

It's like the boiling frog metaphor. Put a frog in boiling water and it will jump out. But put it in regular water and slowly increase the temperature and voila! Frog legs.

## Post 103466 by Forthehorde — 2024-10-17T20:05:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103466#p103466 | page 6 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Too many changes.  Not in the spirit of Vanilla.

KEEP IT SIMPLE.  For each class:
A) List ONE flaw for the class, then suggest ONE thing to make that flaw better (not perfect, just better)
B) Add 1 QOL tweak that would make the class more fun.

Example:

Shaman:
Flaw: mana effiency
Fix: better mana-per-tick regen water shield?
QOL: (pick your favorite.  If none are needed, then that's fine too.)

Hunter:
Flaw: late-game damage scaling
Fix: Pet/weapon scaling
QOL: additional pet stable slots (and summonable stable master w/CD, sold for $ in donation store).

Priest:
Flaw: Lightwell is near-useless (nobody clicks on ground items during raids/dungeons)
Fix: Make lightwell give a drinkable health potion?
QOL: lower group buff mana costs

Warlock:
Flaw:  (pick your favorite)
Fix: (pick your favorite)
QOL: stacking sould shards (and ability to turn down/off pet voices.  Maybe in the new engine)

... and so on.

The idea is to only address the most glaring issue for each class.  1 change, 1 fix.  Then see how it plays out.  Later on you can make another list, and shore up any remaining flaws.  But do them one at time.  Small tweaks go a LONG way.  Retain the flavor of Vanilla.

As for PVP, I strongly advise against changing classes to solely suit PVP, as it will negatively affect PVE, or at least the overall positive player vibe.  Instead, maybe add PVP-only racials that are only active when the character is flagged for PVP.  Then you can go crazy with all the balance you want, since it would only affect PVP.

## Post 103469 by Steakhouse (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-17T20:31:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103469#p103469 | page 6 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Great job ! Excited to see how these play out. These make me want to roll just about every class !

I'm unsure about the change to Intimidation, however. While you are absolutely correct that losing the flat threat in addition to the stun on a resist is problematic, the current function of Intimidation (ie the one prior to the upcoming changes) is that when it lands, you can forget about pulling threat from that mob until it dies, even if your pet stops attacking it, so you could make your pet attack target A, land intimidate, then switch it to target B, and meanwhile, you can damage target A without ever worrying about pulling threat from your pet. I'm afraid the new implementation will require leaving your pet on target A for a bit, even with the threat modifier affecting Growl. A few of the Rogue talents mention "this (de)buff will work even if Blind/Rupture/Distract fails", why wasn't that path chosen ?

Numbers speak a thousand words : Currently, Intimidation deals 580 threat, plus whatever attack damage was dealt, and is often followed by a Growl, which deals 170/240/320/415 threat at ranks for level 30/40/50/60 respectively, for a total of 995 + attack damage at max level. With the new implementation, we're looking at 415 * 1.5 + attack damage * 1.5. If your pet's attack would deal 150 damage, the previous initimidation + growl would deal a total of 1145 threat, while the new would deal 847.5 threat, a pretty steep drop: your pet would need to attack two more times to generate as much threat as a simple application of Intimidation did previously. This isn't a huge difference, to be clear, but is much more significant for leveling hunters, where Intimidation's enormous threat really shines when handling multiple mobs simultaneously, in which case it acts as a pseudo-taunt: at level 30, Intimidation (580) + Growl (170) + 75 damage = 825 threat. With the new Intimidation, a Growl and an attack would only generate 367.5 threat, less than half as much ; your pet would need to attack the target 5 more times to close that gap.

I'm also a bit concerned about Avatar. Making Fear Ward and Spirit Link available to all races was obviously the correct choice, because people should play the race they want, not the one they have to ; but Avatar seems to force 4 dwarf priests in raids so they can cycle Avatar (15 secs vs 1 minute cooldown = 4 dwarf priests can permabuff a tank). If Avatar is here to stay, I think a "Sated" debuff similar to retail Bloodlust is needed so that tanks can't benefit from it permanently.

Nevertheless I'll try it out ! It's hard to make a full opinion on something before actually playing with it. If need be I'll just make a separate thread about this concern.

Special shouthout to the priestess of the moon with a bow. What an excellent lore addition.

## Post 103485 by Phoenixphire (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2024-10-17T21:40:00Z

Overall these are great changes. Many people don’t like change but as much as some people may disagree I think these feel very vanilla like and I think will form a great foundation for the server going forward. I like the scope of the changes, the depth, and the focus on flavor and identity.

I give these an A+ for effort and B+ for execution. Very well done and thank you for the monumental effort this must have taken.

The 2 changes I think need to be revisited are hamstring and wingclip. Sorry lads this is a miss. WAY too many unforeseen consequences of this change. This was the one set of changes I REALLY said, yall didn’t think it through enough. This change makes warriors worse against match ups there were already poor against (kiting) and this makes hunters WAY easier to stick to and dead zone. If your trap don’t save you, or god forbid there is more than one enemy the hunter is immediately cooked. Rogue, shaman, warriors (Ironically), mage deadzoning, warlocks deadzoning, SP deadzoning, are going to eat hunters alive without their feign trap. This makes them sitting ducks in pvp if they god forbid have feign on CD, are fight 2 or more enemies, or miss the trap. Not to mention warriors now not being able to stop flag carriers, are now even worse in their bad matchups (mage druid who will never have to deal with the new Root they get since they can just avoid being parried) and now even can get easily kited buy shamans, locks with CoE and others.

This needs to be looked at again or reworked. Not a good change and will actively harm pvp for hunters (who aren’t melee) and warriors in an overly aggressive way. Reduce the CD AT LEAST. If you think hamstring and wingclip are that big a deal. Give warriors and hunters a better alternative to get a similar result without just taking the tool away and not replacing it adequately. I hope you reconsider this or take a different approach because I believe besides this change, 95% of the others are very good and positive.

Other than that. Fantastic set of changes, i know yall are getting hate right now, but for the most part I couldn’t be happier with the effort shown here. Very proud of this team.   smiling_turtle_head

## Post 103488 by joeycupcakes — 2024-10-17T21:46:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103488#p103488 | page 6 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Greater Demons (Infernal, Felguard, Doomguard):** These flavourful spells that are meant to allow you to summon powerful demons were severely underpowered and/or clunky to use before and did not fit their intended fantasy. That’s why we decided to rework them and address many pain points of using these spells, while also applying numbers balancing. These greater demons will no longer be a valid target for Enslave Demon and will be immediately under the control of the warlock when summoned, will have set duration for how long you can control them, and after the time is up, they will turn on their master (without ensuing chaos for your whole party). Usefulness and power of these greater demons will be further enhanced in the deep Demonology tree.
>
>  **Demon Gate:** renamed from Demon Portal, 30 min cd, 4 sec cast time, no longer is ritual, but instead drops down a demon gate object that spawns the Felguard after anothe 6 sec, 1 min duration.
>
>  **Inferno:** cooldown reduced from 20 min to 10 min, cast time reduced from 2 sec to 1.5 sec, 30 sec duration.
>
>  **Ritual of Doom:** lowered required players for the ritual from 4 to 2, no longer randomly kills one of the participants, 1 min duration

These are the kind of changes I don't like. All the quirky and roleplay elements of the world is what makes classic so different. This feels like a modern Blizzard "streamlining" type change.

> **Rework: Holy Shock**
>  Now acquired at row 5. Can no longer target enemies
>
>  *While we understand that the “shockadin” specialization is beloved by many, it does not fit our vision for the class.*

Not a fan of this. I started playing here with hopes of finally playing a shockadin in classic. I'd prefer some kind of nerf, rather than completely taking it away as a damage source. I care about having options for playstyles and skills. This feels like straying away from options and tailoring the game towards an "expected" way to play. The idea of having a skill that can be used for harm or help has the "hybrid" class feel to it.

Other than that, most of the paladin changes look decent. Hand of Reckoning is great.

> **Wing Clip** now has a 6 second cooldown

> **Hamstring** now has a 6 second cooldown.

Why? What was the conclusion that led to this decision?

> **Subtlety:** This specialization lacks both identity and falls off in performance in raiding environments due to not being able to use their openers after their stealth and vanish are spent.

I always looked at the sub spec as the "PvP" spec. More burst as a trade off for less sustained damage, and tools to escape more often. A true "assassin" class. That's its true identity to me, even though this server does not prioritize PvP.

The Dust of Disappearance sounds like a pretty cool idea.

 **Here's some other general comments on the changes:**

I'd say if you are going to change racials, leave the good ones alone and make the bad ones better (but that can also be a slippery slope). That will create the most amount of player satisfaction, if that is a concern.

People will meme on it, but I like the idea of giving night elf priests bows. It fits with the lore and will increase the roleplay value of the world. Will it be bad? Maybe. I think extra options can be good, though.

Anything I did not comment on either is not a concern, or I glazed over it while trudging through the wall of text. These are just my opinions that I wanted to share, so take them with a grain of salt.

Ok, I've had time to look over the changes from my initial kneejerk reaction and have this to say on my main class and favorite spec in every version of WoW:

I know I cant speak for everyone when I say this, but the appeal for shaman to me is the buffing and utility of the class. Some of my most fun in vanilla is totem twisting WF/Agi, or WF/Nature Res Totem and keeping Ancestral Healing up as often as I could with r1 healing waves in downtime and managing mana regen gear and items and Mana Tide to be able to maintain the buffs.

But with these changes, to my understanding totem-twisting is dead, as resto any micro in regards to mana conservation is dead, and restoration has been handicapped for the lowest common denominator who REFUSE to use their totems on the class who's unique feature is **TOTEMS** and replaced instead with passive proc chances...

Is this retail? This **SOUNDS** like retail.

You guys talk about 'slow-cast high value AOE healing' as well while making a talent that makes it only a 2 second cast and making it just worse for the other specs who are already NOT GEARING FOR HEALING. You guys are actually just devolving the Horde's hybrid class into a specialist by nerfing the base kit and the lower portions of the talent trees.

Why not lock the other trees until you get the capstone while we're at it? Ooo, how about lightning bolt regens your mana too, and maybe add a-a-a-a secondary resource that you build up and spend on different spells? Shamans are AOE healers right? Why not make it, idk, RAIN or something to heal in an AOE? Maybe make healing totem 2 charges? Give shamans an ability to cast while moving while we're at it.

## Post 103537 by Silb — 2024-10-18T03:54:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103537#p103537 | page 7 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I would like to echo the sentiment of "changing too many things too far", potentially turning this project from vanilla+ to a fun server. IMO you need to tweak numbers, not overhaul entire classes.

Removing Holy Shock's damage component is a damn shame, it doesn't affect PvE (the main draw of twow) and only destroys a fun meme spec for pvp and a burst option for healers. Changing Holy Strike is 100% a good thing though.

Disc priests becoming a pure dps spec instead of a support/ hybrid spec is also unnecessary. Smite priests were already pretty decent (mostly lacking longevity), no reason to gut an entire tree to support that spec. I loved being able to do good damage and healing at the same time as a disc priest, guess that's no longer a thing.

Survival hunters being a full on melee spec also means less options for ranged specs. You could have left the spec mostly intact while buffing melee skills (Mongoose Bite, fire traps). The new damage scaling on these melee abilities are also weapon % based, meaning dual wield is no longer an option despite synergizing well with Swift Aspects. Moving Counterattack to warriors and turning Wingclip/ Hamstring into damage abilities with a CD is also a baffling choice and a potentially huge nerf.

My prediction of what the deep prot cookie cutter build would look like.

Feels round and perfect tbh, only a 10-rage tactical mastery for mocking blows, 3 talent points that you can bounce between 3/5 one-hand specialization or anticipation if your aren't def capped, another 3 talent points you can put in 3% crit from Cruelty (cutting them from Improved Taunt + 1 from Toughness) ...

I don't know, I see the talent tree pretty solid for a protection warrior, both for an less geared toon or a BiS one.

We are going to have a LOT of rage for spending in heroic strikes: blocks generate more rage, revenge is basically free and sunder armor's cost now is only 10 rage.

Tbh I can't wait to test all these changes, and I feel the warrior needed a more aggressive and less rage starving playstyle. More room for cleaving and pumping real damage as a deep prot. I like it.

> **Bisalissy wrote: Thu Oct 17, 2024 1:45 am**
> These changes are massive! I really appreciate how much work was put into this. And the reworks for specs like Arcane, Balance and Discipline sound great!
>
>  My only concern is that this might trivialize the game. Classic WoW is already known for having easy raids, meanwhile the slow and challenging leveling experience also matters for some (including me). Even Fury Warriors got buffed and if the support specs also deal so much more damage, I fear everything might become very easy and fast to clear.

I think these are some excellent points. There will probably be some real power creep, and perhaps it would be a good time after this is done to revisit raid content and push the envelope a bit there, bring things up to speed so it can still be a challenge.

I think that power creep is inevitable in most games that offer upward change and progress. Most MMO's get away with the creep by just making new raids at the new level cap with that power in mind. in a more static environment like this, it may be necessary to adjust some things, or perhaps a new opportunity to add more raid content opening up those areas we still have yet to explore in the vanilla world.

I think it's part of what excites me about this project. the passion of the dev's for Old Warcraft lore and play open up exciting new possibilities while still being the game we all loved.

 3. Eliminate gimmicks: Crowd pummeler, totem twisting, Scatter+freezing trap.

 5. Normal taunt for tanking classes: shaman, paladin. And yes, hunters and rogues are not going to be tanks.

They also implemented most requested features for classes at a cost of some nerfs.

## Post 103616 by Akos1896 (Grandmaster of Forum PvP) — 2024-10-18T12:44:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103616#p103616 | page 8 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I know I've written to this thread many times but was thinking about these a lot.
Flavorwise I'm mostly happy, balance-wise we can't tell until experiments happen. At least, mostly.
Really liking the subtlety rogue changes for example, giving a rogue tree utility while perfectly staying in flavor is very nice.
Racials slightly concern me though. You can say that this is a cross-faction PVE server but some PVP still happens.
For specifics:
Many undeads have chosen to be undead for PVP reasons. 2% passive damage against certain races is nice but butchering wof means that many players who picked an undead and played a lot with the char can kinda feel betrayed. Wof needed nerf but this might be too much.
Orc players I have talked to were concerned, too. They had OP racials and nerf was needed but bloodfury being around 4x less potent and hardiness becoming almost nothing (alongside the weapon skill nerfs) might be too much.
Tauren players just got kinda surprised, I guess. Is there any reason war stomp was nerfed? Was it a part of any disgusting rotation? Another thing here is that now we have an objectively better druid race. You could argue in the past that minor HP boost is better but minor dodge boost can help certain specs sometimes more. Now a 'correct' druid is a nelf druid.
Humans and helves seem to stand out a bit too much in the reformed racial-environment.
We'll see. All I'm saying is that it feels weird that horde racials were nerfed to the point where you can't really show a horde race anymore with good PVP racials while the other side had real reworks, including serious buffs.

With holy pala I'm conflicted. Loving the flavor of it and I hope it works out well. But as others have pointed out, many mobs have aoe silence, aoe magic damage etc making it hard for a healer to perform from that range. Will holy palas need to switch to old playstyle when aoe silencer mobs come and run in when it's safe or will they have a way to protect themselves from status effects which disallow their playstyle?

My biggest concern is priest though. I mean partially. I'm really curious about discipline to be honest, and while I find holy changes a bit boring, I think they are very intelligently and well done.
Shadow seems more problematic. Please elaborate on the 'they can't use shields but they can use holy nova thing'. They just start spamming a holy spell in shadowform? Do they need to talent holy nova for it? How does it happen to them?
But my biggest concern is regarding nelves and dwarves here. Nelves being able to use bow can be a nice selection lore-wise but breaks gameplay symmetry. There are 3 relic classes, 3 bow classes and 3 wand classes. Gameplay-wise this feels like a tank shaman saying fck it and getting a plate set or a rogue deciding that it's time to use a shield.
Specially if nelves can equip bows from instances or can buy bow bows. Imagine running dungeons or raids and losing the bow to a random nelf priest because he thinks that SRing Heartstriker is a unique idea.
But dwarves. I love dwarves but still. Avatar. Avatar will be the new spirit link. Spirit link was so broken that it now became an ultimate talent in a tree. Maybe was even nerfed a bit. And while many class racials were nerfed (no more wolf scaling at orcs, taurens have a weird totem tossing thing now), dwarves can increase your armor by 25% for 15 sec every minute plus giving you resistances for everything 150% better than priests, palas and shamans ever can. To put this in perspective. If avatar can be self-cast and it were put to the bottom of the enhancement tree and I'd only have 1 point left, I'd take it over bloodlust anyday for my tank shaman. A class racial over a capstone talent. It's my personal idea but I'd change the CD to 3 minutes, and the buff to 15% armor and 50% resistence of your level.

Don't get me wrong, I really like the changes (mostly). I just wanna point out what I feel unfair or weirdly balanced.

## Post 103647 by Steakhouse (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-18T14:18:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103647#p103647 | page 8 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Upon further thought, one of the bigger feather-ruffling changes I would revert is the removal of certain buttons and playstyles, so I think the devs should consider reverting:

 - Holy Shock being unable to deal damage - many people flock to the server because they want to try a Shockadin

 - Return Counterattack, a crucial Hunter PvP talent for all specs, to the early Survival tree - if the concern is that it will scale too well with the new melee talents, simply reduce its damage. Compounded with the Wing Clip cooldown, the lack of Counterattack greatly reduce Hunters' means of escaping, and I don't think the fact that a deep talent in each spec affects enemy movement (Intimidation, Scatter Shot, Combat Traps) makes up for it.

 - The new WF and Flametongue totems remove Totem Twisting from the game, a mechanic that is fun, engaging, and difficult to master: could the new "weapon" totems give a 10 second buff, like the olds ones did, rather than an aura on the totem ? This would remedy the disappearance of the mechanic

Lastly, a possible oversight : Priests' Wand Spec should instead be Ranged Weapon Spec, such that it also affects the Priestess of the Moon's Bow, otherwise the opportunity cost for using a bow will be too great. The lack of agility on priest gear also means the 25% damage bonus will be more than welcome, but the real kicker will be the mana return.

Iconic class designs and playstyles known from Vanilla WoW is becoming unrecognizable. This will alienate large parts of the playerbase that wanted a Vanilla-esque game with some additions, while still staying reasonably close to the original. With so many changes, it will become a balancing nightmare. It's not without reason that in software development you want to implement a few changes at a time, and check if they work and don't break anything, before moving on. The first round of class changes were much better in that regard.

And why didn't they involve the playerbase more? As of now it seems they've consulted with a few select people for every class, who probably want THEIR class buffed and classes/races they don't like nerfed. And when the devs listen to them, it results in a clusterfuck of changes. Even a voting system like OSRS has, for one feature at a time, would probably be better...Please do not go down the road of SoD.

As an example, you removed Rogue PvP talents in favor of new ones geared towards PvE, not good.

 **PART 2**

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/exteEP4.png)

 4. It's imperative that every change comes with detailed developer notes explaining the reasoning behind each alteration and its intended consequences, as of right now not all changes have them.

 **For instance, simply reducing Tauren stun duration without justification is not acceptable. Why was Heightened Senses (Rogue Talent) turned into baseline? Why is there no developer note? Are you aware of the PvP consequences of that change? Are you aware that's an indirect nerf to Feral Druids and Night Elfs racial? Are you aware the old Improved Kidneyshot Rogue Talent was used by PvPers and had huge synergy in team-based PvP like Battlegrounds and Arenas? Removing it replacing it with a PvE alternative, is not cool... Are you aware that with the new Talents, Rogues will be able to spam Interrupts with 36 yd range? I bet the answer is 'No' for all these questions, because no PvPer was included in your meetings.**
 5. Every change should have near-universal acceptance from the community. This isn't about creating a democratic process, but rather ensuring that each alteration benefits the game as a whole and is widely accepted by players, even those not directly impacted by the change.

 6. TurtleWoW must preserve its "Vanilla+" essence, rather than shifting towards a "Ascencion-like" approach. Instead of removing talents, we should focus on buffing them to create a more balanced experience. The Premeditation Rogue Talent, for example, was an component in niche PvP Rogue builds; it would have been wiser to buff it rather than eliminating it. We should build upon the existing framework and improve what we already have, staying true to Vanilla WoW's spirit (i thought that was TurtleWoW was all about?). ## Post 103673 by Ragetto (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-18T15:46:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103673#p103673 | page 9 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Akos1896 wrote: Fri Oct 18, 2024 3:33 pm**
> Yes, but out of curiosity, what are the limits of Vanilla for you? For example: melee hunter was a joke in Vanilla. Would it be okay to buff up the tree to become a solid DPS by only tweaking existing abilities? F.ex. pushing raptor strike so much that it does a carry. Same premise but now with added abilities to help the rotation. I'm just curious of your pov

The melee hunter was a joke and should remain one (literally), because hunters are a ranged class, not a melee class. However, we can still buff melee abilities, since most hunters wouldn’t pick them anyway. But changing the entire philosophy of the survival tree (which is based on utility/tools) isn’t about correcting something that wasn’t working; it introduces a host of new problems down the line (leading to the cooldown on Wing Clip, for example).

The limits of Vanilla aren’t clearly in the talents or gameplay but in the game modes: the PvP system (based on endless grinding) is a significant limitation. The absence of competitive PvP, which would allow some guilds to specialize in it rather than raids, is another. The need to raid to gear up and then do PvP, but without any motivating PvP goal to achieve, is a real limitation.

The talents in Vanilla are actually quite good, the gameplay is incredibly enjoyable, and all of this was designed and balanced by a much larger and more competent team than Twow devs.

## Post 103698 by Davios92 — 2024-10-18T17:56:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103698#p103698 | page 9 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I do appreciate the Turtle wow Devs taking the time to make this post and ALLLL the changes, as there is ALOOOTTT.

I read a fair amount of this forum thread comments and it seems that despite people like or dislike the changes the common theme was they're was too many changes, going to fast, etc.

Classic is beloved for it's simplicity, it's the reason the game is still popular 20 years later. The class design is an essential part of the game. It needs slight improvements not being nuked.

Less is more.

The minimalist approach is a core tenet of success in good game design, let's give a reasonable example.

Hamstring is an ability that does a small amount of dmg and reduces the target speed by 40% (that has no cd as it uses rage). It's balanced nicely with wing clip that costs a little mana and reduces by 50% (no cd too as it used mana), so eventually a ranged hunter can out run a juggernaut warrior! It's balanced. With a talent the warrior get 15% chance to imbolise the target for 5 seconds. That's a pretty strong talent in PvP, but it's deep in the talent trees and a good hunter can use a defensive cd like scatter shot or pet stun during this time.

But with Turtle wow changes,
If a warrior hamstrings the hunter and it dodges the warrior has been punished not by his player skill but in an unfair and unrewarding way and is let's be real toast... Likewise if a hunter has his wing clip parried by the warrior the hunter is toast.. it doesn't feel very rewarding and infact quite frustrating. It isn't powerful enough to require a cd hence why in all of classics iterations it NEVER had a cd.

The issue when you start to add so much, change so much, alter so much is it feels alienating. People play classic for it's simplicity.

Classic + is about the vanilla essence which is simplicity, but adding on and improving on it hence the +.

Outright changing and removing abilities, racials, etc isn't well.. classic +. It's turtle wow custom?

Hamstring and wing clip 'dont' need a cd, if it dodges or parries they are both kind of screwed. Warriors don't need to have a hunters counterattack. There is a reason why, the greats of original classic made the classes the way they did. And in tbc and wrath they just added to them, they didn't think they knew better. It's because players become accustomed to a certain play style and enjoyed it.

Removing holy shock for example, why? It's a whole play style that people have been enjoying and accustomed too for many years.. if it hits too hard, then just NERF the DMG.. don't remove it entirely?

You don't need to reinvent the wheel.
No offence, but the greats that made classic should have their work respected. SOD failed precisely because it wasn't, it went from the simplicity of classic which everyone loved to a convoluted mess like retail, where you are just spamming stuff constantly.. unrewarding, overturned, impossible to balance, etc.

Just do what is necessary, horde racials did need a nerf like they got in tbc, but alliance racials didn't need insane buffs.. Some people play alliance just for paladin blessings, for RP, or for playing a 'beautiful class', etc. they don't need racials that are op, it's the reason why you nerfed the horde ones? Buffing alliance racials to such a degree is fixing problems that didn't exist and making new problems. It's going beyond balancing? Which is what class patches are meant to used for?

Do what works, if it ain't broke don't fix it.

Finally, the new raids, dungeon content, quests, zones, pets, professions etc are all really good.

Removing gimmicky items like wolfshead helm, manual crowd pummelers etc, is also really good.

To conclude,

The additional content like raids, dungeons, etc and balancing items is great.

But nuking the classes, specs and racials all at once like this is not necessary... Just make the specs BALANCED in PvP and PvE that's enough. That's the whole point of class patches, to balance the classes and specs. It's a 20 year old classic game after all, it's retro gaming people play such classic games for well.. playing them as they are. We are asking for class, spec, racial balances.. NOT total reworks.

Less is more.

Hey. I am amazed by the effort and time that went into this.

Still, I want to give my honest opinion. Even though it probably won't change anything.

These changes are... too much. If they go through, the game will hardly resemble Vanilla anymore. In fact, it will resemble Vanilla not more than it will resemble TBC, or WotLK, or any other old version of the game - it will be just a remade variant of WoW, released 20 years after original game.

Honestly, I am afraid a game in such state won't be able to attract new players. People want to play vanilla. They are willing to accept cosmetic or QOL changes, but this just gives the impression of "for fun custom made" server, even if it's not. And such servers have bad reputation. I played on old Vanilla+ server, and it felt significantly different to Vanilla, even though their changes were still smaller than the ones described here.

Also, what you are doing here is what Blizzard already tried all those years ago, with TBC forward. Rebalancing classes like this will fix many of the old problems, sure, but it is guaranteed to also cause new ones. It is unavoidable. It will create a spiral of constant buffs and nerfs, ultimately fixing nothing and only creating chaos. We already had a taste of that with how paladin was handled since the server release.

Has the devs really considered the impact these changes will have on PvP? Twow isn’t just a PvE server. Vanilla offers a good foundation that balanced both PvE and PvP—please don’t ruin that.
