## Post 103778 by Atreidon (Grandmaster of Forum PvP) — 2024-10-19T06:16:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103778#p103778 | page 10 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

There are some changes i genuinel believe are nice within these patchnotes and undoubtably countless hours of effort have been pouring into these class changes, but i do not know why so many things that werent broken were touched and some spells completely remove the nuance they had.

Firemage ignite juggling is one of the few DPS rotations you actually had to learn and adapt to the current ignite situation the game had. Its main problem was always that you absolutely had to be firemage and there was no opt out option.
Now there is arcane & frostmage if you so choose.
Making ignite share threat makes this spec just another flavor of "throw 3 seconds cast flavored in your element of choice at mob and occasionally press the "more boom" button.

Similarly with moonkin, a "rotation" has been hamfisted in. Ignoring that in classic wrath & starfire had different uses. Starfire was your mana efficient spell, and wrath was your burnspell. But it was held back by lack of nature damage support and druids general lack of mana.
Furthermore wrath had a nice as the spellpushback protected spell for fights with heavy AOE. Instead of leveraging these differences in the spells and allowing for moonkin to choose what to click by giving these spells more unique appeals besides onebeing just better than the other 99% of the time, you now made him install powerauras and let the game decide for them...

Ret paladin a class lammented for their burst potential on twow just got a 115% weapon damage instant hit. Instead of just the holy strike doubledip bug being fixed. Repentence based on the tooltip deals a cool ~9000 dmg when cast on a raidboss...

Flametongue totem now is just macroed to WF and you can forget abouts its entire existence because while before there was a choice, now they might as well be the same spell.

I wont even start on commenting on the priest changes...

To echo what i say on leaving the class balance council a while back. The people who made those changes had their powerfantasies fulfilled instead of respecting what was already there. The game may be perfectly enjoyable, but calling it classic is intellectually dishonest. The classes are further removed from classic than they ever were in tbc.

Also there are some fantastic changes i now have to deal with as a raidleader. First i have to tell basically every dps in the raid that debuff slots are still a prized comodity and they should please keep their dots in the spellbook. Since the debufflimit remains as it was in the last change, and its enough to comfortably play with the current set of debuffs, but you have majorly increased the debuffs players want to apply...

And that on top of making every healer wanna reroll to dps since the dps got all the new shinies

Those changes could be a lot of fun, but having to pay with the server i love is a very steep price to pay

## Post 103874 by Fugus (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-19T18:00:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103874#p103874 | page 11 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

And while I don't play Balance spec on druid often, before WotLK, Wrath and Starfire both had their uses back then which your changes destroy.

Originally you were basically keep Moonfire and Insect Swarm rolling at all times unless the fights were trash that died quick.

Starfire was the bread and butter spell that is mana efficient and you spammed when you are a normal fight. It was good DPS and wasn't SUPPOSED to oom you most times if they hadn't given Moonkin such mana issues.

Wrath was the quick and inefficient spell you spammed when you didn't have much time to attack due to movement or you were in a burn phase at which point you did more damage but you would run yourself out of mana quickly if you tried to use it for long.

Your changes here break that mechanic which was supposed to exist in Vanilla and TBC and replace it with an equivalent of that crap they did in WotLK which sucked to many users, myself included when I was bothering to use it.

As an aside for gaming design philosophy, many users don't want our DPS rotation to be a game of spinning plates to keep up stuff. Just like many tanks hated it where the games changed to where your majority of time and focus was spent keeping up your mitigation rather than watching your surroundings. Blizzard might have enjoyed that because it gave them a reason to dumb down stuff since the users weren't able to focus on mechanics as much.

Many of us don't mind a simple mechanic where each ability actually has a use. It's a mechanic that they seem to be messing up on on the CoA server. I would rather have instances and mechanics in fights that require my situational awareness to be engaged to make the fight fun and challenging. Not trying to turn things into a 5+ button rotation to keep things going while proc watching and counting buffs and debuffs constantly.

Those simpler rotations is part of what classic WoW so fun and allowed game mechanics to actually get more entertaining. Don't need a 1 button rotation, but don't need to go full "John F-ing Madden" meme level either.

## Post 103877 by Griefmaker — 2024-10-19T18:12:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103877#p103877 | page 11 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

As one who played OG WoW back in 2004-2008, then WoW Classic in 2019-2022, then TWoW since 2022...

I am excited and cannot wait for this patch to drop.

I do personally believe some changes should be reverted or modified, but that can be done after deployment.  Not a surprise when so much was done, which is flat out impressive and I appreciated that the developer rationale was given for the change, even if some of them I did not agree with.

Vanilla was half-baked on arrival.  Fun as hell as can be seen by how long I have played it, but it had many issues beyond the good parts.  Many of the problems were inherent though and could not be fixed by minor tweaks.  The good parts could be tweaked slightly to polish them up.  The big issues (such as useless specs) cannot simply be tweaked to work.  If you polish a turd, you still have a turd.

TWoW's attempts at making more unique specs and giving each more of an identity is in my opinion cool and I laud them for that.

Dropping it all at once is smart too.  It gives them a chance to see the big picture in action and make changes/tweaks when all information is available.  That is what you should do in any sort of development when you make even a minor overhaul.

And yes, this is not a "patch", which is usually just a set of small tweaks, bug fixes, and polishing.  This is an overhaul.

It makes for a lot of chaos to begin with, that is the nature of the beast, but then all variables can be seen and assessed instead of making sweeping changes piecemeal, then having to go through all of this every single time.

Some personal comments about 1.17.2:

- I am excited for more Melee hunter support.  The last iteration was definitely lacking.  This is something I have always wanted, especially after learning that OG BM hunter pre-alpha was in fact meant for melee, but Blizz dropped it right before alpha due to balancing issues and not enough time to try and make it work.

- Melee holy paladin healer is interesting.  This change reminds me of Warhammer Age of Reckoning War Priest.  I am curious to see how this works out.

- Discipline priest I am not too jazzed about.  This is one thing I think WotLK did well, where they made discipline into a preemptive shield healer and having holy as a reactive healer.

- The racial changes...lowering the weapon skills was good.  Others, not so certain about.  Warstomp and shadowmeld I definitely hope are reverted and I have not played a NE or Tauren in years.

- Holy Nova for shadow priests makes me sad.

- I am in the boat of wing clip and hamstring CDs being 6 seconds as being way too long.  I could be on board for a 3 second CD though and see how that works out.

- I am excited for the affliction warlock tweaks.  That is still my favorite warlock spec (love the DoTs and watching everything about me rot!)

- Fear ward as a baseline priest spell is good.  Avatar (despite being a dwarf fan) is a bit too much.  Drop it to 15% and I think it would be more balanced and still have a distinct use

- Frost mage:  Icicles.  I am curious to see how that plays out!
One other thought.  A fact of life is that we must all "evolve and adapt...or die."  This goes with TWoW which is Vanilla+.  The definition of "Vanilla+" can be argued forever, but TWoW's current and future popularity is not because it is vanilla, but because it built upon vanilla into something similar and making it more interesting and exciting.  Of course, the trick will be what is the critical mass when the changes become too great, but that is a different topic.

It can be argued that this overhaul is too drastic.  But there is also a fact that if TWoW remains static, it will slowly die.  Purists are one aspect of a fan base.  But catering only to purists is an inevitable death.  Even I stopped playing 6 months ago after all of these years because things were feeling stale.

What I have loved about TWoW is that they take the familiar and do something more with it to spice it up.  That is what keeps me coming back and that is also what keeps a larger playerbase coming back or new players joining as well.

>

I liked the game when my rotation was keeping the mangle debuff up and shred to 5 and rip while weaving in bites when I could and knowing when it was better to pool my resources and wait for the stuff to roll off and refresh as a feral. As a balance I liked the TBC setup. I liked my focus being on what was going on around me.

And in WotLK, I was one of the top druids on my server and even made it onto the top 100 charts for my class for while before I quit.

My rotation was Mangle>Savage Roar>Rake. Then a priority list of
 1) If your Savage Roar drops refresh it with as many combo points as you can.
 2) If your mangle debuff drops, refresh it (This was before it was increased to a 1 minute debuff)
 3) If your Rake falls off, refresh it.
 4) Never refresh your Rip with less than 5 combo points.
 5) Never shred unless Rake, Rip, Mangle and Savage Roar are already applied.
 6) Only use Ferocious Bite if you can do so without risking any of the previous things falling off.

All while making sure you were behind them because the second you weren't shred stopped working. Even killing it on the DPS charts on a raiding guild, it just wasn't half the fun of the old TBC days where the fun part was actually playing the raid, not playing Dance Dance Revolution on my frigging keyboard watching timers and counters more than the target.

Edit: I also enjoyed the fact that I could drop out of form and do a quick self heal or heal another for a bit without having to spend the next 45 seconds just resetting my rotation. I enjoyed actually being a hybrid which is what I LOVED about TBC and (Hopefully) Classic.

Full disclosure, I never played OG Vanilla except when Blizzard rereleased them but refused to stay when I realized that blizzard wasn't going to fix stuff they left broke the first time around and all the metas were set in stone. I started in TBC and LOVED that vision of what a druid was. And actually hate what they did with Tiger's Fury here given what they could have done with it.

Even liked the Resto spec more in TBC than WotLK or what I have seen so far in Classic. I actually liked Lifebloom as a spell and it being an almost fully HoT Based healer. Hated the Nurish change which then just turned them into something that felt like a standard healer with a lot bigger build up before it can actually do the real healing.

## Post 103884 by Fugus (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-19T18:46:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103884#p103884 | page 11 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

My preferred setup as a feral druid in this so far.
 1) Completely redesign Tiger's Fury into a cool down that works for both Cat and Bear form as a form of Sweeping Strikes/Blade Flurry. It doesn't make it part of the normal DPS rotation and instead gives them a limited AoE they lack. I never wanted Kitty Slice and Dice and hated Savage Roar for the same reason.

 2) Actually support having bleeds buff claw. Make it where if they have a full Rake and Rip up, Claw matches Shred for its damage so you can attack them from the front without a DPS loss so long as you keep up your bleeds, you are literally changing one mechanic (Staying behind them) for another (Maintaining bleeds) while doing equal damage so no more major losses when you can't stay behind them.

 3) Actually allow Rake and Rip to scale which they are also doing here.

 4) Ferocious Bite, get rid of the extra energy to damage conversion. It generally is more of a hindrance than a help.

 5) Feral Charge: Give something DEEP in the feral tree that removes its dead zone, makes it usable in both forms with no resource cost so that it can be used as a spell interrupt as neither cat or bear has a viable one which it needs. In TBC I hated the times when I needed to bring my PvP gloves into instances just to spend combo points to interrupt when the PuG lacked a dedicated interrupt or actually having to prepare for a mechanic but running out and going bear form just to interrupt when I know it was coming. Just let us spend the CD interrupting stuff. We have the skill, let us use it.

Main change for Bear form: Extend swipe from 3 targets to at least 5.

Main changes for Moonkin:
 1) Fix the mana issues.
 2) Hurricane: When cast while in Moonkin form, its debuff and cool down are removed. This actually gives Moonkin a spammable AoE and no other spec.

And for the love of frigging god, a normal resurrection spell. I mean First Aid has it already according to AtllasLoot but a healing class still doesnt.

And let my Cats Speed, my PvP Set bonus, and my entangling roots work indoors. And let me open chests, use potions, and quest items without breaking form.

Classic was SO close to getting this down and just barely missed the mark.

## Post 103934 by playerxAyc0d — 2024-10-20T02:31:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103934#p103934 | page 11 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

This isn’t the Vanilla+ we were promised anymore. Yes, the new content you’ve created has attracted a lot of players, but fundamentally, it’s because the foundation is Vanilla. If people just wanted new content, why wouldn’t they go play Blizzard’s version? They’ve already got plenty of new content, but that’s not what Vanilla is about. When a server that claims to be Vanilla+ starts rolling out big changes like Blizzard, trying to turn it into a new game, it becomes a trust issue. For players who’ve sunk hours into this, donated, recommended it to friends, and planned to stay here for the Vanilla+ experience, this feels like a betrayal. Adding new content is a good move, but why change the parts that players have grown accustomed to and love, instead of building on that foundation and giving them more choices? That way both those who love Vanilla and those looking for changes can enjoy the game.

## Post 103936 by Turbosaxophonic (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-20T02:38:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103936#p103936 | page 11 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

The more I think about the warrior changes the more I dislike them, and that goes beyond nerfs.

Hamstring got put on a cooldown because players were spamming it to fish for Overpower procs and because it’s their tool for staying in range in PvP. What’s the problem with that? Warriors are already one of the most kitable classes next to paladins, what players were actually having problems with warriors staying on them? Why is using hamstring for overpower procs something to be “fixed”, especially when the rage cost of Sunder Armor has been reduced so it can serve the same purpose?

All it does is disrupt/kill hamstring kiting for leveling.  Every time a hamstring is missed, blocked, parried and even dodged I can’t help but think of how much damage I’d be unnecessarily taking with that 6 second cooldown unless I spend the extra rage and talent point for Piercing Howl. This change seems like it would slow down warrior leveling than speed it up, regardless of the extra abilities being learned early.

Speaking of the earlier spells, I feel like dual wielding at level 10 and Slam at 14 completely throws off the sense of progression for power fantasy. Level 10 is supposed to be the mark of your first big step in the world, where you unlock your first major class feature and fundamental spell. In the case of warriors that’s defensive stance with taunt, since one of their core functions as a class is tanking; that’s what sets them apart from the hunters and rogues. Dual wielding isn’t unique to one class but it falls more in Rogue’s identity, that’s why they get it at level 10 and not Warriors. Level 20 still feels like the appropriate level for dual wielding warriors, by 20 you’ve likely cleared your first dungeon and have enough accomplishments under your belt to have earned that feeling of being a badass berserker who swings an axe in each hand. Warriors dual wielding at 10 just feels like the same kind of instant-gratification philosophy that Cata had (which it was, Cata was the expac which introduced that change). Why not just buff early dual wielding so it’s actually worth using at 20?

The treatment of Slam also feels weird. It’s a Fury ability, why is its talent in Arms now? Is it going to be moved to the Arms page of the spellbook? The respective flavors of Arms and Fury is a battle tactician/weapon master and a berserker/barbarian, not two-hand user and dual wielder. Slam might synergize with two-handed weapons more but that’s not exclusive to Arms, it’s flavored as a Fury ability because it’s not some precise weapon technique, it’s just taking a big swing at your opponent. As it stands it feels like a nerf to 2h fury which is already an off-meta build.

Also, why is Pummel so pushed? Being usable so early and in battle stance seems like it would leave Shield Bash as completely redundant/only for people who are actively tanking. The daze effect looks like nice icing on the cake at first, but needing a coin flip to work means it can’t even be used reliably in Hamstring’s absence.

All in all, there’s a lot of changes I do like and the devs deserve recognition for such a big undertaking, it’s not like this whole patch is something that needs to be scrapped or reverted like some people are saying. Vanilla+ does mean changes and rebalancing, but not at the cost of simplicity/elegance in design, and especially not spec flavor and identity. I thought I read that the Turtle Devs wanted to preserve original intent with the classes and to avoid total overhauls and reworks, I don’t know what happened to that but these changes fly in the face of that idea. This patch deserves a second pass from devs, and public testing in a PTR before it actually goes live.

@Xudo

Won't quote to keep it more readable. I am still leveling here, I thought they increased the debuff limit. If they haven't done that, then that is a more important change than everything they just included in this list.

And needlessly increasing the DPS complexity also needlessly changes the feeling and play style of the class. If I choose a mage, I wanted to play at least close to what the mage was, same with my druid. Fixing issues doesn't require you to needlessly bloat the rotation to make it fun. Even in WotLK while doing that crap, it was way less fun than actually playing the raid for the mechanics and the ability to monitor others in the raid and occasionally drop out to heal for a second without needing 30 seconds JUST to get my rotation back going.

If I wanted to play a rogue, I would have rolled one. If someone rolled a rogue to play one, they don't want it's style changed into something else either.

My choice on a rotation for feral is simple:
 *) Allow Rake and Rip to buff Claw to match Shred damage per energy spent
 1) Apply Fairie Fire
 2) Apply Rake
 3) Shred/Claw to 5 combo points
 4) Rip at 5 combo points.
 5) Refresh Rake and Rip as needed
 6) Claw/Shred for combo point generation
 7) Ferocious Bite when you can without letting them fall off.

 8) Tiger's Fury was never used in Classic or TBC so instead of forcing it into the rotation, change it into Feral "Blade Flurry
"/"Sweeping Strikes" to give them a small AoE that doesn't impact their overall rotation, their ramp up, or greatly impact most PvP.

 9) Give a deep talent in feral that makes Feral Charge usable in both forms without a dead zone, to give both cat and bear an interrupt but would also put their ability to gap close on cool down as well. Fixes a major issue that plagued them without greatly changing their playstyle or bloating them with no abilities like blizzard did with Skull Bash.

 10) Honestly hated Berserk in WotLK with how it was implemented but I doubt its going anywhere here. Originally it made you immune to all CC like Blade storm, Killing Spree, or Beast Within. But was gutted into turning into a giant red "CC Me NOW" sign with a longer cool down than any CC you would bother using which meant it typically only had use when 1v1 and you already had them stunned so they couldn't stun you. And haven't tested it yet but I am betting it probably fades when you drop form as well which (If true) means they could just snare you and walk away from your 6 minute CD. So I would say either lower the cool down or give it it's original immunity blizzard gave it before it went live.

 11) I haven't bothered to powershift here as I am still leveling, but I remember even on retail powershifting macros would bug and I end up left in caster form way too often. So, just give us an actual command for powershifting instead of relying on macros. At least that way I know it would be reliable.

 12) And for the love of frigging god, allow Cat's Speed, our PvP set bonus, and our Entangling Roots be usable indoors.

Not whining or anything because I’m not sure what to make of it, but take it or ignore… This is my experience so far as a new player.

 - This is the third time I play on a private server, never got to 60 before… Here, I started playing something like 3 weeks ago, with a bit more than 6 days of /played (I’m almost level 50). I chose this server after the 2.0 update hype because it seemed “cool” and it could be nice to have a HL character when/if the whole new chapter starts. Also, let’s face it, this is the only real vanilla option atm…
I was a bit reluctant to start here at first because of the current progression and was wondering if I should wait for a new fresh (and also hyped) competitor server that could launch soon…

 - I chose Horde (orc) because I like the leveling areas and I wanted to play shaman. This is the only class I ever played, but I’m completely noob… Tho, after playing a bit I was wondering (and still am) if I should reroll Ally (I want to play Hunter there) because Horde side is very, very under-populated… It’s almost impossible to pvp queue (I do care a bit, even if I mainly want to pve anyway), and I basically quest alone since the start… What confirmed my plan to play Horde was a bit fueled because of those cool racials…

 - The only shaman spec I want to play is melee (enh). I don’t like waiting for mana… I really don’t… And WF seemed (and really is) a lot of fun… Yeah, it’s a bit memed, but I don’t care, I’m just here for the fun anyway (This is also why Hunter’s huge crits are very compelling to me). Plus, totems are fun, I like totems, they like totems (what if they don’t as much anymore?).

I just arrived here and the 17.2 update was hyped from the start. Now, imagine how confused I am.

 - If Horde loses even more of its appeal, what do I do?
 - I was Orc AND Enh shaman, both got nerfed (“nerf” is perhaps a bit strong, I don’t really know, I’m so noob anyway), but the fact is that my play style I was in for in the first place is completely transformed.

All that to say that, as of now (so only for the past 2 days), I stopped leveling and only farmed gold because of all my uncertainty… Perhaps new players like myself should be more vocal about their confusion… I’m sure the new flow of players is what makes this server sustainable in the long run.

## Post 104059 by Davios92 — 2024-10-21T08:03:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104059#p104059 | page 12 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

After reading many pages of these forums, the counter argument I see thrown up alot 'most people I've spoken to don't mind, are excited about, etc'
This is true, but just because your excited bout it that's the same as SOD in P1 sure it was interesting to find the runes in P1 but I quit after that as I knew what it would metabolize into.. and my hunch was right...

When you implement so many changes, so many custom aspects into the game, you can't see their overall impact without a certain period of time and by then it would already be too late.

That's why In OSRS they have a polling system, 'the customer is always right' as they say. The players are the customers, instead of saying well.. 60% of people don't care, or whatever. That's still 40% of the customer base that will be disatisfied and could quit.

Instead, on taking the middle way they could try and satisfy 90% of the customer base..
Some small balances and minor changes to satisfy those that need to see things improved while also not too much that those that like things as they are, to feel to alien.

It doesn't need to be one or the other, a happy medium could be found.

Will this be beneficial for the overall future prospects of the server only time will tell, but personally I feel it won't be. The number 1 selling point is this is a classic + server regardless of what the turtle wow Devs have said, it's how the customers or community or wider wow audience see it as, so that image might be damaged significantly based upon these massive alterations to core gameplay mechanics of the game.

Or I could be talking bolomi and it turns out to be refreshing to have nerfed horde racials, buffed alliance racials, altered weapon skills, removed gameplay styles like shockadin, new abilities, custom talent trees, etc.

As they didn't make a PTR or ask the customer base we can only now.. wait and see.. but if it's really bad, they have really shot themselves in the foot. As the only bandaid would be to remove them entirely and could then upset the people that preferred the new custom changes... So in my view, it's a catch 22 situation and could further erode trust in the turtle wow server.

Conclusion

Well, in my view these changes are not intended to address balances but to redesign the core aspects of the game and will as a result, will be unsuccessful in the long run. Let's 'wait and see though ' as we haven't tested them on a PTR as it wasn't made available and they didn't ask the customer for their feedback before implementing them which to me seems like a bad approach in a form of polling.. and on them being generally over time disliked removing them entirely again will further upset people and erode trust they know what they are doing..

>

Polling is still an extremely valuable tool, and it should be used as a tool instead of simply forcing through changes which 20-40 % of the community hates. The latter is rather self-centered. Also, what if the devs have biases large parts of the community disagrees with? As far as I know, the devs here don't have degrees in game design.

You're right that polling has problems of its own, which you point out well. But it can be used to try and gauge how much of the community dislikes a certain feature. If 30 % dislikes a new feature, then maybe it shouldn't be implemented. The devs don't have to strictly follow the polls, but it can be taken into account when considering changing or implementing new features. Like this for example; " While we understand that the 'shockadin' specialization is beloved by many, it does not fit our vision for the class", is rather inconsiderate (?) given that style was iconic in Vanilla WoW, loved by many, and that even Arthas could "Holy Shock" his enemies in the RTS-game (which Turtle claims it draws inspiration from).

I also kinda disagree about your point about new players. The problem with trying to appeal to people that already isn't playing the game, is that you quickly will alienate your current playerbase which have been fans for years already. This is exactly what happened in Retail WoW. The game gradually injected changes that many of the 2004-2008 playerbase didn't like, but it brought in new players that love modern WoW. Then Blizzard tried to cater to 'everyone', by appealing to the lowest common denominator, which basically dumbed and watered down the game into something a lot of us strongly dislike, and why servers such as Nostalrius popped up in the first place. So far it has generally been Vanilla-lovers that wants something extra that seeks out Turtle. I'd strongly dislike if the devs suddenly pivots to a more Cataclysm-style game.

## Post 104130 by Yresim — 2024-10-21T15:16:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104130#p104130 | page 13 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I rarely comment on forums but this time I can't hold myself from expressing how much I love the upcoming changes!
Classic WoW released 20 years ago. In 2004 everything was so fresh and so brand new, there were so many things to test and experiment with. In 2024, we all know that druids are healers ONLY in end game environments. Prot paladins are not tanks. Survival was only an option before deleting your hunter or taking a break from the game.
I will not even get into the blizzard classic relaunch and what became of it.

And here comes Turtle WoW. A very big, as of now, team, with a dream to make classic what it never had the chance to become. A "custom private" server with zero pay-to-win elements, without GMs moving around resurrecting people's characters and killing bosses and mobs to help players, making a healthy community as it concerns chat and griefing behavior.
After 6 years of minimal class changes, and after 20 years of classic, I was hungry for a fundamental change and the next step in wow classic. The countless other servers failed to deliver anything new, while retaining the original warcraft lore and the classic experience.
Blizzard has let us down so many times that I stopped caring long ago about anything they announce.
I've never felt more secure and sure to trust someone to take wow to the next step. The Turtle team is that dim hope that came into realization.
They are taking steps towards making every spec playable, or close to playable and surely not obsolete like most in the current state and I just fully support that!

As for the people's reactions, I believe there will always be this small number of individuals, who no matter the change, are waiting for the right opportunity to fill the comments section with bile and tears, without even reading the changes. They just want to externalize their negativity, and what's a better place than an online forum, on an online game that they find fun.

TL;DR: Big hopes on the Turtle team to move forward with all the changes and adjust the power curves accordingly. Can't wait for the patch to come live!

## Post 104156 by Whalemilk (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-21T18:06:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104156#p104156 | page 13 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Uploaded changes into chatGPT and asked it what the most likely issue would come from the changes.

The number 1 class ability change in Turtle WoW Patch 1.17.2 that may cause a class to become overpowered is the Ferocious Bite rework for Feral Druids.

The change allows Ferocious Bite to scale with the Druid’s Attack Power and converts each extra point of energy into additional damage. Additionally, the change where combo points no longer vanish upon switching targets could make this finishing move excessively strong in both PvP and PvE.

This new scaling and retention of combo points can lead to Druids dealing excessive burst damage, especially when they maintain combo points across multiple targets. In PvP, this could allow Feral Druids to put constant pressure on their opponents by delivering high-damage finishing moves without losing resources. In PvE, it may enable Druids to maintain sustained high damage output, particularly in fights with multiple targets.

This rework can cause Feral Druids to be overpowered, especially in content where quick target switching and burst damage are key, making it difficult for other classes to keep pace with their output.

## Post 104207 by Jamey (Turtle WoW Team) [STAFF] — 2024-10-21T23:22:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104207#p104207 | page 13 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

**UPDATES | Dated: October 21 2024**

 **RACIAL CHANGES**

 *Developer Comment: Racials in Vanilla have always been a tricky topic. On one hand, they encourage diversity and avoid homogenization by having races excel in niches through unique traits, this fits Vanilla flavor perfectly. On the other hand however it is common knowledge that the Horde has always had the upper hand when it comes to combat racials, especially in PvP. Our changes to these Racials sought to remedy this issue by keeping Racials unique and flavorful to their race while evening out the power of the outliers. That being said, after extensive discussions and player feedback we realize that some Racials were hit too hard while others got a little less love than they deserve.*
---
 **Will of the Forsaken**: Duration reduced from 4 to 3 seconds. Cooldown increased from 2 minutes to 2.5 minutes. Can now be used while under crowd control to break out as before.
---
 **Vengeance**: Now only affects non-player Humanoids.
---
 **Blood Fury**: Attack Power bonus increased from 100% of your level to 200% of your level, no longer part of the global cooldown.
---
 **Shadowmeld**: Cooldown reduced from 3 minutes to 1 minute.
---
 **War Stomp**: Duration increased from 1.5 to 2 seconds, cooldown increased from 2 minutes to 2.5 minutes.
---
 **Exit Strategy**: No longer slows the user after sprinting.

 **DRUID**

 **Insect Swarm**: Applications of the same rank now stack when cast by two or more druids. This does not apply to the reduced chance to hit component of this spell.
---
 **Mighty Rage Potion** can now be used by Druids.

 **HUNTER**

 **Wing Clip**: Cooldown reduced from 6 seconds to 3 seconds.
---
 **Improved Wing Clip**: Proc chance increased from 7/14/20% to 14/28/40%.
---
 **Piercing Shots**: No longer generate threat to avoid breaking Feign Death with uncontrolled application.
---

 **PALADIN**

 **Shield of the Righteous**: Cooldown increased from 3 minutes to 5 minutes, damage reduction reduced from 40% to 30%.
---
 **Sacred Duty**: Removed.

 **PRIEST**

 **Power Word: Shield** can be cast in Shadowform.

 *Developer Comment: This was already the case but the talent builder did not reflect this. This clears that up for good.*
---
 **Enlighten**: Can now trigger off of healing spells.
---
 **Proclaim Champion**: Now also restores a small portion of damage taken by your Champion as Mana.
---
 **Champion's Resolve**: Removed.
---
 **Revive Champion**: Cooldown increased from 300 seconds to 45 minutes. Cast time reduced from 10.8 seconds to 5 seconds. Mana cost increased. Can now be used in combat.
---
 **Searing Shot**: Mana cost increased from 5% to 10% of base mana, this is equal to 137 mana at max level.
---
 **Avatar**: Cooldown increased from 1 minute to 5 minutes.

 **ROGUE**

 **Improved Backstab**: Now also gives your Backstab a 15/30/45% chance to award an addtional combo point.
---
 **Close Quarters Combat**: Now requires 2 points instead of 5 points, increasing your chance to get a critical strike with Daggers, Fist Weapons and Maces by 2/5%.
---
 **Hack and Slash**: Now requires 2 points instead of 5 points, giving you a 2/5% chance to get an extra attack on the same target after dealing damage with your Sword or Axe.

 **SHAMAN**

 **Lightning Shield**: Now guaranteed to land, this also affects the empowered version triggered by Lightning Strike.

 **WARLOCK**

 **Conjured Stones**: No longer share 30 minute cooldown, they are instead unusable in while in combat.
---
 **Fel Domination**: Changed cooldown to 5 minutes and no longer lock your demon from summoning.
---
Added new effects to **Master Summoner**: In addition, lowers the cooldown of your Inferno spell by 2.5/5 minutes and the cooldown of your Demon Gate spell by 7.5/15 minutes.

 **WARRIOR**

 **Improved Shield Slam**: Effect duration and cooldown reduced from 5 seconds to 4.5 seconds and the cooldown reduction on Shield Slam increased from 0.5/1 seconds to 0.75/1.5 seconds.

Thanks for the update, Jamey ! I think these changes address a lot of the concern from players. Great work to the whole dev team too, it must've been a hell of an undertaking. I'm still a bit iffy about a few things but I'm more than willing to say "let's play it and find out" for just about everything remaining.

> **Jamey wrote: Mon Oct 21, 2024 11:22 pm**
> **Avatar**: Cooldown increased from 1 minute to 5 minutes.

I'd like to comment on this ; correct me if I'm wrong but making Fear Ward baseline was to reduce the demand for Dwarf priests such that players of the class wouldn't feel shoehorned into that race, right ? I think Avatar is a great replacement, but I fear that, even with a 5 minute cooldown, Dwarves will remain the best raid priest available: stacking Dwarf priests means you can always have your tank(s) under the effect of Avatar every time a boss deals high damage. It's a shame, because Avatar is such a flavorful addition.

I think this entire issue can be remedied if the target of Avatar suffers a "cannot be targeted by Avatar" debuff, similarly to Weakned Soul (triggered by Power Word Shield), and Sated (triggered by Bloodlust and Heroism in WoW BC and further): Dwarves get to keep the new, exciting, and lore-rich ability, without being too good.

As a counterpart, Avatar could be even stronger ! In Warcraft 3, Avatar gave armor, health, attack damage, and spell immunity. The armor and spell immunity are already reflected by the current effect, and, to complete it, a % bonus to health, and a flat bonus to strength or attack power, could effectively port a beloved spell from Warcraft 3 to WoW !

## Post 104247 by Fugus (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-22T02:32:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104247#p104247 | page 14 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Another part of the math that came into it when choosing a Tauren Vs Night Elf for my druid.

As a Night Elf, I had to deal with the Orc racial in PvP.
As a Tauren, I had to deal with Perception and Stoneform.

I could juke the perception as its a cool down and most players weren't that great at using it back in the day. And Stoneform doesn't impact feral as much here since it isn't as bleed based. There is no juking a flat 15% resist chance every time that stacked with other talents.

Now, Orc racial is reduced to a non-issue, Perception is an even bigger threat. And Stoneform is just as annoying as before.

So, being a Night Elf with the overall changes is a superior option for PvP and PvE with the changes while also will have the weaker opponents to fight against by comparison.

And before you think that a clutch Regrowth every 2.5 minutes is better, you are comparing it against the ability to out run other druids and even shamans in ghost wolf. The ability to run away from the people chasing you or catch the people running from you is actually a good deal. Especially in exchange for a regrowth every 2.5 minutes that you have to have perfect timing it actually not risk pushback or interruption.

## Post 104270 by Atreidon (Grandmaster of Forum PvP) — 2024-10-22T06:21:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104270#p104270 | page 14 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Super happy the dev team is willing to listen to player feedback about the changes.

But i think a few of the questionable decisions still remain in the game:

 **Perception (Human Racial)**
The ability is really good when fighting stealthed oponents. But otherwide it was useless. With the new change, you will just macro it in with your combat ability and forget it even exists. Pressing a button for 2% crit chance temporarily just doesnt feel engaging.
I'd personally just abandon the buff on perception, but if we have to have it in the game, can it be a 1% crit chance increase while the spell is unused & off cooldown instead?
That way, it is providing its minor bonus but still remains ready for when you might need to use it for its original intended purpose.

 **Savage Bite**
Having mcp removed is a powernerf to druid, but a necessary one. However slapping a 350% threatmodifier on one ability and calling it a day is a bit problematic.
For one, it repeats the main problem that made deep prot so bad. If your one big threat spike gets dodged or parried its a huge deal for the dps. And save to say, a 4-5k threatspike on crit is very noticeable.
Mcp is do good for bear not only because of the extra damage, but more importanty it drastically increases the amounts of maul being casted. How about a ability/talent from bear that increases attackspeed instead? Something like seal or the crusader that increases attackspeed but lowers damage per swing would really help bears use all their rage in raid encounters. (Just spitballing ideas, to smooth out threatspikes a little bit. You could also slap some extra threat on faerie fire or swipe instead. Savage bite is already a very good spell)

 **Crusader Strike**
People have complained about the old holy strike burst. Against anyone with less than ~50% dmg mitigation from armor, the new crusader strike variant bursts harder.
Old holy strike + soc Was 170% weapondamage +130 or so holy damage.
The new combo with autoattack + soc + crusader strike is 215% physical + 70% holy damage at once.
As a pally myself, i am stoked about interesting hs&cs implementations, but thats just plain unfair. Even with the adjustments to reign in holy paladin. Which leads me to

 **Holy Shock**
Holy shock is an extremely cool and flexible ability. Turtle wow even buffed its damage scaling & cooldown quite substantially when soc was made no longer accessable to shockoboys.
The new talent blessed Strikes and the innate chance to reset its cd however necessetate, it cant be used offensively or shock paladins offensive momentum would eclipse many pure dps classes.

But clearly melee healer paladin is not fleshed out. While shockadin is a beloved playstile. If you wanna nerf the dmg scaling back to what it was, i can understand that, but destroying the only fun thing in all of holy tree for some new playstile is flawed. Blessed strikes could simply work for flash or holy light instead. And the small random chance to reset the cd is unreliable and therefore pointless on a healer anyway.

Please consider taking out the changes to holy shock and make blessed steikes interact with the other healspells or give melee healer in general more time in the oven

*Last edited by Atreidon on Tue Oct 22, 2024 6:51 am, edited 1 time in total.*

## Post 104279 by Wolfheart1990 — 2024-10-22T07:35:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104279#p104279 | page 14 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

The amended changes were a step in the right direction, thanks for remaining open to feedback team /bow

I see that the mana cost of Searing Shots for Night Elf priests has been increased, I can only assume that this is the result of it being tested and found strong in practice. Could you please elaborate on whether this use of bows will be subject to the new Wand Specialization talent (improved hit chance, chance to restore mana on successful hit?) otherwise, it will face the following problems:

 1) Not enough damage compared to wands without Searing Shots: Wands naturally have higher dps to compensate for lack of gear scaling. For instance, take a wand and a bow that both drop from same tier MC bosses:

Crimson Shocker:  102 - 191 Fire Damage (73.3 damage per second)
vs
Striker's Mark:       69 - 129 Damage (39.6 damage per second)

Even if we add 17.5 dps from the use of Thorium Arrows to the bow damage, there would still be a 16 dps difference in the wand's favor, before we even factor the added hit chance from the new Wand Specialization talent.

 2) Mana inefficiency compared to wands: priests typically use ranged weapons when trying to recuperate mana between casting intervals (whether they're heals or damage spells). Using Searing Shots will interrupt the 5 second rule, setting mana regen back, as well as failing to benefit from the chance to recuperate mana bestowed by the new Wand Specialization.

In this way we end up in a lose - lose situation vs wands: if we choose not to use Searing Shots to save mana, wands will inevitably hit harder (higher dps) and regen more mana (new talent). If we do choose to use Searing Shots to bridge the dps to wand levels, we'd be significantly hindering our mana regen compared to wanding.

 3) Quality of life: Night Elf priests will find themselves asking, all of the above being considered, is it going to be worth sacrificing a bag slot's worth of inventory space, as well as the expense of arrows, for what appears to be a subpar wands replacement?

Finally, independent on whether bows will benefit from the new Wand Specialization talent, we find ourselves with this question: with both wands buffed and bows introduced, where does that leave poor old Starshards? Who will even look in its direction now, when every other priest race has vastly more functional racials?

## Post 104291 by Akos1896 (Grandmaster of Forum PvP) — 2024-10-22T08:50:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104291#p104291 | page 15 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

There are minor remarks from my end regarding shamans.
Don't get me wrong, these are just personal feedbacks. I am experienced with shamans but I don't wanna act like a know-it-all for a class. I'm a regular Joe who played some shaman before.

For elemental, electify is a step in the right direction in my opinion. Ele PVP was toxic and it both nerfs it (slightly) and helps raiding eles with threat spike smoothing.
In my opinion ele's biggest pain points were mana, threat and nature rez targets. Changes solved the mana problems (probably) and helped with threat. Regarding threat I wished changes enabled eles using tranquil air in a caster group but they will probably spam WF after patch. This always felt weird to me since ele more or less has an existing solution for its own threat problem, it can however rarely be used since it uses up the same element as WF totem. I hoped for a different kind of WF nerf or a tranquil air buff enabling eles to use their whole toolkit to maximize their own viability.
Other small pain-point from me is the lack of nat rez tool in the talent tree. Eles will mostly rely on nature in the future and a talent which helps against resists would have helped avoiding them trying to find TF tanks for AQ at any cost.
Flame shock changes... From one hand, they are extremely clever. The other shocks with the added range would have broken PVP and it enables eles to use shock from normal caster range at raids. I'm curious about it but can be clunky. Let's say that you pulled a pack. 1 target is sheeped. Target B is having a flameshock on. Searing totem is targeting that target. You kill the target super fast - since flame shock target is dead, will the totem randomly pewpew, probably attacking the sheep? What I say is killing targets fast and making sure flame shock is always up on someone to avoid searing totem doing something stupid can be really clunky. In my opinion searing totem behavior was a bug and should have received a baseline hotfix.
But all in all I'm very interested about ele despite the low amount of changes it received.

Enh... Regarding specifics, I have no idea. But the fact that 1/3 of the tree is tanking, 2/3 is enh DPS makes me a bit anxious. Are there surely enough talents to flesh out both playstyles? Feral is a similar tree but there most talents give different buffs for cat form and bear form.
I mean... I am extremely happy that we got the option to properly tank up until mid-raids. This change allowed us to play all roles in the game (which is arguably unfair towards the others, specially now that our 'mirror image' paladin just lost shockadin) but also limits us. I have no idea how good enh will be. But enh tank is admittedly designed to tank until a certain raid difficulty, from which point it is not supported.
On paper, fair. But looking at trends in TWOW, this is not the way things usually happen. TWOW took incomplete builds and made them better. Made incomplete tanks more or less complete (dru and pala). People will spec to tank, people will be happy with the changes then in 1-2 months people will spam the forum with things like 'where shaman defensive CD' and 'bad mitigation with mail, Twins keeps crushing blowing me'. This is basic human nature, you gave us half a cookie. We are happy but will want the other half, too. I don't wanna sound like an entitled brat. But I truly believe this is what will happen based on how people work. If you say that you can do 'x' to a point but not further, people will ask 'why not' and people will also say 'but drus and palas can, unfair etc'. Here you might have created a problem for the future.

For resto. They will be extremely strong unless chain heal sp scale gets real nerf. To have a comparable chain heal speed resto shammies used to give up a bunch of stats and use an otherwise trash 5 gear set. Now shamans have a big passive mana regen, cast chain heals even faster and they can use actually good items while doing so. Meditation items, big +healing items, whatever.
What I'm saying is: it might be too strong, we'll see and more importantly, it can be holy pala 2.0. Shaman healing was mostly about chain heals in the past but the current iteration seems like a 1 button rotation, chain heal is so good. I mean you can healing wave to recharge a water shield orb but you have 6 of them and as a healer you shouldn't be damaged too often anyway. The whole tree basically says 'bro, we made everything we could to boost chain heal, use it'. Even spirit link fits into that idea.

Don't get me wrong, I love most of the changes. I decided to give a deeper opinion about the shaman ones because I am most familiar with them.

Hi. Here some feedback on Fury (2H)
Will try to keep it short and to the point.

 **1. **Hamstring now has a 6 second cooldown**:**
> *and building into Fury should now be less questionable for use in leveling and in battlegrounds*

 - PVE: A fury dps warrior have: Bloodthirst - Whirlwind - Overpower - Hamstring -/ Slam, as skill hit.
Hamstring can be used to fill rotation, when your Bloodthirst or Whirlwind is on CD. No prio for spam or op.
Can try to use when ragestarving as dps, proc overpower, crusader or windfury, which has already gets a cd nerf on proc. You used to have an option between Hamstring and Slam, at least for 2H Fury. (more on reduced talent and freedom of choice further down)

 - PVP: warrior is aleady the weakest overall to play solo pvp. Good with team/healer.
 6 sec cd hamstring (if hit, 12 sec slow) forces you to take a point in Piercing Howl, gcd.
that will use more rage to keep slow. (if hit, 6 sec slow).

 - Leveling/Hardcore: Hardest class to get to 60 in Hardcore.
Even harder now if you pull to many and try to run away, and you can only hamstring once. Hope you hit^^

 **6 sec cooldown is way to long for pvp and pve. How about 3 sec like the Hunter? and add more rage cost?**

 **2. **Bloodthirst**:**
Bloodthirst is now tied up to other talents, that forces to pick some talents. No room for choosing anything else.
 3/3 Blood Craze to get hp back from proc and get Enrage. 1/1 Piercing Howl must, since hamstring has 6 sec. cd.
 5/5 for Improved shout thats give ap for+ 30% Bloodthirst.  2/2 Execute back to gcd.
That makes it so you have to **choose Improved shout or Reckless Execute.**

Leveling/HC: When you hit lev. 40 and and can choose MS or Bloodthirst, that gives a "power spike" for the level. With +flat damage change, it will spike more.

Cant max support talents for Bloodthirst with 31 points in Fury. "Like other classes."

 **3. **Counterattack****
Ehhh. For what, low levling?

Love the other content Twow added. That is Impressive!

Best of luck
Wopp   satisfied_turtle

First of all I love all the changes! Great job fixing the vanilla mess!

Some clarification please on the hit% changes.

So before, with 300 weapon skill, one would need 9% hit, and would get 35% glancing penalty.
With 305 weapon skill, it would go to 6% hit cap and 15% glancing penalty.

Isn't this just worse? Am I missing something?

Also the racials having gone to 3 skill instead of 5, they give 0.6% hit, which seems pretty useless. Which is kinda a good result, making races not matter for what class one would want to play. But it's still a useless racial at this point.

## Post 104409 by Steakhouse (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-22T19:32:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104409#p104409 | page 16 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Yonu wrote: Tue Oct 22, 2024 6:23 pm**
> I'm hyped for the changes!
>
>  One question tho, is it possible for shadowmeld to also affect the hunter's pet?
>  As it is, I rarely find a decent functionality for it, and as a hunter I can't even use it comfortably since my pet remains visible
>  I'd honestly prefer if you could "upgrade" shadowmeld to the way it works in retail, so that you can meld in combat (it doesn't stop combat, it's not a vanish) but if you use it in the moment that a projectile is sent your way you resist/ignore it if timed inside a 0.5s - 1s before the spell hits
>
>  if anyone knows any more utilities for the current state of shadowmeld, let me know, I'm trying to figure out what to do with it lmao

 - re: pet still visible during meld: dismiss it (summon is instant), make it /wait far away from where you're melded, or get a cat, they learn prowl

 - re: retail meld: this would be great but has been suggested many times so I figure it's too hard to implement. It's a shame, as retail meld works more similarly to how meld worked in warcraft 3

 - re: use cases for meld:
 1) extra safety while eating and drinking: start doing either or both then meld. Particularly useful in pvp, wherein you can scatter/intimidate -> freezing trap -> walk away -> eat and drink -> meld right as they approach to get you out of eat/drink -> get the initiative
 2) avoiding a patrol: meld, wait for it to walk past you, patrol skipped
 3) mess with an enemy player's targeting: right before an enemy engages you (warrior charge, any spell vs a caster ...), meld, and send pet. You can stay melded while they deal with your pet for some free damage. Feign death also instantly drops combat so you can use that to get an in-combat meld in pvp.
 4) ambushes: on the pvp server there's a guild exclusively comprised of night elves (though idk if it's still active) ; they'll all use their racial to wait on a road and obliterate horde travelers who walk by. This is also useful in defending pvp objectives

All in all hunter is probably the best class at using meld, just gotta get creative with it. Warrior is also good as meld can greatly help it with intiating with Charge unchallenged.

## Post 104442 by Bigsmerf (Grandmaster of Forum PvP) — 2024-10-22T23:19:00Z

> **Dragunovi wrote: Sat Oct 12, 2024 6:24 pm**
> This specialization has seen the most changes out of all other Hunter specializations, as it lacked a proper identity that differentiates it from the other two.

Hi. Person who's played the game before here. Figured I'd give my opinion.

The fuck?

Anyways, angsty tomfoolery aside, I'd like to actually give some input here and refute this claim.

Survival, as it stands, isn't supposed to be the "melee tree" or "trap tree", or... Whatever else you might want to turn it into. How it functions is more or less just supposed to fill the purpose of being a slippery little bastard that can function both in melee and range, with support to get your ass out of sticky situations that don't favor you. Counterattack, surefooted, deterrence, trap talents, improved wing clip, health and agi talents for extra survivability/mongoose procs. It's all there. You're evasive, tricky, and versatile. Not a pure melee.

I'm not even against the idea of a melee hunter. The issue here is you're practically butchering the old identity (yes it had one) that survival already had. Something players enjoyed. You're effectively taking away someone's preferred method of play and replacing it with mine and a few other's meme dream, except like- actually viable now. Don't get me wrong, I'm gonna play the shit out of it and swap from BM once it comes out, but it'll feel wrong knowing how many survival hunters got fucked over just so I could be a melee hunter.

Rest in peace, lads. You didn't deserve this. Your sacrifice will be mourned.

## Post 104560 by Forthehorde — 2024-10-23T15:24:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104560#p104560 | page 17 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

From a business standpoint, what is the objective of this overhaul?

 1. Attract more retail wow players?
 2. Attract more classic wow players?
 3. Attract more vanilla wow players?
 4. Attract more other-game action/rpg players?
 5. Encourage new and/or existing players to spend more money in the donation shop?

Then consider:

A: Assuming players are gained, how many of those will stick around after the honeymoon period is over?
B: What is the total estimated # players gained vs. the estimated # players lost?

Vanilla wow is a very niche game, with a very narrow customer base.  TurtleWow succeeded where other vanilla servers failed for two key reasons: 1) cross-faction brought the community together through PVE rather than splitting it through PVP and 2) preserving vanilla mechanics/world with only quality-of-life enhancements brought back a much-loved gameplay experience.

Vanilla mechanics, as flawed as they may be, are a 20-year known and beloved product.  Alterning those vanilla mechanics beyond recognition seems like an unnecessary business risk, given that it's at least 50% of the reason people play (and have given their money to) TurtleWow for the past 6 years.

At  minimum, it would be business-wise prudent to survey your customers' preferences (with a poll?) and while not definitive, would at least provide a realistic glimpse into what might happen.  That is, unless it's believed that the players "think they want vanilla, but really don't", which would be the ultimate definition of ironic.

That is, unless it's believed that the players "think they want vanilla, but really don't", which would be the ultimate definition of ironic.

At the risk of quoting myself, I would add this:

First, the fact that they posted the overhaul in advance (i.e. this thread) is already a poll of sorts; clearly someone thought "hey we better run this up the player flagpole first".  Otherwise they wouldn't have bothered.  And since the overhaul has already been modified, it says that TurtleWow both wanted and valued players' feedback, and that's a good thing.

Second, an actual poll could help, but polls are tricky; how a poll is worded can prejudice its results, as can seeing other people's votes in advance; people tend to vote for the majority, regardless of what the majority stands for, making people's actual preferences unclear.  But what is clear, as evidenced by this thread, is that shifting too far away from vanilla has, right or wrong, upset at least some of the customers, and that is something to pay attention to.

And finally, assuming an overhaul is needed/wanted, is it needed right now?

There are already so many updates/changes coming soon™:
a) a new profession
b) expanded dungeons
c) new raids
d) new raid gear
e) gear changes
f) TurtleWow 2.0 (updated/dual graphics with UI enhancements)

For at least the next year, as players enjoy the new profession, dungeons, raids, gear, and UI/graphics, there is all the time in the world to re-think race/class quality-of-life improvements. Maybe dedicated class/race gear sets that achieve similar goals to some issues the overhaul is trying to address, without actually overhauling the classes themselves. This gives players options, options equal happy players, and happy players spend money.

Business-wise, and given vanilla's deep roots in nostalgia, it may be better to improve the nostalgia exerpience rather than to change it.

## Post 104651 by helpfulreluctance — 2024-10-24T09:17:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104651#p104651 | page 18 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

**This post is a short text about SHAMAN TANKING.**

Hey guys, I recently started playing on Turtle and just today read about the upcoming changes. I really hope you re-consider.

I have been playing a Shaman main on Classic. Since I like wonky builds, I have been playing a Shaman tank. I am doing the same on Turtle now. I love the *small* changes that are currently present, like combining the defensive talents and giving Parry as skill. In my opinion Shaman tank was viable in Vanilla and Classic already, so the small changes make it even more so. And they don't change a lot, which is an important part as to why I am playing on Turtle.

However: The changes you are proposing now completely remove the class and play style identity. Sure, you make it stronger. I now have a taunt. The play style is objectively stronger thanks to this single change. **But: do I want a taunt?** Not really.

This is one of the drawbacks of Shaman tanking: huge burst aggro, but if you lose it, you lost it. Yeah, I can't tank bosses with a threat reset mechanic. But that's part of the play style. If I wanted to be a "proper" tank, I'd play a Druid or a Warrior. I want to play with a caveat, I want to play wonky and feel special for it.

Additionally the other changes you are proposing simply don't make sense, which is an important aspect why I like Vanilla/Classic. Why does Rockbiter now increase threat from all sources? I am casting it on my weapon, not myself. Only the weapon and it's attack should change. It's literally called "imbue weapon". You are basically giving Shamans stances. If I wanted to have stances, I'd play a Warrior.

I have more thoughts about the patch, but since I don't think you are seriously even considering our feedback, I'm not going to go into more detail. Rogues with axes? Come on.

>   Why not?

It goes against the proposal presented by the developers of the server itself and defended by them until May of this year.

For 6 years, Turtle WoW has maintained the integrity of its proposal as a Vanilla+ server where the focus is to continue the base game by accomplishing what the original creators couldn’t, while at the same time preserving what was already established. Criticizing those who are unhappy with changes on a server where the population is made up of players who left Blizzard due to questionable changes to the point that the game lost its meaning is unfair.

When you remove a skill or talent that has been working (for 20 years) and replace it with something different just "because," you go against the very proposal of the server.

Every player has their own motivations for playing, and when you simply remove something from a class, you are inadvertently killing the motivation of some players.

If Turtle WoW had been presented as a server where everything could be changed from one patch to another, I wouldn’t have even started playing here.

## Post 104720 by Fugus (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-24T19:17:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104720#p104720 | page 19 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Thinking of the math here choosing between a Night Elf and a Tauren druid. Here is the math as I see it.

Night Elf:
+ Increased Dodge + Haste which is good all around and gets better the more you have. Not only translates to slightly more damage in Balance and Kitty, it also means more threat and rage generation in bear and heals in resto.
+ Increased Stealth making it easier to avoid detection.
+ Activated Racial makes it virtually guaranteed I will get my first attack off as a balance or resto before I am noticed.
+ I am the absolute fastest thing in the game, I can outrun and chase down anything else that isn't mounted.

 - I used to have to worry about the orc stun racial which could wreck my intro but now is only a duration reduction that reduces my stun by maybe half a second. Virtual non-issue now.

 - Other druid can warstomp/regrowth once every 2.5 minutes.

 - Goblins can dash but is also followed by a snare which makes it more manageable.

No other really troublesome racials to deal against.

Tauren:
+ +5% health. Good but doesn't get better per point like above.
+ Once every 2.5 minutes you can get a clutch regrowth assuming you time it perfectly and don't get caught in any CC and left in caster form and vulnerable.

 - I have to worry about perception which can see me from a ways off and lasts a decent amount of time and now actually makes them do even more damage while using it. Doubly a threat if stun locked by a human rogue using it and catching me in stealth and stunlocking me.

 - I have to worry about stoneform clearing my pounce, rake, and rip bleed and becoming immune to them which also guts my claw damage before even thinking about the extra mitigation.

 -I have to worry about gnome engineering pets more than any other race because theirs actually scales to a higher level.

 - I can not chase down or flee from other druids unless I can CC them somehow. They outrun me. So, unless I have a Nature's Swiftness + Hibernate in my arsenal, I will likely never get away or catch them.

No other really troublesome racials to deal against.

The math here is pretty easy which ones the best but in the bonuses you get and against the things you have to fight against in PvP after this.

*Last edited by Fugus on Thu Oct 24, 2024 7:39 pm, edited 4 times in total.*

## Post 104853 by Grinface — 2024-10-26T01:57:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104853#p104853 | page 20 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I'm a potential returning player who has played and enjoyed Turtle WoW before I had to take a lengthy break because life. I'm thinking of coming back probably around the time these changes go live and roll a new class entirely. But, while there's many things that I like, there's of course some changes that I am not a fan of. I'm not gonna touch on balance in PvP or even PvE because first of all I'm not that smart and knowledgeable of most of the classes in the game, plenty of people smarter than me have brought out all of those issues, and frankly speaking I don't care about balance (but I don't completely ignore it) as much as I care about three other main aspects when it comes to race and class changes:

 1. Preservation of the Vanilla class/race core identities and differences in how they play.
 2. The class fantasies and roleplaying aspects (e.g. hunters having to feed their pets and carry quivers for arrows)
 3. And most importantly: the fun factor.

But of course I understand that when you change something dramatically it inevitably means that one or two of those three things may have to be overlooked for the sake of more enjoyable gameplay experience. It's case by case basis. I for example really like Survival Hunter changes because I think melee hunters are cool and a fun idea. I mean we got hybrid classes like Shaman and Druid who can choose between melee and ranged focused gameplay, so I think having a very lore friendly melee option for hunter is perfectly fine. Besides I always thought that Survival tree was the most lackluster out of the three without as strong core identity and even class fantasy that gives some melee and trap focused options but without fully committing to them. But I've never played a max level hunter so I can't say what they're like. Some here seems to enjoy the current Survival hunter tree and gameplay but personally the new melee focused Survival tree would be the only reason I'd roll hunter.

Demonology Warlock was in a similar situation except that it had a clear identity with the focus on demonic pets and their synergy with their masters. But the talent tree was also lackluster as if Blizzard didn't know what to do with it. I really like how Demonic Sacrifice was moved up in the tree and is not a core part of the tree any more but optional and even Affliction and Destruction Warlocks can pick it and play petless if they so choose and I love that. Also loving the Affliction talent option to allow casting Curse of Agony along with other curses. It really fits the specialization perfectly!

Holy Paladin, which is the second class and spec I'm considering to roll and play next since I've never max leveled Paladin before because I've always played Horde (and I'd love to get to dungeons and raids easier as a healer). Holy looks really interesting and flavorful. It'd certainly make Paladin differ from the other healers, like Priest, having to go to melee range and wearing plate is encouraged instead of silly dresses. But while that sounds cool on paper I wonder will it also feel good to play. Because not only would the Paladin have to go to melee range but also cast damaging spells on enemies to decrease the cast time of Holy Light and potentially reset the coolodown of Holy Shock. You'd basically have to shift your focus from the mobs/boss to your party members and back, which no other healer really needs to do to play their classes properly. I just hope that it doesn't make Holy Paladin too stressful to play as in comparison. But that's something I can only find out by playing it.

> **Dragunovi wrote: Sat Oct 12, 2024 6:27 pm**
> Rework: **Holy Shock**
>  Now acquired at row 5. Can no longer target enemies, but the amount of healing is increased and now has a chance to reset its own cooldown which starts at 5% and is increased by 1% for every 100 healing power you have.
>
>  Developer Comment: Holy Paladin’s damage right now can be quite bursty at times, thanks to Holy Shock. With the new talents allowing for it to reset, we felt like the ranged burst could become too dangerous. Overall Holy damage should be higher thanks to the new strikes, but will require you to remain in melee.
>  While we understand that the “shockadin” specialization is beloved by many, it does not fit our vision for the class.

What I'm less enthusiastic about is the rework of Holy Shock because Shockadin is a spec I really wanted to try out as well for the fun of it. Now I can't do that. With all these other changes to Holy Paladin I can see how old Holy Shock could become a problem but couldn't you have just decreased the amount of damage it deals? Even developers themselves admit it's enjoyed by many and so I think essentially removing Shockadin as we know it is a mistake.

Then there's a number of small, some could say meaningless, changes that next to one is bringing up here so I'm gonna point out a few of those:
> **Dragunovi wrote: Sat Oct 12, 2024 6:31 pm**
> **Dark Pact**: Removed.

I don't want Dark Pact removed. Yes, it sucked as the last talent in the Affliction tree and the new talent is obviously way better. But I see Dark Pact as a part of Vanilla Warlock. Why not move it up in the talent tree and maybe even buff it to make it more mana efficient and/or add an additional effect to make it more interesting? Or if nothing else just remove it from the talent tree and add it as a new baseline Affliction spell available for all Warlocks. That'd be way better than just removing it entirely from the game.

> **Dragunovi wrote: Sat Oct 12, 2024 6:31 pm**
> **Ritual of Doom**: lowered required players for the ritual from 4 to 2, no longer randomly kills one of the participants, 1 min duration

This to me is an example of removing roleplaying and unique fantasy elements from the Warlock class. Summoning a greater demon as powerful as Doomguard should come with a hefty price that is more than a few soul shards and I always thought that the fact that you had to summon it with four people and one of them had to die as a sacrifice was really badass. That's the fantasy of it. But with this drastic change that cool factor is gone and it's basically just a spell among all the others. A change that I'd make is that the warlock is guaranteed not to die. I also dislike the change how Doomguard, among other greater demons, can no longer be enslaved, which doesn't make sense to me, but it's under your control immediately for a limited time. Having a Demonology talent further down the tree that improves Enslave Demon even more by allowing you to enslave and control greater demons more efficiently would've also been also really nice to bring the master demonologist fantasy to live.

I've seen a few people here wishing for regular res for Druids and to that, as someone who max leveled and raided as a Feral Druid in WoW Classic and TBC Classic and also as a healer occasionally, I say I don't want that. The whole idea of Druids, at least in my eyes, is to work as a Swiss Army Knife: can fill any role, but isn't necessarily the best at any of them compared to other classes. In the case of healing, while Druids perform great as far as raw healing numbers are concerned, they simply don't have a regular res but a battle res which makes it not only Druid's weakness but also its advantage over the other classes and that I think is cool. Giving Druids a regular res just because other healers have it and for 'balance' leads to class homogenization which is a pitfall that Blizzard fell into. And besides you don't need a regular res to be a good healer. A good healer makes sure you don't need to resurrect anyone, or at least not an entire party, in the first place. I understand that Priest gets a battle res as well but only if they select the last Holy talent, Proclaim Champion, and they can only battle res the target they selected as their champion. I think that's totally fine. Doesn't take away Druid's uniqueness as a healer. But giving them regular res would.

Those are my thoughts on some of the changes. It's too much to digest everything and I didn't even talk about the racials since many people already have but to put it simply; I don't want racials to change too dramatically because they're core parts of races' identities, and just like classes, some races are better at something than others. But I wish that the devs, who have clearly worked very hard on these changes and I greatly appreciate that, will reconsider some of their decisions for the reasons I've mentioned. You can add new stuff, heck we want new stuff, but avoid removing things, whether it's spells like Dark Pact, playstyles like Shockadin or fantasy and roleplaying elements like with the Ritual of Doom.

## Post 104925 by Allarielle — 2024-10-27T06:10:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104925#p104925 | page 20 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

So if I'm understanding correctly, the main issues are as follows:
 * Some of the changes do not seem to be well balanced, at least without having been able to test them out yet.
 * Some of the specs have had their identity radically changed, and not everyone is on board with the changes: Enhancement Shaman, Subtlety Rogue, Discipline Priest, and Survival Hunter in particular.
 * Some parts of the community feel the changes deviate too far from the original vanilla specs, even when considering that the existing state of those specs in Turtle WoW is already pretty far off from how they were in vanilla.

I've also seen two specific issues come up:
 * Dark Pact is considered an important ability for Affliction Warlocks.
 * Holy Shock is a gameplay style that some people like and want to keep.

I'd venture that there's also two more issues people aren't voicing quite so clearly:
 * Some changes are nerfs that people are unhappy about because nerfs always make people unhappy (or buffs to classes they felt were already strong).
 * The scale of the changes are simply too much, too quickly.

On the flip side, there are also many people excited for the changes.

Much of the disagreement also seems to stem from disagreement within the community about what kinds of changes are consistent with a Classic+ feel vs. what kinds of changes are taking things too far.

Out of curiosity, would Hunters who are opposed to changing Survival to be a melee spec also be opposed to instead giving Hunters a fourth spec which does have a melee focus? In the sense that the former is taking away from the identity of the Survival spec, where the latter is simply providing more options.

Also, would some of the people who are against these changes be similarly against rolling them out incrementally? IE, making smaller changes to each spec piece by piece over the course of the next few months so players can get their hands on the changes, get a sense of what the state of balance is, and give feedback to help steer the rest of the changes? Personally that sounds like a development nightmare, but it would facilitate a better back and forth on which changes are good and which are messing with balance too much.

I think that it would be unreasonable to expect that there would/could/should be no more spec changes for the rest of twow's existence, especially considering how drastic some of the existing changes are. I can understand the concerns around spec identity and balance, though. If it were me, and in the spirit of it being 'an expansion of the world that maintains the classic feel', I think giving fourth specs would be awesome... but I'm also not exactly a strong member of this community, haha.
