## Post 104950 by Ishilu (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-27T15:05:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104950#p104950 | page 20 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Wolfra566 wrote: Sun Oct 27, 2024 1:10 pm**
> > **Ishilu wrote: Sun Oct 27, 2024 9:20 am**
> > Wyvern Sting
>
>   I may not be Hunter expert but, what is the good thing about the Wyvern Sting?
>
>  ...
>
>  Is even posible to make a fourth talent tree in this client?

It's an additional CC on top of your traps which works against almost everything that's not immune to poison. That's big. Just like traps, it's also useable in combat if you use feign death properly. A survival hunter is a versatile and powerful CC expert, if played properly. Putting Scare Beast on top of that, a hunter can CC 3 mobs simultaneously for a few seconds which can make a big pull manageable.

However you're right, it is clunky.  Traps and WS in combat without Feign Death were made baseline in TBC and that was a good thing. By the way, TBC hunter with Wyvern Sting and Readiness becomes hilariously powerful in regards of CC.

I honestly don't know if a fourth tree is possible and it could be argued that it's not even a good idea. Let's assume, it's doable and the devs implement a 4th tree for hunters. First of all, that would be weird due to all 4 trees being dps trees (or maybe the Rexxar guys want a tank tree? I don't know and don't care). Then we would get an outcry from some druids to split the feral tree into feral (cat) and feral (bear). Implementing this however would lead to further retailification (btw, the melee hunter reeks of retail, too) and some druids - especially in their leveling phase - would feel and act like they're either a pure melee dps or a pure tank. I have an idea of which we would get more. In a similar way, shamans could call for an enhancement(dps) and enhancement(tank) tree and other classes might come up with similar distinctions.

This sounds cool on the surface but goes against the spirit of vanilla: In vanilla you play Warriors, Shamans, Hunters, Priests and so on (capitals intended) with their big toolkits and then enhancing parts of these toolkits, while in retail you really play Furys, Enhancers, Marksmen or Shadows instead, which are dumbed down versions of the old classes.

## Post 105040 by Aydea (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2024-10-28T07:07:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=105040#p105040 | page 21 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Goodness there certainly seems to be a lot of discussion about this update. Having read through some of it I honestly think that the most that can be said has been stated in one fashion or another so I don't think I have a lot to add in terms of feedback. I also don't expect that my post here is going to accomplish a whole lot or facilitate any change-of-minds and that is okay for me, its not why I write this. My goal with this post is to add some "food for thought" to this free-for-all buffet, considerations, ideas. You can take them or leave them as you like.

First off I have a lot of respect for the life time and ardous and agonizing hours upon hours of modding and then testing and then re-modding and re-testing and play testing that must have gone into this. Like [Grinfaces post](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=104853#p104853) which I adore I won't claim I understand the game to the extent that I could give a whole lot of feedback or tell people that one change is good or another is bad, I simply don't know. All I know is that a LOT of lifetime went into this and not only that also love and dedication and though I loathe to say it, yes, also money. Stuff costs money and *someone* has to pay that money. And that someone isn't us we can just come and play so there is that. Just to set the tone of this post.

That being said the one thing I haven't seen mentioned so far is so called "elemental mages" who build a weird off the beaten path crit focused build around "Shatter". Given Shatter was reduced from +50% crit against frozen targets to a maximum of +35% I don't know if this makes this build less viable given the plethora of other changes to the mage talent tree which elemental mages won't have the talents for to actually invest into. It might make this niche build less viable, but it also might not make it less viable, as I said, I don't know.

As far as my own opinion and feelings go I think [a potentially overlooked post by ProfGiggles](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=103278#p103278) reflects it very nicely and in a grounded fashion that does not hurt anyone's feelings. The only thing I would have to add to that is that in my experience as an amateur modder I understand well the constant temptation of improving things, adding things, making the mod better, updating the mod and most of the time those are very, very valid concerns. Sometimes you get amazing ideas only as you go and you might find that they go far beyond the original plan and as it were actually do make everything better.
However, at the same time with all modding projects there comes a point when the mod is in a good place and further drastic core-gameplay changes simply aren't needed anymore. That is not to say some polish here and there or content (zones, dungeons, quests, etc) additions are bad, they aren't. But changing the core-game play to the extent as is proposed, or indeed, planned here ... I don't know, guys. It reminds me of the proverb "fixing it until its broken" which is definitely something that I see this mod currently being at risk at.

I well understand the temptation to introduce a large amount of changes to a modding project all at once especially if you are 100% convinced of them. I would know, I have done it myself. And because of that I can say that while it -can- be a good idea, it honestly more often than not, isn't. In my experience a slower pace is a better approach because you have more time to undo, rollback or change directions if something does not work without alienating or losing your audience. If you introduce it all at once it is a essentially a gamble of proportions as enormous as your audience is in size.

But who knows maybe this is the best thing that ever happened to this server. Time (and much playtesting I am sure!) will tell.

If you have made it this far, kudos and thanks for being an absolute dear and reading through my at the very least sincere attempt to write something that hopefully adds value to this discussion or at the very least does not detract from it.

*Last edited by Aydea on Mon Oct 28, 2024 7:10 am, edited 2 times in total.*

## Post 105046 by thetruemeccs — 2024-10-28T09:04:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=105046#p105046 | page 21 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

As someone who has just started playing here recently and has not invested much time into my character, I must say that these changes are making me consider if I want to continue my journey on this server. I love all the new zones, quests, new races you have added as it just adds more flavour and more replayability for the characters.

But some of these changes to the classes seem little too radical and remind more of Season of Discovery. I mostly play mage and at a first glance, the arcane and frost rotations seem a little too complicated for classic gameplay (as a frost mage, will I have to stand in melee range of the boss, to refresh my Icicles with Frost Nova on cooldown?). Of course it's not retail level complicated, but the magic of vanilla combat was its simplicity with which a 10 year old or 75 year old could perform somewhat acceptable. I also feel that the changes go against the philosophy you have put forth:

> Our philosophy has always been focusing on enhancing and polishing the existing identity of classes and specializations, rather than reworking or replacing them entirely. As fun as some more wacky concepts may be, we want to keep true to the identity of vanilla classes. This means smaller and less drastic changes overall, which should culminate in a healthy meta allowing each class and specialization to shine in their own way.
>
>  [viewtopic.php?t=13840](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=13840)

I agree with a point I've read here a few times that reworking unviable specs (hence adding stuff) is OK. But removing, nerfing or changing estabilished playstyles is not. I can't speak for everyone, but the appeal of the server for me was the idea of adding unfinished stuff, balancing and generally polishing the original vanilla game. But with these changes I am not sure I am the target audience anymore.

Regardless, I will keep on playing as I want to see for myself how these changes reflect on the spirit of vanilla, however I also hope that maybe in the future you will be more transparent and conservative with the changes.

## Post 105088 by Templar85 (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-28T13:51:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=105088#p105088 | page 21 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> I am saying that vanilla is so popular because it is so simple that it has one button rotations that anyone can play

There are several reasons why vanilla became popular in their time but having one button rotation wasn't the best thing game design philosophy. Game was popular because it had
- Super visual and audio ambiance

- Less punishing death recovery system than other popular MMO

- Questing system and the world felt dangerous

- Warcraft 3 created a super deep and interesting lore and WoW was able to continue it.
And many more just listing a few.

Back in the time when we were children and we have been carried on by the game visuals and atmosphere. Questing in Ashenvale for the first time, that's a memory we never forget. However there were so many flaws, mistakes in the the class design and talent tree because Blizzard team was in hurry to release the game. As a child I don't even recognised this things because I wasn't able to and second even I would not care because there was nowhere near any other MMO that was soo good as Wow.

We became adults (or man-child which is totally valid) and we see the flaws of the game. The more game design flaws in the game the less attention we can have on the atmosphere.

I think a good game should aim for a low skill floor but high skill ceiling system.
Floor is low so beginners can join easily because the rules are simple and you can be on the middle ground power level wise with the basic rotation BUT there should be an options if you are understand the talents well and you are more skilled, determined, putting more effort then you should be ahead of others who doing less of these.

After CC2 will be out you can still press 1 button if that's your preferred playstyle. There are so many guilds on the server where you can find likeminded mates easily.

## Post 105571 by Ragetto (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-10-31T13:18:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=105571#p105571 | page 22 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Xudo wrote: Thu Oct 31, 2024 9:38 am**
> Why rexxar-like hunters have to use 2h is very good question. Assuming that hunters are able to dual-wield in vanilla.

Because melee talents are based on main-hand weapon damage (as they were before 1.17.2). Melee hunters can still use one-handed weapons for RP reasons, but they’ll be less optimal.

It’s worth noting that "Swift Aspects" now boosts attack speed, making faster weapons (like one-handers) more viable in this context. Still, I suspect it’ll turn out like with 'ranged hunters', who typically favor slower weapons when it comes to maximizing performance (for the same reasons).

So... you should know that your perspective isn’t representative. Many of the 'whiners' on the forum are also active in-game.

From what I've observed, reactions are mixed (for those with an opinion). Generally, the more casual a player’s understanding of the game, the more open and enthusiastic they are about changes. More experienced players, who tend to be attached to the finer details, tend to be more cautious since they understand the impact of each change better. It also depends on factors like class (buffed / nerfed) and main focus (PvE / PvP). But most players don’t have strong opinions and are just waiting to see how it plays out.

I was initially quite critical of the update - at least as a hunter (as a disc priest, I found it interesting from the start). Now I’m actually looking forward to it, especially since some crucial adjustments have been made since the initial announcement, probably thanks to some of the 'whiners' you mention.

## Post 105804 by Dragunovi (Turtle WoW Team) [STAFF] — 2024-11-01T17:53:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=105804#p105804 | page 22 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

**UPDATES | Dated: November 1 2024**

 **DRUID**

 **Blood Frenzy**'s attack speed increase reduced from 30% to 20% and the effect duration is increased from 12 seconds to 18 seconds.
---
Reduced **Swipe**'s scaling for all ranks of Swipe from the Druid's attack power from 8% to 6%.
---
Reduced the threat modifier on damage from all ranks of **Swipe** from 175% to 140%.
---
Reduced the threat modifier on damage of **Savage Bite** from 350% to 225%
---
 **Improved Shred** now also increases damage caused by Shred by 5/10% for 5 seconds after entering Cat Form.
---
Increased **Open Wounds**' damage increase for Claw from 3/4/5% to 2/4/6% per combo point spent with Rip.

 **HUNTER**

Swapped the talent tree locations of **Hawk Eye** and **Improved Hunter's Mar**k, moving Hawk Eye to the 3rd row and Improved Hunter's Mark to the 4th row.

 **PALADIN**

 **Crusader Strike**'s weapon damage reduced by 10% for all ranks.
---
 **Righteous Strikes**' Holy Strike damage increase reduced to 5/10/15/20/25%.

 **PRIEST**

The Human Priest racial, **Feedback** has seen its mana burn and damage effects doubled:
- Rank 1 (Level 20): 18 -> 36

- Rank 2 (Level 30): 35 -> 70

- Rank 3 (Level 40): 54 -> 108

- Rank 4 (Level 50): 77 -> 154

- Rank 5 (Level 60): 105 -> 210

---
The Night Elf Priest racial **Starshards** has been reworked with significant damage buffs, doubled mana cost and a new 30 second cooldown. We've also fixed an issue with the damage model, restoring the behavior of the channel causing 2 small ticks, 2 medium ticks, and 2 large ticks of damage. The values are as follows:
- Rank 1 (Level 10): 100 Mana Cost, 24 / 24 / 36 / 36 / 48 / 48 Arcane Damage

- Rank 2 (Level 18): 170 Mana Cost, 40 / 40 / 60 / 60 / 80 / 80 Arcane Damage

- Rank 3 (Level 26): 280 Mana Cost, 70 / 70 / 105 / 105 / 140 / 140 Arcane Damage

- Rank 4 (Level 34): 380 Mana Cost, 105 / 105 / 158 / 158 / 210 / 210 Arcane Damage

- Rank 5 (Level 42): 490 Mana Cost, 145 / 145 / 218 / 218 / 290 / 290 Arcane Damage

- Rank 6 (Level 50): 600 Mana Cost, 190 / 190 / 285 / 285 / 380 / 380 Arcane Damage

- Rank 7 (Level 58): 700 Mana Cost, 240 / 240 / 360 / 360 / 480 / 480 Arcane Damage
Ranks 3-7 have a 0.4 Spell Damage scaling coefficient, while Rank 1 and 2 have 0.2 and 0.35 respectively.
---
 **Force of Will'**s spell damage boost now applies to Channels and DoT effects.
---
Reduced the mana cost reduction granted by **Searing Light** procs from 100% to 40%.
---
Increased the duration of **Purifying Flames** buff from 8 seconds to 10 seconds.

 **ROGUE**

 **Throwing Weapon Specialization** now has a 10/20% chance per combo point instead of a 50/100% chance to interrupt its target.
---
 **Surprise Attack** can no longer be blocked, dodged or parried.

 **SHAMAN**

Reduced **Windfury Weapon**'s internal cooldown from 6 seconds to 0.5 seconds and its proc chance has been increased from 15% to 20%.
---
Increased **Stormstrike** mana cost from 7% to 12% base mana and **Lightning Strike** mana cost from 8% to 15% base mana.
---
Reduced **Shaman's Flurry** attack speed increase from 10/15/20/25/30% to 7/9/11/13/15%.
---
 **Stormstrike** and **Lightning Strike** can no longer trigger chance on hit effects such as Windfury.
---
 **Flame Guidance** now increases your Fire totems' critical strike modifier by 100% to make up for that being removed when Elemental Fury was replaced by Electrify.

 **WARLOCK**

Increased the Shadow damage bonus granted by **Improved Shadow Bolt** from 15% to 20%.
---
 **Power Overwhelming**'s mana cost has been reduced to 80.

 **WARRIOR**

Damage increase bonus granted by **Enrage** reduced from 25% to 15%.
---
 **Bloodrage** now activates your Enrage.
---
 **Slam** cast time increased from 1.5 seconds to 2 seconds.
---
 **Decisive Strike** cast time increased from 2 seconds to 2.5 seconds.
---
 **Rend** now scales by 5% of your Attack Power per tick of damage, for all ranks.
---
 **Mortal Strike** now does 105/110/115/120% weapon damage, instead of weapon damage plus 85/110/135/160.
---
 **Defensive Tactics**' multipliers have been raised to 55/110/165%.

> **ROGUE**
>
>  **Throwing Weapon Specialization** now has a 10/20% chance per combo point instead of a 50/100% chance to interrupt its target.

What a facepalm...

The previous iteration of this talent ('50/100% chance to interrupt') was too overpowered due to its interaction with [Ruthlessness] (a talent that grants 1 combo point when using a finishing move). With the old version, you could theoretically spam ranged interrupts indefinitely until running out of energy.

While a nerf was indeed necessary, this new version is simply **useless**. The nerf hammer has swung too far in the oposite direction. Adding more RNG ('chance per combo point') to the game doesn't make sense, RNG is bad game design. Why not slap a cooldown on it (at least for the interrupt part)?

No one, absolutely no one, including PvPers, will take this after these changes. I guarantee that.

## Post 105810 by Galliformophile — 2024-11-01T18:47:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=105810#p105810 | page 22 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Ouch. My main is a discipline night elf priest, leaning heavily into Starshards as a primary damaging spell with each encounter and focusing on melee weaving and mana efficiency. Virtually every aspect of my character has been removed, with Inner Fire losing its melee power, Elaine’s Grace entirely removed, the discipline tree entirely revamped, with key RP talents like improved Mana Burn moved out entirely, and now Starshards being totally revamped…

I like change, but this may be a bit too much! ![😅](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f605.svg) and the biggest issue not in adding new content, but removing old content. There was nothing inherently wrong with the “odd” trees and just led themselves to more creative playstyles to make better use of them. Not every talent needs to be “meta” to be viable, or at least fun. After all, aren’t games played just to have fun?

I’m pretty sad, actually. The entire character concept has been removed. Nothing about that character can be played like it was before.

Most devastating of all, actually, is loss of Starshards. That’s such an iconic ability. To have it behind a CD means it won’t be part of the regular rotation, which removes a LOT of flavor from the entire NE priest. I get that they’re pushing for using bows.. but that’s an entirely different aesthetic already and uses a whole different kind of magic school (arcane damage is useless). I doubt it will be mana efficient either like Starshards is.

With my other main character being a survival hunter, I feel like I’m just playing new classes outright… and since I do really enjoy the RP aspect, to have those trees and spells revamped so dramatically kills the entire preexisting RP, which is like death of the character (in the figurative sense) itself.

In general this is an amazing server and the devs did a beautiful job creating a real Vanilla+ experience with emphasis on RP. I’m really excited for the patch and all the new content. But… Vanilla+ is about adding new content and keeping the old quirks of Vanilla in line with the original spirit of the game, or along the vision of what the game was supposed to be. Many of these talent changes and class changes reflect that. In the case of some of these, though, go against that grain and are more in line with retail “meta” thinking. Weird spells or talents don’t need to be competitive. It’s fun thinking of creative ways to use those spells! Not every spell needs to have an amazing combat use. Not even racial spell needs to have an amazing combat use. Not every race needs to be perfectly balanced. It’s okay that there’s discrepancy… that adds to the RP and to flavor. Some changes are completely justified and everyone agrees. But some changes, like the removal of Elune’s Grace or now the total rework of Starshards are just too much all at once and can kill entire preexisting builds and RP. I really hope they moderate these changes. I don’t want to lose my priest’s entire flavor.

## Post 105824 by Balzack — 2024-11-01T19:47:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=105824#p105824 | page 23 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

As a solo player who was just getting my feet wet here again the last couple weeks I...didn't actually realize such huge changes were in the pipeline until the game went down for the update and I went to check the patch notes.

I do like a lot of whats been added here as Vanilla plus, but I also like Vanilla.  I'm nostalgic for Vanilla.  And I enjoy playing Vanilla.  Massive changes to the talent trees imo go beyond what I would consider to be vanilla+ and enter a new realm.  If people are happy about that, I guess that's great.  I don't think it will be for me though.

Even an innocuous change like adding threat to Holy Nova will affect me quite a bit with my play style.  One of my favorite ways to level is as a smite priest.  I think it's fun to make the build work in the narrow and niche way that its been possible to do before.  Going against the meta and heavily using Holy Nova is SO MUCH fun for pretty much all 5 man content.  The only extra preparation you need to pull it off is a few extra mana potions while fighting trash and you can do comparable dps to a mage, and blow shadow priests out of the water while doing vastly better passive healing than them (which is even better because it tends to be more targeted at the tank and melee).  And generating zero threat is just icing on the cake that makes the spam so much more fun.

Now, on paper people would probably be like "well this is great for you then.  If you like smite priest, then now you'll have a "proper" one that does even more damage!"  But...if it's not the vanilla talent tree and I'm being guided on rails to a more "proper" build...eh.  Doesn't sound fun.  Sounds like retail tbh.

This is just an example from one build of one class.  I could go into others I play too.  But yeah...suffice it to say I might try to find a new home after this drops.  I really love Turtle WoW, and I hope the project continues to succeed and people who love these kinds of changes have a great time.  I just am pretty on the fence right now if I'll be one of them :(

## Post 105881 by watilla — 2024-11-02T06:10:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=105881#p105881 | page 23 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I just made an account to post this: I'm really disheartened by the frost mage changes, specifically the nerf to Improved Blizzard's slow effect from 65% to 40%.

Looking at the numbers for that it may not seem like much, but it actually matters immensely to the point where I can no longer perform my standard blizzard AOE rotation anymore. What's doubly head-scratching for me, is by the devs' own admission frost is 'tightly designed'.

> There isn’t much to improve on for the Fire and Frost mage specs in vanilla - they are tightly designed and synergize well with other mages very well. That said, Arcane falls far behind despite having an opportunity to fill its own niche and the possibility of encouraging the Elemental Mage playstyle.

So why are we touching what isn't broken here? Furthermore there isn't even a commentary or explanation as to why they decided to just make the Improved Blizzard talent completely non-viable. It doesn't interact with any of the new icicle mechanics so it just almost feels like it was thrown in there in bad faith as a nerf to aoe grinding mages (which is like, one of their main things!).

This is incredibly frustrating and unfair to mages who have spent time learning how to pull off big aoe pulls, which is harder than it looks and takes a lot of trial and error to perfect. Having that suddenly not work anymore just feels awful.

If the goal with this patch was to make nonviable talents (arcane) viable, then it doesn't feel right to be making an important frost talent pointless in the same breath.

I will say, Icicles is an interesting break in the monotony of frostbolt spam (if you are doing dungeons/raiding, which not everyone does) but the accompanying nerf to Improved Blizzard was not needed in the slightest. This hurts mages who are leveling and hurts their ability to farm, which was kind of their main interesting thing they had going for them in my opinion. And most importantly it just kills the fun. Please undo it!!

## Post 108776 by Jamey (Turtle WoW Team) [STAFF] — 2024-11-20T01:10:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=108776#p108776 | page 24 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

The first batch of changes post 1.17.2 release are out. Mind you that with the changed situation of having the launcher we will do updates way more frequently. We're still incredibly busy getting enough data and making sure every bug that impacts class balance is fixed so we're starting conservatively for most classes.

Please make sure to also visit the November 20 changelog as this contains quite some bug fixes that might alter player / class power.

 **UPDATES | Dated: November 20 2024**

 **DRUID**

 **Barkskin (Feral)** is no longer a magic effect, and only direct physical damage consumes its charges.
---
 **Improved Shred** Buff duration increased from 5 seconds to 10 seconds.

 **MAGE**

 **Hot Streak** Increased effect duration from 30 seconds to 3 minutes.
---

 **HUNTER**

 *We're redistributing power of Hunter's Marksmanship a little as Improved Steady Shot was overvalued and Piercing Shot undervalued. We're also looking into reducing the major power upgrade Survival Hunters got this patch while leveling.*

 **Improved Steady Shot** Reduced bonus damage from 13/25% to 8/15%.
---
 **Piercing Shot** Increased bleed damage from 10/20% to 15/30%.
---
 **Carve** Cooldown increased from 6 seconds to 10 seconds and added new ranks, where the highest rank has the current damage while earlier ranks deal less damage.

Carve Lower Rank Nerfs:
Rank 1 (Level 20/Talent): 50% Weapon Damage
Rank 2 (Level 38/NEW): 55% Weapon Damage
Rank 3 (Level 56/NEW): 60% Weapon Damage

---
 **Mongoose Bite** Reduced the weapon damage scaling for earlier ranks. The highest rank will have the same scaling as before.

Mongoose Bite Lower Rank Nerfs:
Rank 1 (Level 16): 45% Weapon Damage + 25 Damage
Rank 2 (Level 30): 50% Weapon Damage + 45 Damage
Rank 3 (Level 44): 55% Weapon Damage + 75 Damage

 **PALADIN**

 *Paladin is another class where the power we gave them for this patch trivialized leveling and even some end game content for Protection. We're addressing both by tuning down some of these talents & abilities.*

 **Redoubt** Reduced block chance bonus from 6/12/18/24/30% to 3/6/9/12/15%.
---
 **Righteous Strikes Zeal** effect reworked to the following: **Zeal** increases the amount of damage blocked by 2/4/6/8/10% per stack. Holy Strike effect is unchanged.
---
 **Crusader Strike** Reduced the weapon damage scaling for earlier ranks. The highest rank will have the same scaling as before.

Crusader Strike Lower Rank Nerfs:
Rank 1 (Level 8): 35% Weapon Damage + 31 Damage
Rank 2 (Level 20): 50% Weapon Damage + 47 Damage
Rank 3 (Level 30): 65% Weapon Damage + 71 Damage
Rank 4 (Level 40): 80% Weapon Damage + 107 Damage
Rank 5 (Level 50): 90% Weapon Damage + 161 Damage

---
 **Judgement of Command** now uses melee hit.

 **PRIEST**

 *We overshot Discipline by quite some, both in PvE and PvP. These changes seek to correct this as well as give Shadow some love back.*

 **Mind Flay** Spellpower scaling increased from 75% to 90%, meaning every tick gains damage equal to 30% of your spellpower instead of 25%.
---
 **Vampiric Embrace** Reduced cast time from 2 seconds to 1.5 seconds.
---
 **Smite** Reduced base damage by 10% for all ranks. This is a return to original Vanilla values.
---
 **Searing Light** Now has a 3 second cooldown and reduced mana cost reduction from 40% to 20%.
---
 **Chastise** Reduced disorient duration from 3 seconds to 2 seconds when used on enemies and reduced range from 30 yards to 25 yards.
Discipline Priest Tier 2.5 3 Set Bonus: No longer affects the disorient duration.

 **SHAMAN**

 *Enhancement DPS is currently doing worse than we'd like it to, therefore we are slowly but surely putting power back in. We have noticed though just like other classes & builds that power we've given overbuffed these builds while leveling, we are addressing this as well.*

 **Stormstrike** can now proc weapon enhancement effects.
---
 **Lightning Strike** Added new ranks, where the highest rank has the current damage while earlier ranks deal less damage.

Lightning Strike Lower Rank Nerfs:
Rank 1 (Level 20/Talent): 20% Weapon Physical + 10% Weapon Nature
Rank 2 (Level 38/NEW): 40% Weapon Physical + 15% Weapon Nature
Rank 3 (Level 56/NEW): 60% Weapon Physical + 20% Weapon Nature

 **WARLOCK**

 **Searing Pain** Increased base damage by 10% for all ranks.
---
 **Drain Soul** Spellpower scaling increased from 16.67% to 20%, mana costs reduced by 20% for all ranks and damage no longer builds up over the duration and instead deals the same damage for all ticks.

 *The Drain Soul build-up we added doesn't quite achieve what we wanted it to and thus we are removing it and instead putting a little extra power in the base damage.*
---

 **Dark Harvest** Spellpower scaling increased from 20% to 25%.
---
 **Nightfall** Now a two pointer talent with a 2/4% chance to proc instead of 1/3/5%.
---
 **Imp's Firebolt** coefficients have been reduced.

---

Expect to see another round of changes soon while we're collecting data on class & build performance.

## Post 108942 by Reaver594 — 2024-11-20T12:31:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=108942#p108942 | page 25 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> Carve Cooldown increased from 6 seconds to 10 seconds and added new ranks, where the highest rank has the current damage while earlier ranks deal less damage.

Question:
Was the nerf intended just reduce AoE Damage, or also to reduce single target damage too?

Mechanics:
On a regular Boss-fight, a survival hunter had to use all their abilities (RS, Trap, MB, Carve, WC - roughly in that priority) to not get a small window, where you are basically doing nothing. (PPl who raided MM before, know how un-intuitive it feels for a Hunter to "waste time" when your performance is dependent a lot on making use of every possible GCD without clipping stuff). With the CD increase to 10s, you created that sort of "empty time window" for survival. This feels a bit weird, and I wonder if there wasn't another path of either tuning the damage instead, or a combination of CD and damage.

Flavor/Identity:
After all a CD increase from 6s to 10s (which is a 66% increase), for the only Weapon (aka WPN dependent) Cleave Ability for a spec, whos Identity is basically being the Cleaving Melee with Long Polearms feels a tiny bit overdone to me, and also homogenizes the ability a bit too much with Whirlwind, with both having the exact same CD now.

Feedback:
Yes the Spec is performing very good right now, and that may be a surprise to many. But we should not forget that **Hunter is one of the few DPS-Only Classes** and therefor should be among the top performers! (On that ground thanks for the Piercing shot buff, MM deserved some improvements), unlike other Hybrid specs that hog the thrown of top dps since forever.. cough wayor* cough

 *Small addition:
It seemed Carve was balanced via reducing the % of WPN damage applied, but giving it a shorter CD in Turn, compared to other melee cleave abilities like WW. Now the nuance here is gone, which again puts me to the conclusion that the nerf was a tad bit overdone.
Also please, please, stop balancing classes mana around having a Palading near to keep JoW up, and thats not only true for survival Hunters.

 - Shaman has taunt,
 - Shield specialisation: Give 5% chance block + 30% value block
 - Totemic alignement: 60% of the threat generated by your totem is transferred to you
 - Ancestral guardian: increases your armor value from item by 15% and chance to dodge by an additionnal 6%
 - Spirit Armor: increases the armor gained from shield by 30%
 - Elemental weapons: Rockbiter reduces your damage taken by 10% (Rockbiter give Power attack and
 30% more threat generated)
 - Enhancing totem: Your Stoneskin Totem's damage reduction is increases by 30% and additionally it increases block amount by 30%
 - Elemental warding : Reduce damage taken from frost, fire and nature effect by 10%

for multi target
 - Nova Totem: it's big AOE spell
 - Chain Lightning: it's big for pull multi target from far away

For single target
 - Lightning: it's good for pull single target from far away
 - Earth Shock: Is an instant spell which has its base threat increased by 1.5
 - Stormstrike: Is an instant spell which increases our next two nature spells by 20% (perfect with Earth Shock)
 - Lightning shield: After having suffered physical damage you deal natural damage and consume a shield charge, this event can only occur every 3 seconds
 - Lightning Strike: Instantly strikes your target, causing 60% weapon damage and 20% weapon damage as Nature damage. This strike also triggers an empowered version of your active shield, consuming 1 charge

Totem use :
Stone skin Totem: for reduce damage
Healing stream Totem: for healing + threat
Grace of air Totem: for agi (crit, dodge and armor)

but no, the shaman was not at all dignified to be able to fulfill the role of tank, so I'm eagerly awaiting your counters :)

## Post 109039 by Talon2e — 2024-11-20T19:52:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=109039#p109039 | page 26 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Dev's, I know you're working through things and balancing passes still need to happen further but, man locks need some help.  In general the Aff tree looks good on paper but the damage out put is missing, NF procs are very clunky and the GCD really needs to be pushed down to 1 second.  It would be nice is soul siphon applied the damage increase to both drain life and shadow bolt.  Also the push back resistance granted by fel concentration should be 100% instead of 70% similar to how arcane missiles works for mages; especially since the tree really turned into a channel spec.  Having push back on drain soul or soul harvester is particularly punishing for both leveling and PvP.

Overall locks feel like they need a flat damage increase by about 30% if the goal is that all classes in a raid setting are comparable.  Right now the parses I have seen have warriors around 1,200 dps while locks are down around 800-850 dps.

I'd also ask that we don't kill off SM/Ruin, this has been a long time spec and one of my favorites and it really sucks seeing that spec get neutered so hard.  Improved shadow bolt really feels like it should just be a 100% application rate, RGN damage increases really feel bad especially when deal with dungeons or trash as you have no reliable way to ensure the debuff is up.

If the goal is to have deep Aff as a viable raiding spec I would argue that soul siphon also has the damage increase changed to all shadow spells and the damage increase changed to 8/16/24% or increase the damage granted by shadow mastery increased significantly.

## Post 109661 by Quidoba (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2024-11-24T13:36:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=109661#p109661 | page 26 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Please revert the Searing Light nerf.

Chain crits was perhaps the only thing that was exciting about the CC2 for smite priest.  Any priests who are into this spec were already planning around this new center piece.  Gutting it is pretty damn harse.

Prior to this nerf, smite was in a good spot in PVE, if not a little weak at end game, and a little too strong in pre-bis/early tiers.  Smite has the least ability to scale with gear of any DPS spec.  Searing light is the only way to scale, if you prioritize crit.  By nerfing searing light you are making that situation worse without addressing the early power of smite in low end gear due to overloaded high-value talents/skills providing flat SP, crit, hit and %damage buffs.

For the sake of PVE and giving smite priests something to look forward to in their gearing curve, please revert the searing light nerf, and look for balance somewhere else.

If you don't do this, then you really need to look for ways to make Smite scale into end-game.  I vote for sticking to the original Vision around searing light, and not bailing on it.

For PVP: Smite is still a hard cast caster in a brutal stun-lock/CC/interrupt PVP environment.  While searing light seems overpowered on paper in PVP, it really doesn't completely break the game any more than the toolkits offered by other strong ranged options such as mages, warlocks, shadow priests, hunters.

Searing light should remain as is.  If you must nerf Smite early game PVE power, please look at flat bonus talents providing hit, crit, etc.  Not at talents that provide scaling, which Smite badly needs.

## Post 109684 by Bahamutxd (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2024-11-24T15:55:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=109684#p109684 | page 26 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Improved Scorch might need some rework. Being limited (by Ignite changes) to 1-2 Fire Mages per raid makes it extremely annoying to stack Scorch 5 times on the target - moreso with the amount of resists Fire Vulnerability (and Winters Chill) are getting. Having your Scorch drop due to a resist mid fight is a huge DPS loss due to the debuff itself not being present + being forced to cast Scorch 5-6-7 times to stack it up again.

Because of the client limitations it's very hard to track debuffs on raids and even harder to track durations. So other than muscle memory to renew Scorch debuff theres not much you can do without advanced addons and even if you do theres always a chance the debuff gets resisted without being able to notice it.

This is not a fair gameplay design by any means.

Hot Streak is still an underwhelming talent even after the increase to 300 seconds. The major problem is that Pyroblast ain't much better compared to Fireball, other than the DoT (which can dissapear on bosses or simply not go enterily on mobs due to them dying before the DoT ends)

Stacking Hot Streak 6-9 times is still painful and very long and casting Pyroblast/Scorch feels like a punishment due to them not adding Hot Streak stacks.

Ignite should either be back to 4 seconds to allow more Fire mages in raid or increase its damage a bit to compensate the damage lost with the patch changes.

Ideally Ignite should just be a personal damage debuff on target but that would break the synnergy between mages we always had but at this point I don't think it even matters.

>  Druids were among the few classes receiving small updates throughout the years following our first round of Class Changes. The ability to equip polearms and the addition of Feral Attack Power on many of the more undesirable weapons found on Azeroth were a great boon to their itemization. While already receiving many alterations before, the Druid class and all its specializations still had some pain points that were in need of some ironing out.
>
>  Starting with their base spells and abilities, there have been many voices lamenting the power of druid's two Area of Effect spells: Hurricane and Tranquility.
>
>  The former has a very useful attack speed slow component attached to it, yet its long cooldown and meager damage output held it back in fights with multiple enemies. In order to rebalance its power, we removed the attack speed slow and moved it to the Balance tree as a talent. This allowed us to reduce Hurricane's cooldown by half, while also strengthening its scaling with the Spell Power stat.
>
>  Tranquility is an iconic spell from Warcraft 3. As the ultimate ability of the Keeper of the Grove hero unit, its World of Warcraft counterpart sadly does not live up to its legacy. More often than not it is not beneficial to use this spell when faced with a lot of incoming damage, as the other healing spells offer a stronger rescue potential. To grant Tranquility an effect worthy of its origin and visual, it will now affect all raid members in close range of the druid, at a significantly decreased healing power and increased cooldown. Only Restoration druids will be able to unlock Tranquility‘s true potential.

>  **BASELINE CHANGES**

> ---
>  **Manual Crowd Pummeler** and **Battery-Powered Crowd Pummeler** now increases swing speed by 20% instead of increasing attack speed by 50%, meaning the haste amount is reduced from 50% to 20% and no longer functions in shapeshifting forms and the ability now has a 20 minute cooldown. Attack speed increased from 2.0 to 2.9, the DPS remains the same.

>
> - Doubled the mana cost.
>
> - Healing tick rate changed from 2 seconds to 1 second.
>
> - Baseline threat removed.
>
> - Now affects all members of your raid instead of just your group.
>
> - Ranks 1 to 4 now last for 4, 6, 8 and 10 seconds respectively.
>
> ---

>  Learned at Level 24
>  Finishing move that causes damage per combo point and converts each extra point of energy into 1 additional damage.  Damage is increased by your Attack Power.

> ---

> ---

## Post 113460 by Jamey (Turtle WoW Team) [STAFF] — 2024-12-20T02:58:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=113460#p113460 | page 27 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

The second batch of changes post 1.17.2 release are coming. Below are the changes outlined that are slated for **this week**. Keep a close eye on our forums and Discord to be notified of the exact time and date.

 **UPDATES | Dated: December 20 2024 [Revised: December 22]**

 **DRUID**

Now several weeks into our second round of class changes, we we’re able to observe how our druid changes played out in the hands of our community. We are overall happy with how Balance and Restoration play out, even if the former still has some minor things that can be ironed out regarding the reward or proper rotation. Feral Combat on the other hand is a double-edged sword at the moment. While both Bear and Cat are performing well, Bear even more than we imagined, there are still details left we wish to address. In case of Feral Cat, we wish to explore and expand their identity more beyond the 20-year-old Powershifting and add power to non-Powershifters.

 **Open Wounds:** Effect reworked to the following: "Increases the damage of Claw by 10/20/30% and Ferocious Bite by 3/4/5% for each of your active Bleed effects on the target."

Feral Aggression and Open Wounds now increase Ferocious Bite's total damage instead of its base damage.

 *Developer Comment: We’ve taken steps in establishing a new identity for Feral Cats before, enhancing their abilities through application of their Bleed effects. We’d like to go further with this design by enabling Open Wounds to all three Bleed effects available to Feral Cats and including Ferocious Bite into its functionality.*
---
 **Ancient Brutality:** Periodic ticks of your Bleed effects restore 2/3/4 Energy while in Cat Form. Dodging an attack while in Bear or Dire Bear Form regenerates 1/2/3 rage per second for 5 seconds. This effect can only occur once every 9 seconds.

 *Developer Comment: Taking this further, we also allow ticks of their Bleed effects to restore energy. This is one of many steps taken to deepen the synergies brought forth by Bleeds. However, the Bear side of this talent was outperforming for the bonus it gives and the amount of uptime. To combat this, we’ve increased the cooldown on the talent and removed the extra vampirism to even out its power.*
---
 **Feral Adrenaline:** Dodge bonus increased from 15/30/45% to 20/40/60%.

 *Developer Comment: We are increasing the Dodge chance to make this talent more reliable when it is triggered.*
---
 **Swipe:** Attack Power scaling reduced from 6% to 4%.

---
 **Frenzied Regeneration:** Cooldown reduced from 6 to 5 minutes.

 *Developer Comment: Frenzied Regeneration feels a bit too weak right now, so we’re giving it power back by reducing its cooldown.*
---
 **Balance of All Things:** Starfire cast time reduction increased from 0.5 to 0.75 seconds.

 *Developer Comment: Casting Starfire to gain Natural Eclipse after finishing Arcane Eclipse can often feel sluggish. We’re upping the granted cast time reduction of Astral Boon to help players who activate Eclipse more consistently.*
---
 **Eclipse:** Now adds a corresponding debuff when triggering an Eclipse, lasting for 30 seconds, showing which Eclipse is on its cooldown.

---
Savage Bite: Damage reduced from 100% Weapon Damage + 61 to 80% Weapon Damage + 30.

 *Developer Comment: While we see Feral Bears as a threat focused tank, their overall power overshot its target. We’re dialing their threat a bit back with this change.*
---
 **Grizzled Hide (Feral Tier 3 8 Set):** Duration increased to 15 seconds, maximum stacks down from 10 to 4, Damage reduction increased from 1% to 2%.

 *Developer Comment: Following Savage Bite’s increased cooldown, we’re giving Grizzled Hide a little bit more wiggle room to play with.*
---
 **Rip** no longer replaces Pounce when applied on the same target.

 **MAGE**

Mages of all specializations are currently performing quite well, so these changes will be quite light. These changes mainly focus on very slightly reducing the performance of Arcane Rupture and making Hot Streak a more active part of a Fire Mage's rotation for all level and gear ranges as the talent struggled severely due to its steep requirement.

 **Arcane Rupture:** Spellpower scaling reduced from 100% to 90%.

---
 **Hot Streak:** Cast time reduction per stack increased from 0.5 to 1 seconds, maximum amount of stacks reduced from 9 to 5.

 *Developer Comment: Hot Streak has quite struggled to be maxed out in stacks, especially in leveling and early raiding so we're reducing the amount of stacks required to max out alongside increasing the effectiveness of each stack, which should make this talent a lot more impactful.*

---
Icicles: Global cooldown reduced from 1.5 to 1 second.

 **HUNTER**

Hunter overall is doing well, with Marksmanship excelling on boss encounters while Survival excels at handling bigger groups of enemies. Even with this being the case, we're making a few changes to Survival to slightly reduce the gap between it and Marksmanship for single target damage with the Vicious Bite change. In addition to this, we'll be slightly improving Carve as the last batch of changes has hit it a bit too harshly, causing it to be worse than its ranged counterpart Multi-Shot.

As for Beast Mastery, we're adding weapon skill to Bestial Precision to improve the Hunter pet's performance for higher level enemies such as raid bosses via higher damaging glancing blows without affecting player combat which should help quite a lot to pull it closer to the other two specializations.

 **Mongoose Bite:** Now requires a weapon to use.

---
 **Vicious Bite:** Renamed to Vicious Strikes and now does the following: Your Mongoose Bite and Raptor Strike now deal 10/20% additional weapon damage.

---
 **Carve:** Increased weapon damage to the following:
- Rank 1: 50% to 60%

- Rank 2: 55% to 65%

- Rank 3: 60% to 70%
 *Developer Comment: Our previous changes to Carve ended up being a bit too heavy, causing it to be not be equal to Multi-Shot in the same levels, so we're slightly increasing its damage to equalize it.*
---
 **Bestial Precision:** Now also increases your pet's weapon skill by 5/10.

 *Developer Comment: This change to Bestial Precision should make it so your pets' glancing blows are way less punishing which greatly helps against high level creatures while having little to no effect for player combat.*
---
 **Steady Shot:** Reduced the weapon damage scaling for lower ranks. The values go as follows:
- Rank 1 (Level 20): 60% + 10

- Rank 2 (Level 30): 70% + 20

- Rank 3 (Level 40): 80% + 30

- Rank 4 (Level 50): 90% + 40

- Rank 5 (Level 60): 100% + 50 (Same as before.)
 *Developer Comment: The current damage of Steady Shot in early levels ended up being too overbearing, allowing hunters to have an even faster kill time in the early levels. For this reason we've made the weapon damage scaling component scale with every rank alongside the flat damage modifier which should curb this issue.*
---
 **Stinging Nettle Lacing:** Talent description now properly lists that Serpent Stings applied with this talent ignore resistances and immunities.

 **PALADIN**

Patch 1.17.2 introduced a significant rework to the Paladin class, with some of the most extensive changes to core abilities among all classes. Overall, we are pleased with the outcome, as the reworked abilities have introduced fresh gameplay dynamics and improved the class's overall feel.
---
 ****Protection Paladin****
Our data indicates that Protection Paladin is currently overtuned, and we are implementing adjustments to address this imbalance. These changes are aimed at bringing the spec closer in line with other tanks while maintaining its unique identity and gameplay strengths.

 ****Retribution Paladin****
To enhance build diversity, we are restoring Seal of Righteousness scaling to a level closer to its pre-patch state. This adjustment should provide greater viability for spell power-based builds, encouraging alternative playstyles and rewarding creative theorycrafting. In addition, Retribution receives minor changes to talents.

 ****Holy Paladin****
The melee-focused Holy Paladin playstyle has been underperforming in terms of raw output, and we are introducing buffs to improve its viability. These adjustments will also slightly increase the overall power of caster-focused Holy Paladins, ensuring both playstyles remain competitive and rewarding.
---
 **Exorcism:** Now generates 70% less threat.

 *Developer Comment: While we believe that additional power of paladins against Undead enemies is a great flavor for the class, the instant threat generation of Protection Paladin in specific Undead fights is a bit too high. For balance reasons, we reduce the threat generated by Exorcism while keeping the damage.*
---
 **Retribution/Protection Tier 3 6 piece bonus:** Now only reduces the cooldown of Exorcism.

 *Developer Comment: This tier set bonus provided an increase against Undead enemies that was simply too high, discouraging paladins from ever using their non-tier offpieces.*
---
 **Crusader Strike:** Damage is now normalized.

 *Developer Comment: All instant melee attacks were normalized in patch 1.8, but this adjustment was inadvertently overlooked during the introduction of Crusader Strike. Normalization ensures that, when calculating the ability's damage, the attack speed component of the formula defaults to 3.3 for two-handed weapons and 2.4 for one-handed weapons. This change results in a damage increase for faster weapons and a slight reduction for slower ones.*

---
 **Seal of Righteousness:** Spell power scaling increased to 0.082 * weapon speed for One-Handed Weapons and 0.098 * weapon speed for Two-Handed Weapons.

 *Developer Comment: This change is meant to increase the viability of hybrid Retribution Paladin builds and allow Protection Paladins to have more threat generation built into their basic attacks.*
---
Righteous Strikes: Holy Strike additional threat generation reduced from 10/20/30/40/50% to 6/12/18/24/30%.

 *Developer Comment: To offset the Seal of Righteousness scaling increase, we are reducing the additional threat provided from Holy Strike.*
---
Holy Shield: Spell power scaling reduced from 33% to 15%, block chance reduced from 50% to 45% and additional threat generation reduced from 45% to 30%.

 *Developer Comment: To offset the Seal of Righteousness scaling increase, we are reducing scaling and additional threat provided from Holy Shield. We believe this change will allow Protection Paladins to perform better as off-tanks, while weakening their main tank threat generation.*

 *Developer Comment (Update): The cooldown for this ability will remain unchanged for now. However, we are exploring potential adjustments in the future to better distinguish its functionality from the warrior's Shield Block, ensuring each ability feels unique and aligns with its intended design philosophy.*

---
 **Vengeance:** Now increases all damage dealt instead of just Holy and Physical.

 *Developer Comment: This change is aimed to simplify and streamline the way Paladin scales, while removing some unintended power from abilities that benefited from both Physical and Holy schools at once.*
---
 **Crusading Strikes:** Renamed to "Vengeful Strikes" and Crusader Strike damage bonus reduced from 3/6/9/12/15% to 2/4/6/8/10%.

---
 **Holy Strike:** Self healing reduced by 50% and now targets up to 4 wounded allies within 10 yards instead of being limited to your party.

---
 **Blessed Strikes:** Holy Strike base healing increase reduced from 30/60/90/120/150% to 20/40/60/80/100% but now benefits from an additional 5/10/15/20/25% of your healing power.

Developer Comment: Reduction of self-healing aims to reduce strength of Paladins in leveling and solo content.
In addition, we decided to modify how the heal provided from Holy Strike works: the healing is now raid-wide. We believe this change will help close the gap between melee and caster Holy Paladin. In addition, while base increase from talent is reduced, it now scales much better with gear, which will ultimately make it more worthwhile to use for geared paladins.
---
 **Divine Favor:** Holy Shock critical chance bonus increased from 6/12/18/24/30% to 10/20/30/40/50%.

---
 **Daybreak:** Healing taken from Holy Shock increased from 20% to 30%.

---
 **Blessing of Light:** Now also increases the healing power of Holy Shock by the following amounts:
- Rank 1 (Level 40): 120

- Rank 2 (Level 50): 180

- Rank 3 (Level 60): 240
 *Developer Comment: Changes above are meant to make Holy Shock a more valuable button to press. It should incentivise using Holy Shock compared to Flash of Light for both melee and caster builds.*

---
Normally we do not share bugfixes in balance changes posts but because there are some that are particularly important to Paladin's balance they will be shared here too:

- Judgements applied by other paladins will now be refreshed by Crusader Strike and Holy Strike.

- Healing Light talent now increases total healing instead of base healing.

- Corrected damage gain from Improved Seal of Righteousness.

 **PRIEST**

Even though the specializations are performing well and we're very happy with the flavor of our Discipline tree, we have a few things on our sights for Priest. A few of the capstones and keystones haven't been performing up to our standards, which will see improvements with this round of balance changes. Additionally, we'll be changing Wand Specialization so it also functions for bows, making them more of a viable alternative for Night Elf Priests that want to live out their fantasy.

 **Holy Champion:** Mana returned from damage taken by your champion increased from 1% to 2%.

---
 **Chastise:** Global cooldown reduced from 1.5 to 1 seconds.

---
 **Resurgent Shield:** Holy spellpower granted when Power Word: Shield breaks increased from 6% to 10% of the shield's total absorption amount.

 *Developer Comment: While this talent was aimed at reinforcing the supportive side of Discipline, it fell a bit short of being powerful enough to warrant shielding an ally over casting another Smite. This is quite a hefty increase, so we'll be monitoring its performance for further adjustments if needed.*
---
 **Wand Specialization:** Now also affects Bows.

 *Developer Comment: This change is aimed at making the Night Elf Priest racial ability to wield bows more equal to using a conventional wand.*
---
 **Night Elf Priest:** Casting a spell resets your bow's shot timer.

---
 **Starshards:** Has seen several adjustments:
- Damage has been reduced by 10% for all ranks.

- Channeling effect has been changed from Physical to Magic.

- Range reduced from 30 to 25 yards.
 *Developer Comment: Starshards has been performing quite well but it has increased creature and player kill times a bit more than we have intended. While the damage reduction is small, we've added further counterplay against this spell for player combat.*

 **SHAMAN**

The shaman class has proven to be one of our most stable and popular class after the initial set of changes, we are excited to see how the community will flesh the class' specs out thanks to its rising popularity as a damage dealer as well, it has also proven to be one of the most balanced and well-structured classes too.

We are generally satisfied with how elemental has risen among the other classes as a very capable and efficient multi-target damage-dealer while not falling behind on its single-target capabilities. Future efforts will be devoted to increasing the class' complexity while maintaining a generally simple rotational playstyle more in line with the other casters, we hope you'll be as excited as us to see how efforts in this regard play out.

Enhancement, thanks to a steady supply of cautious buffs, the class is rising as a top contender for high single-target damage-dealing during its windows of power, namely Bloodlust. We are looking closely at player-driven performance optimization for the specialization itself and are glad to see the bustling playerbase forming around the specialization now that it is equipped with a more modern and coherent framework in tune with the base shaman toolkit. Future efforts will be devoted to carefully tuning the class and bring it on par with other melee single-target damage-dealers.

As with Elemental, Restoration's changes were driven by the will to whittle away at the class' shortcoming and flesh out its established gameplay in a manner that would keep it both fun and effective. We are satisfied with its performance after the changes and how players are now able to confidently pick its dedicated talents and enjoy a level of power driven by their choice of class customization and a more linear and less restraining gear progression which does not stifle creativity and player agency.

With these closing remarks, we hope the shaman community keeps expanding as we are excited to see where and how our players bring out the class' potential.

 **Flurry (Shaman):** Attack speed bonus increased from 7/9/11/13/15% to 8/11/14/17/20%.

---
 **Ancestral Knowledge:** Effect changed from 2/4/6/8/10% base stats to 1/2/3/4/5% total stats.

---
 **Flame Shock:** Duration increased from 12 to 15 seconds & initial damage scaling increased from 6% to 8.5% Attack Power.

 *Developer Comment: Our vision for Shaman is to have all the shocks hold a position across the 3 specs. This small bump to Flame Shock's quality should make it easier to keep up for Elemental as well as to make it a valuable option for the Enhancement rotation.*
---
 **Lightning Strike:** Can now proc Windfury Weapon.

 *Developer Comment: True to a line of incremenetal buffs to Enhancement over the course of multiple weeks coupled with a close analysis of player performance, we are confident this final wave of buffs will bring Enhancement to a satisfactory performance level, especially as a strong single-target damage dealer outside of the Bloodlust window. We are also sure this Lightning Strike buff will make the specialization come together as a more coherent and enjoyable iteration of the Shaman class.*
---
 **Electrify:** Maximum stacks reduced from 5 to 2. Each stack grants 50% critical strike damage bonus and 5% increased Nature damage. Effect duration reduced from 20 to 15 seconds.

 *Developer Comment: Balancing the value of Electrify's stacks will ensure the class can still enjoy a ramping power level over the course of a fight without over-reliance on Elemental Mastery as a cooldown or the use of unintuitive tactics to perform at an appropriate level.*
---
 **Elemental Mastery:** Now grants 1 stack of Electrify instead of 2 stacks.

---
 **Elemental Tier 3 (8 Set):** Shock damage bonus increased from 4% to 10%.

 *Developer Comment: This change is to compensate for the maximum stack reduction on Electrify, its overall power should be slightly better with it being maxed out faster.*
---
 **Improved Water Shield:** Reworked, new function is the following: "You restore 3/6/9 mana per 5 sec while your Water Shield is active, and for each charge currently active your total passive mana regeneration rate is increased by 1/1.5/2%."

---
 **Elemental Weapons:** Flametongue Weapon's Fire damage bonus increased from 5/10/15% to 10/20/30%.

 **WARLOCK**

After a majority of larger bugs being fixed and players getting used to the new specs and itemization for them Warlocks seem to be pushing above average dps with some of the specs performing below expectations.

For Shadow and Fire Destruction Warlocks, the changes aim to bring more consistency and smaller dependency on others.

Affliction is receiving various damage increases to bring it up to other specs with also a change to Resilient Shadows talent to make it more useful.

Demonology needed the most help with making Soul Link more desirable to pick by leaning more into Greater Demons synergy. Unleashed Potential is also getting tweaked to make it more interesting to keep up without having to solely rely on RNG. Many of the spells of your demons received Spell Power scaling to properly benefit from the stats they are getting from Fel Intellect and Unleashed Potential.

 **Improved Shadow Bolt:** Now has a 20/40/60/80/100% chance to be applied on critical hit. Chance on hit application chance reduced from 5/10/15/20/25% to 2/4/6/8/10%.

---
 **Improved Soul Fire:** The buff is now applied on cast instead of when the Soul Fire hits, and the buff duration is increased from 25 to 30 seconds.

 *Developer Comment: Having the chance for this crucial part of your rotation to miss didn't feel good and made Destruction Warlock's performance too inconsistent at moments where it should reward you so we're guaranteeing the buff's application alongside allowing it to have a near full uptime.*
---
 **Resilient Shadows:** Reworked to the following: "Now reduces the chance your Affliction spells will be dispelled by an additional 3/6/9%."

---
 **Improved Drains:** Now increases the effectiveness of your Drain Soul, Drain Life and Drain Mana by 5/10%.

 *Developer Comment: This change means that Improved Drains also increases the damage of your Drain Soul alongside its previous benefits.*
---
 **Nightfall:** Shadow Bolts casted with Nightfall are now guaranteed to land.

---
 **Soul Siphon:** Damage increase for each of your Affliction effects increased from 2/3/4% to 2/4/6%.

---
 **Fel Domination:** Cast time reduction increased from 4 to 4.5 seconds.

---
 **Fel Intellect:** Reduced to 3 points from 5, Intellect transferred amount is changed from 7/14/21/28/35% to 10/20/30% and Mana regeneration while casting changed from 15/30/45/60/75% to 5/10/15%.

---
 **Fel Stamina:** Stamina transferred amount changed from 7/14/21/28/35% to 10/20/30/40/50%.

---
Unleashed Potential: Reworked to the following effect "Your direct damage spell critical strikes grant your demon a stack of Unleashed Potential for 20 sec. Your funnel spell ticks refresh its duration.

Unleashed Potential allows your demon to benefit from 5/10/15% of your bonus spell damage. Stacks up to 3 times."

---
 **Demon Armor**: Reduced mana cost by 30% for all ranks.

---
 **Demonic Precision:** Reworked to the following effect "Your demons now benefits from 33/66/100% of your own spell hit and critical strike chance for both melee and spell hit and critical strike chance respectively."

 *Developer Comment: This talent was a bit simplified and now allows your demons to benefit from your critical strike chance, allowing Demonology to mesh better with critical strike equipment.*
---
 **Master Demonologist:** Change several demon specific buffs:
 **Voidwalker:** Now increases healing taken by 4/8/12/16/20% instead of increasing pushback resistance
 **Infernal:**  Healing taken reduction increased from 50% to 75%
 **Felguard:**  Mana cost increase increased from 20% to 30%
 **Greater Demons (Demon Gate, Inferno, Ritual of Doom):**  Summoned demon duration increased from 30 seconds/1 minute to 3 minutes.

---
 **Soul Link:** Damage transferred to your demon increased from 20% to 25% and now also prevents Enslaved Demons from breaking free early.

---
 **Succubus Soothing Kiss:** Reworked to the following effect "Soothes the target, reducing threat of the Succubus and the Warlock by X% against the target." 3 min cooldown. Higher ranks increase the threat reduction:
- Rank 1 (Level 22): 15%

- Rank 2 (Level 34): 20%

- Rank 3 (Level 46): 25%

- Rank 4 (Level 58): 30%

---
 **Felhunter Tainted Blood:** Now applies on Felhunter's attacks instead of when it's hit and the buff duration is reduced from 60 to 30 seconds.

---
Felhunter: Increased attack speed from 2.0 to 1.4 seconds.

---

- Increased Infernal's health from 3544 to 4032.

- Increased Felguard's health from 3832 to 4032.

- Increased Doomguard's health from 4517 to 4951.
 *Developer Comment: These values put all of the Greater Demons above Voidwalker.*

---
Added spellpower scaling to **Voidwalker's Sacrifice** and adjusted base values to account for Voidwalker's base Intellect.
- Rank 1 (Level 16): 305 -> 278, 100% Scaling

- Rank 2 (Level 24): 510 -> 475, 100% Scaling

- Rank 3 (Level 32): 770 -> 727, 100% Scaling

- Rank 4 (Level 40): 1095 -> 1045, 100% Scaling

- Rank 5 (Level 48): 1470 -> 1413, 110% Scaling

- Rank 6 (Level 56): 1905 -> 1835, 120% Scaling

---
Added spellpower scaling to Succubus' Lash of Pain:, adjusted base values to account for Succubus' base Intellect and reduced cooldown from 12 to 10 seconds.
- Rank 1 (Level 20): 33 -> 20 Shadow Damage, 40% Scaling

- Rank 2 (Level 28): 44 -> 27 Shadow Damage, 40% Scaling

- Rank 3 (Level 36): 60 -> 36 Shadow Damage, 40% Scaling

- Rank 4 (Level 44): 73 -> 44 Shadow Damage, 40% Scaling

- Rank 5 (Level 52): 87 -> 52 Shadow Damage, 50% Scaling

- Rank 6 (Level 60): 99 -> 60 Shadow Damage, 60% Scaling

---
Added 5 Shadow Damage to **Felguard's Legion Strike**. This damage has a 60% Spell Power scaling coefficient.

---
 **Felguard's Felstorm's** additional damage now has a 25% Spell Power scaling coefficient.

---
Added 25% Spell Power scaling to **Infernal's Immolation Aura**.

---
Greater and Enslaved Demons will now be affected by your **Fel Intellect** and **Fel Stamina** talents.

 *Developer Comment: Scaling on all of these demon spells benefit from the demon's Intellect stat that each converts to 1 Spell Power. It further scales from the Fel Intellect talent and the raw Spell Power from Unleashed Potential talent.*

 **ROGUE**

The damage output of Rogue hasn't quite met our expectations, with Combat and Assassination struggling to compete with other damage dealers. For this reason we'll be adding scaling to class-specific poisons to allow them to shine above other widely available options such as sharpening stones while increasing the importance of Assassination specific talents. In addition to this, Surprise Attack has seen a small rework to make it feel more like a surprise attack, Relentless Strikes feeling especially relentless with it gradually increasing the lethality of your finishers and much more.
We hope that with these changes that Rogues will once again shine as the lethal assassins they were meant to be.

 **Relentless Strikes:** Energy return reduced from 25 to 20 and now also increases the damage of your finishing moves by 5%, stacking up to 5 times. Lasts 30 seconds.

---
 **All Rogue Finishers** (Eviscerate, Envenom, Deadly Throw, Flourish, Slice and Dice, Expose Armor, Rupture and Kidney Shot): Energy cost reduced by 5.

 *Developer Comment: Energy return from Relentless Strikes and the energy cost for the finishers were reduced at the same amounts as a Quality of Life change, allowing you to use your finishers without having to wait for another energy tick required to use your finisher. Additionally, the stacking finisher damage increase should not change much for player combat but should be quite effective for creature combat, rewarding consistent finishers.*
---
 **Instant Poison:** Now gains damage equal to 5% of your Attack Power.

---
 **Deadly and Corrosive Poison:** Now gains damage equal to 2% of your Attack Power for each tick of damage, equaling to 8% for the full duration for each stack of the application.

---
 **Tricks of the Trade:** Buff duration increased from 10 to 12 seconds.

---
 **Surprise Attack:** Now an instant attack and now deals 25% of your Attack Power instead of 120% Weapon Damage.

 *Developer Comment: Our first iteration of Surprise Attack didn't quite nail the feeling of actually being a surprise attack due to it being a queued attack, so we're changing it to an instant attack which should also reduce cases where its activation period runs out before you can use it with your next auto-attack.*
---
 **Adrenaline Rush:** Cooldown reduced from 5 to 3 minutes.

---
 **Blade Rush:** Cooldown reduction has been reduced from 30/60 to 15/30 seconds, attack speed bonus increased from 5/10% to 10/20%.

 **WARRIOR**

Warrior has seen numerous changes in 1.17.2 with some of them being design-altering. We're mostly happy with the changes we've made thus far but do have some upcoming key changes that will be implemented.

---
 **Arms** is mostly in a good spot right now. We've tried to push Arms into the more precise and calculated gameplay design and our Execute changes have helped with that. That being said, we feel that it could use a little extra push to really play out that design.

 **Protection**, especially Deep Protection, was something that was not very attractive to play in 1.12 Vanilla and in CC1 because of better alternatives. In 1.17.2 we tried to spice the tree up so this would change and while it's certainly in a better state than it was previously we're not fully there yet so we're giving it some love in the deep talents.

 **Fury**. We liked the state 1.12 and CC1 Fury was in (disregarding its overly good scaling) but felt that a core part of its kit, Enrage, was heavily tied to receiving damage and thus would not shine in certain situations. 1.17.2 saw changes to Fury to address this by allowing Enrage to proc from Bloodthirst. However, while we've had plenty of indifferent feedback the negative feedback outweighed the positive especially in end-game. The main criticism that came from these changes is that Fury's DPS done per fight didn't reflect their skill as much as it used to, key moments of a fight without having an Enrage proc would feel worse. Because of this, we will be partially reverting the changes we've made and continue to monitor how Fury does in all types of content.
---
 **Bloodthirst** has seen numerous changes:
- No longer damages you, therefore can no longer proc Enrage.

- Now increases your movement speed by 5% for 6 seconds. This effect stacks with other movement speed increases.

- Base damage has been increased:
 - Rank 1: 80 -> 100

 - Rank 2: 100 -> 130

 - Rank 3: 120 -> 160

 - Rank 4: 150 -> 200

- Attack Power scaling has been increased from 30% to 35%.
 *Developer Comment: The reasoning of why has been explained up top.*
---
 **Enrage:** Damage bonus has been increased from 3/6/9/12/15% to 4/8/12/16/20%.

---
 **Concussion Blow** has seen several changes:
- Cooldown has been reduced from 45 to 20 seconds.

- Armor penetration has been increased from 50% to 100%.

- Stun duration has been reduced from 5 to 2 seconds.
 *Developer Comment: This ability should now better serve as a very strong threat opener for tanks, while remaining similarly okay for mid-fight threat and for crowd control elsewhere.*
---
 **Decisive Strike:** Removed.
 **Slam:** Now has a 2.5 sec cast time, continues your weapon swing timer, and lets you move while casting, just like Decisive Strike did.
 **Slam:** Now has multiple ranks with the following level requirements and damage values:
- Rank 1 (Level 14): 50% Weapon Damage

- Rank 2 (Level 24): 60% Weapon Damage

- Rank 3 (Level 34): 70% Weapon Damage

- Rank 4 (Level 44): 80% Weapon Damage

- Rank 5 (Level 54): 90% Weapon Damage
 *Developer Comment: In 1.17.2, we launched Slam in a state where it only pauses your swing timer. However, Decisive Strike shipped with a bug that allowed the timer to keep going. There was an overwhelming feedback to keep the behavior of this Decisive Strike, and very little was said about Slam's pause. Upon further reflection, we do not feel that the difference between these two abilities as is, is distinct enough to warrant keeping both in (similar to our self-cricisim about old Decisive Strike being just a Movement version of old Slam.). As such, we are shelving the swing timer pause idea and have promoted Decisive Strike to Slam's place. If you did prefer the pause version, keep note that we are still interested in seeing it back in the game, just under a more sensible game system than a copied baseline ability.*
---
 **Master of Arms:** Mace armor penetration reduced from 2/4/6/8/10 to 1.2/2.4/3.6/4.8/6 per level, meaning its reduced from 600 to 360 at Level 60.

 *Developer Comment: The intention of this talent's design is to empower those who switch weapons to match the sitatuion. While we identify that the Mace aspect can be useless when up against a target with no armor remaining, the values we had before were far too strong against most encounters.*
---
Precision Cut: Now causes Execute to refund 10/20/30% of the rage spent upon hit.

---
Execute: Values reverted to original values:
- Rank 1 (Level 24): 125 Damage + 3 Damage for each extra point of rage.

- Rank 2 (Level 32): 200 Damage + 6 Damage for each extra point of rage.

- Rank 3 (Level 40): 325 Damage + 9 Damage for each extra point of rage.

- Rank 4 (Level 48): 450 Damage + 12 Damage for each extra point of rage.

- Rank 5 (Level 56): 600 Damage + 15 Damage for each extra point of rage.

Developer Comment: We've taken another look at Execute, and with the realization that with this change, whirlwind would have become higher priority than Execute. We've decided to simply bring Execute back to vanilla values, and we will see how Arms feels now that there is no longer an incentive to maximize rage before Executing.

The fact that Slam is normalized has been overlooked, we want to bring this to the attention that those with 3.8s weapons should see about a -18% damage nerf with this ability, and less of a nerf for those with faster weapons.

As we have gone back on the Precision Cut nerf, we also will go back on the Mortal Strike buff in effort to tighten the variance of Arms' performance in various settings.
---
 **Execute:** Cooldown reduced from 5.5 to 4.5 seconds.

---
 **Reckless Execute:** Rank 1 cooldown reduction reduced from 2 to 1.5 seconds. Rank 2 removes Execute cooldown as it did before.

---
 **Defensive Tactics:** Threat modifier has been increased from 55/110/165% to 60/120/180%.

 *Developer Comment: We're still cooking up a good way to re-word this talent. The point of this talent is to allow tanks wearing shields to sacrifice mitigation for more threat by swapping in and out of Defensive Stance. With this buff to this talent, players should experience noticably higher threat done, outside than inside Defensive Stance.*
---
 **Improved Shield Slam:** Cooldown reduction increased from 0.5/1 to 0.75/1.5 seconds and block buff duration reduced from 5 to 4.5 seconds.

---
 **Revenge:** Cooldown increased from 5 to 6 seconds.

 *Developer Comment: Revenge, and Shield Slam and all Execute variations shall now be able to align with the GCD, for a more fluid experience with these short cooldowns. As Whirlwind is a longer cooldown, it has deliberately not be given the same treatment.*

 **Items**

- **Stratholme Holy Water**: No longer causes any threat.

- **The Black Book**: Damage and armor bonus reduced from 100% to 50%.

- **Halycon's Muzzle**: Reduced Intellect from 22 to 17, added 10 Spellpower.

- **Wyrmthalak's Shackles**: Reduced Intellect from 9 to 7, Spirit from 15 to 14, and added 12 Healing Power.

- **Demonfork**: Increased health leech from 50 over 25 sec. to 125 over 25 sec., and increased PPM from 1 to 2.

- **Tattered Hakkari Cloak**: Removed 6 Stamina and 6 HP5, added 1% Physical Crit and Vampirism, and increased Strength from 7 to 8.

- **Faded Hakkari Cloak**: Removed 5 Stamina and 6 MP5, added 1% Spell Crit and Vampirism, and increased Intellect from 8 to 10.

- **Shadow Oil & Frost Oil** no longer scale with spell power.

- **Chillpike**: Increased PPM from 1 to 1.8.

- **Sphere of the Endless Gulch**: Stacks required to activate reduced from 10 to 8, and cast speed increase duration reduced from 15 to 12 seconds.

---

That's it for this round of balance changes! As always, we will closely monitor the impact of these changes and act accordingly.

In regards to Rogue changes;

 **Relentless Strikes and Rogue finishers.**

This is a welcome one.

However I think the reduction of energy generation from 25 down to 20 is unneeded, I understand that its to balance the new energy costs of rogue finishers but one of the main problems rogues have is lack of energy generation, with these changes the problem persists, if Relentless Strikes kept its 25 energy over the course an encounter it would give rogues more energy to play with and less down time waiting for energy ticks.

The 5% damage stacking buff if nice but ultimately doesn't address the problem with the finishers in the first place, which is that they still scale very poorly with AP (if at all).

 **Poison scaling.**

I have no complaints here, this is one of the main requests rogues had for a long time and I'm glad its been added.
 *Edit*(please make all poisons last 1 hour on weapons as opposed to its current 30 mins)

 **Tricks of the trade.**

Making it easier to maintain the buff is a good change but its essentially just a worse version of leader of the pack that druids have and don't have to worry about having to maintain it, But many rogues have an issue with the sub tree beyond this and I wont get into it here.

 **Surprise Attack.**

[All rogues could see this change coming from a mile away, now that its instant it'll be actually useable for rogues without having to do quick math's to see if their SS/BS will rob them of the energy needed to use SA or immediately pressing pause on their rotations.
