 **Adrenaline Rush.**

Need I say more? the reduction to 3 mins is a god send, hell maybe the best change in the class.
(please make thistle tea a 2 min cd like all other consumables).

 **Blade Rush.**

This is a contentious one, I'm really pleased with the restoration of 20% attack speed, not so pleased that its now a1.5 min CD.

With its 1 mins cd rogue could pop it roughly every trash pack, it helped us feel like we were helping clear our way to bosses since we dont have any aoe(only cleave via BF) without it our only option is to single target mobs during large trash packs and it just feels bad.

Overall, nice

I sure there are other rogues out there still ass mad about sub, hopefully their frustrations can be addressed later

## Post 113495 by Piacrt (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2024-12-20T06:47:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=113495#p113495 | page 27 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Thank you for addressing Rogues. My initial reaction:

Relentless Strikes: Energy is probably our #1 biggest restraint right now, with scaling being right behind it. That 5 energy being taken away from this likely isn't going to a finisher, but more likely a SS or BS right afterward in order to continue pumping out combo points. I think this hurts us in the long run, but the stacking damage buff is very nice for sustained fights like Patchwerk.

Poisons: Much needed scaling. I am concerned that this really only gives noticeable scaling to assassination, but I will reserve my judgement for after I can test this change.

Tricks of the Trade: Awesome, more subtlety changes please!

Surprise Attack: This is what we all desperately wanted, the damage seems a bit low at a glance but will also reserve judgement for after I can test it.

Adrenaline Rush: Very nice, this definitely helps with energy. At least, I can have AR up for every boss instead of every 2nd boss. Please consider making Thistle Tea a 2 minute cooldown, and removing the 8 second cooldown on Vigor or significantly lowering the cooldown.

Blade Rush: Thanks for this soft-revert on the Attack Speed. I think the cooldown nerf was a bit unnecessary, but this lines up with the new AR cooldown so I will try it before I complain more about it.

What I would like to see in the short-term:
 -Better scaling on finishers. Bigger percentile AP scaling like what you did with poisons would be great.
 -Thistle Tea brought to 2 minute cooldown. If you don't want this to affect the leveling experience, perhaps introduce a level 60 variety that uses Thistle Tea and a high-end herb as reagents to craft.
 -More options for energy regen. Combat Potency, Darkmantle 4 pc as a helm enchant, there are many avenues that could be explored here, Relentless Strikes and a capstone is just not enough to keep up.
 -Improvements to PvP-centric talents that also affect PvE. Hemo and Seal Fate come to mind here.
 -Some way to extend Flourish for Rogue Tanking. There are still dedicated players that enjoy this playstyle, please do not abandon them.

<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=113497#p113497 | page 27 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

In the classic level 60 version, the paladin could be regarded as a profession with unbalanced development. At that time, its gameplay was almost limited to the field of healing. Fortunately, the Turtle Team had made a lot of efforts to improve the professional integrity of the paladin. However, as far as the current situation is concerned, this profession seems to have fallen into the embarrassing predicament of the past again. When appearing as a damage-dealing role, it is very difficult for the paladin to deal remarkable amounts of damage at the present stage. When taking on the role of a tank, its performance pales in comparison with that of warriors and druids. The current situation is that only by joining the team in the role of a healer can the paladin maximize its contribution.
I sincerely hope that the Turtle Team can improve the paladin's damage-dealing and tanking talents once again. In my opinion, such measures will not take away the roles of warriors and druids. On the contrary, it will give the team a richer and more diverse personnel allocation choice. Especially in terms of the optimization of damage-dealing talents, it can also prevent those players who are wholeheartedly devoted to studying the gameplay of the retribution paladin and going all out from falling into the quagmire of despair. After all, we have spent a lot of energy exploring its damage-dealing skills, but we have always been unable to reach the damage-dealing level of warriors and mages, which is really frustrating and disheartening.

Is it just me or is anyone else annoyed by the bizarre and messy feel to some of the design changes, including point intervals? Vanilla had such a simple clean feel to class design and it feels like every round of class changes just tangles us more and more in some incoherent mess.

E.g.
> **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> **Flurry (Shaman):** Attack speed bonus increased from 7/9/11/13/15% to 8/11/14/17/20%.
>
>  **Master of Arms:** Mace armor penetration reduced from 2/4/6/8/10 to 1.2/2.4/3.6/4.8/6 per level, meaning its reduced from 600 to 360 at Level 60.

This kind of stuff just looks odd on the tooltip. It confirms my fears that rather than reverting some of the more problematic talent/ability changes with CC2 all they are doing is adjusting numbers. It seems they aren't considering that the new talents and new/removed abilities might be the issues. Once again, it's starting to feel like a [CC2 sunk cost fallacy](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=111804).

As another example of this, they keep shaman Electrify but just reduce the number of stacks rather than removing/reverting the ability entirely. While I'm glad the stacks are at least reduced, it's like they don't even consider there are other design options than needing to stack. Once again, why do shamans have a stacking mechanic for their 100% crit bonus but destro locks and balance druids get theirs permanently?

## Post 113530 by Verdict — 2024-12-20T09:20:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=113530#p113530 | page 27 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> Patch 1.17.2 introduced a significant rework to the Paladin class, with some of the most extensive changes to core abilities among all classes. Overall, we are pleased with the outcome, as the reworked abilities have introduced fresh gameplay dynamics and improved the class's overall feel.
> ---
>  ****Protection Paladin****
>  Our data indicates that Protection Paladin is currently overtuned, and we are implementing adjustments to address this imbalance. These changes are aimed at bringing the spec closer in line with other tanks while maintaining its unique identity and gameplay strengths.
>
>  ****Retribution Paladin****
>  To enhance build diversity, we are restoring Seal of Righteousness scaling to a level closer to its pre-patch state. This adjustment should provide greater viability for spell power-based builds, encouraging alternative playstyles and rewarding creative theorycrafting. In addition, Retribution receives minor changes to talents.
>
>  ****Holy Paladin****
>  The melee-focused Holy Paladin playstyle has been underperforming in terms of raw output, and we are introducing buffs to improve its viability. These adjustments will also slightly increase the overall power of caster-focused Holy Paladins, ensuring both playstyles remain competitive and rewarding.
> ---
>  **Exorcism:** Now generates 70% less threat.
>
>  *Developer Comment: While we believe that additional power of paladins against Undead enemies is a great flavor for the class, the instant threat generation of Protection Paladin in specific Undead fights is a bit too high. For balance reasons, we reduce the threat generated by Exorcism while keeping the damage.*
> ---
>  **Retribution/Protection Tier 3 6 piece bonus:** Now only reduces the cooldown of Exorcism.
>
>  *Developer Comment: This tier set bonus provided an increase against Undead enemies that was simply too high, discouraging paladins from ever using their non-tier offpieces.*
> ---
>  **Crusader Strike:** Damage is now normalized.
>
>  *Developer Comment: All instant melee attacks were normalized in patch 1.8, but this adjustment was inadvertently overlooked during the introduction of Crusader Strike. Normalization ensures that, when calculating the ability's damage, the attack speed component of the formula defaults to 3.3 for two-handed weapons and 2.4 for one-handed weapons. This change results in a damage increase for faster weapons and a slight reduction for slower ones.*
>
> ---
>  **Seal of Righteousness:** Spell power scaling increased.
>
>  *Developer Comment: This change is meant to increase the viability of hybrid Retribution Paladin builds and allow Protection Paladins to have more threat generation built into their basic attacks.*
> ---
>  **Righteous Strikes:** Holy Strike additional threat generation reduced from 10/20/30/40/50% to 3/6/9/12/15%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: To offset the Seal of Righteousness scaling increase, we are reducing the additional threat provided from Holy Strike.*
> ---
>  **Holy Shield:** Cooldown increased from 10 to 12 seconds, spell power scaling reduced from 33% to 15% and additional threat generation reduced from 45% to 30%.
>
>  Developer Comment: To offset the Seal of Righteousness scaling increase, we are reducing scaling and additional threat provided from Holy Shield. We believe this change will allow Protection Paladins to perform better as off-tanks, while weakening their main tank threat generation.
>
>  In addition, the cooldown has been increased to weaken Protection’s survivability.
> ---
>  **Vengeance:** Now increases all damage dealt instead of just Holy and Physical.
>
>  *Developer Comment: This change is aimed to simplify and streamline the way Paladin scales, while removing some unintended power from abilities that benefited from both Physical and Holy schools at once.*
> ---
>  **Crusading Strikes:** Renamed to "Vengeful Strikes" and Crusader Strike damage bonus reduced from 3/6/9/12/15% to 2/4/6/8/10%.
>
> ---
>  **Holy Strike:** Self healing reduced by 50% and now targets up to 4 wounded allies within 10 yards instead of being limited to your party.
>
> ---
>  **Blessed Strikes:** Holy Strike base healing increase reduced from 30/60/90/120/150% to 20/40/60/80/100% but now benefits from an additional 5/10/15/20/25% of your healing power.
>
>  Developer Comment: Reduction of self-healing aims to reduce strength of Paladins in leveling and solo content.
>  In addition, we decided to modify how the heal provided from Holy Strike works: the healing is now raid-wide. We believe this change will help close the gap between melee and caster Holy Paladin. In addition, while base increase from talent is reduced, it now scales much better with gear, which will ultimately make it more worthwhile to use for geared paladins.
> ---
>  **Divine Favor:** Holy Shock critical chance bonus increased from 6/12/18/24/30% to 10/20/30/40/50%.
>
> ---
>  **Daybreak:** Healing taken from Holy Shock increased from 20% to 30%.
>
> ---
>  **Blessing of Light:** Now also increases the healing power of Holy Shock by the following amounts:
> - Rank 1 (Level 40): 120
>
> - Rank 2 (Level 50): 180
>
> - Rank 3 (Level 60): 240
>   *Developer Comment: Changes above are meant to make Holy Shock a more valuable button to press. It should incentivise using Holy Shock compared to Flash of Light for both melee and caster builds.*
>
>
>
> ---
>   Normally we do not share bugfixes in balance changes posts but because there are some that are particularly important to Paladin's balance they will be shared here too:
>
> - Judgements applied by other paladins will now be refreshed by Crusader Strike and Holy Strike.
>
> - Healing Light talent now increases total healing instead of base healing.
>
> - Corrected damage gain from Improved Seal of Righteousness.
>
> - **Stratholme Holy Water**: No longer causes any threat.
>
>
> - **Shadow Oil & Frost Oil** no longer scale with spell power.
>
>
>
>
> ---
>
>  That's it for this round of balance changes! As always, we will closely monitor the impact of these changes and act accordingly.

I am utterly disappointed, not because we got nerfed, we deserve to get nerfed, but because of the absolutely moronic train of thought that went into these nerfs for Protection Paladins.

The Holy Shield increase from 10 -> 12 seconds must not get shipped, this will absolutely kill the Spell Power playstyle and will force us into deep Defensive Play because you can factually die in 2 seconds of being crushed twice or even crit once + crush. This can happen and will happen on every 12 second cycle. This change is done by a person who's either not aware of what they did or is detesting the Paladin to extend where they wish to cripple them.
The Exorcism -70% threat and T3 dmg from Set is looking too doubleded down.
Holy Strike threat nerfs were warranted.
Crusader Strike normalization with new SoR might be good to use, depending on many factors which we do not know until this is shipped.

## Post 113539 by Elesion (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-12-20T10:53:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=113539#p113539 | page 28 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> **Savage Bite:** Cooldown increased from 6 to 9 seconds.
>
>  *Developer Comment: While we see Feral Bears as a threat focused tank, their overall power overshot its target. We’re dialing their threat a bit back with this change.*

I don't think it is much of a secret that bears generated absurd amounts of threat and that there needed to be balance adjustment. But while the values needed tweaking, the rotation already felt fine. The cooldown increase is not warranted and extremely detrimental. Note that you decreased the cooldown of Concussion Blow for warriors so it's better for snap threat and has more utility mid-fight. The same reasoning applies to Savage Bite. This is our snap threat. Our catch-up going beyond our regular threat-curve. Parries/Dodges already feel pretty bad on a skill this expensive, but with +50% cooldown it's going to increase the influence of combat RNG in a bad way. Note that on page 1 of this thread you said that Savage Bite getting a buffed threat multiplier is the replacement for taking away MCP. Then the threat multiplier has been substantially decreased, now the cooldown is +50%. In effect Savage Bite will now be outputting much *lower* threat than pre-patch when we still had MCP. And note that bears didn't just use MCP for "more threat" but for "smoother threat" because more instances of attacks means a single attack getting parried or dodged is less detrimental. We are forced to tank with a 2.5 second swing timer and our main threat ability is queued on the next auto-attack. We can't just equip a fast weapon. Putting our ability to counter-act bad combat RNG on +50% cooldown is horrible.
Also do note that you "double-dipped" on threat balance. You nerfed bears substantially *and* buffed other classes to high heaven. This is not a sensible approach to achieve balance imo.

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> **Ancient Brutality:** Periodic ticks of your Bleed effects restore 2/3/4 Energy while in Cat Form. Dodging an attack while in Bear or Dire Bear Form regenerates 1/2/3 rage per second for 5 seconds. This effect can only occur once every 9 seconds.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Taking this further, we also allow ticks of their Bleed effects to restore energy. This is one of many steps taken to deepen the synergies brought forth by Bleeds. However, the Bear side of this talent was outperforming for the bonus it gives and the amount of uptime. To combat this, we’ve increased the cooldown on the talent and removed the extra vampirism to even out its power.*

I applaud the approach to make the talents valuable for both cats and bears. This is something that has rubbed me the wrong way about the first iteration of CC2 talents.
But do note that you took away the identity of the talent. Vampirism was the cool part about Ancient Brutality, the unique part, the part that had universal utility even for soloing content. Note that his is a row-6 talent - it's supposed to feel powerful.
I don't think people were even able to fully evaluate this talent given that Vampirism doesn't show up in combat logs. This feels like a rushed and poorly reasoned change.

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> **Grizzled Hide (Feral Tier 3 8 Set):** Duration increased to 15 seconds, maximum stacks down from 10 to 4, Damage reduction increased from 1% to 2%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Following Savage Bite’s increased cooldown, we’re giving Grizzled Hide a little bit more wiggle room to play with.*

This is the most marginal improvement (stun mechanics are now less likely to drop your stack) but still has the same substantial problems as before. It hides a basic role-identity skill that all the other tank classes get by default or from a talent behind a set bonus. And it's still hard and slow to enable and easy to drop. Rethink this set bonus completely, maybe move (part of) it to talents.

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> In case of Feral Cat, we wish to explore and expand their identity more beyond the 20-year-old Powershifting and add power to non-Powershifters.

This is not "expanding" beyond powershifting, this is simply systematically neglecting powershifting Shred. A lot of people like the spec they've been playing for years. Go figure, that's probably why they picked this class. CC2 already basically forgot about Shred until a tiny buff was added last minute. Cats are already underperforming substantially and now this balance patch will buff our direct competition further (warriors and rogues). I think the alternative playstyle with bleeds and Claw is interesting and I'm not against it. As an *alternative*. The tried and true powershifting Shred gameplay should be competitive. This patch basically tells you to completely rethink your rotation because Shred won't be supported going forward.

## Post 113549 by Proworx31 — 2024-12-20T12:05:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=113549#p113549 | page 28 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

My feedback for the druid bear changes:

Swipe: Nerf seems fine.

Feral Adrenaline: Remains mostly pointless to spend talent points on with the 30 seconds cooldown. I would consider using this talent with 10 or 15 seconds cooldown.

Ancient Brutality: Nerfs seem random. Quoting inital CC2 log: "This talent will allow druids to gain benefit from it by generating rage on successful dodges.". The nerf from 6 to 9 seconds CD and removing he healing portion at the same time seems too harsh.

Frenzied Regeneration: Quoting CC2 log: "Frenzied Regeneration feels a bit too weak right now, so we’re giving it power back by reducing its cooldown." How does reducing the CD by one minute give it power back? The effect is literally still the same. That developer comment makes no sense to me. Giving power back to the ability would mean to tweak the numbers of the healing.

Savage Bite: As many other forum posters pointed out the savage bite nerf is more than unreasonable. The developer comment says "We’re dialing their threat a bit back with this change.". Increasing the CD of a ragedump and snapthreat ability by 50% is not the way. Adjusting the attackpower scaling or the threat scaling would be appropriate, not increasing the CD from 6 to 9 seconds.

Grizzled Hide: That change is whatever. With the Savage Bite nerf we have other things to worry about.

In general throwing out so many changes and/or nerfs to CC2 at once seems not the best way to handle balance changes.
Especially the Savage Bite nerf must be reconsidered. It is nowhere near reasonable.

## Post 113566 by Elesion (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-12-20T13:23:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=113566#p113566 | page 28 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> **Feral Adrenaline:** Dodge bonus increased from 15/30/45% to 20/40/60%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: We are increasing the Dodge chance to make this talent more reliable when it is triggered.*

I appreciate that you're taking another look at this talent. It seems pretty underpowered and hard to justify putting points into it. Buffing the dodge value helps address 1 major concern, but there are more than that.

 1) The way the hit table works, incoming crits are the last thing pushed out by stacking more dodge. So the main utility of Feral Adrenaline - preventing deadly consecutive crits - relies on getting to 100% avoidance against the mob. Boosting the total value to +60% goes a long way in achieving this goal. Good job.

 2) For this reason Feral Adrenaline has very little effect or value below maxing out the talent (3/3).

 3) Feral Adrenaline is on a 30s cooldown.This is not a reliable answer to the randomness of combat rolls. Your chance to be crit can be lower than 1% but the server can still roll it several times in a row. As a row-5 talent with 3 points it feels like this doesn't do enough to *reliably* mitigate bad luck.

 4) Feral Adrenaline is very raid-oriented. There is little value to take this talent while leveling (even as a dungeon tank since you don't have the gear to get to 100% avoidance even with +60% from the proc). And individual points feel pretty weak - 1/3 is not really do much of anything for you as a leveling feral.

 5) Feral Adrenaline loses value as you gear up. You need some pretty decent gear to enjoy the talent's full benefit (reaching 100% avoidance after being crit), but that usually goes hand in hand with dropping the likelihood of being crit. The new bear-oriented tier sets feature the Defense stat, which passively reduces your chance to be crit by mobs. The better gear you have, the less (on average) Feral Adrenaline will proc. But you still need 3/3 for it to fulfill its basic function.

I think the spirit of the talent is great - help bears mitigate incoming crits when we have no shield block. But the execution is just very unreliable, expensive, and hard to justify the talent point cost for. I think this talent probably deserves a full rework. It's just so incredibly niche right now. If that is not an option consider making +60% dodge baseline and scale the internal cooldown with talent points spent so the talent has value from the first point and you can adjust your points as your gear makes you get crit less and less.

Warlock Changes (Demonology):

>

Master Demonologist: Change several demon specific buffs:

Okay, so the Voidwalker Master Demonologist Buff is still pretty bad. Pushback was kinda useful solo-wise when you out aggro'd the blueberry, but adding healing % increase doesn't really incentivize the use of a VoidWalker. I mean, the whole point of the thing being tanky is so that it soaks up hits instead of the warlock.

The talent should be something like "Now transfers 10/20/30/40/50% of threat from warlock to demon." THAT would be an interesting and useful way of making the demonology Voidwalkers unique to its spec in solo and group play.

As for the Greater Demons changes - NOBODY USES GREATER DEMONS. Make them permanent or at least 30 minutes of enslavement, otherwise don't even bother. They are pretty weak pets and not worth the hassle to summon and maintain.

A better version of this would be to transfer power from warlock to demon - something like a %25 damage debuff to warlock for a 100-150% buff to demon.

>
>  I don't think it is much of a secret that bears generated absurd amounts of threat and that there needed to be balance adjustment. But while the values needed tweaking, the rotation already felt fine. The cooldown increase is not warranted and extremely detrimental. Note that you decreased the cooldown of Concussion Blow for warriors so it's better for snap threat and has more utility mid-fight. The same reasoning applies to Savage Bite. This is our snap threat. Our catch-up going beyond our regular threat-curve. Parries/Dodges already feel pretty bad on a skill this expensive, but with +50% cooldown it's going to increase the influence of combat RNG in a bad way. Note that on page 1 of this thread you said that Savage Bite getting a buffed threat multiplier is the replacement for taking away MCP. Then the threat multiplier has been substantially decreased, now the cooldown is +50%. In effect Savage Bite will now be outputting much *lower* threat than pre-patch when we still had MCP. And note that bears didn't just use MCP for "more threat" but for "smoother threat" because more instances of attacks means a single attack getting parried or dodged is less detrimental. We are forced to tank with a 2.5 second swing timer and our main threat ability is queued on the next auto-attack. We can't just equip a fast weapon. Putting our ability to counter-act bad combat RNG on +50% cooldown is horrible.
>  Also do note that you "double-dipped" on threat balance. You nerfed bears substantially *and* buffed other classes to high heaven. This is not a sensible approach to achieve balance imo.
>

> >
> >  *Developer Comment: Taking this further, we also allow ticks of their Bleed effects to restore energy. This is one of many steps taken to deepen the synergies brought forth by Bleeds. However, the Bear side of this talent was outperforming for the bonus it gives and the amount of uptime. >
>  I applaud the approach to make the talents valuable for both cats and bears. This is something that has rubbed me the wrong way about the first iteration of CC2 talents.
>  But do note that you took away the identity of the talent. Vampirism was the cool part about Ancient Brutality, the unique part, the part that had universal utility even for soloing content. Note that his is a row-6 talent - it's supposed to feel powerful.
>  I don't think people were even able to fully evaluate this talent given that Vampirism doesn't show up in combat logs. This feels like a rushed and poorly reasoned change.
>
>
> > **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> > **Grizzled Hide (Feral Tier 3 8 Set):** Duration increased to 15 seconds, maximum stacks down from 10 to 4, Damage reduction increased from 1% to 2%.

It hides a basic role-identity skill that all the other tank classes get by default or from a talent behind a set bonus. And it's still hard and slow to enable and easy to drop. Note that you decreased the cooldown of Concussion Blow for warriors so it's better for snap threat and has more utility mid-fight. The same reasoning applies to Savage Bite. This is our snap threat. Our catch-up going beyond our regular threat-curve. Parries/Dodges already feel pretty bad on a skill this expensive, but with +50% cooldown it's going to increase the influence of combat RNG in a bad way. Note that on page 1 of this thread you said that Savage Bite getting a buffed threat multiplier is the replacement for taking away MCP. Then the threat multiplier has been substantially decreased, now the cooldown is +50%. In effect Savage Bite will now be outputting much *lower* threat than pre-patch when we still had MCP. And note that bears didn't just use MCP for "more threat" but for "smoother threat" because more instances of attacks means a single attack getting parried or dodged is less detrimental. ## Post 113643 by Templar85 (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2024-12-20T21:55:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=113643#p113643 | page 29 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

I am really sad reading druid changes. Lets elaborate

> While both Bear and Cat are performing well

This is a HUGE fundamental mistake if devs think this way.
Bear wasn't performed too bad, but most of the cc2 talents for them are absolute dogshit and already having uncorrected design flaws in the toolkit.

Cats are even more further from the "performing well" standpoint than bears. They are mediocre and even have more class design flaws in their system than bears.

> In case of Feral Cat, we wish to explore and expand their identity more beyond the 20-year-old Powershifting and add power to non-Powershifters.

I don't believe it. If that would be the case you would listen of the community feedback instead coming up illogical and horrible talent reworks. The very first thing that non powershifter cat need is to eliminate glancing blows.

> Open Wounds: Effect reworked to the following: "Increases the damage of Claw by 10/20/30% and Ferocious Bite by 3/4/5% for each of your active Bleed effects on the target."

That's a good change but need to completely rework Pounce and need to buff Rake by lowering energy cost or giving 2 CP if the target has no bleed effect on it. Still there are no talents that increases Bleed duration and Rip Damage.

> Ancient Brutality: Periodic ticks of your Bleed effects restore 2/3/4 Energy while in Cat Form. Dodging an attack while in Bear or Dire Bear Form regenerates 1/2/3 rage per second for 5 seconds. This effect can only occur once every 9 seconds.

The first part is a good concept but very weak materialisation. Need like around triple(12/dot) energy return to make powersthifting less favourable for bleed cats
Second part is a gigantic nerf. Vampirism was good part on the talent. Have to give us back. Dodge tanking style is still not viable, its incomplete and unreliable. The talent needed a buff and you give us a nerf. The rage return needed slight buff from 1/2/3 rage for 5 seconds to 2/3/4 or even 3/4/5 rage for 5 seconds. The ICD increase from 6 seconds to 9 seconds making this talent absolutely useless now for Bears

> However, the Bear side of this talent was outperforming for the bonus it gives and the amount of uptime. To combat this, we’ve increased the cooldown on the talent and removed the extra vampirism to even out its power.

What does outperforming means? In what scenario does it? I tell you in which scenario was underperforming. For the intended high dodge style scenario. The rage return is low if the druid have high dodge chance (more than 40%).  The talent is in the 6th row so it should have an impact. The talent was performed well when druid had a mixed gear and around 30% dodge. Now this changes killed this talent for Bears.

> Feral Adrenaline: Dodge bonus increased from 15/30/45% to 20/40/60%.
>
>  Developer Comment: We are increasing the Dodge chance to make this talent more reliable when it is triggered.

This is everything but not reliable. Can explain anybody with logic and in-game scenario where is with the 30 sec internal CD makes it useful? Horrible talent. Have to completely redesign.

> Swipe: Attack Power scaling reduced from 6% to 4%.

Again total garbage change. Should have reduce the threat on the spell not the scaling.

> Frenzied Regeneration: Cooldown reduced from 6 to 5 minutes.
>
>  Developer Comment: Frenzied Regeneration feels a bit too weak right now, so we’re giving it power back by reducing its cooldown.

You giving back ZERO power to it. Needs to return at least 80% of our HP. Still have to use with the 10 minute CD Barkskin spell to have a tolerable effect.

> Savage Bite: Cooldown increased from 6 to 9 seconds.
>
>  Developer Comment: While we see Feral Bears as a threat focused tank, their overall power overshot its target. We’re dialing their threat a bit back with this change.

How the heck any experienced druid (assuming many on the class council) can come up with this change? Reduce the threat but not increase the cooldown. How many buttons tank warrior can use for tanking? Around 5? Druids have Maul, swipe nerfed and not much worth to use on single target and the 3rd we had was savage bite but now it on 9 seconds cooldown. We should happy with our 2.5 second maul and auto attack toolkit because that is "Vanilla style gameplay" right?

> Grizzled Hide (Feral Tier 3 8 Set): Duration increased to 15 seconds, maximum stacks down from 10 to 4, Damage reduction increased from 1% to 2%.

This should be in our base toolkit and in the talent tree and not fixing it by high end 8/8 Gear.

Summary. I am extremely disappointed with the feral changes. I was held back my thoughts when the first iteration of cc2 released. They told us need time and ingame experience to try out the talents before giving our concerns. There were already many things that was obviously bad and not needed ingame experience to point out, but after we tested and gave our detailed feedback, just a couple of them was considered (even those implemented in a horrible way)

There were so many good druid change suggestion on the discord and forum. How can be so stubborn for choosing a seriously bad takes? Is there somebody in the druid class council sabotaging us so we will never have a fully functional toolkit with working synergies? Is there somebody always saying about the good suggestions that "those are not vanilla gameplay effects so we wont even consider" and just letting through the horrible ones?

I always defended the devs after the first changes saying they have good intentions, just they can not implement them in a good way because they ran out of time. After seeing they doubling down on horrible talent changes my opinion changed. Whoever in control about the feral druid changes the persons don't have enough experience or they do not care about making the druid gameplay fully functional, they are ok if they are slightly ok. Please let people in the druid class council who are passionate and experienced with them.

## Post 113648 by Shambakriger — 2024-12-20T22:15:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=113648#p113648 | page 29 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Some thought on the recently announced balance changes for feral druids dec 20th:
I believe the devs original intention was to create an alternative to powershifting but that failed since the original Open Wounds build still benifitted massively from powershifting. The new change to Ancient Brutality, letting ticks from DoTs grant +energy, is a nice incentive to actually stay in form. It seems like the Vampirism was removed from the talent, it was mostly useful for soloing and AoE but weird to nerf an already not-great talent, especially the 9 sec icd is going to make this useless for bears basically ruining the point of making it benefit both forms
Open Wounds change is nice, having it simply tied to active DoTs is a lot simpler and more manageable. The wording atm implies that the damage bonus will be as large from having a 1cp Rip up, not sure if that's intentional but it would allow for easier weaving of Ferocious Bite into the rotation.
Nice to see the FB talents finally getting buffed a bit, my prediction regarding the bleeds playstyle is that it will be intended for bear MTs who don't want to powershift. They'll be able to skip Furor and instead pick up all Bear mitigation talents in the feral tree. I think it's important to keep the bleeds playstyle at no more than 90%DPS of Powershifting, or we risk homogenising the class entirely.
Atm there are no listed changes that would benefit powershifting cats, except for the change to FB scaling on Feral Aggression. We are still quite far below a lot of other classes on DPS, so I hope that we'll see some powershifting buffs if cat DPS continues being this subpar. I still believe that granting Ferals +5 weapon skill through the Natural Weapons talent would help a lot.
For Bears we mainly saw nerfs, Swipe was admittedly a bit too strong perhaps, but it did feel amazing going into Bear form wearing full Cat gear and just swiping away.
To keep this synergy of cats being able to aoe dps in bear form, I’d much rather that the threat was nerfed.
Frenzied Regen buff was needed as the original nerf was way too severe. Feral Adrenaline is no longer completely useless, but still seems like a very niche talent, if they intend to keep it i'd follow the same route as Ancient Brutality and add some Cat synergy to it as well.
The Savage Bite change is by far the worst and most head-scratching as it makes Bears already slow gameplay even slower, I'd much rather that the threat modifier was dialed back a bit to reach a similar result. Bear catch-up threat is still very bad and missing a 9sec CD Savage Bite is going to feel horrible.
All in all this round of changes feels like the devs trying to make up for the fact that their added cc2 talents saw so little use by the feral community. It’s all well and good that you want to flesh out and expand your own ideas some more, but you need to remember that this isn’t the reason most of us are playing the game. We want slightly more fine-tuned versions of vanilla classes, and cc1 feral was honestly so close to being perfect imo. Everything else is just icing on the cake, remember that only a small minority asked for cat bleeds and dodge tanking, most of us play feral because we like the way it plays in vanilla!!:))
The vision for feral druids feel all over the place atm, I think the dev team needs to sit down and try to reimagine these changes more aligned with the spirit of vanilla feral and then go from there.
Absolutely enormous and extremely impressive amount of work y’all have done but don’t get in over your heads and don’t fall for a sink cost fallacy, there’d be nothing wrong with reverting some of the changes.

But while the values needed tweaking, the rotation already felt fine. The cooldown increase is not warranted and extremely detrimental. Note that you decreased the cooldown of Concussion Blow for warriors so it's better for snap threat and has more utility mid-fight. The same reasoning applies to Savage Bite. This is our snap threat. Our catch-up going beyond our regular threat-curve. Parries/Dodges already feel pretty bad on a skill this expensive, but with +50% cooldown it's going to increase the influence of combat RNG in a bad way. Note that on page 1 of this thread you said that Savage Bite getting a buffed threat multiplier is the replacement for taking away MCP. Then the threat multiplier has been substantially decreased, now the cooldown is +50%. In effect Savage Bite will now be outputting much *lower* threat than pre-patch when we still had MCP. And note that bears didn't just use MCP for "more threat" but for "smoother threat" because more instances of attacks means a single attack getting parried or dodged is less detrimental. We are forced to tank with a 2.5 second swing timer and our main threat ability is queued on the next auto-attack. We can't just equip a fast weapon. Putting our ability to counter-act bad combat RNG on +50% cooldown is horrible.
>  Also do note that you "double-dipped" on threat balance. You nerfed bears substantially *and* buffed other classes to high heaven. This is not a sensible approach to achieve balance imo.

Two things regarding the recent changes on druid spec.

[Tranquility is an iconic spell from Warcraft 3. As the ultimate ability of the Keeper of the Grove hero unit, its World of Warcraft counterpart sadly does not live up to its legacy.
> More often than not it is not beneficial to use this spell when faced with a lot of incoming damage,

as the other healing spells offer a stronger rescue potential. To grant Tranquility an effect worthy of its origin and visual, it will now affect all raid members in close range of the druid, at a significantly decreased healing power and increased cooldown. Only Restoration druids will be able to unlock Tranquility‘s true potential.]

 1.
Regarding incoming damage when using tranquility and even the threat mechanic.  No druid in their right mind would cast tranquility without first casing Barkskin.  This spell was a great "Oh Shite" button for feral druids to regain mass aggroo if they lost it by chance, which they would do by quickly leaving bear form, casting barkskin, then tranquility "Oh throwing an innervate on the healer just for giggles, and then when the hate began to build on them, reshift into bear and pickup the action.  These changes particularly the threat elimination makes this no longer an effective Oshit sequence.  The uptick of 5mins to 30mins is a bit heavy handed.  Generally not liking this change at all. I would seriously ask reconsideration of these changes to tranquility.

 2.
If we are going off and doing things Vanilla+ style which is totally cool with me.  One thing druids should have always had was an OOC resurrection spell.  It was added in TBC I believe, and it's not a game breaking mechanic it just one of those things that always should have been from day 1.

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Dec 20, 2024 2:58 am**
> **Fury**. We liked the state 1.12 and CC1 Fury was in (disregarding its overly good scaling) but felt that a core part of its kit, Enrage, was heavily tied to receiving damage and thus would not shine in certain situations. 1.17.2 saw changes to Fury to address this by allowing Enrage to proc from Bloodthirst. However, while we've had plenty of indifferent feedback the negative feedback outweighed the positive especially in end-game. The main criticism that came from these changes is that Fury's DPS done per fight didn't reflect their skill as much as it used to, key moments of a fight without having an Enrage proc would feel worse. Because of this, we will be partially reverting the changes we've made and continue to monitor how Fury does in all types of content.
> ---
>  **Bloodthirst** has seen numerous changes:
> - No longer damages you, therefore can no longer proc Enrage.
>
> - Now increases your movement speed by 5% for 6 seconds. This effect stacks with other movement speed increases.
>
> - Base damage has been increased:
>     - Rank 1: 80 -> 100
>
>     - Rank 2: 100 -> 130
>
>     - Rank 3: 120 -> 160
>
>     - Rank 4: 150 -> 200
>
> - Attack Power scaling has been increased from 30% to 35%.

It always felt like a struggle to get the second buff stack at the start and I just had to hope that RNG was on my side with four combo points spent to hopefully trigger the effect.

I, however, think that Sub rogue could use a little more buffs. Mark for Death feels bad to use; the duration is so short that if you blink once it's over AND the cooldown feels too long for such a short effect. Maybe from balance standpoint the numbers are good and buffing it too much would make it too strong. But right now it just feels underwhelming. Especially when it misses. Maybe decrease the amount of increased bonus damage dealt to the target from 15% to 10% and double the duration, make it guaranteed to hit and/or reduce the cooldown from 3 to 2 minutes? Or make the debuff effect guaranteed to be applied even if you miss the melee attack and won't get the combo points.

I'd love to see some other smaller buffs here and there for Sub rogue. Not to make it deal as much damage as Combat and Assassination rogues but to feel more impactful and utilities more useful. Make Sub rogues feel good and useful enough that every raid would want to have at least one in their raids.

There’s some good or great ideas for cc2 but some implementations are messy or “out of nowhere” imo. And some of these patch changes don’t help, seem to be going in the wrong direction, or focusing on weird things. Something something ptr. Although I’m glad at least some of the original proposed changes were reversed because of feedback. :D

In general, REMOVING some key parts of vanilla wow (damage on holy shock being the obvious example, without any replacement to the style, to justify melee holy) does not fit what vanilla *PLUS* should be (and also killing fun playstyles). Same with removing shadow oil scaling all together, and whatever else.
The changes to bloodthirst seemed unnecessary and don’t make much sense to me, the other version was a nicer concept. Don't need to mention the upset paladins and druids. Rogue changes seem nice enough.

Rather than doing things to priest/discipline tree that people have suggested, the focus was put on bows and starshards for SOME reason? Problems like

 - smite lacking good spec specific support abilities
 - making chastise haste buff useful/last longer or even reworking the entire spell
 - searing light (bigger mana reduction being the main one)
 - mana issues
 - no smite tier sets other than 2.5 and lack of *at least some* general +damage/healing on a lot of those items
 - removing reduced/no threat on holy nova which was a key part of its spec identity (maybe scaling more with the threat reduction talent if someone wants to keep the threat for some reason I dono)
 - spiritual healing feeling *too* required to heal (doesn't help if smite is supposed to be an off-healer of sorts. as well as the mana issues)
 - resurgent shield being behind too many points or whatever, etc. It being buffed was kinda cool at least.

 - And for shadow, vamp embrace having a cast time
 - pain spike feeling pointless (low damage, maybe it could proc spirit tap if the mob dies within 5 seconds of using it or be redesigned in some way)
 - weird itemization for shadow on its tier gear (too much crit and hit).

I’m hoping the next balance patch fixes some of these issues and is an improvement over this one :D happy holidays

For Night Elf Priest, Maintaining the War III style is a great idea, but I feel the current skills are not effective during my leveling process.

 1.Regarding automatic shooting: Due to the priest lacking Aspect of the Cheetah and control skills, they will be approached by monsters after shooting the target 1-2 times, making it impossible to use.

 2.Regarding the Scorching Shot, why not make it fully follow the War III style, where each shot adds damage? If a priest chooses to use shooting as a damage skill, it means they are giving up other casting skills for damage. I suggest strictly adhering to the original design of War III skills.

 3.Regarding the StarSharps, I've noticed that it has been adjusted, but I can't think of any benefits it offers. The damage is mediocre, the range is small, the casting time is long, it's easily interrupted, and there's nothing appealing about it. Why wouldn't I just use Smite?

## Post 121947 by Amyloriley — 2025-03-07T10:10:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=121947#p121947 | page 31 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **987004590 wrote: Wed Mar 05, 2025 8:30 am**
> 3.Regarding the StarSharps, I've noticed that it has been adjusted, but I can't think of any benefits it offers. The damage is mediocre, the range is small, the casting time is long, it's easily interrupted, and there's nothing appealing about it. Why wouldn't I just use Smite?
>
>  I suggest increasing its cooldown to 3-5 minutes to make it a meaningful ultimate ability, Deals multi-target damage.

Starshards in Vanilla WoW has been positioned as a mana-efficient damage spell. And even with the changes in Turtle, that is still true.

 **Starshards** has a 6 second channel time that uses your mana at the start of the cast. So by the 5 second mark, you start regenerating mana from Spirit as if out of combat. Roughly, with 400 Spirit you gain 100 mana every 5 seconds.

Follow it up by using your Wand, and you continue regenerating mana without having to wait 5 seconds of not casting.

Alternatively, follow it up with **Holy Fire**, a 3.5 second cast, that's 9.5 seconds of mana regen. Better yet, wait 0.5 seconds between Starshards and Holy Fire to get two ticks of mana-every-five-seconds mana regeneration.

Before in Vanilla, Arcane Priest had a soloing rotation [Power Word: Shield] -> [Holy Fire] -> [Starshards] -> [Holy Fire] -> [Starshards] -> Wand. With the new 30 second cooldown on Starshards, this doesn't work anymore. But the idea of gaining back mana after casting Starshards is still there.

Starshards might not be the most damage dealing spell. Though, with the almost doubling of damage dealt it it could be close. The [**Mental Agility**] priest talent also affects Starshards in Turtle WoW, which wasn't the case in Vanilla.

Starshards is also a Discipline spell, so it can be used while in Shadowform. Even though Shadowform doesn't buff the effect.

Lastly, the way I used it back in the day, was to play a healer in a dungeon. When I got almost full mana and nobody needed healing, instead of Wanding, I channeled Starshards. It's more damage-dealing, while with the mana cost paid at the start of the cast rather than the end, I could regain some incidental mana after five seconds that might be great when someone suddenly needed healing.

## Post 124504 by Torta (Turtle WoW Team) [STAFF] — 2025-03-30T22:08:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=124504#p124504 | page 32 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

**UPDATES | Dated: April 1th 2025**

 **DRUID**

Druids will receive a fair share of number adjustments aimed at improving performance, as well as quality of life changes for the betterment of day to day play.

---
You can now shift between Druid forms without having to shift out of it first.

 *Developer Comment: To provide a more fluid way of changing between forms, we're enabling the function to change forms while already being shapeshifted. This was already more or less possible through macro play but we want to level the playing field this way.*

---
 **Ancient Brutality:** Now only requires two talent points. Energy granted increased from 2/3/4 Energy to 5/10 Energy. Rage generation after a successful dodge changed from 1/2/3 Rage to 2/4 Rage.

 *Developer Comment: We were quite restrained with the Energy regeneration offered by Ancient Brutality before. To aid non-shifting druids, we're upping its power substantially, allowing them to gain a more powerful way to regenerate Energy. Additionally, Bear druids will gain more Rage after dodging an attack, making the Dodge stat a tad more attractive.*

---
 **Claw:** Increased the weapon damage of Rank 5 by 5%.

 **Shred:** Increased the weapon damage of Rank 6 by 5%.

 **Rake:** Increased base damage and damage over time effect of Rank 4 by 5%.

 *Developer Comment: We’ve observed that the combo point generating Cat Form abilities could do with a small boost in power. This grants Cat druids a small edge in their single target niche.*

---
 **Predatory Strikes:** Now increases total Attack Power by 3/6/10% instead of granting Attack Power equal to 50/100/150% of your level.

 *Developer Comment: This talent was quite static in its functionality, capped at Level 60 with a bonus of 90 Attack Power. Changing it to a total increase of Attack Power enables druids to scale even further from several Attack Power sources, as well as main stats.*

---
 **Mark and Gift of the Wild:** Now castable in Moonkin Form.

 *Developer Comment: To put Moonkin Form in line with its other humanoid shapeshift form, the Tree of Life form, we’re permitting Moonkin druids to buff their fellow compatriots without leaving their feathery costume.*

---
 **Balance Tier 3 (6 Set Bonus):** Can no longer be resisted.

 *Developer Comment: This effect was falsely able to be resisted.*

---
 **Owlkin Frenzy:** Pushback reduction is now always 30% instead of scaling with talent tiers. Cooldown now scales with talent tiers, now only triggering once every 30/25/20 seconds instead of being 25 seconds flat.

 *Developer Comment: Following our observation, we’ve noticed players were taking this talent with simply one point in investment, which didn’t really fit the intention we had with this talent. To remedy this, we’re changing it to allow for the maximum pushback reduction up front, while making spending more talent points into it more worthwhile.*

---
 **Hurricane:** Cooldown reduced from 30 seconds to 10 seconds.

 *Developer Comment: We’re aiming to have Hurricane be a more frequent tool for area damage with this change.*

---
 **Nature's Focus:** Removed Wrath from the description of the talent as it never actually affected it.

 *Developer Comment: As Wrath is now part of Guidance of the Dream, we’re removing this redundant part of the tooltip that slipped past us.*

---
 **Feral Combat Tier 2.5 (3 Set):** Now also reduces the Energy cost of Shred by 3.

 *Developer Comment: Since our approach to Feral Cat has been shifted from its first iteration, we’re including Shred into the energy reduction of this set bonus to grant it more flexibility in its utility.*

---
 **Eclipse:** Arcane and Nature damage bonus increased from 25% to 30%.

 *Developer Comment: It came to our attention that in some cases ignoring the capstone talent of the Balance Tree yielded equal results in performance, which is something we were not anticipating. To strengthen our design vision, we’re adding a small buff to Eclipse to make using it more rewarding.*

 **MAGE**

Mage is currently in quite a good state, so these changes will primarily aim to improve Quality of Life and solve a few minor issues mages have to deal with such as being reliant on a set bonus to properly utilize Arcane Power, mana issues and smoothing out Hot Streak-Pyroblast usage with Fire Mage.

 **Arcane Rupture:** Base damage reduced for lower ranks, being reduced by 10% for ranks 1-4 and by 5% for rank 5. Rank 6 is unchanged.

---
 **Pyroblast:** Reduced global cooldown from 1.5 seconds to 1 second.

 *Developer Comment: This was done to prevent Pyroblast from clipping your global cooldown when its casted with maximum stacks of Hot Streak, removing any friction when using it.*

---
 **Flash Freeze:** No longer activates on temporary immunities such as Free Action Potion or Blessing of Freedom.

 *Developer Comment: This change is primarily aimed at Player versus Player interactions, removing the possibility of being punished for using immunities to slow and root effects when fighting against a Frost Mage.*

---
 **Dampen Magic:** Spell damage taken reduction increased from 2% to 3%, healing taken reduction increased from 1% to 2%.

 **Amplify Magic:** Healing taken bonus increased from 2% to 3%, spell damage taken bonus increased from 1% to 2%.

 *Developer Comment: The original values for these effects after our rework ended up way too weak for practical usage even with their Arcane Attunement buffed versions, so we're giving them a boost to fit better into their roles.*

---
 **Arcane Power:** Haste granted reduced from 35% to 30%, mana drained reduced from 2% to 1%, mana regeneration penalty reduced from 75% to 50%.

 **Arcane Mage Tier 3 (6 Set):** No longer removes the mana regeneration penalty.

 *Developer Comment: Arcane Power ended up being too taxing to use after our initial rework, constantly posing the risk of blowing up without a specific set bonus which also ended up feeling mandatory to use as Arcane Power is a major part of an Arcane Mage power. For this reason we've relaxed the mana drain and penalty on the base ability and removed the mana renegeration reduction effect from the set bonus, which should help make gear loadouts less reliant on this effect especially with the release of Tier 3.5.*

---
 **Fireball:** Reduced the mana costs of the following ranks:
Rank 3 (Level 12): 65 -> 60
Rank 4 (Level 18): 95 -> 85
Rank 5 (Level 24): 140 -> 120
Rank 6 (Level 30): 185 -> 160
Rank 7 (Level 36): 220 -> 190
Rank 8 (Level 42): 260 -> 220
Rank 9 (Level 48): 305 -> 245
Rank 10 (Level 54): 350 -> 265
Rank 11 (Level 60): 395 -> 275
Rank 12 (Level 60/Book): 410 -> 295

 **Flamestrike:** Reduced the mana costs of the following ranks:
Rank 2 (Level 24): 330 -> 250
Rank 3 (Level 32): 490 -> 360
Rank 4 (Level 40): 650 -> 470
Rank 5 (Level 48): 815 -> 580
Rank 6 (Level 56): 990 -> 680

 *Developer Comment: Fire Mages quite struggle with mana even with the help of talents such as Master of Elements and tend to feel reliant on them, for this reason we're reducing the mana cost of the two aforementioned spells.*

---
 **HUNTER**

These batch of changes are primarily aimed at Survival, opening different ways of gearing with support for dual wielding, reducing the mana strain fire traps have on their rotation and slightly reducing their leveling proficiency.

 **Mongoose Bite:** Reduced flat damage values by around 40%:
Rank 1 (Level 16): 25 -> 15.
Rank 2 (Level 30): 45 to 25.
Rank 3 (Level 44): 75 to 45.
Rank 4 (Level 58): 115 to 70.

 *Developer Comment: These reductions are primarily aimed at leveling to reduce the speed at which Survival Hunters kill at that stage and won't affect endgame much as its targeted towards the non-scaling part of the ability.*

---
 **Untamed Trapper:** Now also reduces the mana cost of your Fire traps by 20%.

 *Developer Comment: While this capstone talent made fire traps an integral part of the Survival Hunter rotation it didn't accomodate for this as the fire trap mana costs ended up being too high when used on cooldown, this change should help alleviate this issue.*

---
 **Savage Strikes:** Now also increases the damage of your offhand weapon by 13/25%.

 *Developer Comment: Addition of a boost to your offhand weapon damage aims to make dual-wield a just as viable alternative to two-handed Survival Hunters.*

 **PALADIN**

Paladins continue to perform well across all three specializations in both raid and dungeon environments. This update focuses on improving underperforming talents and abilities while introducing minor quality-of-life improvements and parity adjustments. Certain aspects of the Paladin toolkit remain under evaluation, with additional changes planned for future updates.

---
 **Hammer of Wrath:** No longer resets your swing timer.

 *Developer Comment: Hammer of Wrath has been significantly underutilized in PvE due to its current mechanics. This adjustment enhances the execute phase, making the ability more viable and rewarding to use.*

---
 **Blessing of Salvation:** Threat reduction reduced from 30% to 25%.

 *Developer Comment: Current tank threat generation significantly outpaces DPS output. Reducing the effectiveness of Blessing of Salvation restores the importance of active threat management during combat.*

---
 **Vindication:** Damage reduction increased from 1/2/3% to 3/6/9%. The tooltip has been updated to clarify that boss enemies are unaffected.

 *Developer Comment: Vindication previously offered insufficient value for talent investment. This buff makes it a more appealing choice, particularly for solo play and PvP engagements.*

---
 **Seal of Righteousness:** Spell power scaling increased to 0.092 * Weapon Speed for One-Handed Weapons and 0.128 * Weapon Speed for Two-Handed Weapons.

 *Developer Comment: Hybrid builds utilizing Seal of Righteousness have consistently underperformed compared to Seal of Command. This change aims to bridge the gap and provide a more competitive alternative.*

---
 **Judgement of Righteousness:** Now properly benefits from melee critical strike and hit chance instead of spell critical strike and hit chance.

 *Developer Comment: The previous interaction caused inconsistency with Judgement of Command, leading to confusion. This update unifies the mechanics of these Judgements for improved reliability and ease of play.*

---
 **Eye for an Eye** has swapped positions with **Two-Handed Weapon Specialization** in the talent tree.

 *Developer Comment: The Retribution talent tree contained awkward pathing, particularly in the fourth row. Moving Two-Handed Weapon Specialization down improves accessibility to key talents and enhances the leveling experience.*

---
 **Vengeance:** No longer applies its threat reduction if Righteous Fury is active.

 *Developer Comment: Retribution Paladins faced significant drawbacks when off-tanking due to the innate threat reduction of Vengeance. This change ensures that no talent actively hinders a Paladin’s ability to perform their role, improving off-tanking viability and creating new build opportunities within the Protection tree.*

---
 **Reckoning:** Proc chance increased from 5/10/15/20/25% to 10/20/30/40/50%. The tooltip has been clarified.

 *Developer Comment: Reckoning has struggled to provide sufficient value for the talent points invested. This improvement makes it a more viable and impactful option for Protection Paladins.*

---
 **Holy Light:** Reduced spellpower coefficient from 71.4% to 20% for Rank 1.

 **PRIEST**

These changes primarily aim to improve Discipline Priest's personal damage and support capabilities and to improve Shadow Priest's Player versus Player environment power as the changes brought with the initial class changes release ended up being harsher than we've intended it to be.

 **Smite:** Spellpower scaling increased by about 5% for all ranks.

 *Developer Comment: Discipline is slightly underperforming compared to Shadow, so we're slightly boosting its damage to match the performance of its fellow supporty-damage specialization.*

---
 **Chastise:** Effect duration increased from 6 seconds (Non-critical) and 9 seconds (Critical) to 8 seconds (Non-critical) and 12 seconds (Critical), attack and casting speed boost increased from 10/13/15% to 13/17/20%, cooldown increased from 30 seconds to 40 seconds.

 *Developer Comment: Chastise ended up struggling to be worth its global cooldown.*

---
 **Pain Spike:** Spellpower scaling increased from 25% to 43%.

 *Developer Comment: The earlier scaling reduction on Pain Spike ended up being more harsh than we've intended with it compounding with the cooldown increase, so we're increasing its spellpower scaling back up.*

---
Swapped the talent locations of **Spell Warding** and **Blessed Concentration**.

 *Developer Comment: Shadow Priests struggled quite a bit with build diversity since we've moved Blessed Concentration to the Holy talent tree. We've moved its location to make the latter talent more accessible and enable a wider variety builds in the Player versus Player environment.*

---
 **Enlighten:** Chance to trigger from heals reduced from 15% to 10%.

 *Developer Comment: While Enlighten is a powerful option for Discipline Priests and their support capabilities, its usage by Holy Priests ended up heavily outweighing the usage of Holy Champion, so we're dialing back its proc chance to give the Holy Champion some time in the spotlight.*

 **SHAMAN**

Shaman's popularity as a class keeps growing as it attracts more players who are interested in the damage-dealer aspects of the class and players interested in its benefits as a healer. These small changes reflect our contentedness with the current evolution of the entire class' design over the past months as we believe this mini-patch did not warrant any substantial changes to the design of the class. Though we are aware of areas on which to improve, understand that homogenizing the class with design aspects and roles covered by other classes and their relative specializations is absolutely not in our objectives. We are continuously looking at properly-shared player feedback and have taken extensive note of them, with the above comment in mind we are confident expectations will be met in an elegant manner.

 **Elemental Focus:** Mana cost reduction now also affects Stormstrike and Lightning Strike.

 **Lightning Strike:** Cooldown reduced from 10 seconds to 9 seconds. The nature part of the ability now gains damage equal to 5% of your spellpower.

 *Developer Comment: With these changes, we hope to address some of Enhancement's mana issues and its overbearing reliance on classes capable of providing boosts to mana regeneration, as their absence often signifies a drastic drop in gameplay quality and flow over longer encounters, while remaining a critical point of levelling as the spec. The reduction to Lightning Strike's cooldown, though minor, should directly increase its role as both a more efficient and engaging contributor to Enhancement's damage dealer and mana regeneration role.*

---
 **Bloodlust:** Attack and casting speed granted to party members on critical strike increased from 5% to 8% and its duration is increased from 5 seconds to 6 seconds, attack and casting speed granted to the caster increased from 15% to 20%. The attack and casting speed granted to party members on critical strike is no longer applied to the caster itself.

 *Developer Comment: After closer analysis from the team, we've come to the conclusion that the buff to the party members feels minor enough to warrant a small increment. We're generally satisfied with Enhancement's solo performance and would like to not magnify its group support performance further in order to strike a balance between the group bonuses brought forth by the other specializations.*

---
 **Fire Nova Totem and Grounding Totem:** Now trigger the global cooldown.

 *Developer Comment:These totems are de facto powerful abilities which by design already warrant a cooldown. Given their impact on normal gameplay, we've decided to have them trigger the global cooldown to spur a more thought-out use from the playerbase, which we're sure will quickly adapt and hone their skill accordingly. We are aware of how enjoyable it is to have full creative agency when it comes to setting totems and are confident this change will not restrain it.*

---
 **Enhancement Tier 3 (6 Set Bonus):** Duration increased from 5 seconds to 10 seconds.

 **WARLOCK**

Warlock is getting further adjustments and design corrections across its many specializations. These range from carefully distributing power to the underperforming abilities to reasonable containment of heavy outliers. Affliction Warlock should now be able to better keep up with other specializations, namely on trash encounters. On the other hand, deep Demonology talents funneled too much power into the Warlock, so the focus is being shifted more towards the demons.[/o]

 **Resilient Shadows:** Increased dispel resistance from 3/6/9% to 5/10/15%.

---
 **Malediction:** Now also causes your Curse of Recklessness, Curse of Elements and Curse of Shadows to apply your highest rank of Curse of Agony, if there isn't one.

 *Developer Comment: To combat lengthy setup time during Dungeon trash encounters, which is Affliction Warlock's main pain point, we're making this talent more aggressive.*

---
 **Siphon Life:** Total spell power scaling has been increased from 50% to 100%.

---
 **Dark Harvest:** Now increases haste by 30% instead of 20% and resets its cooldown if its target dies during its channel.

---
 **Soul Funnel:** Now causes the Warlock to pay 30% of transferred health or mana.

 **Demonic Sacrifice:** Now removed when you enslave a demon.

 *Developer Comment: The goal behind this change is to encourage more strategic choices for deep Demonology, when it comes to controlling demons, instead of having a simple numbers increase for the "cooldown spec". Controlling a demon goes against the Demonic Sacrifice's precursor talent, Soul Entrapment, too. We'll keep looking into finding a way to make this talent unique and rewarding.*

---
 **Master Demonologist (Infernal):** Healing reduction reduced from 75% to 50%.

 **Master Demonologist (Felguard):** Damage increase reduced from 20% to 10%.

---
Imp's **Firebolt** ability has now the following scaling with spell power:
Rank 1: 10%
Rank 2: 15%
Rank 3: 20%
Rank 4. 25%
Rank 5. 30%
Rank 6: 35%
Rank 7. 40%

 *Developer Comment: We will be closely monitoring Imp's power level and be ready to provide future adjustments.*

---
 **Legion Strike (Felguard):** Now deals 50% weapon damage with a 4 sec cooldown instead of 130% weapon damage with a 6 sec cooldown. Felguard can now crit with all attacks.

 *Developer Comment: While the damage got scaled down more than the cooldown, keep in mind that Felguard will get a notable power increase through critical strikes.*

---
Related Item Change:
 **The Black Book** trinket buff is now removed if the trinket is unequipped.

 **ROGUE**

These changes are primarily aimed at the Assassination specialization, reworking Deadly Throw to be a properly viable abilty with its own identity and reworking Throwing Weapon Specializationn alongside it, improving poison related talents and improving Subtlety Rogue's personal damage output via a boost to Hemorrhage damage.

 **Hemorrhage:** Weapon damage increased from 100% to 110%.

---
 **Deadly Throw:** Reworked:
 - No longer spends combo points.
 - Energy cost increased from 35 to 40.
 - Now deals 100% weapon damage.
 - Has a shared cooldown with Kick and has the same cooldown as Kick.
 - Now interrupts the target for 3 seconds baseline.

 **Throwing Weapon Specialization:** Now has a 50/100% chance to apply your off-hand weapon poison instead of an increasing proc chance for a 3 second interrupt per combo point spent. Range increase remains the same.

 *Developer Comment: Deadly Throw has been the underdog of finisher abilities for a long time, so we're giving it a complete makeover, making it an alternative to Kick for cases you can't reach a caster in time with a slightly shorter interrupt duration. Additionally, Throwing Specialization was reworked to interact with your poisons, as most talents in the Assassination tree do, allowing you to apply poisons from range which should provide a lot of utility.*

---
 **Vile Poisons:** Damage increase bonus increased from 7/14/20% to 10/20/30%.

 **Envenom:** Effectiveness and application chance bonus increased from 25% to 30%.

 *Developer Comment: Assassination has been underperforming compared to other specializations, so we're giving a few of its talents a boost to reduce the gap.*

 **WARRIOR**

All Warrior specializations are currently in a strong position, with each seeing consistent play across all forms of content. We are pleased with the overall performance of Warriors but will closely monitor their impact in the Tower of Karazhan. Given Warriors’ well-documented scaling potential, the new raid loot may further enhance their power.

 **Concussion Blow:** Stun duration increased from 2 seconds to 3 seconds.

 *Developer Comment: The stun duration reduction that came with the cooldown reduction for Concussive Blow ended up making it too short to properly utilize, so we're slightly increasing it so it can be an useful tool for both threat generation and crowd control.*

---
 **Improved Pummel:** Now applies a normal 50% movement speed reduction instead of a Daze effect and its application chance is increased from 25/50% to 50/100%.

 *Developer Comment: While we've liked the interaction of the slow applied by Improved Pummel being more sticky against players, it proved to be problematic so we're changing it to a normal slow and guaranteeing its application when fully talented to make up for this change.*
