## Post 141255 by Akos1896 (Grandmaster of Forum PvP) — 2025-07-25T09:50:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=141255#p141255 | page 36 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

When do these changes get applied?
Will react to shaman, I didn't really play anything else for months, I am not qualified to give opinion elsewhere.
Will focus on PVE aspect because PVP is not my thing.

Totem range increase:
Has some minimal use for enhancement, specially if team is moving a lot, but they are by design put together with melee.
Resto had it always.
Easily grabbable by ele.
It's a good qol improvement but also a power push. Question is if this further push was justified.

Molten blast:
Definitely welcome. Ele had problems with high nat rez enemies. Sure, mages have similar problems, f.ex. fire mages in MC. But the difference is that mages have 3 caster builds, shaman has 1. For a player it is easier to switch to another caster with a different element than giving up his preferred playstyle (caster) and going melee or heal. As long as molten blast remains by design kinda mediocre, I think it is a totally justified spell to fall back on.

Rockbiter: Interesting. I welcome tank buffs but if I had to guess a weakness for shaman tanks, it was rather aoe threat after a gear level, lack of defensives and subpar mana recharge for example compared to a prot pala. I think 5% is fine but keep in mind the T2,5 set bonus which further enhances rockbiter. Just make sure you don't push us too far.

Grounding Totem: Fair. For a class which can interrupt you and lock you out from a school of magic every 5/6 sec, can purge you and also has this totem, it is fair to increase this CD. It is too much meddling with other mana users.

Chain heal nerf: Welcome one. To explain why this was mindlessly OP before. Before CC2 you had to get T2,5 for fast chain heals. In exchange you got shít stats. You were a chain heal 'machine gunner' but went oom rather quick. Clever downgrades or using other heals were required.
After CC2 chain heal was even faster by default(!), you could still gear up with actually good stats and you also got good mana regen with the shield-related talents. Made resto extremely effective at spamming an extremely effective heal very fast.

 **Ele**

Convection/Concussion: Logical since you added new spells.

Reverberation: I have no idea why this buff happened. Helps my shaman tank but might be an unnecessary push. For a build wanting to spam shocks (rather enh than ele), this was already a strong talent.

Improved Fire Totems: Sure, searing totem was kinda bad, this change is okay.

Improved Molten Blast: Same as earlier. As long as Molten Blast remains a serviceable but not strong backup spell, it's okay. But shouldn't be more.

Call of Flame: Perfect. Earth Shock and Frost Shock should never be castable from 30 yards but Flame Shock is less toxic at PVP and at PVE allows ele to use shocks more often.

Electrify: Honestly, this version is OP. You're telling me we get 10% baseline damage buff and a 100% crit damage buff for 2 tp? Honestly, this is too strong as it is.

Elemental Mastery: I like the direction, helps with mana more and gives a maintained damage window with less initial burst (unless you crit).

Earthquake: Not sure if ele needed an aoe. It was a nice build-limitation. Having spell cleave and pseudo-aoe (magma, fire nova) was enough. If anything, this seems rather an enhancement capstone talent. If you'd really want to add another new spell, I'd advice a non-aoe frost one so you can fully say that ele is using frost, fire and nature besides just the shocks and weapon imbues.

 **Enh**

Totemic Alignment: I welcome this but with a caution. Makes aoe threat better but scaling will still be off. Shaman tanks might have super OP aoe threat initially which falls off anyway by the time you wanna raid tank. And again: adding some threat buff is okay. But you gotta consider how much you wanna give. Rockbiter was already buffed. Now this. And each are further buffed by the T2,5 set bonus. If you really go this way, you should change that set bonus to extra defense at this point.

Calming winds: Nice, cool for offtanking.

Spirit armor: Way too OP. You already gave us a super strong talent under spirit armor. Now you add extra threat for it. I'm against this. Just add together all the threat buffs you're distributing left and right. I want a good shaman tank build which is not a second-class citizen amongst tanks. But I don't want an unfair OP tank fiesta.

Enhancing totems: It's okay. 99% of the time grace of air won't be used anyway since team wants WF and there is no totem twisting here. Question is if a 20< strength party buff worths 2 TP for you.

SS: I honestly think this is overkill. Vanilla had SS at 20 sec CD. Now it is 8 sec, stronger and enh has other melee attack, too. I mean it further helps enh shaman but their problem was not damage in my opinion. They mostly struggle with random threat spikes (any hit is a random 20% for 2 extra hits, each of which can crit) and some mana (water shield is kinda underwhelming). This buff might be unnecessary.

Element's grace: Big push again. +10% at every LS, SS and shock for a bunch of damage and to activate clearcasting, elemental devastation and flurry. Those things will be way too consistent.

 **Resto**

Improved healing wave: It's clever. This heal is barely used at raids, this can give some niche.

Healing Way: Including Lesser Healing Wave is clever but Chain Heal should have been removed. Give the healer a system where each heal has its advantages and limitations. Otherwise you might end up with a cool system totally ignored because resto will just go chain heal brr, even with the reduced coefficient.

Spirit Link: I like this. Bigger CD is justified. In exchange added range and instant cast makes it much less awkward.

__

Overall I like some of these but imo you push us a bit too much.

## Post 141260 by Ellifta (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2025-07-25T10:43:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=141260#p141260 | page 36 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Speaking of warrior tank changes, I'd like to offer a few basic QoL suggestions seeing the spec was barely changed even though I believe it requires some buffs. At high gear levels such as T2.5 to T3.5, warrior tank is behind bear and paladin tank by a decent amount in terms of threat generation. The concussion blow change is a very nice one, effectively a 25 rage increase compared to now whenever it is used. However, the scaling on it is quite poor still, perhaps it could use a higher rank, or maybe more base threat, or maybe higher AP coefficient?

 1- Shield Block and Improved Shield Slam overriding each other
As it is now, if you use shield block when you have shield slam up, it removes the existing buff and replaces it with shield block and vice versa. Why not just make shield slam add one more stack of shield block to make the rotation much more manageable? Currently you need to be looking at every hit you take in Dstance to see if your 1 charge of shield slam is spent and then use shield block to not overlap buffs. It is unnecessarily tedious compared to paladin crit and crush immunity, which is a flat 5 shield blocks lasting for 10 seconds. Why not make warrior have 2 shield blocks lasting 5 seconds as before CC2? Two different shield block abilities each giving 1 shield block every 5 seconds, but also cancelling each other out is kind of unpleasant to play around.

 2- Defensive Tactics number tweaks
At the highest levels of play, I think warrior tank has fallen behind other tanks in terms of threat generation. A bear tank will have more effective HP and better threat generation, a paladin can generate more threat as well and these are some sizable buffs to shaman tanks -when threat generation wasn't their issue to begin with, it was their itemization and survivability-. Full BiS or close to full BiS bear and paladin tanks outthreat warrior to a noticeable extent already and this patch bear was buffed and paladin was untouched. I believe a small number tweak to Defensive Tactics would solve this, by upping the threat increase the talent gives from 180% to 210%. Battle stance tanking already means 10% more damage taken compared to defensive stance and not being crit or crush immune, so at the very least the payoff should mean really competitive and superior threat generation for warrior tank.

 3- Slight scaling to revenge
Currently revenge and reprisal are excellent for dungeon tanking, but due to not having ANY scaling at all on them, the threat generation from them falls behind at higher item levels. The only way to increase revenge damage is the 2 piece T3 bonus which is frankly not enough. A bit of AP scaling to its damage could make it scale better with gear and make it not fall off at top end (T3-T3.5).

*Last edited by Ellifta on Fri Jul 25, 2025 11:08 am, edited 1 time in total.*

> **Ellifta wrote: Fri Jul 25, 2025 10:43 am**
> Speaking of warrior tank changes, I'd like to offer a few basic QoL suggestions seeing the spec was barely changed even though I believe it requires some buffs. At high gear levels such as T2.5 to T3.5, warrior tank is behind bear and paladin tank by a decent amount in terms of threat generation. The concussion blow change is a very nice one, effectively a 25 rage increase compared to now whenever it is used. However, the scaling on it is quite poor still, perhaps it could use a higher rank, or maybe more base threat, or maybe higher AP coefficient?
>
>  1- Shield Block and Improved Shield Slam overriding each other
>  As it is now, if you use shield block when you have shield slam up, it removes the existing buff and replaces it with shield block and vice versa. Why not just make shield slam add one more stack of shield block to make the rotation much more manageable? Currently you need to be looking at every hit you take in Dstance to see if your 1 charge of shield slam is spent and then use shield block to not overlap buffs. It is unnecessarily tedious compared to paladin crit and crush immunity, which is a flat 5 shield blocks lasting for 10 seconds. Why not make warrior have 2 shield blocks lasting 5 seconds as before CC2? Two different shield block abilities each giving 1 shield block every 5 seconds, but also cancelling each other out is kind of unpleasant to play around.
>
>  2- Defensive Tactics number tweaks
>  At the highest levels of play, I think warrior tank has fallen behind other tanks in terms of threat generation. A bear tank will have more effective HP and better threat generation, a paladin can generate more threat as well and these are some sizable buffs to shaman tanks -when threat generation wasn't their issue to begin with, it was their itemization and survivability-. Full BiS or close to full BiS bear and paladin tanks outthreat warrior to a noticeable extent already and this patch bear was buffed and paladin was untouched. I believe a small number tweak to Defensive Tactics would solve this, by upping the threat increase the talent gives from 180% to 210%. Battle stance tanking already means 10% more damage taken compared to defensive stance and not being crit or crush immune, so at the very least the payoff should mean really competitive and superior threat generation for warrior tank.
>
>  3- Slight scaling to revenge
>  Currently revenge and reprisal are excellent for dungeon tanking, but due to not having ANY scaling at all on them, the threat generation from them falls behind at higher item levels. The only way to increase revenge damage is the 2 piece T3 bonus which is frankly not enough. A bit of AP scaling to its damage could make it scale better with gear and make it not fall off at top end (T3-T3.5).

Yeah I agree for the most part.

 1. Yeah with this issue I had to create a macro to prevent me from using shield block and removing the Shield slam block. I love this suggestion, just add charges of shield block.

 2. Defensive Tactics - While this talent has its uses I think it should be removed. I think most heavy prot warriors are going to be a MT in a raid/group. And forever in wow we as warriors are taught defensive stance is for tanking and the other are for DPS. Now this talent just changes all of that and makes defensive stance less used overall. We need more threat yes but not to remove our most useful stance. I mean there isn't a talent in the shadow priest tree that increases all shadow damage outside of shadow form by 180% as a 25 talent. We need to replace Defensive Tactics and either add some hit on key skills with increased threat. Or Make a talent focus on using defense gear worth it, each time you parry/dodge/block an attack it gives you a stacking buff that increases your threat and rage generation to the mob attacking you. Most heavy prot tanks want to be a TANK don't punish us for wanting to use the gear we want or stance we prefer.

 3. Yes yes yes, revenge should be scale with either AP like you suggest or armor. Or make it skill based some, it becomes a buff that can stack up to 10 times. Use at 1 stack does normal threat, save it up and do 10 times the threat, but can fall off if you dont parry/dodge/block in those 5 secs.

## Post 141305 by ForumGentleman (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2025-07-25T12:29:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=141305#p141305 | page 36 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Very solid patch.

My feedback, **mostly on PVP:**

 **Druid:**
Interesting changes. Carnage healing seems pretty strong. Let's see if it brings feral from top tier to broken

 **Mage:**
Small arcane rupture dmg nerf. Probably needed. Arcane rupture could use a small dmg nerf also imo.

 **Hunter:**
Thank you so much for the new pet abilities and Pet Command: Take Position. Awesome.
 - Survival - New ability Lacerate seems nice. Survival will still be in a weird spot for PVP - big damage but still trash tier mobility and control.
 - beastmaster: Removing OG Bestial Wrath? Quite a change. You know what: what you replace it with is fair and interesting. The CC removal on pet is crucial so Kill Command including that is great. CANT WAIT to try it.

 **Paladin:**
Subtle changes except for Holy Shock. Happy with the changes.
Contrary to many ppl's opinion; I think pala is in a great spot overall in PVP.

 **Priest:**
Small changes. Class feels good already anyways. Yes; smite is dangerous in PVP but also has many counters.

 **Shaman**
Overall, LOVING those changes. **Molten Blast** really enriches gameplay imo
Grounding totem nerf is spot on.

 - Restoration: good changes; last talent being more usable is nice
 - Enh: Solid changes BUT I still think Ancestral Guardian is a bit too easy to get and OP in PVP. I would nerf the armor and dogde or make the talent less accessible.
 - Elemental: Finally a complete rework that makes sense. In LOVE with **Earthquake** - At last; spell that is not just pure damage for elemental. So happy with that

 **Rogue**
Decent changes. The 8% speed bonus is actually spot on for PVP. Rogue was lacking that.
Blind not being a poison is controversial, but probably needed.

 **Warlock:**
Thanks for bringing back Spellstone. New version seems more funcional.
 - Affliction: **THANK YOU**  for nerfing curse of exhaustion for other specs while preserving it for Affliction. Been asking for that for months. Spot on.
 - Demonology: THANK YOU for making Power Overwhelming usable in PVP. Great change.
 - Destruction: Like Ele shamans, **I still believe it needs one more PVP cc**. ability. Similar to Elemental new eathquake ability; I would give it something like a redesigned shadowfury. (even if it means nerfing dmg to compensate)

 **Warrior:**
Buff some charges/speed talents. Cant say no to that.

> Speaking of warrior tank changes, I'd like to offer a few basic QoL suggestions seeing the spec was barely changed even though I believe it requires some buffs. At high gear levels such as T2.5 to T3.5, warrior tank is behind bear and paladin tank by a decent amount in terms of threat generation. The concussion blow change is a very nice one, effectively a 25 rage increase compared to now whenever it is used. >
>  1- Shield Block and Improved Shield Slam overriding each other
>  As it is now, if you use shield block when you have shield slam up, it removes the existing buff and replaces it with shield block and vice versa. Why not just make shield slam add one more stack of shield block to make the rotation much more manageable? Currently you need to be looking at every hit you take in Dstance to see if your 1 charge of shield slam is spent and then use shield block to not overlap buffs. It is unnecessarily tedious compared to paladin crit and crush immunity, which is a flat 5 shield blocks lasting for 10 seconds. Why not make warrior have 2 shield blocks lasting 5 seconds as before CC2? Two different shield block abilities each giving 1 shield block every 5 seconds, but also cancelling each other out is kind of unpleasant to play around.
>
>  2- Defensive Tactics number tweaks
>  At the highest levels of play, I think warrior tank has fallen behind other tanks in terms of threat generation. A bear tank will have more effective HP and better threat generation, a paladin can generate more threat as well and these are some sizable buffs to shaman tanks -when threat generation wasn't their issue to begin with, it was their itemization and survivability-. Full BiS or close to full BiS bear and paladin tanks outthreat warrior to a noticeable extent already and this patch bear was buffed and paladin was untouched. I believe a small number tweak to Defensive Tactics would solve this, by upping the threat increase the talent gives from 180% to 210%. Battle stance tanking already means 10% more damage taken compared to defensive stance and not being crit or crush immune, so at the very least the payoff should mean really competitive and superior threat generation for warrior tank.
>
>  3- Slight scaling to revenge
>  Currently revenge and reprisal are excellent for dungeon tanking, but due to not having ANY scaling at all on them, the threat generation from them falls behind at higher item levels. The only way to increase revenge damage is the 2 piece T3 bonus which is frankly not enough. A bit of AP scaling to its damage could make it scale better with gear and make it not fall off at top end (T3-T3.5).

What we need are actual threat multipliers on our abilities. All the threat modifiers we have, be it Revenge, Shield slam, Heroic strike, etc, are ALL flat extra threat, and these numbers are the old vanilla numbers that were meant to tank for the vanilla dps classes, not the absurdly overtuned dps we have on turtle. Meaning our threat is mostly unchanged from what it was on vanilla whereas everyone else got massively buffed.

Druid's Maul is the only tank ability with a threat multiplier on it, with no cooldown, so they scale exponentially with gear and they have been dominating twow's tanking for a long time now. And now they're getting buffed even more with the removal of armor cap, which by the way, is a druid buff that does not say its name. *"Some classes and specializations are running into the issue of getting hard-capped by armor"* Some classes you say? No no, it's just druids. No other class can reach this amount of armor, and you know this, devs.

Warriors only have the meek flat bonus threat from vanilla and we have cooldowns.
AP scaling on revenge will not save warrior, your shield slam will still get dodged/parried and your threat will be non-existent.
Now seeing them massively buff shaman tank's threat all across the board (when this wasn't even shaman tank's issue to begin with), I think we can confidently say warriors are now the worst tanking class on twow.

What I think tank warr needs :

 - TBC's Tactical Mastery talent from protection tree (threat multiplier on Bloodthirst/Mortal strike when used in def stance) + revert the AP scaling nerf to bloodthirst. Fury prot's snap threat is outright pathetic currently. Using Deathwish cuts our armor and resistance by 20% just to pull barely more threat than a paladin all while being exposed to crits and crushing blows.
 - Allow Enrage to proc from crushing blows, for only half its bonus.
 - Just scrap Concussion Blow altogether honestly, it just sucks. Deep prot needs some proper dodge/parry fail-safe and crit chance bonus to Shield slam, it doesn't make sense to me how deep prot is more gear dependant than fury prot. Put current concussion blow somewhere else in the tree for those who like it, and instead make the last talent a buff like this : "Your next Shield Slam has 30 % bonus chance to critically hit and cannot be dodged, blocked or parried (20sec cooldown)"
 - Buff Defiance talent
 - Change Revenge's threat modifier, from a flat extra to a **multiplier**, give it some AP scaling
 - Change Shield Slam's threat modifier, from a flat extra to a **multiplier**

Lastly :
 **STOP BALANCING WARRIOR AROUND THUNDERFURY**. Or rework bindings into splinters like Atiesh, seriously. Some of us have never seen a binding in 15 months of Molten core. Screw us, I guess ?

It's simply baffling to me that CC2 nerfed fury prot so harshly while you made something so much more broken with the current bear druid.

## Post 141379 by Grinface — 2025-07-25T15:19:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=141379#p141379 | page 37 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

As someone who rolled and currently mains rogue for the first time mostly because I was interested in a more support oriented rogue and played as Subtlety from level 1 all the way to Naxxramas on Turtle trying to make "support rogue" work, I really like what you've done to Subtlety. I thought the current spec was just too weak and didn't do enough to compensate for the loss of damage. You pretty much did what I'd have done to buff Subtlety (making Mark for Death guaranteed to hit, rogue himself also able to trigger Honor Among Thieves cos it was a dead weight talent in solo play and removal of Dust of Disappearance for being too niche/situational) and more!

The only nitpick that I have is with Cloaked in Shadows and how it works; giving shields doesn't sound something a rogue would do. It's more about class fantasy than gameplay. I'd have given it a more Cloak of Shadows from TBC kind of effect (even if a slightly nerfed version of it) that also gives lots of dodge as well. But as an ability it looks really neat and should do the job of supporting your team.

Or if you really want to be bold and give Subtlety rogues a cool support ability: a targetable Vanish you can cast on a friendly player to save them from danger. Imagine saving a healer that way and then have them ress your party after a wipe. Just an idea I've had for quite a while.

One thing that bothers me about these rogue changes is the removal of Blade Flurry from the Combat tree and, apparently, not getting anything new in return. Couldn't Combat rogues get a new keystone talent to compensate for the loss of Blade Flurry from the tree?

First i would like to thank the dev team for keeping the game fresh and trying to make it better, thanks to you. But here are my two cents:

 -Warriors dont need another active damaging skill…. Unless it is victory rush or victory rush adjacent

 1-Keep row three capstone a proc ability just change the chance or the proc condition, maybe can be crit strike(yours or enemies) maybe it can be on bleed proc it does something(i would recommend not go the route of weapon type because it can easily fall to the trap of one weapon type having a obviously better ability making players even those that are not min-maxing feel bad for their decision) it can be change on getting hit, you name it maybe making it viable for pvp and pve

To push these two spells in scenarios with many different healer healing at once, we’ve reduced the time needed for them to heal, making them heal less but more frequently.*

As partly mentioned in [this post](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=141246#p141246) already, this is a bit of a weird change. If there's competition from other healers, HoT-healing by-and-large relies on predictive application. You generally don't put a HoT on a target that has an incoming heal to full already, so sneaking a single tick in before your HoT gets invalidated by another healer is still a really bad use of your time and mana. So you want a HoT on the target before it takes damage, and then you still want a beefy tick to make a difference. So it's not at all clear, whether this change is actually beneficial or whether it will decrease output because the few ticks you get in before you get sniped will now be smaller (example: another healer snipes you 3.5s after application - right now you get 1/4th of the total healing in, after the change only 1/6th). It's an interesting idea, but so far I felt the identity was that our ticks were bigger than a priest could do with Renew. Still, I'll have to see it in practice to understand whether smaller faster ticks are good or not.

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jul 25, 2025 1:32 am**
> **Aessina's Bloom:** Now requires Improved Healing Touch as a pre-requisite talent instead of Swiftmend, effect reworked: "Healing a target affected by Regrowth or Rejuvenation with your Healing Touch spells reduces the casting time of your next Healing Touch spell by 0.15/0.3 sec and refunds 5/10% of its mana cost within 20 seconds."

This is an awesome change for dungeon healing. Rejuvenation is a much more common HoT compared to Regrowth and it's awesome that both now work.
For raiding it's great to move away from RNG towards guaranteed procs as you shouldn't base tank healing on luck. I think this talent will shine in the very few fights where Healing Touch was already king, but will not on the grand scale make Healing Touch suddenly viable as a generalist build (those builds died when CC2 made Regrowth way too mana-efficient and thus virtually without drawback). The trigger condition pretty much prevents cross-healing (non-tank targets that have HoTs usually don't need additional healing, it would only snipe the HoT).
I like it as a concept, but it's very different from the old implementation and we're not really in a world where a lot of druids end up as full-time tank healers (since other classes are more tailored towards that).

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jul 25, 2025 1:32 am**
> **Tree of Life Form:** Now increases armor contribution from items by 180%.

Very nice, Trees are often lightning rods for aggro from spawned adds. This will help a lot and is quite thematic.

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jul 25, 2025 1:32 am**
> **Nature's Reach:** Now also increases the range of Abolish Poison and Remove Curse.

Again, very nice, very unique and great utility. This will be super handy in lots of situations, from dungeons to endgame raids. A really great addition to Moonglow healing builds.

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jul 25, 2025 1:32 am**
> **Physical Damage Reduction** from **Armor** is no longer capped at 75%. The extra reduction gained from Armor beyond this point will be diminished. The updated formula will be shared later.
>
> ---
>  **Feral Adrenaline:** Removed.
>
> ---
>   New Talent (Row 6 / 2 Points): **Carnage**
>  "Maul, Swipe and Savage Bite return 5/10% of their damage as healing to you. Ferocious Bite has a 10/20% chance per combo point spent to refresh your active Rake and Rip effects and add an additional combo point."

Let's talk about all bear survivability points together. Feral Adrenaline 2.0 has big problems, chiefly the cooldown. But (unlike Feral Adrenaline 1.0) it actually does something against the number 1 killer of bears - damage spikes. We have zero ways of avoiding Crushing Blows and we cannot (at least with sensible gear) reach Critical Strike immunity either (unlike all the other tanks who have active block abilities). So on harder-hitting bosses two crits in a row usually spell doom for bears. Feral Adrenaline was one way of slightly mitigating that danger, though it was expensive and unreliable.
So what are the replacements? The Vampirism talent looks like a ton of fun and I'm glad it's back. But the healing won't be meaningful against damage spikes during boss fights at all. So how about the armor cap thingy then? This is really interesting, but also still very unclear. The part about diminishing returns is quite ominous though, as armor already scales pretty slowly. I think the balance problem lies more in the way Inspiration/Ancestral Fortitude and Improved Lay On Hands can stack if you organize your raid around it. But in regular day-to-day operation a bear would not be suddenly hitting 20k armor. Partly because bears are often employed as threat tanks and not as mitigation tanks (getting crit and crushed with no recourse makes us really poor mitigation tanks). So we usually wear threat gear with lower armor anyway. And if the fight calls for a full mitigation tank - most raids will turn to a warrior (or paladin) anyway as it would take close to 20k armor to merely match the -10% damage reduction that is built into Defensive Stance. And that would be with the current armor formula, not accounting for the upcoming diminishing returns. And it would be disregarding the very real chance of regular Crushing Blows (+50% damage) and Critical Strikes (+100% damage). To tone those down to damage levels that would be average for other tank classes already takes obscene amounts of armor.
Knight in the K40 Chess encounter is a really instructive example. It debuffs the tank with -50% armor and 80% of damage comes from a skill that cannot crit or crush. So this fight seems engineered for bear tanking. Yet when you look at real numbers, warriors still win out - half of moderate armor + 10% damage reduction + flat reduction from block value leads to lower damage intake than half of higher armor. And that's not even accounting for the occasional white hit that can crit or crush a bear (but not a blocking warrior).
It's great that the hard armor cap is finally softened. This will open up a lot of possibilities for the future (especially concerning the planned T4 raid). But this is by no means a solution to the problems bear tanks face. Feral Adrenaline wasn't either, but as bad as it is, it feels more targeted at bear problems than a diminished armor contribution above the cap. I like that bears have to take crits and soak them, but there should be some kind of protection against really bad RNG with serial crits and that will need a bit more creativity than stacking armor for diminishing returns.

lt;dr: Resto Druid and Bear Tank changes include some amazing utility, but the big-picture changes miss the mark a little bit. They seem great on paper, but not really made with real-world scenarios in mind. They do have potential and seem made with good intentions and understanding of some of the problems the specs currently faces, so keep up the good work. This is a good start to a longer conversation and moving in the right direction.

*Last edited by Elesion on Sat Jul 26, 2025 1:19 am, edited 1 time in total.*

One thing I DO like about what Project Epoch is doing is adding more complexity/difficulty to the open world. If TWoW were to add in some extras to the open world like mobs with frontal cones you have to dodge or totems you have to destroy during combat that could feel great IMO. As for dungeons, I can't speak since my characters are all low level, but I've always been of the opinion that if you can AoE down a pack without using CC, or chain pull one pack after another without drinking in between, the dungeon is tuned to be too easy. A simple way to improve this is to add CC abilities in to the pack - polymorphs, interrupts, mana drains, armour breaks... Back in Vanilla WoW, CC was an absolutely fundamental part of every pull, and I loved it.

Edit: I think that in the open world there's this idea that you can't give mobs too many abilities because then only some classes could kill them... but isn't that part of the point of making every class unique? If you run into situations where you just don't have the tools to win, but know that if you had another class it'd be easy, that actually goes a long way to reinforce class fantasy.

<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=141497#p141497 | page 38 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jul 25, 2025 1:32 am**
> **ROGUE**
>
>  **Baseline Changes**
>
> ---
>   New Passive: **Quickfooted**
>  Learned at Level 30.
>  "Your movement speed is increased by 7%. This stacks with other movement speed increasing effects."
>
>  Developer Comment: Rogues are famously known for their nimbleness but this wasn't seen outside of Sprint, making them struggle keeping up with other classes at times.
>
>  We first considered adding effects that increase movement speed to each specialization's talent tree but decided on doing a baseline passive as this is class and not build specific.
>
> ---

I was very happy with the changes to Feral Druids, but one thing really struck me. Rogues are a fairly mobile class, able to both remove slows with Vanish and continue chasing them with sprint, with the ability to reset the cooldown of these abilities. So why add anything else to them?

For example, take a fight between a warrior and a rog, where the bandit exhausts the warrior to death with kiting and bloodshots. With this practice, a "simplification" in the form of fast movement from the melee zone will be added to this fight for the rog (obviously, the fight is no longer in the warrior's favor).

If you're giving a buff that increases movement speed permanently, you need to remove something, otherwise it feels too unbalanced.

For example, reduce the effectiveness or duration of the poison that slows the target. Or reduce the Sprint time.

Personally, I would suggest making the movement speed not constant, but dependent on the ability to `Slice and Dice`. This seems more balanced, since the rogue pays for this speed with combo points, which does not make him completely insane in PvP. With this approach, it will not be that he is constantly faster than the target and spends all his power only on control and damage to you.

## Post 141541 by Elesion (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2025-07-26T10:25:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=141541#p141541 | page 39 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Sylerann wrote: Sat Jul 26, 2025 9:55 am**
> That makes a lot more sense, thank you. I haven't personally seen a renew priest do better than tree but perhaps that's something I've yet to run into.
>
>  I think the fix to Efflorescence is going to help a lot. I would generally agree with those points, and I don't see how any of the other changes to Resto would fix the issues. Making hots tick differently is just going to be weird, and probably buff druid in pvp as mentioned previously. The change feels like something somebody would come up with after needing to offspec for a dungeon and playing resto for 1 hour. "WTF why does it take so long to heal!" Rejuv takes 3 seconds to heal, you just  anticipate the damage. It's how the spec plays.

Yeah, priest is a *very* strong HoT healer. Renew having 5 ticks (and thus 100% scaling) baseline goes very hard, plus they have much better mana regeneration. At the top end of gear a priest with no consumables can keep up with a tree chain-chugging mana pots. Tree only pulls firmly ahead when using full T2.

But that also brings up the one thing I really like about the tick-rate change - it helps fix itemization in a roundabout way. Right now 8/8 T2 is oppressively strong for Reju Tree. It's just a flat +25% output / +25% concurrent HoTs. Healing gear beyond T2 doesn't scale well enough to make up for that.
We'll have to see if set bonuses get adjusted as well (the Itemization changelog is still unknown), but keeping set bonuses as they are 8/8 T2 would go down to 16.6% more output (instead of 25%) and down to 1 additional target (instead of 2). While 2/9 T3 would get +50% energize procs on the raid. That's a substantial buff and seems really valuable. Weaker full T2 set and much higher incentive to break it is a very good thing for gearing as you're not perma-married to T2 any longer.

## Post 141636 by Zamera — 2025-07-27T00:00:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=141636#p141636 | page 39 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Warriors at the moment are just glorified target dummies in PvP. We provide no useful utility, crowd control, and our damage is mediocre at best. We require multiple other specific classes/specs to perform at a baseline level. The upcoming patch addresses nothing, specifically for Arms PvP. I always saw Arms warrior as a tactical juggernaut, but none of this fantasy is felt in the game.

The upcoming patch provides a 10% buff to Mortal Strike and Slam, this is nerfed in instanced pvp combat and is really a win more buff. We will not really feel this. This is really a compensatory buff for PvE due to the execute changes.

Master Strike is very mediocre. While it is interesting to swap weapons in and out depending on the situation, not all weapons are created equal and acquiring multiple high end weapons seems like a tall tale to ask all warriors to do. Combine this with the rage cost and swapping weapons imposes a GCD penalty and resets your swing timer.

Some suggestions:

Unlink our big 3 cooldowns, Retaliation, Recklessness, and Shield Wall. It feels ancient that these are all the same cooldown still. Impose a 2 min cooldown when you activate one of them. Preferably I would like the big 3 cooldowns to be about 15 mins. Remove the Improved Disciplines talent from the game. It is border line useless with all the restrictions/other talents we can take.

Remove the shared cooldown on intervene and intercept.

Create a new spell, War Banner. Let this provide some sort of buff utility. Potentially we could see 3 of these for each spec/stance or we could limit it to one version. Let the banners be placeable and warriors can intervene them like an ally.

Arms Banner: Group movement speed increase, movement speed cannot go below x%, maybe reduces incoming crowd control (not CC that has already been applied)

Fury Banner: Some sort of group crit buff/crit dmg modifier increase?

Prot Banner: Mimics your health/armor, increases threat generation, pulses threat, if you cast taunt or maybe if you taunt it, it aoe taunts mobs onto it for 2s. Gives you the threat when it expires/dies.

Spell reflect or some sort of spell block.

Second Wind- health/rage when crowd controlled/immobilized

Victory Rush- medium damage- heals for 20% of max hp, resets on kill/hk (and assist) 20 sec cd

Holmgang- preventing most attacks from reducing your HP to less than 1. Duration: 10s chains a target to the warrior (stolen from ff14)

Nascent Flash- grants a high amount of vampirism for 10s (maybe like 50%) (stolen/similar to ff14)

Please note I am not asking for all this, these are suggestions in a way the game can go for Warriors (arms mainly).

Please comment on what you would like see/improve for Warriors or the direction you would like to see them go for us.

>
>  So: Make sure to write consistent negative posts on forums and discord about the MM hunter situation. Make your complaints heard. It seems devs might listen.

I dont want to be overly negative, just provide some insight of my own thoughts from a years long hunter player. There is sa core frustration of BM hunters that by now, retail wow fixed for good, but classic did not and most of the part SOD as well fix it.

The Double Micro Burden:

Managing your character's positioning, cooldowns, rotation, and simultaneously controlling your pet's positioning, target, and abilities is objectively more demanding than managing just your character. This requires:

Constant attention splitting.

Extra keybinds and situational awareness.

Reacting to mechanics affecting two entities.

The double buff burden. If you want to min max, you have to farm buffs for yourself and your pets. Exhausting and gold consuming. And annoying in raids to always have to ask for pet buffs.

You need to beware of your characters position and your pets position. Yet, in return for doing it, you only do the same DPS as any other class that simply has to control itself. So you pay a tax for it, which the devs doesnt seem to consider. Since pet survivability is HUGE in raiding, if they want the spec to do any good, they have to also provide QOl. Give mend pet higher range, make a hot, AND give it a basic sort of RAP scaling to keep it with higher tiers of content and damage. Its mana cost is already crazy high for a heal ability.

Make the pet straight up immune against certain debuffs and so on. Only in raids!

If people miss the big RED kitty aspect of the spec, it is easy enough to provide a cosmetic change to either kill command or bait shot, by giving the pet the effect while bait shot is active or something.

*Last edited by Jiav on Sun Jul 27, 2025 9:41 am, edited 1 time in total.*

>

>
>  *Developer Comment: The bouncing healing of Chain Heal has been dominant in the Restoration Shaman healing gameplay, even moreso in bigger group sizes. For this reason we're pulling slightly back on its scaling to give its other healing spells some room to shine.*

>
>  *Developer Comment: Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave quite struggle compared to Chain Heal in terms of throughput, so we're giving them some love alongside the Chain Heal scaling nerf to incentivize their usage, with a cast time reduction buff on Improved Healing Wave and the inclusion of Lesser Healing Wave in Healing Way, both allowing it to benefit from the effect and the shorter cast time of Lesser Healing Wave making it faster to gain stacks of Healing Way on the target.*

On the topic of the armor cap remooved, I will point out like other tanks did already, that the class that benefit the most from the change is Druid, and paladin and warior actualy have a hard time reaching it and required several other class buffs to get it. To remedy this stretch between the tank classes, i have a suggestion to improove the block value system. Block value is realy bad in cases it is meaningfull IE bosses and raid tanking in general (exemple out of my ass but you will get the gist : tank get hit for 2500 dmg after armor count-> miss parry dodge delete the dmg completly while block remoove lets say 300 dmg with full gear towards block value and the tank still gets hit for 2200 damage) and realy good in cases it can be exploited in the world (IE aoe farming you get hit by 350 after armor count, now you see how good it is especialy for classes with alot of block built in (paladins).
Point being a percentage value on top of armor Damage reduction would work well. Lets say you realy want paladins to be the BIG BLOCKERS of the tanks and lets imagine an alternative block value system.
Now we think shields have % DR when blocking instead of statick dmg value. Lets say 1% per 10 level of the shield and then 1% more per raid tier that would be 1% for shields level 1-10 6% for lvl 60 shields (and maybe some epics before i let you play with the numbers) and 9.5% for khara 40 tank shield (you can decide if healer shields and caster shields get the same treatment or a lower value)
It means in raid environment now block will work as a percent of the original damage and now will be more valuable example : boss hits for 10K you take a normal hit at armor cap its 2500 dmg now you block with tier 4 shield block value (or trinket or blabla this is tuning now) 10% dr you take 1500 dmg thats a much better swing for us and it FEELS relevent (right now when im soaking patchwork I RLY rather parry miss or dodge). Now lets check aoe farming scenario (that you seem to not like with the aoe vamp nerf) mobs hit for 700 dmg with armor dr around 63% (mine in T3 without raid buffs) you take unblocked dmg of 259 while blocking with 10% dr you would take 189 (so the reduction is much much less valuable than with the flat value of current version). That way you make the block stat much more desirable in raid while keeping variety of tank meta, you still have the druid HP monster, the war can both be furyprot or deep prot and now blocking is very nice for him to have and same goes with paladin but with adds (because you realy want to push him into add management.

Now I would like to add something on the topic of paladin tanking in particular (which is what i play mostly in tanking) you said they are in a good place at the moment and didnt change them but you did nerf the spellpower on all tiers (xept maybe tier 1 which is not all that relevent until fresh server). I say sure but what is your plan for the threatloss (we already are pushed into SP flasking to hold threat against the big pumpers of the server) You want to push Strength on paladin as a tanking stats (atleast that is what i take from the gear changes) If strength was directly translated into our threat and our mitigation somehow I wouldnt mind, but in the current state of the class we want spellpower for threat and agility for both dodge and crit. Most paladin threat set is T2.5 and you cannot wear that in khara 40. If you realy want paladins to use strength on their gearsets I heavily recommend that you translate that into the talent and/or spellbook of tankadins. Lets say you improove block either in the way suggest or in your own creative way, you could make holy shield and blessing of sanctuary (which should be reworked along block value btw) scale with strength. It would also be nice to not have Holy strike and Crusader strike on the same gcd (its another topic but rotation even in dps feels bad) in current state we just use HS for threat and you cannot use CS because you loose too much threat.
Capstone of Prot is still a bit clunky because its threat/DR and need a target and to be in range, would love to see another iteration imagined. Not necessarily retail solutions, could be like a fist of heaven thingy for threat or something.
In most cases we dont have a lot of tools at our disposale: press holy shield the holy strike and consecration on cd. A good paladin will bop threat overtakes and bubble reset different kind of stacks but thats about it. You dont even have to create new tools, you could make use of whats alrdy their but make them more broad use. Think of exorcism and holy wrath, now make them hit everything and a condition for holy wrath to be instant cast (like a proc that happens under some conditions) and give them a better sp scaling against UD (dont need to be retail version that crits but a 30% more sp scaling is noticeable) now you have alot of tools at your disposale. You killed exorcism threat because... I dont know but now it has bad threat. Aleast now we could press it on everything just for the little +when everything else is on cd against everything (it would also be our range pull we are still the only tanks that requires a hunter to range pull or grenade pull or god forbid a boomerang pull....). I have read good ideas on the forum to improve the talent tree (for exemple merge divine strength and intellect to give a nice alternative to compete with (both talent arent so good on their own anyway) anyway twas just an example.
I do think you did a good job overall with CC2 but some aspects of paladins still feels off somewhat especialy HS and CS (great work on leveling zones and new dungeons/raid tho).
I do love this server and I intend to play more, but with the paladin tank gear gutted next patch and the fact that you still didnt fix T3.5 yes you gave T3.5 some stamina but not nearly enough (144 with all pieces vs 161 for war and less mitigation stat IE agi + def parry dodge(but its even more because of the piece we can switch around))to even tank Kharazan and as of current stats that we want for paladin tanking, strength is bad and i mean REALY BAD. And the tier set bonus for tanks are underwhelming to say the least (especialy compared to their brother dps and heal versions the 5% healing received while in your consecration IS a joke and the block value is irrelevent in raid as previously stated, the threat COULD be good IF Holy shield had a better SP scaling. But now you compare that to 192 holy shock heal and 2 more target and 2% on holy strike or a 6% bonus strength and a groupewide buff...) Then again I AGREE that the previous tier were overtuned, bringing both defensive stats and offensive stats in too big numbers. But with the current t3.5 we STILL rather use T2.5 for threat and T3 and other pieces for mitigation. So I encourage the dev team to look it up and come with A solution not necessarily mine, to improve T3.5 tank version and hopefully change and tweak a bit the spells/talents.
Meanwhile ill be taking a break from paladin tank.
Even if my message seems like a harsh critic I DO think you are doing a good work overall (I wouldnt post otherwise i would just leave), I just wanted to bring a paladin that tanked everything up to khara 40 POV.
I believe in the slow and steady wins the race. Learn from your past choices and improove to give us the perfect V+ experience.

## Post 143842 by Elesion (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2025-08-08T14:14:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=143842#p143842 | page 41 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Everran wrote: Wed Aug 06, 2025 5:39 pm**
> On the topic of the armor cap remooved, I will point out like other tanks did already, that the class that benefit the most from the change is Druid, and paladin and warior actualy have a hard time reaching it and required several other class buffs to get it. To remedy this stretch between the tank classes, i have a suggestion to improove the block value system. Block value is realy bad in cases it is meaningfull IE bosses and raid tanking in general (exemple out of my ass but you will get the gist : tank get hit for 2500 dmg after armor count-> miss parry dodge delete the dmg completly while block remoove lets say 300 dmg with full gear towards block value and the tank still gets hit for 2200 damage) and realy good in cases it can be exploited in the world (IE aoe farming you get hit by 350 after armor count, now you see how good it is especialy for classes with alot of block built in (paladins).

I don't share your assessment that druid is a good mitigation tank right now. I would argue it's the worst out of the three major tank classes. It takes by far the most damage, but it does higher (single target) threat so people are willing to take that trade-off.

druid has a hefty armor multiplier - warrior/pala does not
druid gets a 20% bonus stamina - warrior/pala does not
vs
warrior/pala can parry - druid cannot
warrior/pala can block - druid cannot
warrior/pala can easily be immune to crits and crushing blows - druid can never remove crushing blows and only become crit immune using meme enchants/gear
warrior gets 10% baseline damage reduction from stance, pala gets 10% baseline damage reduction from talents - druid does not

Patchwerk is a really bad example, because the fight is very atypical. For soakers all the damage comes from a skill (Hateful Strike) that cannot crit or crush. And yet warrior/pala with 10% damage reduction and block value on top is very competitive in terms of damage taken. From my personal experience only 8/9 T3 set bonus allows a bear to actually take less damage than a warrior when soaking Hatefuls.
Any regular fights where the mob will do 15% crushing blows (150% damage) and 5.6% critical strikes (200% damage) the average damage intake of a warrior/pala will be enormously lower. And it will be far less dangerous to use them, because what kills tanks isn't taking 300-400 damage more or less because of block value. It's taking a spike of double damage (crit). Or even two in a row. Druid has no recourse against that, warrior/pala just presses active block and will never take more than a regular hit.

You can complain about a lot of things when it comes to balance between tank classes. You can complain a lot about the direction they're taking by removing armor cap. But that druids are somehow out-classing warrior/pala on mitigation fights is quite ridiculous. Block is already a super strong mechanic and druid doesn't have access to it.

## Post 144456 by Zypx — 2025-08-11T09:33:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=144456#p144456 | page 41 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

Hello,

I will just write a post here to comment on the Warrior class. This is only PvP related, and I assume your goals was to give utility to the class. However, there are some serious issues here that I would like to address:

New Keystone (Row 3 / 1 Point): Master Strike
"Perform a skillful attack with a weapon, dealing 35% weapon damage and causing an additional effect depending on your main hand weapon.
Mace - Disorient the target for 3 sec. Any damage caused will remove the effect.
Sword - Disarm the target for 3 sec.
Axe - Immobilize the target for 4 sec.
Polearm - Deal an additional 100% weapon damage if target is mounted, and dismounts them.
Fist Weapon - Knock down the target for 2 sec.
Staff - Increases your chance to parry by 25% for 10 sec.
Dagger - Silence the target for 3 sec."
(20 Rage Cost, 30 Second Cooldown, Melee Range)

Let's start with this. Obviously, you will swap weapons to use this ability then swap back to your main weapon. The problem here is already that you swap weapons twice, which is 3 seconds (2 GCD's) before you can deal damage.

Most of the effects have already expired, making this pretty useless for the effort that you need to do. We know very well that you won't sit with fist weapons, staff or daggers after you have used the ability, so everything except staff is pretty bad.

The mace effect is useless as well as you may have deep wounds or even if you use rend, this will break the effect. Also, you have to watch your auto swing to not break it as well. At least make it not break the warriors bleed ticks and have auto hit cancel like rogues Gouge.

Sword is bad as well since you have your own disarm ability, and 3 seconds is way too low.

Now that arena is coming out, warriors are not looking very well. Here are the main concerns I have:

 - Hamstring has a 6 seconds cooldown
 - Intercept and Intervene sharing cooldown
 - Iron Will is in the protection tree
 - No Spell Reflection - Making warrior sitting ducks vs casters with crowd control
 - No Second Wind will is also reducing the survival rates while sitting in crowd control. There are already no defensive abilities to use so it is extermely squishy, even with the damage debuffs in pvp instances

My aim is not to be negative but to give feedback since I do have the pvp experience to actually see the problems here and give criticism that may help you.

The warrior class seems pretty good in PvE, no arguments there, but for PvP it is absolutely butchered that it may be one of the worst classes to play.

I hope this brings some clarity to the bad situation the class is in, and hope it helps your PvP balancing in the future.

## Post 145508 by Halfgeek9 (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2025-08-14T23:20:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=145508#p145508 | page 41 | era: pre-1.18.1 -->

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jul 25, 2025 1:32 am**
> **DRUID**
> - **Improved Balance of All Things (Balance T3.5 5p):** Increased bonus from 33% to 50%.

So you nerf the bonus to the proc from 0.8 to 0.5 cast time reduction for Starfire, but buff the proc rate to compensate for the T3.5..

What this means is Balance Druids T3 or below are nerfed in DPS.

Eclipse scaling with spell crit is a terrible idea, because it needs 34% spell crit to have the same 30% damage bonus currently, meaning T1-T3 Druids are shafted with weaker Eclipse. Balance Druids lack talents that boost spell crit, only Moonfire gets boosted, not overall spell crit, thus with their gear, T1 Druids only have ~20% spell crit. T2 ~25%.

This results in Eclipse being a 20-25% dmg bonus for T1 & T2 Druids. Nerfing their DPS further on top of Starfire DPS loss.

The proc rate of Eclipse is not going to make up for it, because Wrath only gives 30% proc rate, and Arcane Eclipse is where Druids pump out the high dps due to interactions with raid debuffs (Curse of Shadows).

Spamming Wrath to fish for a 20% dmg bonus Arcane Eclipse is a DPS loss vs straight up Starfire spam taking advantage of raid debuffs.

These changes for Balance Druid is very poorly thought through, especially the fact that only T3.5 set bonus compensate for weaker Balance in All Things. Meaning for 99% of Balance Druid players, they are being nerfed. For no reason whatsoever because Moonkins are not even in the top dps meters for casters.
