Beast Mastery is effectively dead with these changes, and I will explain why.
For those who don’t know me, my name is Skurridizo, and I am one of the very few Beast Mastery enthusiasts, especially in end-game content. Sadly, the game currently forces you to switch to something else, and these are the reasons I want to share.

 1. Pet choices

The current pet metagame revolves entirely around Spell Power pets, leaving no real variety. If you are using a cat, raptor, or wolf, I’m sorry to say this, but you are essentially trolling. ![🦂](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f982.svg)![🐍](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f40d.svg)![🐉](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f409.svg)

Suggestion:
Make Chimeras tameable by Beast Mastery hunters through a quest or specific requirement. Give them strong but balanced stats (for example, +7% to all attributes) and the ability to learn all pet abilities. Let players experiment and create their own builds.

 2. Itemization

At the moment, Beast Mastery aims to maximize the Spirit Bond talent, which shares part of our Ranged Attack Power with the pet as both Attack Damage and Spell Power. However, in late-game content, hunters are forced to sacrifice Attack Power in favor of higher Critical Strike chance.

It is true that Kill Command has been added, but let’s be honest: with only ~20% crit chance, you should not realistically expect to use it on cooldown.

Suggestion:
Introduce dedicated Tier 3 and 3.5 sets for hunters with less crit, more Attack Power, and Beast Mastery-oriented bonuses.

 3. Raid tempo

Beast Mastery shines in long encounters and fits perfectly in progression-focused guilds. For raids that clear content quickly with 40 players, the solution was Wind Serpent combined with Kill Command + Baited Shot. This provided insane burst damage and was, in fact, the best PvP Beast Mastery setup.

Now that option is gone forever. I will miss it. :(

Suggestion:
Chimeras, as mentioned above, would solve this issue.

 4. Pet survivability

In many encounters, pets lack sufficient survivability. In pug raids, nobody cares about keeping pets alive, which makes the spec nearly useless. Even in hardcore guilds, there is a lot of unavoidable global damage that is not classified as AoE (e.g., Thaddius or void zones).

Suggestion:
Buff Improved Mend Pet and make it offensively relevant. For example, while channeling Mend Pet, apply the +30% damage bonus from Improved Eyes of the Beast.
Currently, it is a 5-second channel costing 480 mana that barely heals 1,000 HP, which feels extremely weak.

 5. Defensive tools

Previously, Kill Command was our only way to protect the pet by removing fears and other crowd-control effects. With its removal, we gain Bestial Wrath. While iconic and beloved, let’s be honest—it was functionally useless in most scenarios.

This effectively results in a nerf, as the cooldown of our only real defensive tool has been increased.

Suggestion:
Rework Bestial Wrath to have a much shorter duration and cooldown.
For example: reduce duration from 18s to 3s and cooldown from 90s to 15s (dividing both by six).

 6. Melee Beast Mastery

This is not a major issue, but it would be great if one day melee support Beast Mastery was viable—using Nightfall alongside BM talents. This way, the personal DPS loss from Nightfall would not heavily impact pet damage.

Suggestion:
Move the part of Lightning Reflexes that converts Agility into Attack Power (1 Agi = 2 AP) to an earlier row in the Survival tree.

Conclusion

With these changes, my prediction is that Beast Mastery will remain unplayable in fast-paced raids. There is too much RNG involved in the new mechanics, while the core issues remain unresolved. Overall, Beast Mastery has become even harder to play effectively.

Additionally, ranged weapons are still one or two steps behind two-handed melee weapons in terms of DPS. Best-in-slot ammunition is locked behind LBRS and Stratholme (Scarlet Living). This might be an oversight carried over from Classic.

I’m afraid most players will end up playing pet-less builds, investing only 7 points into Survival—losing an essential and iconic part of the hunter class that should instead be encouraged and rewarded.

That said, I do appreciate the effort put into updating all three hunter specializations. I will enjoy testing the new changes, and hopefully, one day, we will see a Scorpion at the top of the DPS charts. ![🦂](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f982.svg)![🦂](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f982.svg)![🦂](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f982.svg)

![Image](https://i.gyazo.com/65060cab49b7f873834e313a6b62fc7c.png)

## Post 166186 by Caixiao99999 (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2026-01-24T01:09:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166186#p166186 | page 45 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

I feel like the Turtle team is very good at destroying things players have already invested in.
I play Fire Shaman and T1 Healing Shaman, and I’ve spent a lot of time gearing and refining my builds.
But every balance patch is a huge rework that completely overturns previous setups, often without proper testing.
If something is overpowered, it can be adjusted with numbers. It doesn’t need to be completely destroyed.
This approach feels very disrespectful to players’ time and effort.

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jan 23, 2026 7:24 pm**

>  Please note that this is a **Preliminary Changelog**. Further changes may still be made.

>  **ALL**
>

>
>  *Developer Comment: This was an ongoing quirk that was being (ab)used. Normally we would fix these in our weekly changelogs but because of the gravity of this change we've moved this to a Class Changes cycle.*
>
>
>
>  **PvP**
>
>  The **PvP Dampening Debuff** introduced in 1.18.0 will now have dynamic reductions of Magical and Physical damage based on your class / spec instead of a flat number for all classes.
>
>  More information regarding numbers will be given at a later date.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Turning these values class-dependent means that we will be less restricted in Design space of making all specs come to life and be viable without adding Player-target exceptions on a lot of spells.*
>
>
>  **DRUID**
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  Reduced the threat modifier of **Maul** by 15%.
>  Reduced the threat modifier of **Savage Bite** by 12%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Feral Bears have been overly prominent in their threat output, leaving little room for other tanks to shine. To reign in their presence, we’re reducing the threat modifiers on Maul and Savage Bite.*
>
>  **Balance**
> ---
>  **Balance of All Things:** Reduced from 5 points to 3 points and functionality reworked:
>  "Damaging a target affected by **Insect Swarm** with your **Wrath** spell returns 10/20/30% of its mana cost back to you.
>
>  **Starfire** has a 2/4/6% higher chance to critically strike against targets affected by **Moonfire**."
>
>
>
>
>  **HUNTER**
>
>  Ranged variant of Hunter has been one of the least changed classes in Class Changes 2 and has fallen behind other damage dealers and melee Hunter not only in raw DPS, but also in terms of gameplay.
>  Ranged Hunter is extremely timing-dependent and offers little reactivity in its rotation. In this patch, we are reviewing the Hunter kit as a whole to ensure more abilities are useful and impactful, and reworking the talent trees to make them more engaging in endgame content.
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  New Spell: **Aspect of the Viper** - Learned at Level 56.
>
>  "The hunter takes on the aspect of the viper, regenerating 5% of maximum mana every 5 second. Only one Aspect can be active at a time."
>
>  (No Mana Cost)
>
>  *Developer Comment: Hunter is a class that cannot reliably regain mana without proper set bonuses and can be quite mana-hungry. To offset this, we are adding a passive way to regain mana with the small drawback of occupying an Aspect slot.*
>
> ---
>  **Trueshot Aura:** Now baseline, learned at Level 40.
>
>  "Increases the attack power of party members within 45 yards by 3%, plus an additional 30."
>
>  *Developer Comment: Trueshot Aura was a design-limiting ability and an uninteresting capstone. For that reason, we are making it baseline for all Hunters in a slightly toned-down version.*
>
> ---
>  **Steady Shot:** Now baseline, learned at Level 20.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Steady Shot has been a must-have ability for all ranged Hunters, while Aimed Shot was rendered almost useless by its existence. We believe such a core ability should be part of the baseline kit, so we are returning Steady Shot as one.*
>
> ---
>  **Volley:** Has seen various changes.
>  - Now a 3 second cast instead of a continuous channeled ability.
>  - Mana Costs reduced:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 40):** From 350 to 210
>  **Rank 2 (Level 50):** From 420 to 270
>  **Rank 3 (Level 60):** From 490 to 330
>  - Now has Attack Power scaling:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 40):** 4% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 2 (Level 50):** 5% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 3 (Level 60):** 6% Attack Power Scaling
>  Any spell power scaling remains unchanged.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Volley has always been interesting in concept but too weak to justify use in practice. Due to its channeled nature, its damage would have had to be increased to unreasonable levels to be viable. We are therefore converting it into a casted ability that does not require the Hunter to stop performing other actions for 10 seconds to reach its full potential.*
>
> ---
>  **Arcane Shot:** Base damage values reduced but now scales with ranged weapon damage.
>
>  Damage Values:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 6):** Damage reduced from 13 to 10, added 10% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 2 (Level 12):** Damage reduced from 21 to 17, added 15% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 3 (Level 20):** Damage reduced from 33 to 27, added 20% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 4 (Level 28):** Damage reduced from 59 to 48, added 25% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 5 (Level 36):** Damage reduced from 83 to 71, added 30% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 6 (Level 44):** Damage reduced from 115 to 101, added 35% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 7 (Level 52):** Damage reduced from 145 to 129, added 40% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 8 (Level 60):** Damage reduced from 183 to 166, added 45% ranged weapon damage.
>
>  Any spell power scaling remains unchanged.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Arcane Shot has been another Hunter ability that was underused and underpowered, lacking a meaningful place in the rotation. We are adding weapon damage scaling to make it a more rewarding button to press.*
>
> ---
>  **Rapid Fire:** Now also decreases the cast time of **Aimed Shot** and **Steady Shot** by 40%.
>
> ---
>  **Aimed Shot** and **Arcane Shot** are now on separate independent cooldowns.
>
>
>  **Marksmanship**
> ---
>  **Aimed Shot:** Returned as the 3rd Row Keystone talent.
>  Cast time reduced from 3 seconds to 2 seconds, Cooldown increased from 6 seconds to 26 seconds.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Due to its long cast time, Aimed Shot struggled to find a place in the Hunter rotation. We are reducing its cast time and adding several Aimed Shot–centric talents to make it a cooldown worth pressing for Marksmanship.*
>
> ---
>  New Keystone: **Experimental Ammunition** (5th Row)
>
>  "Your **Aimed Shot** deals an additional 5% of its damage as Fire, Arcane or Nature damage and grants you a benefit depending on the element:
>
>  **Fire Ammunition:** Your next Multi-Shot hits explode for 20% ranged weapon damage in 5 yard radius.
>
>  **Arcane Ammunition:** Your next Arcane Shot deals 100% increased damage and weakens target's resistance to magic, increasing magic damage taken by 3% for 6 seconds.
>
>  **Nature Ammunition:** Your next Serpent Sting deals 100% increased damage and applies a corrosive poison that reduces target's armor by 4 per level (240 at Level 60) for 15 seconds."
>
>  These effects last 1 minute and cycle between each other in the order of Fire, Arcane and Nature.
>  Only one type of ammunition can be active at a time.
>
>  *Developer Comment: The goal of this talent is to give unique, thematic effects to existing abilities that reinforce their roles, while encouraging the use of Aimed Shot and lesser-used Hunter abilities in combination with it.*
>
> ---
>  New Capstone Talent: **Lock and Load** (1 rank, 7th row)
>  "Your **Steady Shot**, **Aimed Shot** and **Arcane Shot** critical strikes have a chance to reset the cooldown of **Aimed Shot** and trigger Lock and Load. Lasts 10 seconds or until you cast **Aimed Shot**.
>
>  Lock and Load reduces the cast time of **Aimed Shot** by 1 second and causes your **Aimed Shot** to damage all enemies in between you and the target."
>
>  *Developer Comment: This capstone is intended to make the rotation more interactive through procs, improve endgame scaling, and reduce the impact of slight auto-shot delays by shifting more power into active abilities.*
>
> ---
>  **Improved Stings:** Has been changed to:
>  "Increases the damage done by your **Serpent Sting** by 6/12/18/24/30% ,increases the mana drained by **Viper Sting** by 1/2/3/4/5% and **Scorpid Sting** reduces attack speed by an additional 2/4/6/8/10%.
>  and **Scorpid Sting** reduces attack speed by additional 2/4/6/8/10%"
>
> ---
>  **Improved Scorpid Sting:** Removed. Most of the effect has been merged with **Improved Stings**.
>
> ---
>  **Swiftshot:** Has been changed to:
>  "Reduces the cooldown of your **Arcane Shot** by 0.5/1/1.5 seconds and cooldown of your **Aimed Shot** by 2/4/6 seconds"
>
> ---
>  **Ranged Weapon Specialization:** Ranged damage increase buffed from 1/2/3/4/5% to 2/4/6/8/10%.
>
> ---
>  **Barrage:** Now also reduces the cast time of **Volley** by 1/1.5/2 seconds.
>
> ---
>  **Improved Steady Shot:** Renamed to **Improved Marksmanship** and changed to:
>  "Increases the damage of **Steady Shot** and **Aimed Shot** by 5/10%."
>
>
>
>  **Beast Mastery**
>
>  In the last patch, we reworked Beast Mastery, but the changes did not hit the mark.
>  The specialization played awkwardly, so we are redesigning it again with a focus on smoother gameplay and preservation of core Beast Mastery mechanics.
>
>
> ---
>  **Endurance Training:** Health increase buffed from 1/2/3/4/5% to 2/4/6/8/10%.
>
> ---
>  **Thick Hide:** Armor value increase buffed from 4/7/10% to 7/14/20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Pets have been too fragile in open world content, and these changes should restore some of their durability.*
>
> ---
>  New Talent: **Scent of Blood:** (3 Ranks, 5th Row)

> ---

>  *Developer Comment: Bestial Wrath has been one of the most requested abilities to return. We agree it is iconic, so we are restoring it with an additonal method of activating its effect for a limited duration.*
>
> ---
>  **Kill Command:** Moved to be the Capstone talent and reworked:

>  (8 Second Cooldown, 5% Base Mana Cost, 45 Yard Range, No Global Cooldown)

>  *Developer Comment: Our previous version of Kill Command was underpowered and required too much setup. This new version, inspired by The Burning Crusade, should provide familiar and beloved gameplay while being attack speed–agnostic.*
>
> ---
>  **Baited Shot:** Removed.

>  *Developer Comment: Baited Shot struggled to fit into the Hunter rotation. For that reason, it has been removed, with its core concept preserved within the Scent of Blood talent. The barbeque is over.*

>
>  **Survival**

>  *Developer Comment: The lack of throughput caused Lacerate to fall into the wayside in the hierarchy of ability priorities, so we're giving it an increase in damage a bigger incentive to use it from the sides. Hopefully these changes should make it feel more like the reactive ability it was meant to be.*

>
>

>

>

>  *Developer Comment: Protection Paladins were extremely strong during leveling and early endgame but scaled poorly in high-end raids. These changes slightly reduce early power while significantly improving late-game scaling.*
>
>
>  **Retribution**
> ---
>  **Repentance:** Repent effect applied on immune creatures now scales with 8% of your Attack Power per tick.
>
> ---
>  **Seal of Command:** Procs per minute increased from 7 to 9.
>
> ---
>  **Crusader Strike:** Rank 5's weapon damage percentage increased from 90% to 100%.

>  *Developer Comment: Retribution paladins that leaned into attack power have been underperforming for the last few patches. These three changes should bring them closer in line to their hybrid counterparts.*
>
>
>  **Holy**
> ---
>  **Daybreak:** Base healing value reduced from 289 to 248 and healing power scaling reduced from 43% to 32%.
>
>  Developer Comment: In the previous patch, we changed the Holy Paladin capstone talent to offer something more unique than a simple healing increase. While the change was thematically successful, the raw power of Daybreak—especially when combined with the Tier 3.5 set bonus—was significantly too high.
>  We are therefore reducing the healing values and scaling of Daybreak substantially to give other healers more room to perform, while preserving the core identity of the talent.
>
>
>  **Tier Bonus Changes**
> ---
>  While usually we keep set bonus changes in the itemization changelog, the changes for paladin are significant enough to warrant being put here.
>
> ---
>
> - **Retribution Paladin Tier 3.5 (5 Set):** **Crusade**'s attack speed bonus increased from 2% to 4% and its duration increased from 15 seconds to 20 seconds but no longer stacks.
>
> ---
>
> - **Holy Paladin Tier 3.5 (5 Set):** No longer adds additional affected targets to **Holy Strike**.
>
> ---
>
> - **Protection Paladin Tier 3.5:** Moved 5 Set Bonus to 3 Set Bonus. New 5 Set Bonus is the following: "**Holy Shield** decreases your damage taken by 4%.".
>
> ---
>
> - **Retribution/Protection Paladin Tier 2.5 (3 Set):** Effect changed to the following: "Increases damage done by your **Judgement of Righteousness** and **Judgement of Command** by 15%.".
>
>
>  **PRIEST**
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  **Heal** (Rank 4): Healing increased from 605-684 to 702-793.
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 1): Healing increased from 764-862 to 840-948.
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 2): Healing increased from 977-1097 to 1075-1207.
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 3): Healing increased from 1222-1369 to 1344-1506.
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 4): Healing increased from 1528-1706 to 1681-1877
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 5): Healing increased from 1671-1866 to 1881-2053
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 3): Healing increased from 278-335 to 297-358.
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 4): Healing increased from 340-407 to 364-435.
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 5): Healing increased from 440-524 to 471-561.
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 6): Healing increased from 548-651 to 586-697.
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 7): Healing increased from 690-815 to 738-872.
>
>  Developer Comment: We've initially pulled down on the healing values of Priest healing spells with the tradeoff of increasing the power of Spiritual Healing in the Holy talent tree to offset this power, encouraging priests that want to heal to specialize into it and less so towards the Discipline support elements.
>  This inadvertently led to some ranks barely having any number difference between pre-level 30 and post-level 30 ranks as the healing reduction change was only applied to healing spells level 30 or higher. This also caused healing without specializing into Holy much harder while leveling after level 30, so we've looked into these healing spells to increase the base healing values for a middle ground between original and current healing numbers.
>  We hope these changes mend these problems and make healing without specializing smoother in leveling, don't mind the pun.
>
> ---
>  **Pain Spike:** Cooldown reduced from 40 seconds to 30 seconds.
>
> ---
>  **Fade:** All ranks now reduce your total threat by 15% in addition to the flat amount of threat.
>
>  Developer Comment: Fade being a flat amount of threat did not scale well both for the endgame and in the cases the threat values reach high values in longer fights, causing it to feel like a drop in the bucket.
>  For this reason we're adding on a percentage threat reduction in addition to the current flat threat, keeping Fade a powerful tool no matter the situation.
>
> ---
>  **Prayer of Healing:** Functionality reworked: "A powerful prayer healing your target and their party members within 30 yards for X to Y."
>  This means it can now be targeted to heal parties other than your own. Cast range remains at 40 yards.
>
>  Developer Comment: Prayer of Healing had the unwieldy limitation of only healing your own party, which made it very limited in raid environments.
>  With this change we aim to make it more versatile for its intended function of group healing and give agency over who gets the healing via the target and their party selection.
>
> ---
>  **Lightwell:** Now only has one rank, cooldown is reduced from 10 minutes to 5 minutes and its functionality is reworked: "Creates a holy Lightwell at a chosen location. When healing a friendly target with Lesser Heal, Flash Heal, Heal or Greater Heal, the Lightwell will heal an injured friendly target within 30 yards of its location with Splendor of Light, healing it for an amount equal to 20% of the initial healing spell, depleting a charge. Players cannot benefit from this effect more than once every 5 seconds. Lightwell lasts for 1 minute or 10 charges."
>
>  Developer Comment: Lightwell has stayed largely unused even after the additions of an earlier rank, a new talent and becoming a baseline spell due to it requiring manual use to utilize and often forcing players out of position.
>  Now it acts as a limited charge healing amplifier, causing your healing to be repeated as a percentage of its value on a wounded target if the target is within the range of the Lightwell and its healing amplification hasn't been triggered on the target for a few seconds.
>  We hope that this change shines some much needed light on Lightwell as a proper healing tool.
>
>  **Discipline**
> ---
>  **Searing Light:** Mana cost reduction increased from 50% to 60%.
>
>  **Holy**
> ---
>  **Reservoir of Light:** Effect reworked: "Increases the effectiveness of your Lightwell's Splendor of Light by 33/66/100%."
>
>  Developer Comment: We've changed the effect of this talent due to the major rework done on Lightwell and its functionality.
>  This means the healing amplification is increased from 20% of the healing to 26.6/33.3/40%.
>
> ---
>  **Spirit of Redemption:** Granted spirit increased from 5% to 10%.
>
> ---
>  New Talent: **Book of Prayer** (Row 5 / 2 Points):
>  "Whenever you cast a healing spell, you regain 15/30% of its mana cost if it is not a repeat of the previous healing spell."
>
> ---
>  **Swift Recovery:** Renamed to "Empowered Recovery" and now also increases duration of **Renew** by 3/6 seconds.
>
> ---
>  **Proclaim Champion**, **Empower Champion**, **Champion's Grace**, **Champion's Bond** and **Revive Champion**: Removed.
>
> ---
>  New Capstone: **Ascendance**
>  "Call upon your faith for divine aid. When activated, your healing spells cost 33% less mana, are cast 20% quicker and grant their targets the Apotheosis effect, increasing their healing taken by 15% for 10 seconds. Lasts for 30 seconds.
>
>  This spell can be cast while under crowd control effects and clears you of any of those when activated."
>  (280 Mana, 5 Minute Cooldown)
>
>  Developer Comment: Proclaim Champion and its connected spells have struggled to find its place, feeling more like a capstone you give to your target rather than elevating yourself and suffered from some conflicts in its functionality, increasing damage of the target, reducing damage taken and giving the Priest mana when the target takes damage which benefit damage dealers and the tank the most respectively which meant its full power could never be utilized on the same target in group content.
>  For this reason we've pivoting from a direct target buff to a power boosting capstone, meant to feel like a proper reward for mastering your role as a bringer of the Light.
>
>  **Shadow**
> ---
>  **Improved Fade:** Effect reworked: “Reduces the threat returned when Fade ends by 25/50%.”. Also moved to Row 4 from Row 3.
>
>  Developer Comment: Improved Fade has largely stayed unused, only having niche uses such as triggering tier set bonuses related to Fade more often.
>  In combination with the Fade total threat reduction addition, this rework should allow the Priest to instead permanently remove part of the normal temporary threat reduction, making it a valuable tool for threat management.
>
> ---
>  **Improved Mana Burn:** Moved from Row 3 to Row 4.
>
>  *Developer Comment: We've slightly adjusted Improved Mana Burn's talent location as Mana Burn is learned at level 24, meaning the talent upgraded a spell you didn't learn yet when the talent became accessible.*
>
> ---
>  **Shadow Reach:** Now a 2 pointer instead of 3 pointer, increasing the range of your Shadow damage spells by 10/20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: This point requirement reduction should better align this talent with similiar range increase talents that also cost 2 points.*
>
> ---
>  **Shadow Weaving:** Effect reworked: “Your Shadow damage spells have a 20/40/60/80/100% chance to grant you Shadow Weaving for 10 sec. Your Shadow damage spells apply a vulnerability increasing Shadow damage taken by 3% per stack of Shadow Weaving for 15 sec. Stacks up to 5 times.”
>
>  Developer Comment: Shadow Weaving struggles heavily when there are multiple targets the Priest has to focus on, especially in the cases those targets die faster than Shadow Weaving can be accumulated on them, preventing them from reaching their full potential both in terms of damage and supporting other Shadow damage dealers.
>  We've shifted Shadow Weaving to be instead an effect that accumulates on the Priest themselves that applies the amount of stacks you accumulate on yourself as the Shadow damage increase debuff on the targets, allowing easier application for multiple targets and carrying over these stacks between creature packs if they're close.
>
>
>
>
>  **ROGUE**
>
>  We’re generally happy with the recent changes to Rogue, and community feedback shows that the class is largely performing as intended. That said, in reviewing data across multiple environments, we've identified that Rogue is currently a bit overperformant in certain areas.
>
>  To address this, we're making a few targeted numerical adjustments aimed at bringing performance back in line without changing how the class fundamentally plays.
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  **Poisons:** Reduced scaling at lower ranks:
>
>  Deadly Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 30):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 2 (Level 38):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 3 (Level 46):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 4 (Level 54):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> 1% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (4% Scaling Total)
>
>  Instant Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 20):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 2 (Level 28):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 1% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 3 (Level 36):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 1% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 4 (Level 44):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 2% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 5 (Level 52):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 2% Attack Power Scaling
>
>  Corrosive Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 56):** 1.9% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (7.6% Scaling Total) -> 1% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (4% Scaling Total)
>
>  Dissolvent Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 52):** 4.75% Attack Power Scaling -> 2% Attack Power Scaling
>
>  *Developer Comment: Early access to higher poison scaling was resulting in stronger-than-intended performance during leveling and early gearing. This change smooths out that curve while preserving endgame effectiveness.*
>
> ---
>  **Blade Flurry:** Reduced Energy regeneration penalty from 30% to 20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Blade Flurry should feel like a powerful cleave tool without overly punishing resource flow. This adjustment helps improve its usability while keeping its overall power in check.*
>
>  **Assassination**
> ---
>  **Taste for Blood:** Physical damage bonus reduced from 1/2/3% to 1/1.5/2% and no longer increases damage dealt by Corrosive Poison and Dissolvent Poison.
>  **Noxious Assault:** Attack Power- scaling reduced from 35% to 30%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: As mentioned earlier, adjusting the power of Rogue.*
>
>  **Combat**
> ---
>  **Opportunity:** Opportunity: Damage bonus reduced from 4/8/12/16/20% to 3/6/9/12/15%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Combat dagger rogues are performing tad better than with any other weapons, this nerf will bring them more in line.*
>
>
>
>
>  **SHAMAN**
>
>  Physical DPS Enhancement will see some small tweaks in patch 1.18.1. Tank Enhancement and spell-power–focused Enhancement, however, are getting more meaningful updates to their core talents. These changes are aimed at strengthening each playstyle’s identity and reducing overlap with similar mechanics found in other classes.
>
>  **General**
>
>  **Lightning Shield:** Mana cost reduced across the board by roughly 25%
>  **Rank 1 (Level 8):** 45 -> 40
>  **Rank 2 (Level 16):** 80 -> 70
>  **Rank 3 (Level 24):** 125 -> 105
>  **Rank 4 (Level 32):** 180 -> 150
>  **Rank 5 (Level 40):** 240 -> 200
>  **Rank 6 (Level 48):** 305 -> 255
>  **Rank 7 (Level 56):** 370 -> 310
>
>
>  **Enhancement**
>
>  **Stormstrike:** Can no-longer roll and trigger **Windfury Weapon**'s effect twice.
>
> ---
>  **Windfury Weapon:** Each hit now has a 25% chance (was 20%).
>
> ---
>   All of the following changes are to affect **Elemental Weapons** and its sub-effects:
>
>  **Windfury:** Reworked to the following effect: “Gaining extra attacks increases your attack speed by 1% for 5 sec. Stacks up to 2/4/6 times.”
>
>  **Flametongue:** Reworked to the following effect: “Hitting enemies with your attacks increases the damage done by your Fire Totems and spells by 10/20/30% for 5 sec.”
>
>  *Developer Comment: Requiring the Shaman to actively engage in melee combat to keep the Fire damage increase active should make this effect lean more towards spell oriented Enhancement Shaman gameplay while requiring pure Fire damage Elemental Shamans to stay in melee range to utilize its full power.*
>
>  **Rockbiter:** Reworked to the following effect: “Your physical damage builds up an earthen bulwark for 20% of the damage dealt, tripled while you're wearing a shield. The earthen bulwark absorbs 5/10/15% of incoming damage for 8 seconds or until the bulwark mitigates enough damage. The bulwark's durability cannot exceed 20% of your maximum health.”
>
>  *Developer Comment: Changing the Rockbiter Weapon effect from a passive damage reduction into an active component that's kept up by attacking should feel make it feel more active in active usage while deterring non-Enhancement specializations from using the effect as a passive benefit which led to them being more durable, especially in Player vs Player environments.*
>
> ---
>  **Flurry:** Reworked to the following effect “Increases your attack speed by 8/11/14/17/20% for your next 3 swings after dealing a critical strike.”
>
>  *Developer Comment: This change should increase the uptime of Flurry especially for spell oriented Enhancement Shaman gameplay, making it less punishing to have less physical critical strike chance compared to their physical oriented counterpart.*
>
> ---
>  **Lightning Strike:** Water Shield's Attack Power-to-Mana ratio changed from 20:1 to 18:1.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Shields are central to our vision of Enhancement, they are the specialization's biggest sink of mana, expecially in contexts where AOE damage is involved. This should improve the dependability of the specialization's mana bar.*
>
>
>  **Elemental**
>
>  **Eye of the Storm:** Renamed to **Call of Earth:**
>
>  "Earth Shield gains 1/2 additional charges and grants an additional 35/70% chance to avoid interruption while casting a spell."
>
> ---
>  **Elemental Fury:** Now also affects Frost spells.
> ---
>  **Earthquake:** Base damage values increased by 15%, cooldown reduced from 20 seconds to 18 seconds.
>  New Damage Values:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 40):** 227-253 -> 262-291
>  **Rank 2 (Level 50):** 343-387 -> 395-446
>  **Rank 3 (Level 60):** 510-551 -> 587-634
>
>  Developer Comment: When designing a class, we often look for ways to blend flavor with function. While this frequently involves fitting a square peg into a triangular slot, Elemental is particularly well suited to aligning form and function when enough creativity is applied. Proper spell pushback resistance has long been missing from Elemental, as Eye of the Storm saw little use in either PvP or PvE: in the former, critical hits occurred infrequently enough that the talent was often skipped, while in the latter, critical hits were almost always fatal regardless. As a result, we’ve decided to retire the talent in favor of a solution that better serves its intended purpose, while also reinforcing Elemental’s thematic identity. With this change, the Elemental tree now answers the call of Earth, Flame, and Thunder—now if only we could find a way to introduce the Call of Wind in time for the 21st of September.
>
>  Although we generally view Elemental Shields as a concept better suited to Enhancement gameplay, and Water Shield as central to Restoration’s mana sustain, we are happy to give Earth Shield a place within the Elemental specialization. This allows Elemental shamans to make more meaningful use of the Earth element beyond its capstone talent. Note that the bonus from Earth’s Poise, the buff granted by this talent, stacks additively with other sources of spell pushback reduction.
>
>  The changes to Earthquake are intended to elevate the spell into a capstone worthy not just in form, but in function. While the adjustments themselves are straightforward, our goal is to encourage shamans to use the spell in a wider range of scenarios, addressing the fact that its original damage values often felt underwhelming.
>
>
>  **Tier Bonus Changes**
>
> - **Restoration Shaman Tier 1 (3 Set):** Changed description to clarify the totem radius is increased by 10 yards and not set to 30 yards.
>
> ---
>
> - **Restoration Shaman Tier 1 (8 Set):** Reworked to the following: "Your Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave have a 25% chance to surround the target with an earth wall, absorbing 250 damage. Lasts 6 sec.".
>  *As a final note, the Shaman class development team would like to sincerely thank the small, close-knit Shaman community. The thoughtful feedback shared on community servers and forums has been incredibly valuable, and it has played an important role alongside our usual log analysis work. We're confident it will continue to be valuable for the future development of the class as a whole.*
>
>
>
>
>
>
>  **WARLOCK**
>
>  This patch aims to bring more quality of life and to deal with some unresolved issues limiting certain playstyles. We will also address parts of warlock's kit that are problematic in PvP.
>
>  **General**
>
> ---
>  **Curse of Exhaustion:** mana cost increased from 8% to 14% base mana. (from 110 to 190 at lvl 60)
>
> ---
>  **Curse of Tongues:** Rank 1 cast speed reduction reduced from 50% to 30%.
>  Rank 2 Mana cost increased from 110 to 240.
>
>  *Developer Comment: We're giving the most powerful debilitating curses a cost increase better matching their impact.*
>
> ---
>  **Enslave Demon:** Now reduces healing taken by the enslaved demon by 50%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: The healing reduction is getting adjusted and shifted from Master Demonologist, so instead of affecting the warlock, it'll now affect Greater demons and enslaved demons found in the world (and instances).*
>
> ---
>  **Ritual of Doom:** initial cast time increased from 5 seconds to 7 seconds and the ritual channel duration reduced from 5 sec to 3 sec.
>
> ---
>  **Felhunter** and **Infernal:** Armor reduced by 30%, resulting in about 5% lower damage reduction against physical attacks.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Felhunter is a bit too well-rounded while Infernal's damage and health increase compared to vanilla justifies a little pull on their damage reduction when targeted.*
>
> ---
>  **Felguard:** **Legion Strike**'s healing reduction increased from 10% to 25%.
>
> ---
>  **Felguard:** **Axe Toss**' stun duration reduced from 4 seconds to 2 seconds.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Stun of such duration often means a guaranteed kill in combination with Felguard's raw power, so we're giving the victim a more fair chance at survival.*
>
> ---
>  **Searing Pain:** Global cooldown reduced from 1.5 seconds to 1 second.
>
>  *Developer Comment: We're resolving the Searing Pain's lack of ability to benefit from haste effects, leaning into its swift spikey character.*
>
> ---
>  **Hellfire:** Spell power scaling increased from 2.2% to 4.125% per tick and mana cost is now reduced on the initial cast while costing mana for every second channeled.
>  **Rank 1 (Level 30):** 645 Mana -> 160 Mana + 30 Mana/Second
>  **Rank 2 (Level 42):** 975 Mana -> 240 Mana + 50 Mana/Second
>  **Rank 3 (Level 54):** 1300 Mana -> 325 Mana + 65 Mana/Second
>
> ---
>  **Ritual of Souls:** Soul Shard requirement increased from 1 to 3.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Since its creation it has been intended for the Ritual of Souls to require more Soul Shards than simply conjuring a single Healthstone.*
>
> ---
>  **Soulwell:** Now has a new model.
>
>  *Developer Comment: This is to differentiate it from the Ritual of Doom.*
>
> ---
>  **Curse of Recklessness:** Global cooldown reduced from 1.5 seconds to 1 second.
>
>  *Developer Comment: For too long has the fear-juggling technique gone unnoticed, unsupported - no more.*
>
>
>  **Affliction**
> ---
>  **Sinister Pursuit:** Changed into a 2-point Demonology talent, permanently increasing your pets movement speed by 5/10%. This includes greater demons.
>  **Master Conjuror:** Removed.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Since this talent has been having trouble finding its niche, we're moving it to be a staple Demonology talent in much simpler form. Being able to have 3 types of the same Healthstone has also not been intended.*
>
>
>  **Demonology**
> ---
>  **Master Summoner:** Now also reduces the cooldown of **Ritual of Doom** by 25/50%.
>
> ---
>  **Master Demonologist:** Greater Demons' healing reduction removed from its effect.
>
> ---
>  **Unleashed Potential:** Now also provides the Warlock with a tracking buff.
>
> ---
>  **Soul Link:** Damage transfer reduced from 25% to 20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Due to removal of the healing reduction from the warlock with Greater demons and because the recently introduced PvP dampening has been more beneficial for classes focusing on survivability, we're balancing out demonology warlock's durability.*
>
>  **Tier Bonus Changes**
>
> - **Affliction Warlock Tier 3 (4 Set):** Effect changed to the following: "Your Curse of Agony does 100% increased damage for the first 4 ticks.".
>
> ---
>
> - **Affliction Warlock Tier 3.5 (3 Set):** Amount of mana gained from health drained by Siphon Life reduced from 50% to 25%.
>
>  **WARRIOR**
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  Removed cooldown from **Hamstring**.
>
>  *Developer Comment: ![💀](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f480.svg).*
>
>
>  **Fury**
> ---
>  **Improved Whirlwind:** Renamed to **Ravager** and now has an additional effect:
>  "Reduces the cooldown of **Whirlwind** by 1/1.5/2 seconds and rage cost of **Cleave** by 1/2/3."
>
>  *Developer Comment: Talent points could previously be spent before Whirlwind was learned, which caused confusion for new players. We’ve added a small rage cost Reduction to cleave to fix this inconsistency without affecting balance in a significant way.*
>
> ---
>  Cast time reduction granted to **Slam** by **Flurry** has been corrected. For example, with 5 points spent in Flurry, Slam cast time will now properly be 1.92 seconds instead of 1.75 seconds.
>
>  *Developer Comment: In the previous patch, Flurry was updated to reduce Slam cast time, but an incorrect formula resulted in more reduction than intended.*
>
>
>  **Arms**
> ---
>  Swapped position of **Boundless Anger** and **Precision Cut** talents.
>
> ---
>  **Precision Cut:** Changed to the following:
>  "Increases the damage done per extra rage point spent on **Execute** by 25/50/75%."
>
>  *Developer Comment: The previous redesign of Precision Cut did not deliver satisfying Execute gameplay and made the ability feel underwhelming. Restoring increased damage per Rage spent allows Execute to better fulfill its role as a high-impact finisher for Arms Warriors.*
>
>
>  **Protection**
> ---
>  **Defiance:** Changed to:
>  "Increases the threat generated while in Defensive Stance by an additional 4/8/12/15/20%."
>
> ---
>  **Shield Slam:** Attack Power scaling increased from 15% to 20% and its additonal threat modifier is increased from 50% to 75%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Protection Warriors have been falling behind other tanks. These changes provide targeted improvements, while a more comprehensive review of the Protection talent tree and overall kit is planned for the future.*
>
>  **Tier Bonus Changes**
>
> - **Arms/Fury Warrior Tier 1 (3 Set):** Effect changed to the following: "Whenever you hit with an ability, you have 10% chance to gain 15 rage.".
>
> ---
>
> - **Arms/Fury Warrior Tier 3 (4 Set):** Effect changed to the following: "Increases the critical strike damage bonus of your abilities by 4%.".

First time posting on forum, finally got around to logging in here to voice my concerns about holy priest's changes. Love you guys, but not fond of these holy priest changes at all.

> This also caused healing without specializing into Holy much harder while leveling after level 30, so we've looked into these healing spells to increase the base healing values for a middle ground between original and current healing numbers.
>  We hope these changes mend these problems and make healing without specializing smoother in leveling, don't mind the pun.

Shouldn't the two priest specs dedicated to other niches (discipline, shadow) *have difficulty healing at such levels?* Why shouldn't they struggle to heal, if they haven't put enough points into healing talents? Will leveling holy priests (don't laugh, I really did it) be given changes to increase their DPS and general utility ala shadow/discipline above 30 as well? Why allow them to (competently) heal without a healing spec at high levels when holy priests can't (competently) DPS at high levels?

> Lightwell: Now only has one rank, cooldown is reduced from 10 minutes to 5 minutes and its functionality is reworked: "Creates a holy Lightwell at a chosen location. When healing a friendly target with Lesser Heal, Flash Heal, Heal or Greater Heal, the Lightwell will heal an injured friendly target within 30 yards of its location with Splendor of Light, healing it for an amount equal to 20% of the initial healing spell, depleting a charge. Players cannot benefit from this effect more than once every 5 seconds. Lightwell lasts for 1 minute or 10 charges."
>  Developer Comment: Lightwell has stayed largely unused even after the additions of an earlier rank, a new talent and becoming a baseline spell due to it requiring manual use to utilize and often forcing players out of position.
>  Now it acts as a limited charge healing amplifier, causing your healing to be repeated as a percentage of its value on a wounded target if the target is within the range of the Lightwell and its healing amplification hasn't been triggered on the target for a few seconds.
>  We hope that this change shines some much needed light on Lightwell as a proper healing tool.

I always liked lightwell for its relatively unique utility. I recall a few situations where I'm healing a small group A, and small group B is in trouble; drop a lightwell to tide them over and pick up group B, easy. The ability to leave a self-healing station anywhere is interesting, and it's quite useful for focus-healing a tank if you drop it in a tactical position.

> Swift Recovery: Renamed to "Empowered Recovery" and now also increases duration of Renew by 3/6 seconds.

Actually very fond of this change, the original talent felt a little useless for a spec that typically isn't taking hits otherwise

> Proclaim Champion, Empower Champion, Champion's Grace, Champion's Bond and Revive Champion: Removed.
>  New Capstone: Ascendance
>  "Call upon your faith for divine aid. When activated, your healing spells cost 33% less mana, are cast 20% quicker and grant their targets the Apotheosis effect, increasing their healing taken by 15% for 10 seconds. Lasts for 30 seconds.
>
>  This spell can be cast while under crowd control effects and clears you of any of those when activated."
>  (280 Mana, 5 Minute Cooldown)

This is the one that really irks me the most. I really loved proclaim champion for the flavor and unique utility that it provided, especially with the different additional buffs associated with it. This change feels extremely bland and boring.

Feels like these changes are encroaching on what made holy priests unique, and are a step towards issues that previous rebalances sought to (and largely did) resolve

## Post 166189 by Kallegan — 2026-01-24T01:41:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166189#p166189 | page 45 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

> **Blade Flurry:** Reduced Energy regeneration penalty from 30% to 20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Blade Flurry should feel like a powerful cleave tool without overly punishing resource flow. This adjustment helps improve its usability while keeping its overall power in check.*
>
>  **Assassination**
> ---
>  **Taste for Blood:** Physical damage bonus reduced from 1/2/3% to 1/1.5/2% and no longer increases damage dealt by Corrosive Poison and Dissolvent Poison.
>  **Noxious Assault:** Attack Power- scaling reduced from 35% to 30%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: As mentioned earlier, adjusting the power of Rogue.*
>
>  **Combat**
> ---
>  **Opportunity:** Opportunity: Damage bonus reduced from 4/8/12/16/20% to 3/6/9/12/15%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Combat dagger rogues are performing tad better than with any other weapons, this nerf will bring them more in line.*

Assasination:
Prior to this patch, Assassination Rogues faced two main issues:

- 1. Poor scaling, resulting in above-average performance in early raids and below-average performance in late raids.

- 2. A lack of weapon progression, resulting in little variety despite the specialization's intention to make use of fast weapons. For example: After Alcor (a pre-raid item) provides more damage thanks to poison procs than weapons from subsequent raids, up to Naxx.
These changes have done nothing to change the situation, and will even exaggerate it. The nerf to Noxious Assault will make it less viable as time goes on, and since most of the damage comes from poisons and not Nox, things will not change for Ambershire, and Assa will remain dominant.

Now then, how can we fix these issues? My proposal is as follows:

- Modify the scaling of poisons while reducing their base damage, so that their damage would be slightly lower in early raids, but by scaling better, they would be much more effective in later raids.

- Add a damage modifier to Noxxious Assault, which increases its damage by 5% for every 0.1 less speed (per hand), up to a maximum of 1.8 or 2.0. This would aim to make slower weapons more competitive, granting physical damage that slightly compensates for the loss in poison procs that comes with equipping a slower weapon. If it is too strong, it can be reduced; if it is too weak, it can be increased, and it remains to be seen whether the correct range is 1.30 to 1.80 or 1.50 to 2.0. With this, slower weapons in later raids would become useful, given that weapons with a speed of 1.8 are plentyful, while 1.3 weapons are non-existant.
Combat:

On the other hand, Combat faced two problems:
- 1. It was unviable in early raids due to its need for agility to be competitive.

- 2. Sinister Strike had an energy overcap due to its high agility with late raid gear (unlike its counterpart, Backstab).
Although the changes to Taste for Blood and Opportunity are understandable, this has not solved the other problems with the spec.

- The first of these problems is difficult to solve, given that it is due to a combination of power creep, high assassination effectiveness, and a lack of decent bonuses. In my opinion, the best way to solve it would be to include tiers that grant more agility.

- As for the second problem, the proposal would be to create: Either a new finisher that consumes all energy to deal damage and is limited to maces/swords/axes/fist weapons. Or a new combo point generator that consumes 80 energy, grants 2 combo points, and inflicts high damage (at least comparable to 2 Sinister Strikes). This will alleviate the problem by providing a way to dump energy without reaching the cap.
Subtlely

Broadly speaking, this is the spec that has undergone the fewest changes, but even so, it has been hit hard by the nerf to Taste for Blood, an unnecessary change that offers no compensation. At the same time, the useless Smoke Bomb talent still exists. For this reason, I propose replacing Smoke Bomb with another talent:
Code: Select all

```
Improved Bleeds: Enemies affected by Garrote or Rupture take 5% more damage from the rogue.
```

This serves three purposes: it returns the damage unfairly lost due to the Taste for Blood nerf, replaces the useless Smoke Bomb talent, and grants an extra damage benefit accessible during leveling (something that is currently lacking).

## Post 166192 by Snoof — 2026-01-24T02:05:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166192#p166192 | page 45 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Swapping Precision Cut and Boundless Anger's places in the talent tree is super detrimental to Arms. Boundless Anger has always been a talent barely anybody takes because a Warrior who's actively using their abilities only ever shoots up to 100 rage from big Windfury crits. Making it mandatory forces Arms warriors to choose between Master of Arms and Enrage from the Fury tree, which are both core talents that having a little more damage on high rage executes doesn't even come close to making up for the loss of. It feels like the rework was made around this idea that warriors are gonna sit there in execute phase building up this huge 130 rage bar to land one huge execute to end the fight, but that's just not how the ability is used; in execute phase, you spam execute because the base damage of the ability is so high it would be silly not to and because the chance of scoring a WF proc to raise your rage for the next one is too good to pass up, and the numbers presented aren't anywhere near high enough to change that play-pattern.

Right now, this would just a big fat nerf for a spec that's already underperforming. I would strongly suggest at least removing the requirement to take one talent before you can have the other if you're gonna do this because, I can't stress this enough, nobody wants to have to take Boundless Anger.

As for the Flurry Slam changes... Why?
I do understand that the way it works right now happened by accident, but is it really an accident that needs fixing? People like playing 2H Fury. It's fast, it's hard hitting, it feels great to use and there's enough timing and resource management that goes into it that it feels really rewarding to practice and get better at. These changes look like they're gonna break the spec's ability to use WW and BT in between auto attacks, which would gut the spec's damage on bosses and, worse yet, make it less fun to play. To do that in a patch where the only 'new' alternative being offered up is 'Arms but slightly worse' would be really disappointing.

It's not like it's horrendously broken either. It's pretty good, don't get me wrong, but if you go look at Turtlogs it's not like warriors are crushing everybody on the meters. Look at any given high tier boss fight; you won't find a 2H warrior at the top of the meters unless it's a cleave fight, which, notably, are the only ones where they barely use slam at all.

## Post 166216 by Fugus (Patch Note Conspiracy Theorist) — 2026-01-24T06:43:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166216#p166216 | page 46 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

> **Eluaria wrote: Sat Jan 24, 2026 6:33 am**
> No, they absolutely shouldn't. That is one of the worst takes I have heard in a while. PvP Balance is absolute garbage unless you tackle it separately from PvE. It's always been this way. And when it hasn't been seperate, some classes were next to unplayable.

I have to disagree, the worst possible take to me as the idea that abilities should work differently in PvP than they do in PvE so that you have to relearn how your class plays between the two because you abilities aren’t the same. Doubly so when they not only change in PvE to PvP but they also changed differently per class and spec.

PvP balance can actually be handled while keeping PvE in line with it. Some simple rules to help achieve it.

 1. If the damage is too high in PvP, it’s too high in PvE, tone it down and adjust PvE accordingly.

 2. If the mitigation is too high in PvP, it’s too high in PvE, tone it down and adjust PvE accordingly.

 3. If the healing is too high in PvP, it’s too high in PvE, tone it down and adjust PvE accordingly.

 4. If the spell is too strong in PvP, it shouldn’t even exist in PvE, remove it from the spell book and adjust PvE accordingly.

The luxury of PvE is that you can adjust those values per mob and encounter any way you need without breaking anything else.

If you are talking about being 100% balanced in all areas, you never will in PvP or PvE so that’s not really a argument, you just strive to get as close as you can.

## Post 166270 by Possum — 2026-01-24T13:16:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166270#p166270 | page 46 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

What's the goal with all the tank changes long term? Across all the patches turtle wow has had, tanks have been brought closer into line with each other in what they do: more equal threat on single target and multi target, more equal mitigation passively and from class cooldowns. Is the long term goal to eventually have all tank specs as equals with raiders favouring whichever happens to currently be slightly stronger?

It feels like a very slow but steady departure from what were very specific and defined niches. I will lay these niches out to illustrate the point, please don't take them as literal points to be argued but as examples of what a designer may be writing down as defining points for each respective tank spec that needs to be used as a framework when making balance adjustments to maintain clear and unique reasons for each different tank class/spec existing within the game:

- Paladins excel at AoE tanking with abilities like consecrate to generate big AoE threat, buffs like reckoning that scale up in power the more enemy hits you are taking at the same time, and even the old "kings spam" that they would do to generate AoE threat at ranged distances.

- Warriors in base vanilla had access to the best defensive cooldowns that no other tanks could compete with: shield wall, last stand and lifegiving gem. They also had the best selection of passive mitigation talents and gear to pair with these cooldowns (+defense/block/dodge/parry etc.). If you needed serious mitigation, you needed warriors tanking. *Warriors deviated from intended design goals using dual wield furyprot, but even this still occupied the unique niche of "deals the best threat, but takes the most damage"*

- Druid tanks in vanilla did not have strong defensive cooldowns or passive mitigation like warriors, and they did not have strong AoE threat like paladins. What they did have though was exceptional *balance* between threat and mitigation. For every point of damage a bear may take, they would be building up threat quicker than any other tank class regardless of whether they were wearing mitigation or threat heavy gear sets.

- Shaman tanks were never good at level 60 in vanilla, and this was confirmed by the developers as intentional. They were supposed to be viable while levelling but deliberately fall off at the higher levels. Not much to say except that the design goal of having extra classes available to act as tanks while levelling is always useful considering how necessary the role is in group content.
In turtle we can still see paladins are unmatched AoE tanks, but they also seem to deal similar single target threat as other tank classes.

Prot warriors can still mitigate damage very effectively, but other tank classes have been given similar defensive cooldowns and lots of new mitigation gear choices so the prot warriors claim as "mitigation kings" doesn't really hold up like it used to.

Bears now have strong defensive cooldowns like warriors (berserk, feral barkskin and buffed frenzied regen) alongside lots of new gear choices leading them out of their beautiful "jack of trades, master of none" between threat and mitigation into some unbalanced ground where they are still doing good threat but simultaneously occupy the mitigation niche that prot warriors had. Now we see their threat is being nerfed in this most recent balance patch, pushing them further towards the same niche that prot warriors occupied and away from the original bear niche of having the most threat generated per point of damage mitigated (but not the best mitigation, or the best threat in isolation).

Shaman tanks have been made viable at 60 which begs the question: what is their tanking niche? I haven't played with shaman tanks closely enough to comment on this, or how shaman tanks are affecting the niches other tanks occupy so I can say no more about them.

If you want all the tanks to be meta, you don't need to make them all the same. You can make each tank class different. Really, really different. If there's a tank class that far excels all others when it is tanking 10+ enemies, does better than most when it is tanking 2-9 enemies, and does poorly when it is tanking 1 enemy, that tank class is meta for AoE fights. As long as AoE fights exist that tank fills a useful role. It should not be as good as the other tank classes when it is tanking 1 enemy, that would ruin the distinctive and tasty flavour of it and all the other tank classes as they all blend into one similar, unremarkable flavour. This goes for every possible situation tanks land in - fights that check mitigation (e.g. enrages, raid-wide CC, or high constant damage dealt), fights that check threat (dps gain temporary buffs that increases their damage dealt massively, tank threat gets reduced/removed by enemy abilities, time-bomb raid wipe mechanics that leave no time for "wait for tank to build threat"), fights that interact with specific resource bars (enemy casts spells on players with/without specific resource e.g. detonate mana, or reduce rage generation to 1/10th of normal), plus the oddities like having a boss that casts polymorph or unique movement impairing effects (druid tank required) or is immune to physical damage so a caster tank is needed (twin emperors). All of these things can be used to exclude or demand specific tank classes in a way that lets each one be properly unique.

This approach lets you solve a problem posed as "Tank class X has no defensive cooldowns compared to tank class Y" as not a problem at all, because tank class X isn't designed to be a defensive cooldown tank. That's tank class Y's niche so of course it has more defensive cooldowns. Tank class X makes up for it by generating far more threat than tank class Y. Both X and Y can be useful and appreciated in end game content as tanks despite being nothing like each other. And if everyone starts using the tank class X (threat focused) and tank class Y (mitigation focused) isn't seeing anyone play it because its "underpowered", instead of trying to homogenise the two, lean further into them to maintain balance: *reduce the mitigation capabilities of tank class X instead of buffing the threat capabilities of tank class Y*

If any developers read this through and it gets you thinking, thank you for your time. I appreciate the effort that goes into the development and want to see the game continue to carry on the legacy of vanilla+ that you are all putting so much effort in to

## Post 166311 by Zogzogladin — 2026-01-24T17:14:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166311#p166311 | page 47 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Swapping Librams, Totems, and Idols in combat was not just a “quirk”, it was a source of real gameplay depth for the classes that use them. It added decision-making, skill expression, and life to the game. Knowing when and what to swap makes combat more engaging and rewarding, especially for players who enjoy optimizing and mastering their class.

This mechanic also created unique content for these classes, helping them feel distinct and interesting compared to others. Removing or heavily penalizing it by enforcing a GCD reduces that depth and makes gameplay feel more rigid and less dynamic.

On a personal level, I spent over a month developing an addon specifically designed around this mechanic, because I believed it was a meaningful and interesting part of the game. Seeing it effectively invalidated by this change is genuinely disappointing.

I understand the desire to prevent abuse, but I believe this decision removes more value than it adds. The ability to swap these items in combat gave the game personality and rewarded player investment. Enforcing a full GCD on every swap feels like an unnecessary restriction that hurts gameplay rather than improving it.

## Post 166320 by Zephyer123 — 2026-01-24T18:34:00Z

For the Bear Druid Nerf:

I feel the percentage reduction is too much, huge nerf. Currently when tanking on druid I'm either battling top dps for threat, or after some random good crits I start to pull ahead in threat (Ambershire). A better approach would be to reduce threat produced by crits only, otherwise bears suck now.

My main focus has been prioritizing attack power to increase threat over mitigation gear to be able to maintain threat. At 850 AP in bear +/- unbuffed. I get about 800-900 threat for one hit with maul non crit, and generally the same for savage bite also non crit. So if i don't miss, my opening threat is about 1.5k. Rage pots are mandatory for tanking, to be able to build that initial threat, and a prehot before a fight. Druids are doing everything available to them to be able to build good single target threat and currently its managable. I feel like if you look at the threat produced unbuffed, its actually subpar, but when full buffed, everyone on salv, rage pot, prehot, we still battle dps until we can pull ahead off of random crit threat. I can see better gear resulting in more crits and better threat, but certainly not on ambershire yet.

Please watch some of the meters in raids, from my perspective this is crazy.

For the Prot Paladin Nerf:

I also tank on a paladin (Ambershire). Spell power has become priority over mitigation to increase threat as well. With a build that includes sanctity aura to increase holy damage threat. Currently with 368 SP and 361 Def unbuffed i battle top dps, however I do feel i pull ahead mid fights similarly to druid with the additional threat produced from seal, holy shield, sanc. With an opening judgement of seal of righteousness and a holy strike I can produce about 2.9k threat (damage from holy strike hits for around 650 = 1.75k threat), add 6 seconds of concentration its 4000 threat. Sustained unbuffed TPS around 600-650per second without holy shield/sanc. When everyone is buffed in raids we are essentially equal to dps in threat production versus damage production while they are salved. Add in holy shield and blessing sanc holy damage and we pull slightly ahead in TPS. Crits definitely help.

By reducing righteous strike threat from 30% to 25% this hurts. Now 1.66k threat.

By scaling with spell power at first it seems nice, but 650 holy damage per holy strike now to around 400 holy is a lot of threat reduced. From 1.66k to 1k threat, excluding the 40% weapon damage because thats like 75 damage who cares.

 40% physical damage is crap, its 1 to 1 threat without a modifier and all caster weapons are also locked at 40 dps, and most are fast, which makes this addition junk until t3.5 desecration sword.

Paladins have better threat production than druids but its always a battle. With this nerf my threat opener will be reduced from 4000 in 6 seconds to 3000. Hard to calc what that will do to TPS, maybe now were 650 buffed, where dps is doing 700 dps with salv (1000 no salv) it ultimately means now warriors are MT only, or flask every raid to do the same threat you do now and barely get by.

Please look at reworking this as TPS is would be reduced to shit until t3+. I'm in favor of buffing warrior threat, but not at the expense of druids and paladins because quite honestly their threat is on par with dps salved now.

## Post 166324 by Clockeyes — 2026-01-24T19:15:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166324#p166324 | page 47 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

MM hunter changes are interesting but I think will ultimately not translate very well to engaging gameplay. Hunters being flavoured around adaptability would be awesome, and this is a step in the right direction. The idea of a Primer and Detonator system is super cool, but we should be able to choose which ammos we are using, like how our Aspects have a toolbar. Viper will help with mana issues, but will come at a dps cost. We will go OOM much, much faster than we currently do spamming steady shot, so the burst dps would have to be significant to offset a more sustainable rotation like SS spam. I don't think we are going to get that. As it stand, the ammo types feels like bells and whistles more than an engaging, game-sense check and skill-expressive rotation. Letting us choose the ammo type fixes some of this. I would personally also swap the stings to being the primers to the aimed shot being the detonater, but that's just me.

Steady shot and Aimed Shot will also need better scaling, hunters' scaling up into t3 is abyssmal.

I also wouldn't change Aimed Shot's cast time by that much. The drama of slowly taking aim and then seeing a huge damage number feels amazing when it hits. Making it just another steady shot takes away it's identity for no reason. The problem isn't the cast time, it's the damage. To fix this, Aimed Shot should do True Damage and for pvp give 50% healing like in later iterations. This will give MM hunters a flavor like that of a ranged Arms warrior, which feels appropriate.

For pvp hunters are still bottom of the barrel. They are the easiest to kill. They have no mobility (cheetah is a trap especially if you have even a little lag or don't have extremely meme builds around move speed), have no cleanse, have no counterattack anymore, MM and BM can't use traps for cc in combat, have no self heal, have no bubble or armor boosting talents/spells. They are one shot by WF shamans, killed by rogues before their stunlock is over, killed by warlocks before their Fear is over, etc. There are two easy fixes for this. First, make Cheetah actually useful. Hunters' skill expression is in kiting and positioning. Cheetah, being their greatest tool for this, it should give the hunter an edge not be a deathwish (especially if you are pvping with less than perfect latency and getting warrior charged from half a mile away). To do this, Cheetah should not daze, you should only lose the bonus movement for the 3 second period, hell for longer even, I'm all for punishment if you fail to kite well, but the punishment is too severe. That way if you fail to kite well you are still punished by a charge/hamstring, but getting a random hit while kiting well won't make you instant honor for enemies. At the very least, it shouldn't be a 30% daze, maybe 10% daze for 2 seconds. Second, hunters have no identity as marksmen in pvp. Our guns are are on equal range footing as mages hurling huge chunks of ice. MM hunters should out range all other casters by 5m-10m (with talent points deep in MM tree). Doing this means that hunters' horrible survivability is justified. If something gets onto you it's your fault, not the design, not lag. Those two simple changes will justify hunters being the easiest class to kill while not breaking the game and having to introduce new abilities like adding counterattack back. And it allows them to actually play with the identity they were designed to have.

Steady Shot needs to be castable while moving.

Others have mentioned wanting a Trap Launhcer, I very much agree.

One other idea I had was for a sniper ability, like Camoflauge. Where hunters become stealthed (low grade, easily spottable within 20m) and their first shot out of Camo is a Crit. This will give area denial like a rogue, if you know one is holding a flag you think twice. This is another way to gived Aimed Shot its identity, and feels perfectly in line with what MM hunter is all about.

Sorry for wall of text. Thanks for your time.

*Last edited by Clockeyes on Sun Jan 25, 2026 6:47 pm, edited 1 time in total.*

## Post 166329 by Icedxylophone — 2026-01-24T19:40:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166329#p166329 | page 47 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Just a quick, but long posts of some of my thoughts.

I've asked to get more talents Points, and 2 extra points from Boat was an example I used, so I'm happy with that, and being able to have some flexibility and potentially have mana talents, with my pushback protection, but I don't understand why we would get a dmg nerf when our dmg is already among the lowest, and we have minor utility. Every other caster has had a build with functional mana, and pushback protection, so it was just a fix to make us more aligned with the other casters. I'm also unsure how the change to BoaT will change our mana, 2 points in reflection is nice, but with an increased cost to wrath on trash/mobs that die quickly like in dungeons/raids, we can't use the last kill target as our dot mob, or while leveling it will be worse, and on bosses it will be more reliable ofc unless the boss had multiple mobs, but with the 5 set we almost had a free Wrath per proc, so I don't expect it to move the needle.

I wanted the difference in power between nature and astral boon to be closer in value and make the nature version more interesting, but I didn't expect this. Making insect swarm buff wrath makes more sense than the previous version and have no issues with it and is a clear buff against the retarded full immune mobs/bosses. It did remove a rng factor, but it didn't change the one we really wanted changed. The BoaT Rng was a minor thing that was brought up because of the eclipse low proc rate on Wrath, and it being annoying with multiple low proc rate functions with high impact, which just does not feel good or perform well, and I think most of us expected an increased proc rate or possible stacks. Either way, the most important change to make the boomkin gameplay feel less rng and sluggish is to change eclipse. I would like to see 35-40% as the Wrath proc rate if we use the same system, because I used to love wrath last patch when I had 39-42% with my full crit gear. I suppose other options could include a base % that then increases after each cast, so Wrath starts at 30 and then increases with 10% per cast or after a set amount of casts it's guaranteed.

With the significant nerf to starfire cast speed, I'd buff the passive cast speed through the talent imp starfire as well.

Another thing that could be done with the dots to make them more viable for trash etc would be that rather like CoA you would do the opposite where the dots are front heavy and dials down their dmg with time, or just buff the dots. I played around with the idea that dots would spread to 1 mob after the mob died either with the remaining dot timer or rank 1 or whatever, but might be annoying to do.

The rotation became easier, but also lost a min/max function. Trash dmg, and leveling dmg was reduced by a hefty margin, and our boss dmg is also reduced far more than I think many realize, but again we are already among the worst dps by a decent bit, with minor utility, so I don't understand why we would be nerfed again. The latest changes made starfire feel strong, but Wrath feel bad, and overall dmg significantly lower. With these changes wrath and starfire will feel bad, wrath low proc rate, starfires long cast time, makes me think of the good old time when you had to cancel the spell at 2.8-2.9 sec and move to not die from boss mechanics, or mobs just dying before i could cast a high dmg spell and relative low dmg for the long cast, the 6% crit chance to starfire is nothing when compared to both feel and performance.

I would also hope down the line they make changes to owlkin frenzy, because it's a joke of a talent, gaining mana to be hit and it has 3 points? My rework idea was to have it proc on dmg, you increase dmg taken, and you can reduce it with the amount of talent points taken. When procced you also deal a bit more dmg and either that's it or you add on the pushback protection, which makes a lot more sense with the name. It would be a double-edged sword with the increased dmg taken in pvp and pve, but it could be interesting. The other idea could be the opposite, and you take a bit less dmg with the pushback protection, and you keep it a pvp talent, but people would use it.

Sylvan Blessing needs a buff for the levelers, and Gale Winds isn't a finished product, we desperately need mana everywhere we can get it, but it's just not enough and nobody cares about the attack speed reduction, it's just more threat and we don't want it. I still find imp moonfire into vengeance a bit lackluster, if they want to keep it connected to dots you can gain 1% crit per point when IS, is on the target. Either way you need to have a general crit talent into vengeance, it just makes sense. You can also go with; you gain 1% mana or whatever when you crit on a moonfired target if you want it only connected to moonfire.

Other changes that would be deeply appreciated is to be able to cast BR in form, we are mana starved, and it cost us so much to cast that shitty spell and then get back in form. We even have the god-awful 2.5 5-set, yet we can't cast it, doesn't make any sense.

Barkskin should not reduce cast time, it makes it barely worth using, and you end up stuck casting instant casts instead.

Resto druids has such a boring gameplay, and could really use a nourish/lifebloom/ or a talent to make tranquility into a 5 man wild growth. Would require some nerfs in terms of numbers, but would make the gameplay significantly more interesting and fun.

Not a fan of ferals having to get nature's grasp or other non-feral talents to get to omen, which is a must-have for their kit, but it would require other types of nerfs etc so that's gonna take some time to figure out. Mangle or mangle-esque is something to consider as well.

I would consider giving hunters misdirection, would help a lot with the things that can go wrong the first seconds of a fight, and would increase the value of hunters in raids. Can limit it to only be used out of combat if you want.

Warriors should likely get a small buff to their aoe threat.

The last thing I'll ask to consider is for all players with mana. Can we change the goblin respecc to not remove all our mana, maybe 25%? When warriors, rogues or ferals switches spec it means nothing, but for us, it's very painful.

 -Hotverdomme
