## Post 166366 by Allarielle — 2026-01-25T01:44:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166366#p166366 | page 47 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Can someone explain to me what the gameplay/design/fun benefit is for including the Fire Mage stacking mechanic with Ignite? Why not design it such that each Mage is responsible for their own separate Ignite stack, and increase the duration enough that they can reasonably do so? Or have it so that any Mage can refresh the Ignite stack with crits from Frost or Arcane spells? Or have it so that anyone critting with any source of fire damage, such as Shamans with Flame Shock or Warlocks with their various fire damage spells? It just seems to me that the fun of designing a raid group around keeping Ignite rolling is almost directly at odds with the fun of Mages wanting to play with whatever playstyle they like.

Personally, the need to play around Ignite or be handicapped relative to other specs is why I simply don't want to play Fire at all. Instead of it being a spec about fast-paced burning-things-up, as you'd expect from a spec themed around fire, it's a spec about making careful calculations, perfect timing, and group coordination? What part of that says 'fire'? I appreciate that some people may enjoy the playstyle, but it seems to me that it is costing much more than it is benefitting. At least give us the option to not have to play around it, maybe via a toggled skill or something?

## Post 166371 by Leafdottxt — 2026-01-25T02:09:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166371#p166371 | page 47 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jan 23, 2026 7:24 pm**
> **ROGUE**
>
>  We’re generally happy with the recent changes to Rogue, and community feedback shows that the class is largely performing as intended. That said, in reviewing data across multiple environments, we've identified that Rogue is currently a bit overperformant in certain areas.
>
>  To address this, we're making a few targeted numerical adjustments aimed at bringing performance back in line without changing how the class fundamentally plays.
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  **Poisons:** Reduced scaling at lower ranks:
>
>  Deadly Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 30):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 2 (Level 38):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 3 (Level 46):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 4 (Level 54):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> 1% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (4% Scaling Total)
>
>  Instant Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 20):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 2 (Level 28):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 1% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 3 (Level 36):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 1% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 4 (Level 44):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 2% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 5 (Level 52):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 2% Attack Power Scaling
>
>  Corrosive Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 56):** 1.9% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (7.6% Scaling Total) -> 1% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (4% Scaling Total)
>
>  Dissolvent Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 52):** 4.75% Attack Power Scaling -> 2% Attack Power Scaling
>
>  *Developer Comment: Early access to higher poison scaling was resulting in stronger-than-intended performance during leveling and early gearing. This change smooths out that curve while preserving endgame effectiveness.*
>
> ---
>  **Blade Flurry:** Reduced Energy regeneration penalty from 30% to 20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Blade Flurry should feel like a powerful cleave tool without overly punishing resource flow. This adjustment helps improve its usability while keeping its overall power in check.*
>
>  **Assassination**
> ---
>  **Taste for Blood:** Physical damage bonus reduced from 1/2/3% to 1/1.5/2% and no longer increases damage dealt by Corrosive Poison and Dissolvent Poison.
>  **Noxious Assault:** Attack Power- scaling reduced from 35% to 30%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: As mentioned earlier, adjusting the power of Rogue.*
>
>  **Combat**
> ---
>  **Opportunity:** Opportunity: Damage bonus reduced from 4/8/12/16/20% to 3/6/9/12/15%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Combat dagger rogues are performing tad better than with any other weapons, this nerf will bring them more in line.*

A lot of the changes in this update are really well done, but some of these rogue changes are completely off the mark.

Right now, Assassination Rogue, from a raiding perspective, is dealing Tier 3 level damage the moment it hits Level 60 - it will continue to deal Tier 3 level damage throughout the entire gearing process, from Tier 0 to Naxx BiS. The "scaling" is absolutely meaningless, stats don't matter outside of Haste, gear doesn't matter outside of a few set piece bonuses. You do not "feel" any upgrades with Assassination, and your best weapon even at Naxx BiS is a dagger from Dire Maul.

The problem isn't that Assassination "scales too hard", the problem is that Assassination deals too much damage fresh out of the box, and then barely ever gets any more powerful. Nerfing the scaling on Assassination exacerbates the problem, it does not solve it - Assassination will still be outperforming other classes in Naxx while using dungeon blues, and gear upgrades will now feel even LESS impactful on your damage.

The reworks in the previous class changes, from a game design perspective, were phenomenal, every rogue spec has a unique playstyle and really feels fun to play in their own right - the problem was always the numbers. Assassination just deals too much fucking damage, Dissolvent Poison completely trivializes the options for different poisons because it works on enemies that are immune to poison, ignores armor, and also deals ridiculous damage, and completely trivializes the gearing process because Dissolvent poison alone does more damage than some neglected DPS specs entire kits.

(Personally, I don't think Dissolvent Poison should exist in the first place, but if it's going to exist, it should not completely invalidate Instant Poison in raiding environments. Maybe make it *not* ignore armor so that there's a reason not to use it on mobs that aren't poison immune. Or whatever sounds good.)

Removing Taste for Blood affecting Dissolvent Poisons was a really good decision that will do some good work to reign in Assassination's damage, but the problem still exists that there will be zero impact on the spec's damage from gearing up. It's still going to be "Get two 1.3 attack speed weapons and deal more damage than anyone else with 10% of the effort".

I don't really have any good suggestions for how you fix that, because with Noxious Assault completely ignoring Weapon Damage, and 50% of the spec's damage being *JUST* poison procs, there really is no reason not to just ignore every stat other than weapon speed and haste so that you can get more poison procs. Maybe that means the spec needs another rework, maybe that means I'm not smart enough to come up with a good solution, but "nerfing the scaling" on a spec that already did not scale with gear feels like a step in the wrong direction.

Also lol thanks for Blade Flurry buff we didn't deserve that but I'll take it

Imo, their  "Experimental Ammo" design is just off.
Randomly rotating effects is poor gameplay—it removes player agency and will definitly feel frustrating and not efficient.

Proposed Replacement:

Make it an active ability (1 min cooldown) that prepares one choice of enhanced ammunition for your next shot within 10 seconds.

Experimental Ammunition – 1 min CD
The Hunter loads specialized ammunition, empowering the next shot fired within 10 sec.
- [Fire Ammunition] – Your next Multi-Shot hits explode for 20% ranged weapon damage in a 5-yard radius. (PvE AoE / cleave tool)

- [Arcane Ammunition] – Your next Arcane Shot deals 50% increased damage, silences the target for 2 sec, and weakens their resistance to magic, increasing magic damage taken by 3% for 6 sec. (Crucial PvP utility MM currently lacks)

- [Poison-Soaked Ammunition] – Your next Serpent Sting deals 50% increased damage, reduces the target's armor by 4 per level (240 at 60) for 15 sec, and slows the target by 30% for 3 sec. (Hybrid PvP/PvE utility)

SOUND AND LOGICAL ESSENTIAL CHANGES TO MAKE PVP HEALTHY AGAIN.

Rogues - 1. Make dissolving poison NOT ignore armor, or cut the damage by 40% ( yes that's how busted it is )

## Post 166382 by Captain4k (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2026-01-25T04:06:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166382#p166382 | page 48 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jan 23, 2026 7:24 pm**
> **Protection**
> ---
>  **Defiance:** Changed to:
>  "Increases the threat generated while in Defensive Stance by an additional 4/8/12/15/20%."
>
> ---
>  **Shield Slam:** Attack Power scaling increased from 15% to 20% and its additional threat modifier is increased from 50% to 75%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Protection Warriors have been falling behind other tanks. These changes provide targeted improvements, while a more comprehensive review of the Protection talent tree and overall kit is planned for the future.*

Happy to see the Protection Warrior's problems finally being acknowledged. Better late than never.

A "***comprehensive review of the Protection talent tree***" should have happened during the first wave of Class Changes 2. As it stands, several talents in the deep Protection tree fail to support the intended sword & board playstyle.

Talents like [**Defensive Tactics**] attempt to, but *do not* fix deep Protection gameplay and should be removed entirely. A talent requiring Prot Warriors to leave ***Defensive Stance*** is flawed and fundamentally antithetical to the tank identity. Prot Warriors shouldn’t have to abandon tanking mechanics in order to perform the role efficiently.

Instead of stance-dancing incentives, Protection Warriors need:

 - Increased threat generation while using sword & shield
 - A focus on rewarding Defensive Stance uptime
 - Removal or rework of weak, outdated talents

Subpar talents like [Concussion Blow] should be replaced with something more impactful to the spec. Capstone talents should be a necessity to the role, not optional. An example of a meaningful replacement would be [Vitality] from the TBC Prot Warrior tree, which directly supports survivability and is an essential choice for warrior tanks in the TBC expansion.

> **Ellifta wrote: Fri Jan 23, 2026 11:36 pm**
> Protection warrior talents are in the right direction, but if some number changes are all we are going to get, some further number changes could be made. I won't reinvent the wheel seeing a bigger rework is in the plans. Currently warrior abilities like sunder armor or revenge do a fixed amount of threat, and that means they're kind of bad at high gear levels. Adding some scaling to their threat could be nice.
>
>  If any complex changes will happen at a later date and all we can get are simple number changes, simply improving Defensive Tactics values from 180% to 225% would fix a lot of issues, even if its technically a bandaid fix. Warriors already have an inherent 0.8 threat modifier in battle or berserker stance, so the written 180% doesn't actually do a lot. It puts the real threat at 1.51x on battle stance compared to 1.49x on defensive stance. An increase from 180% to 225% or %250 would substantially increase the threat output by putting it at 1.7x or 1.8x respectively.
>
>  Again, there's a lot to be said about defensive tactics, but if simple number changes are all we will get, this would help massively.
>
>  Further info on protection warrior threat can be found here: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ ... d=90747100](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1G0SqEf1Su67M0oEaiS8DYx-Nu9jlN-eOleoTLDn6PA4/edit?gid=90747100#gid=90747100)
>
>  Unfortunately, not a lot of guilds run warrior tanks if given the chance between choosing a bear tank and warrior, or a paladin tank and warrior tank after CC2. Some further tweaking on threat modifiers could help us massively.

I think Defensive Tactics is bad game design and should be removed altogether. You shouldn't be required to leave Defensive Stance in order to tank effectively. That's like forcing a Druid tank to leave Bear form in order to generate threat. A talent that lets you generate a percentage of bear form threat while in cat form would sound silly, wouldn't it? The obvious solution would be to just fix bear form...

## Post 166389 by Allarielle — 2026-01-25T06:01:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166389#p166389 | page 48 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

I always thought Defensive Tactics was for Warriors who wanted to tank with mostly non-prot specs or with 2h/dw... or it would be if it was in Rows 1 or 2 -_- Maybe the issue isn't that Defensive Tactics is poorly designed so much as that it's in the wrong place and there aren't enough incentives to stay in Defensive Stance full time? Maybe a deep prot talent something like this?:
> Resounding Aegis: While in Defensive Stance, whenever you successfully block an attack, you return damage to the attacker equal to 75/150% of your Block Value. This damage causes a high amount of threat.

OTOH. If the intention was for Defensive Tactics to be about opening up the other stances to full Prot tanks, then it's just a question of tweaking it downward just enough that you still get higher threat in Defensive Stance with a sword and board. Or tweaking threat in Defensive Stance upward...
I've always been of the opinion of that full-tank specs need more viability in PvP for roles other than just a flag-runner. What if there was a deep prot talent that was something like this:
> [Defensive Oath: While in Defensive Stance, whenever a party or raid member within 30yds deals damage, your attacks gain 1/2% of the damage dealt as additional damage for the next 15 sec. The additional damage gained this way cannot exceed 5/10% of your total Health. Leaving Defensive Stance removes this effect.]

With this, while your initial threat and damage stay more or less as they are now, you'll eventually scale until you're dealing as much damage as your top damage dealers and naturally out-threating them by a huge margin. In PvP it's even more fun, as now there's a dynamic of the enemy having to choose between focussing the high-mitigation target early, or letting it ramp until it's a serious threat. As the Warrior, you're now heavily incentivized to try to keep your allies alive.

Disclaimer: I don't PvP, I actually have no idea if Prot is viable in PvP as it is, lol.

## Post 166396 by Lane13 (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2026-01-25T07:36:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166396#p166396 | page 48 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

> **Lane13 wrote: Fri Jan 23, 2026 10:54 pm**
> To improve hunter/pet interaction, Kill Command should refund its mana cost when it crits. Additionally, increase the range to 100 yards, like Intimidation and Bestial Wrath.

After thinking about it, I believe Kill Command should do more. It's the capstone of the BM tree but not only it costs mana, it also deals less damage over time than Coordinated Assault (50% every 8s for KC vs an average of 10% per second for CA or 80% over 8s), an 11-points passive talent.

One possible addition is to make each successful KC hit provide the pet with one stack of the current KC, which ensures a critical hit with 50% extra damage on the next pet ability (or CA if desired). If KC crits, the pet could perhaps get two stacks instead. Alternatively, make the buff a flat 20 or 30% damage increase on the next offensive pet ability (although maybe it should specifically not work with Scorpid Poison, or at least not snapshot forever). Numbers can be adjusted as needed.

Another effect it could have is leave the target wounded, making it take more damage from a specific hunter ability. Or KC used against a target that has a Sting would make the target septic, taking additional damage, increasing the pet's damage on the target or even mimicking the effects of Chimera Shot in later iterations of the game, causing a different effect depending on the Sting present on the target. KC could also have a different effect depending on the pet that uses it, so that families can be further balanced this way.

There's also the possibility of having each KC give one stack of a buff (perhaps two when critting) that can go up to 8 and causes the next specific hunter ability, let's say Arcane Shot, to summon a random pet from your stable a la Pack Ally for a short period of time to attack the target you hit with Arcane Shot. You would need 5 stacks for Arcane Shot to be able to summon the guardian, and the logic behind having up to 8 is to avoid overcapping if you get a crit at 4 stacks, for instance. The guardian could also have an additional effect when up, such as giving your pet more Focus when attacking, giving you mana or simply benefiting from all effects that affect your pet, perhaps at a reduced rate.

I am just spitballing some ideas here but the point is that KC will be a very underwhelming capstone if released as it is right now. Please, consider this feedback.

> >
> >  If any complex changes will happen at a later date and all we can get are simple number changes, simply improving Defensive Tactics values from 180% to 225% would fix a lot of issues, even if its technically a bandaid fix. > **Captain4k wrote: Sun Jan 25, 2026 4:20 am**
> > **Ellifta wrote: Fri Jan 23, 2026 11:36 pm**
> > Protection warrior talents are in the right direction, but if some number changes are all we are going to get, some further number changes could be made. I won't reinvent the wheel seeing a bigger rework is in the plans. Currently warrior abilities like sunder armor or revenge do a fixed amount of threat, and that means they're kind of bad at high gear levels. Adding some scaling to their threat could be nice.
> >
> >  If any complex changes will happen at a later date and all we can get are simple number changes, simply improving Defensive Tactics values from 180% to 225% would fix a lot of issues, even if its technically a bandaid fix. Warriors already have an inherent 0.8 threat modifier in battle or berserker stance, so the written 180% doesn't actually do a lot. It puts the real threat at 1.51x on battle stance compared to 1.49x on defensive stance. An increase from 180% to 225% or %250 would substantially increase the threat output by putting it at 1.7x or 1.8x respectively.
> >
> >  Again, there's a lot to be said about defensive tactics, but if simple number changes are all we will get, this would help massively.
> >
> >  Further info on protection warrior threat can be found here: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ ... d=90747100](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1G0SqEf1Su67M0oEaiS8DYx-Nu9jlN-eOleoTLDn6PA4/edit?gid=90747100#gid=90747100)
> >
> >  Unfortunately, not a lot of guilds run warrior tanks if given the chance between choosing a bear tank and warrior, or a paladin tank and warrior tank after CC2. Some further tweaking on threat modifiers could help us massively.
>
>
>  I think Defensive Tactics is bad game design and should be removed altogether. You shouldn't be required to leave Defensive Stance in order to tank effectively. That's like forcing a Druid tank to leave Bear form in order to generate threat. A talent that lets you generate a percentage of bear form threat while in cat form would sound silly, wouldn't it? The obvious solution would be to just fix bear form...

As I've said, there's a lot to be said about defensive tactics. I'm neutral about it. I can see why most people don't like it. Having the ability to choose between more threat or more protection at the cost of latter is a unique idea, and I doubt developers will just ditch their own talent they worked on when they realize its problematic. In their own words, they are already planning a revamp of protection warrior, so I just shared my 2 cents on a bandaid fix that would absolutely fix the threat issue by just changing one simple number. Then, protection warrior would not struggle in threat at least.

Because clearly, they haven't put any thought into protection warrior at all for this patch, and probably don't have any developers playing it, so they are incapable of analyzing whether more complicated suggestions are good or bad at the moment. They'll look at it in future.

## Post 166492 by Duraluminium — 2026-01-26T08:07:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166492#p166492 | page 49 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

> **Zvyrhol wrote: Sun Jan 25, 2026 10:36 pm**
> > **Duraluminium wrote: Sun Jan 25, 2026 9:10 pm**
> > Survival hunter got no ranged or melee interrupt, and got no gap closing abilities.
>
>  You have freezing trap. It does interrupt casting after all.

Well, there are several problems with traps:
 1. It's additional source of damage, and a big one. Not only fire trap does damage, it also puts serpent sting on target (from the talent), and from T2.5 first set bonus serpent sting causes a proc of additional damage. It's huge against armored classes and those who can dodge melee attacks. On top of that, fire trap immobilizes target (another surv talent). So I use traps for damage by CD, I cannot save trap CD for CC cause I will have way less damage so I will not be able to kill the target.
If frost traps and fire traps used different cooldowns, it could probably work, BUT
 2. Traps are triggered by literally anything that stays around it, like totems and pets, so putting them under a caster to interrupt cast in many situations does not work out well. Especially when I'm trying to kill some resto shaman (totems) or warlock (pet).

## Post 166581 by Lichslap — 2026-01-26T21:05:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166581#p166581 | page 50 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

First off, my brother & cousins have our family gaming session every weekend. Since we installed Turtle WoW we haven't looked at another game, great job expanding on the vanilla WoW experience with new content and more fun and viable specs while keeping the spirit of old alive. I love Survival Hunter.

smiling_turtle

Regarding the proposed changes, I will only speak for Hunter since I'm clueless about most of the other classes.

> Ranged Weapon Specialization: Ranged damage increase buffed from 1/2/3/4/5% to 2/4/6/8/10%.

I was wondering why other classes would get 10% increased damage for the same investment. 5 points for 5% of extra damage didn't feel epic that deep into the MM tree, so I appreciate that.

> New Spell: Aspect of the Viper - Learned at Level 56.

This also seems like a sensible addition. It could be interesting to have this earlier in the game so that leveling as Survival or MM could catch up with BM, although I know Hunter is already spoilt in the leveling department.

> Trueshot Aura: Now baseline, learned at Level 40.

Wonderful that we keep a group buff while also getting a capstone talent more focused on our own gameplay.

The other MM changes sound very creative and I look forward to testing them.

> Baited Shot: Removed.

Baited Shot is my favourite ability in the game. It synergizes beautifully with Kill Command and Ferocity. It slaps in PvP, where Hunters are struggling if you go by the forums. It's a great source of up-front damage. And I really like talents that synergize with pet abilities and pet focus and not just straight-up damage, especially since you've expanded so much on the various pet types and talents. To me, Baited Shot is great design. It also has more uptime than Scent of Blood will likely have.

With re-adding Bestial Wrath, I do think Scent of Blood makes sense to complement BW's long cooldown window.

> **Skurridizo wrote: Sat Jan 24, 2026 12:57 am**
> Beast Mastery shines in long encounters and fits perfectly in progression-focused guilds. For raids that clear content quickly with 40 players, the solution was Wind Serpent combined with Kill Command + Baited Shot. This provided insane burst damage and was, in fact, the best PvP Beast Mastery setup.

> **Jago03 wrote: Sun Jan 25, 2026 11:14 am**
> I enjoy BM Hunter so much that by now I have two level 60 Hunters. The rotation of watching the pet’s focus bar while separately casting pet abilities with Kill Command to keep Baiting Shot active is very fun and rewarding.

I'm with these two pros on this matter.

Is there a way to still integrate Baited Shot or its effect somehow (talent tree, trainable pet ability, legendary weapon effect ..) ? I thought Baited Shot's design was better than Blizzard's Bestial Wrath for BM Hunters.

In conclusion, looking forward to buffed MM hunting, excited to see how everything plays out. Bummed about Baited Shot. But such are class changes, you rarely love all of them. Keep up the good work.

Dear Turtle WoW team!
Huge thanks for all the hard work you've put into this! You've created an unforgettable experience in a game that means the world to us!
Playing shadow priest in the world you've created is a whole new level of experience in Classic WoW.
At the same time i find the current moment appropriate to suggest some mechanical changes to certain abilites, which you might find suitable for the upcoming patch notes.

 1. Mind flay base range of spell 20 -> 30 (or with talent 2/2)

 2. Mind flay type of spell dot -> channeling magic spell (like arcane missiles) (to increase variaty of gear sets for better perfomance)

 3. Remove GCD of Fade spell (or increase t 3.5 3 pieces duration bonus 10 -> 12 sec)

 4. Improved shadowform grants you 70% (or 100) chance to avoid interruption caused by damage while casting any shadow spell.

 5. Holy nova casted in shadowform consume health instead of mana (We want to participate in speedruns too)

 6. Tier 3.5 5 pieces bonus proc chance 20% -> 25% (sometimes dot fades even if you are pumping solo target all the time)

 7. Tier 3.5 5 pieces bonus dot type (pestilence) disease -> magic (disease can't affect some types of creatures)

All the suggestions mentioned above are based on my personal experience gained while playing on your wonderful server.

Keep up the great work!

## Post 166606 by Rafale (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2026-01-27T10:39:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166606#p166606 | page 50 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

I will give my opinions on some specific points.

> Swapping Librams, Totems and Idols in combat now properly incurs a GCD.

The change is good, it prevents abuse.

> The PvP Dampening Debuff introduced in 1.18.0 will now have dynamic reductions of Magical and Physical damage based on your class / spec instead of a flat number for all classes.

I understand the will behind PvP dampening. Now I think this is just bad because it breaks the game between 2 parts and it is just weird to get X damage outside a bg and X-30% in a bg.
If you want to balance pvp and pve, work on synergy in PVE : Curse of elements increasing nature damage allow you to increase PVE damage without affecting PVP burst too much.

> New Talent: Alone Against the World (2 Ranks, Row 2)
>  While you have no pet under your control, all damage dealt is increased by 3/6%.

Some hunters waited that for a long time.
 2 points came to my mind : 6% is not enough to make ppl take it, it needs 6-12% and the best would be to add an effect like this :
 ****[...] and you get an effect from your last pet alive****

> Daybreak: Base healing value reduced from 289 to 248 and healing power scaling reduced from 43% to 32%.

Good nerf. Daybreak was absurdly OP.

> New Talent: Book of Prayer (Row 5 / 2 Points):
>  "Whenever you cast a healing spell, you regain 15/30% of its mana cost if it is not a repeat of the previous healing spell."

Very good change, it will make the rotation less spammy and force priests to think.

> Proclaim Champion, Empower Champion, Champion's Grace, Champion's Bond and Revive Champion: Removed.
>
>  New Capstone: Ascendance
>  "Call upon your faith for divine aid. When activated, your healing spells cost 33% less mana, are cast 20% quicker and grant their targets the Apotheosis effect, increasing their healing taken by 15% for 10 seconds. Lasts for 30 seconds.
>
>  This spell can be cast while under crowd control effects and clears you of any of those when activated."
>  (280 Mana, 5 Minute Cooldown)

very happy about that. Proclaim Champion was just a talent for others, not for the priest. The new cooldown will help in pvp too. It reminds me the PI.

> Spirit tap: Now also triggers on Mind Blast critical strikes.

Stop this, Spriests don't rely on crit. Just make Spirit tap proc even if you are not the one finishing the mob.

> Shadow Weaving: Effect reworked: “Your Shadow damage spells have a 20/40/60/80/100% chance to grant you Shadow Weaving for 10 sec. Your Shadow damage spells apply a vulnerability increasing Shadow damage taken by 3% per stack of Shadow Weaving for 15 sec. Stacks up to 5 times.”

Great change, it will also change a lot of things in pvp, i'm quite unsure of the consequences there.

> Rockbiter: Reworked to the following effect: “Your physical damage builds up an earthen bulwark for 20% of the damage dealt, tripled while you're wearing a shield. The earthen bulwark absorbs 5/10/15% of incoming damage for 8 seconds or until the bulwark mitigates enough damage. The bulwark's durability cannot exceed 20% of your maximum health.”

Good idea but it seems underpowered compared to previous effect. I ask to see it in game.

> Lightning Strike: Water Shield's Attack Power-to-Mana ratio changed from 20:1 to 18:1.

Good for mana which is quite problematic as enh.

> Defiance: Changed to:
>  "Increases the threat generated while in Defensive Stance by an additional 4/8/12/15/20%."
>  Shield Slam: Attack Power scaling increased from 15% to 20% and its additonal threat modifier is increased from 50% to 75%.

great change, prot needs more love. I would love a "second wind" talent to help while alone in pvp too.

## Post 166609 by Auralys — 2026-01-27T11:18:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166609#p166609 | page 50 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

**Please reconsider these changes on Druid.**

 *Balance Druid Performance Context* :
Balance Druids are already underperforming relative to other pure DPS classes.
Even within the Turtle WoW community, multiple threads have pointed out that Balance DPS is mediocre or bottom-tier on average, despite requiring higher complexity and crit dependency to function.

For example, players have noted that Balance Druids sit at the bottom of the median DPS range and rely heavily on crit streaks to reach competitive parses, meaning top logs are outliers rather than representative performance. ([viewtopic.php?t=18468&utm_source=chatgpt.com](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=18468&utm_source=chatgpt.com))
Others have previously questioned why Balance was nerfed despite not doing excessive DPS at all.
([viewtopic.php?t=20903&utm_source=chatgpt.com](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=20903&utm_source=chatgpt.com)) and I am sure there is many more compaints about the output of balance druids.

Given that Mages, Rogues, and Warlocks still dominate top-end damage across most encounters, it is unclear why Balance Druids are targeted for throughput nerfs instead of receiving compensatory improvements.

 *Balance of All Things Rework – Design Concerns :*
The reduction from 5 points to 3 and the rework significantly lowers mana economy and crit synergy, which are already weak points in the Balance kit. Although I do not see where those 2 extra talent points could be spent to compensate the global nerf.
Balance Druids already suffer from:
 - Low built-in spell crit scaling
 - Heavy reliance on RNG procs
 - Complex rotational requirements compared to other casters

This change increases complexity while decreasing reward, which historically discourages players from engaging with the spec. Also, DPS output is lower than other caster at equivalent gear

 *Caster Cooldown Proposal (Constructive Alternative)*
Balance Druids currently lack a meaningful throughput cooldown, unlike healers and tanks who all have meaningful cooldown to use.

Introducing a Balance-exclusive caster cooldown would:
 - Create a skill-based burst window
 - Let us be part of the burst when RL calls "use your cooldowns!"
 - Improve raid desirability beyond utility roles
 - Align Balance with Turtle WoW’s philosophy that every role should have a “moment to shine”

Example implementation (Vanilla-friendly):
Elune's grace (2 min cooldown, 15 sec duration)
+15% spell damage
Wrath and Starfire cast time reduced by 0.2s
This is simple, non-intrusive, and consistent with Classic design principles.

 *On Idol Swapping and GCD Changes*
Combat idol swapping is not just an exploit; it is a form of skill expression aligned with Classic WoW’s core design philosophy.

Classic rewarded:
 - Gear micro-optimization
 - Consumable planning
 - Situational item swapping

Punishing idol swapping discourages mastery and preparation rather than abuse.
If technical or PvP reasons require a GCD, consider compensating Balance mana economy or throughput to preserve PvE viability.

 *Hybrid Utility Tax Problem*
Balance Druids already pay a significant utility tax through:
 - Innervate
 - Battle Resurrection
 - Tranquility
Nerfing throughput without compensation further pushes Balance into a support-only niche, contradicting Turtle WoW’s stated goal to uplift Balance gameplay and viability.

 *Constructive Path Forward*
If these changes are necessary, consider at least one of the following:
 - Add real crit synergy talents for Wrath/Starfire
 - Introduce a Balance DPS cooldown
 - Restore or buff Balance mana economy
 - Provide passive throughput compensation

These adjustments would preserve Balance identity while preventing the spec from sliding back into meme-tier DPS status as it was in Classic.

Thank you for your continued work on Turtle WoW.
Balance is one of the most engaging specs mechanically and I love it but please avoid reducing its reward curve while increasing its complexity.

## Post 166618 by 1mrbulla1 — 2026-01-27T14:29:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166618#p166618 | page 50 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Fire needs a real DPS reason to exist: either ST parity or real stacking value

Fire is basically dead in PvE right now because it’s just a DPS downgrade compared to Arcane. This isn’t a “playstyle preference” thing — it’s numbers. In BiS conditions the gap is huge (for example, over a full Kara-40 run the total damage difference can be around ~1.5M in Arcane’s favor). That’s why almost every Mage you see is Arcane.

So from a design point of view, Fire needs one clear reason to be picked. Right now it has neither.

Option A: Make Fire a proper single-target spec

If Fire is supposed to be a normal ST DPS spec, then the target should be simple:
 1 Fire should do the same ST boss DPS as 1 Arcane (roughly within a couple percent) with equal gear/consumes and decent play.

Option B: If Fire is meant to be co-op then it has to actually win players over.

If the goal is that Fire becomes strong when you bring multiple Fire Mages, then it needs to be worth it in real raids:
 2 Fire Mages should at least match 2 Arcane Mages (and honestly should beat them slightly, otherwise nobody will bother stacking Fire).

Right now the “Ignite cooperation” style just doesn’t feel rewarding enough, and if bringing more Fire ever causes extra maintenance or lost uptime, people will always default back to Arcane.

Either way, Fire needs a real DPS bump.
Pick one direction until Fire has an actual reason to exist in raids again.

I like that you've allowed spirit tap to trigger of mind blast critical strikes, this may help with shadow spec and its leveling problems with mana.

I leveled my priest to 50 as disc then thought I'd try shadow but it is horribly inefficient by comparison mana wise and the talents feel dated compared to other classes, there's also zero protection against push back which means you've got to have power word shield up ALL the time.

Yeah you can talent into disc but that talent relies on the player taking a critical hit first, it's also not feasible for players at lower levels.

Many shadow talents are also too functional rather than fun if you catch my drift, e.g: "reduces the cool down of this" rather than adding a fun aspect to the class.

A 2 pointer in improved mana burn for half a second, really?

The same is true of improved fade and improved mind blast, and that shadow affinity talent, they don't do anything interesting.
I'm also puzzled as to why shadow has nothing to make pain spike more have more utility, I thought there would be.

My recommendation:

- Remove the Improved Psychic Scream talent and make it Improved Pain Spike, improved pain spike would increase the damage it deals/contribution from shadow spell power and cause the healing effect to shift from the target to the priest.

So instead of "healing temporary damage" on the target after hitting, it instead heals the priest for 50/100% of the damage. Psychic scream could have its cooldown reduced by default to compensate.

Improved Fade: 50/100% change to remove a root/snare and or increase run speed for a few seconds when it is activated, in addition to its current effects.

Improved Mind Blast: Chance to root the target when striking, in addition to its current effect. Like that mage talent in frost.

Improved Mana Burn: Have this take a full second off the cast time when fully talented, not half a second.

Shadow Affinity: Chance to prevent pushback on your shadow spells in addition to its current effects. Could go 40/80 or something.
As for Improved Shadowform at 60, why does this exist?
I say give shadowform these upgrades from the moment it is talented as a baseline ability and give shadow priests something new at level 60, perhaps an AoE ability like mind sear.

I'm betting that would be welcome as that holy nova while in shadowform thing feels kinda dumb, plus you have to spec into holy for it. This would also have the added bonus of making levelling as shadow much more fun since you get the mana regen right from the off.

Bit of a rant I know but my primary points for shadow priest out in the world:

Pushbacks.
Mana Issues.

Please give the spec something to make levelling/grinding less tedious.

Thank you!

I think, ultimately, the best way to go about it is to simply add a new conditional in regards to how Blade Rush is calculated. Changing around tier pieces to include enough Agi to make combat viable basically has to do two things:
- 1. Have so much Agi that it offsets completely ignoring the fact that the set bonuses for both T1 and T2 are genuinely garbage compared to .5, to the extent that Rogue's will, yet again, come out swinging with absurd levels of damage. They'll have far higher levels of AP, Crit and Uptime compared to literally any other class.

- 2. Repeat the same issue of Rogue itemization generally being too spikey. Rogue gearing thus far pretty much always boils down to "Yeah these items are far and away the best ones you can use to the extent that nothing else is worth really looking at." and also have the added malus of making it so that Rogues constantly have extremely weird power-spikes. You do literally zero damage until you obtain XYZ item(s) and then you basically couldn't care less after you obtain XYZ item(s) unless you care about niche optimizations that result in a 1% to 3% increase in DPS. Compare it to the relatively smooth scaling of most other classes outside of attaining legendary items or phase non-tiered BiS items the moment a new phase releases.
I think simply forcing Blade Rush to provide a minimum amount of energy tick reduction is just the simplest and best way to go about it.

## Post 166699 by Huihuibuhuifei — 2026-01-28T02:22:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166699#p166699 | page 51 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Subject: Feedback regarding the proposed changes to Searing Pain
Please reconsider the adjustments to Searing Pain for the following reasons:
The current PvP meta for Warlocks primarily revolves around the 20/31 Affliction/Demonology build. This talent distribution does not allow players to access the Destruction talent that reduces Immolate's cast time by 0.5 seconds.
By increasing Searing Pain’s cast time to 2 seconds, Warlocks will lose their only viable "fast-cast" Destruction spell whenever the Affliction tree is locked (silenced). This change would leave Warlocks extremely vulnerable against classes with interrupts, such as Warriors, Rogues, and Mages. Furthermore, since the 0.5s cast-time reduction talent is inaccessible in this build, this change acts as a significant indirect nerf to the overall DPS of Searing Pain vs other class, as its base damage has not been increased to compensate for the longer cast time.

## Post 166730 by Roninm — 2026-01-28T09:52:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166730#p166730 | page 51 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

**SHAMAN**

---
All of the following changes are to affect **Elemental Weapons** and its sub-effects:

 **Windfury:** Reworked to the following effect: “Gaining extra attacks increases your attack speed by 1% for 5 sec. Stacks up to 2/4/6 times.”

 **Flametongue:** Reworked to the following effect: “Hitting enemies with your attacks increases the damage done by your Fire Totems and spells by 10/20/30% for 5 sec.”

 *Developer Comment: Requiring the Shaman to actively engage in melee combat to keep the Fire damage increase active should make this effect lean more towards spell oriented Enhancement Shaman gameplay while requiring pure Fire damage Elemental Shamans to stay in melee range to utilize its full power.*

 **Rockbiter:** Reworked to the following effect: “Your physical damage builds up an earthen bulwark for 20% of the damage dealt, tripled while you're wearing a shield. The earthen bulwark absorbs 5/10/15% of incoming damage for 8 seconds or until the bulwark mitigates enough damage. The bulwark's durability cannot exceed 20% of your maximum health.”

 *Developer Comment: Changing the Rockbiter Weapon effect from a passive damage reduction into an active component that's kept up by attacking should feel make it feel more active in active usage while deterring non-Enhancement specializations from using the effect as a passive benefit which led to them being more durable, especially in Player vs Player environments.*

 **Elemental**

 **Eye of the Storm:** Renamed to **Call of Earth:**

"Earth Shield gains 1/2 additional charges and grants an additional 35/70% chance to avoid interruption while casting a spell."

---
 **Elemental Fury:** Now also affects Frost spells.
---
 **Earthquake:** Base damage values increased by 15%, cooldown reduced from 20 seconds to 18 seconds.
New Damage Values:
 **Rank 1 (Level 40):** 227-253 -> 262-291
 **Rank 2 (Level 50):** 343-387 -> 395-446
 **Rank 3 (Level 60):** 510-551 -> 587-634

Developer Comment: When designing a class, we often look for ways to blend flavor with function. While this frequently involves fitting a square peg into a triangular slot, Elemental is particularly well suited to aligning form and function when enough creativity is applied. Proper spell pushback resistance has long been missing from Elemental, as Eye of the Storm saw little use in either PvP or PvE: in the former, critical hits occurred infrequently enough that the talent was often skipped, while in the latter, critical hits were almost always fatal regardless. As a result, we’ve decided to retire the talent in favor of a solution that better serves its intended purpose, while also reinforcing Elemental’s thematic identity. With this change, the Elemental tree now answers the call of Earth, Flame, and Thunder—now if only we could find a way to introduce the Call of Wind in time for the 21st of September.

Although we generally view Elemental Shields as a concept better suited to Enhancement gameplay, and Water Shield as central to Restoration’s mana sustain, we are happy to give Earth Shield a place within the Elemental specialization. This allows Elemental shamans to make more meaningful use of the Earth element beyond its capstone talent. Note that the bonus from Earth’s Poise, the buff granted by this talent, stacks additively with other sources of spell pushback reduction.

The changes to Earthquake are intended to elevate the spell into a capstone worthy not just in form, but in function. While the adjustments themselves are straightforward, our goal is to encourage shamans to use the spell in a wider range of scenarios, addressing the fact that its original damage values often felt underwhelming.

 *As a final note, the Shaman class development team would like to sincerely thank the small, close-knit Shaman community. The thoughtful feedback shared on community servers and forums has been incredibly valuable, and it has played an important role alongside our usual log analysis work. We're confident it will continue to be valuable for the future development of the class as a whole.*

There is certainly a whole lot more depth and player interaction in relic twisting, than in using one of the cheaty client mods like Nampower (spell and macro queuing, up to 5 actions with a single button press), SuperWoW (cast spells on mobs without manual targeting, more information about enemies than available through the combatlog), RaidVisuals (outlines of aoe on the floor so you don't have to learn the area size). All of those have *massive* impact on gameplay performance and "parses" while automating or dumbing down the game, but those are completely fine and even supported by the developers, despite only a minority of players being savvy enough to use them.

But a couple people not wanting a dead item slot and actually engaging with the game is one step too far...   neutral_turtle_head

> **Fugus wrote: Sat Jan 24, 2026 6:43 am**
> > **Eluaria wrote: Sat Jan 24, 2026 6:33 am**
> > No, they absolutely shouldn't. That is one of the worst takes I have heard in a while. PvP Balance is absolute garbage unless you tackle it separately from PvE. It's always been this way. And when it hasn't been seperate, some classes were next to unplayable.
>
>   I have to disagree, the worst possible take to me as the idea that abilities should work differently in PvP than they do in PvE so that you have to relearn how your class plays between the two because you abilities aren’t the same. Doubly so when they not only change in PvE to PvP but they also changed differently per class and spec.
>
>  PvP balance can actually be handled while keeping PvE in line with it. Some simple rules to help achieve it.
>
>  1. If the damage is too high in PvP, it’s too high in PvE, tone it down and adjust PvE accordingly.
>
>  2. If the mitigation is too high in PvP, it’s too high in PvE, tone it down and adjust PvE accordingly.
>
>  3. If the healing is too high in PvP, it’s too high in PvE, tone it down and adjust PvE accordingly.
>
>  4. If the spell is too strong in PvP, it shouldn’t even exist in PvE, remove it from the spell book and adjust PvE accordingly.
>
>  The luxury of PvE is that you can adjust those values per mob and encounter any way you need without breaking anything else.
>
>  If you are talking about being 100% balanced in all areas, you never will in PvP or PvE so that’s not really a argument, you just strive to get as close as you can.

This has straight-out been disproven so many times over the years. Not to mention the idea that a mob should be rebalanced because a class has issues with PvP balance is insane. There is, fundamentally, no reason to NOT adjust numbers differently in PvP and PvE. Saying you have to "Relearn your class for PvP" is a given. You literally always do, PvP is fundamentally different from how it plays for every single class in comparison to PvE. You can't just balance one side, the other will not work in the same way.

Your "rules" go against every bit of game design ethic and ruling ever. You don't touch a game world because a tiny part of it has to be changed. You change the tiny part. If you need to change the World, then you don't change it for the tiny part, but for everything else too.
And "Oh, if it's too strong in PvP, it shouldn't exist" is, to say it kindly, an absolute idiotic take. Go ahead. Holy fuck, dude.
The game is PvE first, PvP second. Always has been, always will be. The balancing is not made after PvP, it's made after PvE. If something is too strong in PvP after balancing, then make it weaker for PvP situations. If something is too weak after balancing, make it stronger for PvP situations. That's it. That's the cleanest, easiest, most straight forward way of balancing that can and will exist.

And while we could just ignore envenom, any changes to the spec will affect both of them (And sinister is way behind backstab).

Well the general reason why Combat lacks efficacy early on isn't even necessarily that there's no high damage weapons available (Otherwise we'd see Rank 14 Rogues dominating with Combat), it's the lack of Agility to help Blade Rush scale.

Every point of Agility is 0.0012s off your Energy Tick.

So at base without Blade Rush, Rogue's get 30 energy ticks a minute.

At 400 Agi, Rogue's get around 39 energy ticks per minute.

At 600 Agi, Rogue's get around 46 energy ticks per minute.

The issue ultimately is that it isn't until 600 Agi that your rotation isn't necessarily fundamentally changed. Sub-600 Agi, you still:
- Stall after SnD

- Significantly delay builders

- Drift Rupture and Taste for Blood

- Turn Surprise Attack into a tempo loss

- Accumulate idle GCDs that cascade into lower SnD uptime and white damage
So the execution of your rotation sub-600 Agi is primarily constrained by energy.

At 600 Agi, you gain enough extra full ticks per minute that the rotation becomes constrained primarily by combo points instead of energy. Or, basically, you get to click your buttons the moment they're off CD without messing up the rotation.

There's no real way to change this outside of itemization. And again, it's hard to balance, because if you made T1 modify Blade Rush, to make it so that a set bonus made Blade Rush x% more effective, than any full prog Rogue is going to chuck it on and have an insane amount of energy tick reduction.

When I say give Blade Rush a certain minimum to work with, the overall goal is to, at a baseline, at least have it so that Blade Rush is coded to provide a minimum level of effective Agi when calculating tick reductions, overriding that baseline when your Agi is high enough to provide more than that baseline.
