>
>   Please note that this is a **Preliminary Changelog**. Further changes may still be made.
>
>  **ALL**
>
>  Swapping **Librams**, **Totems** and **Idols** in combat now properly incurs a GCD.
>
>  *Developer Comment: This was an ongoing quirk that was being (ab)used. Normally we would fix these in our weekly changelogs but because of the gravity of this change we've moved this to a Class Changes cycle.*
>
>
>
>  **PvP**
>
>  The **PvP Dampening Debuff** introduced in 1.18.0 will now have dynamic reductions of Magical and Physical damage based on your class / spec instead of a flat number for all classes.
>
>  More information regarding numbers will be given at a later date.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Turning these values class-dependent means that we will be less restricted in Design space of making all specs come to life and be viable without adding Player-target exceptions on a lot of spells.*
>
>
>  **DRUID**
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  Reduced the threat modifier of **Maul** by 15%.
>  Reduced the threat modifier of **Savage Bite** by 12%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Feral Bears have been overly prominent in their threat output, leaving little room for other tanks to shine. To reign in their presence, we’re reducing the threat modifiers on Maul and Savage Bite.*
>
>  **Balance**
> ---
>  **Balance of All Things:** Reduced from 5 points to 3 points and functionality reworked:
>  "Damaging a target affected by **Insect Swarm** with your **Wrath** spell returns 10/20/30% of its mana cost back to you.
>
>  **Starfire** has a 2/4/6% higher chance to critically strike against targets affected by **Moonfire**."
>
>
>
>
>  **HUNTER**
>
>  Ranged variant of Hunter has been one of the least changed classes in Class Changes 2 and has fallen behind other damage dealers and melee Hunter not only in raw DPS, but also in terms of gameplay.
>  Ranged Hunter is extremely timing-dependent and offers little reactivity in its rotation. In this patch, we are reviewing the Hunter kit as a whole to ensure more abilities are useful and impactful, and reworking the talent trees to make them more engaging in endgame content.
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  New Spell: **Aspect of the Viper** - Learned at Level 56.
>
>  "The hunter takes on the aspect of the viper, regenerating 5% of maximum mana every 5 second. Only one Aspect can be active at a time."
>
>  (No Mana Cost)
>
>  *Developer Comment: Hunter is a class that cannot reliably regain mana without proper set bonuses and can be quite mana-hungry. To offset this, we are adding a passive way to regain mana with the small drawback of occupying an Aspect slot.*
>
> ---
>  **Trueshot Aura:** Now baseline, learned at Level 40.
>
>  "Increases the attack power of party members within 45 yards by 3%, plus an additional 30."
>
>  *Developer Comment: Trueshot Aura was a design-limiting ability and an uninteresting capstone. For that reason, we are making it baseline for all Hunters in a slightly toned-down version.*
>
> ---
>  **Steady Shot:** Now baseline, learned at Level 20.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Steady Shot has been a must-have ability for all ranged Hunters, while Aimed Shot was rendered almost useless by its existence. We believe such a core ability should be part of the baseline kit, so we are returning Steady Shot as one.*
>
> ---
>  **Volley:** Has seen various changes.
>  - Now a 3 second cast instead of a continuous channeled ability.
>  - Mana Costs reduced:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 40):** From 350 to 210
>  **Rank 2 (Level 50):** From 420 to 270
>  **Rank 3 (Level 60):** From 490 to 330
>  - Now has Attack Power scaling:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 40):** 4% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 2 (Level 50):** 5% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 3 (Level 60):** 6% Attack Power Scaling
>  Any spell power scaling remains unchanged.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Volley has always been interesting in concept but too weak to justify use in practice. Due to its channeled nature, its damage would have had to be increased to unreasonable levels to be viable. We are therefore converting it into a casted ability that does not require the Hunter to stop performing other actions for 10 seconds to reach its full potential.*
>
> ---
>  **Arcane Shot:** Base damage values reduced but now scales with ranged weapon damage.
>
>  Damage Values:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 6):** Damage reduced from 13 to 10, added 10% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 2 (Level 12):** Damage reduced from 21 to 17, added 15% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 3 (Level 20):** Damage reduced from 33 to 27, added 20% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 4 (Level 28):** Damage reduced from 59 to 48, added 25% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 5 (Level 36):** Damage reduced from 83 to 71, added 30% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 6 (Level 44):** Damage reduced from 115 to 101, added 35% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 7 (Level 52):** Damage reduced from 145 to 129, added 40% ranged weapon damage.
>  **Rank 8 (Level 60):** Damage reduced from 183 to 166, added 45% ranged weapon damage.
>
>  Any spell power scaling remains unchanged.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Arcane Shot has been another Hunter ability that was underused and underpowered, lacking a meaningful place in the rotation. We are adding weapon damage scaling to make it a more rewarding button to press.*
>
> ---
>  **Rapid Fire:** Now also decreases the cast time of **Aimed Shot** and **Steady Shot** by 40%.
>
> ---
>  **Aimed Shot** and **Arcane Shot** are now on separate independent cooldowns.
>
>
>  **Marksmanship**
> ---
>  **Aimed Shot:** Returned as the 3rd Row Keystone talent.
>  Cast time reduced from 3 seconds to 2 seconds, Cooldown increased from 6 seconds to 26 seconds.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Due to its long cast time, Aimed Shot struggled to find a place in the Hunter rotation. We are reducing its cast time and adding several Aimed Shot–centric talents to make it a cooldown worth pressing for Marksmanship.*
>
> ---
>  New Keystone: **Experimental Ammunition** (5th Row)
>
>  "Your **Aimed Shot** deals an additional 5% of its damage as Fire, Arcane or Nature damage and grants you a benefit depending on the element:
>
>  **Fire Ammunition:** Your next Multi-Shot hits explode for 20% ranged weapon damage in 5 yard radius.
>
>  **Arcane Ammunition:** Your next Arcane Shot deals 100% increased damage and weakens target's resistance to magic, increasing magic damage taken by 3% for 6 seconds.
>
>  **Nature Ammunition:** Your next Serpent Sting deals 100% increased damage and applies a corrosive poison that reduces target's armor by 4 per level (240 at Level 60) for 15 seconds."
>
>  These effects last 1 minute and cycle between each other in the order of Fire, Arcane and Nature.
>  Only one type of ammunition can be active at a time.
>
>  *Developer Comment: The goal of this talent is to give unique, thematic effects to existing abilities that reinforce their roles, while encouraging the use of Aimed Shot and lesser-used Hunter abilities in combination with it.*
>
> ---
>  New Capstone Talent: **Lock and Load** (1 rank, 7th row)
>  "Your **Steady Shot**, **Aimed Shot** and **Arcane Shot** critical strikes have a chance to reset the cooldown of **Aimed Shot** and trigger Lock and Load. Lasts 10 seconds or until you cast **Aimed Shot**.
>
>  Lock and Load reduces the cast time of **Aimed Shot** by 1 second and causes your **Aimed Shot** to damage all enemies in between you and the target."
>
>  *Developer Comment: This capstone is intended to make the rotation more interactive through procs, improve endgame scaling, and reduce the impact of slight auto-shot delays by shifting more power into active abilities.*
>
> ---
>  **Improved Stings:** Has been changed to:
>  "Increases the damage done by your **Serpent Sting** by 6/12/18/24/30% ,increases the mana drained by **Viper Sting** by 1/2/3/4/5% and **Scorpid Sting** reduces attack speed by an additional 2/4/6/8/10%.
>  and **Scorpid Sting** reduces attack speed by additional 2/4/6/8/10%"
>
> ---
>  **Improved Scorpid Sting:** Removed. Most of the effect has been merged with **Improved Stings**.
>
> ---
>  **Swiftshot:** Has been changed to:
>  "Reduces the cooldown of your **Arcane Shot** by 0.5/1/1.5 seconds and cooldown of your **Aimed Shot** by 2/4/6 seconds"
>
> ---
>  **Ranged Weapon Specialization:** Ranged damage increase buffed from 1/2/3/4/5% to 2/4/6/8/10%.
>
> ---
>  **Barrage:** Now also reduces the cast time of **Volley** by 1/1.5/2 seconds.
>
> ---
>  **Improved Steady Shot:** Renamed to **Improved Marksmanship** and changed to:
>  "Increases the damage of **Steady Shot** and **Aimed Shot** by 5/10%."
>
>
>
>  **Beast Mastery**
>
>  In the last patch, we reworked Beast Mastery, but the changes did not hit the mark.
>  The specialization played awkwardly, so we are redesigning it again with a focus on smoother gameplay and preservation of core Beast Mastery mechanics.
>
>
> ---
>  **Endurance Training:** Health increase buffed from 1/2/3/4/5% to 2/4/6/8/10%.
>
> ---
>  **Thick Hide:** Armor value increase buffed from 4/7/10% to 7/14/20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Pets have been too fragile in open world content, and these changes should restore some of their durability.*
>
> ---
>  New Talent: **Scent of Blood:** (3 Ranks, 5th Row)
>  "Your attacks have a 5/10/15% chance to send your pet into a rage causing it to deal 40% additional damage for 8 sec."
>
> ---
>  Returning Talent: **Bestial Wrath:** (1 Rank, Row 5)
>  "Send your pet into a rage, giving it the **Scent of Blood** effect for 18 sec.  While enraged, the beast does not feel pity or remorse or fear and it cannot be stopped unless killed."
>
>  (1.5 Minute Cooldown, 12% Base Mana Cost, No Global Cooldown)
>
>  *Developer Comment: Bestial Wrath has been one of the most requested abilities to return. We agree it is iconic, so we are restoring it with an additonal method of activating its effect for a limited duration.*
>
> ---
>  **Kill Command:** Moved to be the Capstone talent and reworked:
>  "Give the command to kill, causing your pet to instantly attack for 50% of its attack power.  Can only be used after the Hunter lands a critical strike on the target."
>
>  (8 Second Cooldown, 5% Base Mana Cost, 45 Yard Range, No Global Cooldown)
>
>  *Developer Comment: Our previous version of Kill Command was underpowered and required too much setup. This new version, inspired by The Burning Crusade, should provide familiar and beloved gameplay while being attack speed–agnostic.*
>
> ---
>  **Baited Shot:** Removed.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Baited Shot struggled to fit into the Hunter rotation. For that reason, it has been removed, with its core concept preserved within the Scent of Blood talent. The barbeque is over.*
>
>
>  **Survival**
> ---
>  New Talent: **Alone Against the World** (2 Ranks, Row 2)
>  While you have no pet under your control, all damage dealt is increased by 3/6%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Pet management is an important part of Hunter gameplay, but for some players it can be overwhelming. This talent allows Hunters to raid and run dungeons without managing a pet, even though optimal play with a pet will still yield slightly higher DPS.*
>
> ---
>  **Surefooted:** Now increases hit chance by an additional 1/2/3% while dual wielding.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Dual Wield Hunter has struggled to reach hit cap, and this change should help players who enjoy that playstyle.*
>
> ---
>  **Lacerate:** Damage increased from 35% to 40% of melee Attack Power, extra damage from the sides increased from 10% to 15%. No longer makes the bleed tick faster when struck from the sides.
>
>  *Developer Comment: The lack of throughput caused Lacerate to fall into the wayside in the hierarchy of ability priorities, so we're giving it an increase in damage a bigger incentive to use it from the sides. Hopefully these changes should make it feel more like the reactive ability it was meant to be.*
>
>
>
>
>  **MAGE**
>
>  **Frost**
> ---
>  **Ice Barrier:** Frost damage granted while the barrier is active is reduced from 15% to 5% but now increases your Frost damage by 10% for 1 minute when cast, seperately and independently from the barrier.
>
>  Developer Comment: The addition of the Frost damage increase while Ice Barrier is active has been successful in making it a desired capstone outside of instances you expect to be attacked or damaged semi-frequently but that same damage now feels punishing when it breaks the barrier and makes you lose that throughput power.
>  For this reason we've moved a big chunk of the damage increase to be on the Ice Barrier cast, allowing it to stay as a part of the rotation without being as punishing as it was before when its lost to area of effect damage especially in group content.
>
>
>
>
>  **PALADIN**
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  Base damage of **Consecration** has been increased by 8% and now deals more damage initially, and less damage with every tick.
>
>  Developer Comment: Consecration has been underperforming in faster paced content due to its slow damage profile. We are putting more power on the initial ticks to help with intant threat of Protection and AoE damage capabilities of Retribution.
>  On the first tick, Consecration deals 156% of the 1.18 base value, followed by 140%, 124%, and so on.
>  Full damage progression per tick is as follows:
>  156% → 140% → 124% → 108% → 92% → 76% → 60% → 44%.
>
>
>  **Protection**
> ---
>  **Holy Shield:** Additional threat modifier increased from 30% to 50%.
>
> ---
>  **Righteous Strikes:** Has been changed to:
>  "Increases the damage and threat of your **Holy Strike** by 5/10/15/20/25%.
>  **Crusader Strike** now grants you Zealous Defence for 10 seconds. Zealous Defence reduces the damage of your next blocked attack by 6/12/18/24/30%."
>
> ---
>  **Holy Strike:**
>  "Strike your target for X% weapon damage and additional Y as Holy damage, restoring Z health and Z mana to you and 4 allies within 10 yards. The healing effect is reduced by half on yourself."
>
>  Damage Values:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 4):** 25% Weapon Damage + 11-13 Holy Damage
>  **Rank 2 (Level 12):** 25% Weapon Damage + 22-28 Holy Damage
>  **Rank 3 (Level 20):** 30% Weapon Damage + 34-38 Holy Damage
>  **Rank 4 (Level 28):** 30% Weapon Damage + 52-58 Holy Damage
>  **Rank 5 (Level 36):** 35% Weapon Damage + 71-77 Holy Damage
>  **Rank 6 (Level 44):** 35% Weapon Damage + 91-98 Holy Damage
>  **Rank 7 (Level 52):** 40% Weapon Damage + 106-118 Holy Damage
>  **Rank 8 (Level 60):** 40% Weapon Damage + 129-146 Holy Damage
>  Spellpower scaling has been increased from 43% to 71%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Protection Paladins were extremely strong during leveling and early endgame but scaled poorly in high-end raids. These changes slightly reduce early power while significantly improving late-game scaling.*
>
>
>  **Retribution**
> ---
>  **Repentance:** Repent effect applied on immune creatures now scales with 8% of your Attack Power per tick.
>
> ---
>  **Seal of Command:** Procs per minute increased from 7 to 9.
>
> ---
>  **Crusader Strike:** Rank 5's weapon damage percentage increased from 90% to 100%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Retribution paladins that leaned into attack power have been underperforming for the last few patches. These three changes should bring them closer in line to their hybrid counterparts.*
>
>
>  **Holy**
> ---
>  **Daybreak:** Base healing value reduced from 289 to 248 and healing power scaling reduced from 43% to 32%.
>
>  Developer Comment: In the previous patch, we changed the Holy Paladin capstone talent to offer something more unique than a simple healing increase. While the change was thematically successful, the raw power of Daybreak—especially when combined with the Tier 3.5 set bonus—was significantly too high.
>  We are therefore reducing the healing values and scaling of Daybreak substantially to give other healers more room to perform, while preserving the core identity of the talent.
>
>
>  **Tier Bonus Changes**
> ---
>  While usually we keep set bonus changes in the itemization changelog, the changes for paladin are significant enough to warrant being put here.
>
> ---
>
> - **Retribution Paladin Tier 3.5 (5 Set):** **Crusade**'s attack speed bonus increased from 2% to 4% and its duration increased from 15 seconds to 20 seconds but no longer stacks.
>
> ---
>
> - **Holy Paladin Tier 3.5 (5 Set):** No longer adds additional affected targets to **Holy Strike**.
>
> ---
>
> - **Protection Paladin Tier 3.5:** Moved 5 Set Bonus to 3 Set Bonus. New 5 Set Bonus is the following: "**Holy Shield** decreases your damage taken by 4%.".
>
> ---
>
> - **Retribution/Protection Paladin Tier 2.5 (3 Set):** Effect changed to the following: "Increases damage done by your **Judgement of Righteousness** and **Judgement of Command** by 15%.".
>
>
>  **PRIEST**
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  **Heal** (Rank 4): Healing increased from 605-684 to 702-793.
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 1): Healing increased from 764-862 to 840-948.
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 2): Healing increased from 977-1097 to 1075-1207.
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 3): Healing increased from 1222-1369 to 1344-1506.
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 4): Healing increased from 1528-1706 to 1681-1877
>  **Greater Heal** (Rank 5): Healing increased from 1671-1866 to 1881-2053
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 3): Healing increased from 278-335 to 297-358.
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 4): Healing increased from 340-407 to 364-435.
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 5): Healing increased from 440-524 to 471-561.
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 6): Healing increased from 548-651 to 586-697.
>  **Flash Heal** (Rank 7): Healing increased from 690-815 to 738-872.
>
>  Developer Comment: We've initially pulled down on the healing values of Priest healing spells with the tradeoff of increasing the power of Spiritual Healing in the Holy talent tree to offset this power, encouraging priests that want to heal to specialize into it and less so towards the Discipline support elements.
>  This inadvertently led to some ranks barely having any number difference between pre-level 30 and post-level 30 ranks as the healing reduction change was only applied to healing spells level 30 or higher. This also caused healing without specializing into Holy much harder while leveling after level 30, so we've looked into these healing spells to increase the base healing values for a middle ground between original and current healing numbers.
>  We hope these changes mend these problems and make healing without specializing smoother in leveling, don't mind the pun.
>
> ---
>  **Pain Spike:** Cooldown reduced from 40 seconds to 30 seconds.
>
> ---
>  **Fade:** All ranks now reduce your total threat by 15% in addition to the flat amount of threat.
>
>  Developer Comment: Fade being a flat amount of threat did not scale well both for the endgame and in the cases the threat values reach high values in longer fights, causing it to feel like a drop in the bucket.
>  For this reason we're adding on a percentage threat reduction in addition to the current flat threat, keeping Fade a powerful tool no matter the situation.
>
> ---
>  **Prayer of Healing:** Functionality reworked: "A powerful prayer healing your target and their party members within 30 yards for X to Y."
>  This means it can now be targeted to heal parties other than your own. Cast range remains at 40 yards.
>
>  Developer Comment: Prayer of Healing had the unwieldy limitation of only healing your own party, which made it very limited in raid environments.
>  With this change we aim to make it more versatile for its intended function of group healing and give agency over who gets the healing via the target and their party selection.
>
> ---
>  **Lightwell:** Now only has one rank, cooldown is reduced from 10 minutes to 5 minutes and its functionality is reworked: "Creates a holy Lightwell at a chosen location. When healing a friendly target with Lesser Heal, Flash Heal, Heal or Greater Heal, the Lightwell will heal an injured friendly target within 30 yards of its location with Splendor of Light, healing it for an amount equal to 20% of the initial healing spell, depleting a charge. Players cannot benefit from this effect more than once every 5 seconds. Lightwell lasts for 1 minute or 10 charges."
>
>  Developer Comment: Lightwell has stayed largely unused even after the additions of an earlier rank, a new talent and becoming a baseline spell due to it requiring manual use to utilize and often forcing players out of position.
>  Now it acts as a limited charge healing amplifier, causing your healing to be repeated as a percentage of its value on a wounded target if the target is within the range of the Lightwell and its healing amplification hasn't been triggered on the target for a few seconds.
>  We hope that this change shines some much needed light on Lightwell as a proper healing tool.
>
>  **Discipline**
> ---
>  **Searing Light:** Mana cost reduction increased from 50% to 60%.
>
>  **Holy**
> ---
>  **Reservoir of Light:** Effect reworked: "Increases the effectiveness of your Lightwell's Splendor of Light by 33/66/100%."
>
>  Developer Comment: We've changed the effect of this talent due to the major rework done on Lightwell and its functionality.
>  This means the healing amplification is increased from 20% of the healing to 26.6/33.3/40%.
>
> ---
>  **Spirit of Redemption:** Granted spirit increased from 5% to 10%.
>
> ---
>  New Talent: **Book of Prayer** (Row 5 / 2 Points):
>  "Whenever you cast a healing spell, you regain 15/30% of its mana cost if it is not a repeat of the previous healing spell."
>
> ---
>  **Swift Recovery:** Renamed to "Empowered Recovery" and now also increases duration of **Renew** by 3/6 seconds.
>
> ---
>  **Proclaim Champion**, **Empower Champion**, **Champion's Grace**, **Champion's Bond** and **Revive Champion**: Removed.
>
> ---
>  New Capstone: **Ascendance**
>  "Call upon your faith for divine aid. When activated, your healing spells cost 33% less mana, are cast 20% quicker and grant their targets the Apotheosis effect, increasing their healing taken by 15% for 10 seconds. Lasts for 30 seconds.
>
>  This spell can be cast while under crowd control effects and clears you of any of those when activated."
>  (280 Mana, 5 Minute Cooldown)
>
>  Developer Comment: Proclaim Champion and its connected spells have struggled to find its place, feeling more like a capstone you give to your target rather than elevating yourself and suffered from some conflicts in its functionality, increasing damage of the target, reducing damage taken and giving the Priest mana when the target takes damage which benefit damage dealers and the tank the most respectively which meant its full power could never be utilized on the same target in group content.
>  For this reason we've pivoting from a direct target buff to a power boosting capstone, meant to feel like a proper reward for mastering your role as a bringer of the Light.
>
>  **Shadow**
> ---
>  **Improved Fade:** Effect reworked: “Reduces the threat returned when Fade ends by 25/50%.”. Also moved to Row 4 from Row 3.
>
>  Developer Comment: Improved Fade has largely stayed unused, only having niche uses such as triggering tier set bonuses related to Fade more often.
>  In combination with the Fade total threat reduction addition, this rework should allow the Priest to instead permanently remove part of the normal temporary threat reduction, making it a valuable tool for threat management.
>
> ---
>  **Improved Mana Burn:** Moved from Row 3 to Row 4.
>
>  *Developer Comment: We've slightly adjusted Improved Mana Burn's talent location as Mana Burn is learned at level 24, meaning the talent upgraded a spell you didn't learn yet when the talent became accessible.*
>
> ---
>  **Shadow Reach:** Now a 2 pointer instead of 3 pointer, increasing the range of your Shadow damage spells by 10/20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: This point requirement reduction should better align this talent with similiar range increase talents that also cost 2 points.*
>
> ---
>  **Shadow Weaving:** Effect reworked: “Your Shadow damage spells have a 20/40/60/80/100% chance to grant you Shadow Weaving for 10 sec. Your Shadow damage spells apply a vulnerability increasing Shadow damage taken by 3% per stack of Shadow Weaving for 15 sec. Stacks up to 5 times.”
>
>  Developer Comment: Shadow Weaving struggles heavily when there are multiple targets the Priest has to focus on, especially in the cases those targets die faster than Shadow Weaving can be accumulated on them, preventing them from reaching their full potential both in terms of damage and supporting other Shadow damage dealers.
>  We've shifted Shadow Weaving to be instead an effect that accumulates on the Priest themselves that applies the amount of stacks you accumulate on yourself as the Shadow damage increase debuff on the targets, allowing easier application for multiple targets and carrying over these stacks between creature packs if they're close.
>
>
>
>
>  **ROGUE**
>
>  We’re generally happy with the recent changes to Rogue, and community feedback shows that the class is largely performing as intended. That said, in reviewing data across multiple environments, we've identified that Rogue is currently a bit overperformant in certain areas.
>
>  To address this, we're making a few targeted numerical adjustments aimed at bringing performance back in line without changing how the class fundamentally plays.
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  **Poisons:** Reduced scaling at lower ranks:
>
>  Deadly Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 30):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 2 (Level 38):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 3 (Level 46):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 4 (Level 54):** 2% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (8% Scaling Total) -> 1% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (4% Scaling Total)
>
>  Instant Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 20):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> No Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 2 (Level 28):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 1% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 3 (Level 36):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 1% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 4 (Level 44):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 2% Attack Power Scaling
>  **Rank 5 (Level 52):** 5% Attack Power Scaling -> 2% Attack Power Scaling
>
>  Corrosive Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 56):** 1.9% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (7.6% Scaling Total) -> 1% Attack Power Scaling per Tick (4% Scaling Total)
>
>  Dissolvent Poison:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 52):** 4.75% Attack Power Scaling -> 2% Attack Power Scaling
>
>  *Developer Comment: Early access to higher poison scaling was resulting in stronger-than-intended performance during leveling and early gearing. This change smooths out that curve while preserving endgame effectiveness.*
>
> ---
>  **Blade Flurry:** Reduced Energy regeneration penalty from 30% to 20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Blade Flurry should feel like a powerful cleave tool without overly punishing resource flow. This adjustment helps improve its usability while keeping its overall power in check.*
>
>  **Assassination**
> ---
>  **Taste for Blood:** Physical damage bonus reduced from 1/2/3% to 1/1.5/2% and no longer increases damage dealt by Corrosive Poison and Dissolvent Poison.
>  **Noxious Assault:** Attack Power- scaling reduced from 35% to 30%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: As mentioned earlier, adjusting the power of Rogue.*
>
>  **Combat**
> ---
>  **Opportunity:** Opportunity: Damage bonus reduced from 4/8/12/16/20% to 3/6/9/12/15%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Combat dagger rogues are performing tad better than with any other weapons, this nerf will bring them more in line.*
>
>
>
>
>  **SHAMAN**
>
>  Physical DPS Enhancement will see some small tweaks in patch 1.18.1. Tank Enhancement and spell-power–focused Enhancement, however, are getting more meaningful updates to their core talents. These changes are aimed at strengthening each playstyle’s identity and reducing overlap with similar mechanics found in other classes.
>
>  **General**
>
>  **Lightning Shield:** Mana cost reduced across the board by roughly 25%
>  **Rank 1 (Level 8):** 45 -> 40
>  **Rank 2 (Level 16):** 80 -> 70
>  **Rank 3 (Level 24):** 125 -> 105
>  **Rank 4 (Level 32):** 180 -> 150
>  **Rank 5 (Level 40):** 240 -> 200
>  **Rank 6 (Level 48):** 305 -> 255
>  **Rank 7 (Level 56):** 370 -> 310
>
>
>  **Enhancement**
>
>  **Stormstrike:** Can no-longer roll and trigger **Windfury Weapon**'s effect twice.
>
> ---
>  **Windfury Weapon:** Each hit now has a 25% chance (was 20%).
>
> ---
>   All of the following changes are to affect **Elemental Weapons** and its sub-effects:
>
>  **Windfury:** Reworked to the following effect: “Gaining extra attacks increases your attack speed by 1% for 5 sec. Stacks up to 2/4/6 times.”
>
>  **Flametongue:** Reworked to the following effect: “Hitting enemies with your attacks increases the damage done by your Fire Totems and spells by 10/20/30% for 5 sec.”
>
>  *Developer Comment: Requiring the Shaman to actively engage in melee combat to keep the Fire damage increase active should make this effect lean more towards spell oriented Enhancement Shaman gameplay while requiring pure Fire damage Elemental Shamans to stay in melee range to utilize its full power.*
>
>  **Rockbiter:** Reworked to the following effect: “Your physical damage builds up an earthen bulwark for 20% of the damage dealt, tripled while you're wearing a shield. The earthen bulwark absorbs 5/10/15% of incoming damage for 8 seconds or until the bulwark mitigates enough damage. The bulwark's durability cannot exceed 20% of your maximum health.”
>
>  *Developer Comment: Changing the Rockbiter Weapon effect from a passive damage reduction into an active component that's kept up by attacking should feel make it feel more active in active usage while deterring non-Enhancement specializations from using the effect as a passive benefit which led to them being more durable, especially in Player vs Player environments.*
>
> ---
>  **Flurry:** Reworked to the following effect “Increases your attack speed by 8/11/14/17/20% for your next 3 swings after dealing a critical strike.”
>
>  *Developer Comment: This change should increase the uptime of Flurry especially for spell oriented Enhancement Shaman gameplay, making it less punishing to have less physical critical strike chance compared to their physical oriented counterpart.*
>
> ---
>  **Lightning Strike:** Water Shield's Attack Power-to-Mana ratio changed from 20:1 to 18:1.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Shields are central to our vision of Enhancement, they are the specialization's biggest sink of mana, expecially in contexts where AOE damage is involved. This should improve the dependability of the specialization's mana bar.*
>
>
>  **Elemental**
>
>  **Eye of the Storm:** Renamed to **Call of Earth:**
>
>  "Earth Shield gains 1/2 additional charges and grants an additional 35/70% chance to avoid interruption while casting a spell."
>
> ---
>  **Elemental Fury:** Now also affects Frost spells.
> ---
>  **Earthquake:** Base damage values increased by 15%, cooldown reduced from 20 seconds to 18 seconds.
>  New Damage Values:
>  **Rank 1 (Level 40):** 227-253 -> 262-291
>  **Rank 2 (Level 50):** 343-387 -> 395-446
>  **Rank 3 (Level 60):** 510-551 -> 587-634
>
>  Developer Comment: When designing a class, we often look for ways to blend flavor with function. While this frequently involves fitting a square peg into a triangular slot, Elemental is particularly well suited to aligning form and function when enough creativity is applied. Proper spell pushback resistance has long been missing from Elemental, as Eye of the Storm saw little use in either PvP or PvE: in the former, critical hits occurred infrequently enough that the talent was often skipped, while in the latter, critical hits were almost always fatal regardless. As a result, we’ve decided to retire the talent in favor of a solution that better serves its intended purpose, while also reinforcing Elemental’s thematic identity. With this change, the Elemental tree now answers the call of Earth, Flame, and Thunder—now if only we could find a way to introduce the Call of Wind in time for the 21st of September.
>
>  Although we generally view Elemental Shields as a concept better suited to Enhancement gameplay, and Water Shield as central to Restoration’s mana sustain, we are happy to give Earth Shield a place within the Elemental specialization. This allows Elemental shamans to make more meaningful use of the Earth element beyond its capstone talent. Note that the bonus from Earth’s Poise, the buff granted by this talent, stacks additively with other sources of spell pushback reduction.
>
>  The changes to Earthquake are intended to elevate the spell into a capstone worthy not just in form, but in function. While the adjustments themselves are straightforward, our goal is to encourage shamans to use the spell in a wider range of scenarios, addressing the fact that its original damage values often felt underwhelming.
>
>
>  **Tier Bonus Changes**
>
> - **Restoration Shaman Tier 1 (3 Set):** Changed description to clarify the totem radius is increased by 10 yards and not set to 30 yards.
>
> ---
>
> - **Restoration Shaman Tier 1 (8 Set):** Reworked to the following: "Your Healing Wave and Lesser Healing Wave have a 25% chance to surround the target with an earth wall, absorbing 250 damage. Lasts 6 sec.".
>  *As a final note, the Shaman class development team would like to sincerely thank the small, close-knit Shaman community. The thoughtful feedback shared on community servers and forums has been incredibly valuable, and it has played an important role alongside our usual log analysis work. We're confident it will continue to be valuable for the future development of the class as a whole.*
>
>
>
>
>
>
>  **WARLOCK**
>
>  This patch aims to bring more quality of life and to deal with some unresolved issues limiting certain playstyles. We will also address parts of warlock's kit that are problematic in PvP.
>
>  **General**
>
> ---
>  **Curse of Exhaustion:** mana cost increased from 8% to 14% base mana. (from 110 to 190 at lvl 60)
>
> ---
>  **Curse of Tongues:** Rank 1 cast speed reduction reduced from 50% to 30%.
>  Rank 2 Mana cost increased from 110 to 240.
>
>  *Developer Comment: We're giving the most powerful debilitating curses a cost increase better matching their impact.*
>
> ---
>  **Enslave Demon:** Now reduces healing taken by the enslaved demon by 50%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: The healing reduction is getting adjusted and shifted from Master Demonologist, so instead of affecting the warlock, it'll now affect Greater demons and enslaved demons found in the world (and instances).*
>
> ---
>  **Ritual of Doom:** initial cast time increased from 5 seconds to 7 seconds and the ritual channel duration reduced from 5 sec to 3 sec.
>
> ---
>  **Felhunter** and **Infernal:** Armor reduced by 30%, resulting in about 5% lower damage reduction against physical attacks.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Felhunter is a bit too well-rounded while Infernal's damage and health increase compared to vanilla justifies a little pull on their damage reduction when targeted.*
>
> ---
>  **Felguard:** **Legion Strike**'s healing reduction increased from 10% to 25%.
>
> ---
>  **Felguard:** **Axe Toss**' stun duration reduced from 4 seconds to 2 seconds.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Stun of such duration often means a guaranteed kill in combination with Felguard's raw power, so we're giving the victim a more fair chance at survival.*
>
> ---
>  **Searing Pain:** Global cooldown reduced from 1.5 seconds to 1 second.
>
>  *Developer Comment: We're resolving the Searing Pain's lack of ability to benefit from haste effects, leaning into its swift spikey character.*
>
> ---
>  **Hellfire:** Spell power scaling increased from 2.2% to 4.125% per tick and mana cost is now reduced on the initial cast while costing mana for every second channeled.
>  **Rank 1 (Level 30):** 645 Mana -> 160 Mana + 30 Mana/Second
>  **Rank 2 (Level 42):** 975 Mana -> 240 Mana + 50 Mana/Second
>  **Rank 3 (Level 54):** 1300 Mana -> 325 Mana + 65 Mana/Second
>
> ---
>  **Ritual of Souls:** Soul Shard requirement increased from 1 to 3.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Since its creation it has been intended for the Ritual of Souls to require more Soul Shards than simply conjuring a single Healthstone.*
>
> ---
>  **Soulwell:** Now has a new model.
>
>  *Developer Comment: This is to differentiate it from the Ritual of Doom.*
>
> ---
>  **Curse of Recklessness:** Global cooldown reduced from 1.5 seconds to 1 second.
>
>  *Developer Comment: For too long has the fear-juggling technique gone unnoticed, unsupported - no more.*
>
>
>  **Affliction**
> ---
>  **Sinister Pursuit:** Changed into a 2-point Demonology talent, permanently increasing your pets movement speed by 5/10%. This includes greater demons.
>  **Master Conjuror:** Removed.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Since this talent has been having trouble finding its niche, we're moving it to be a staple Demonology talent in much simpler form. Being able to have 3 types of the same Healthstone has also not been intended.*
>
>
>  **Demonology**
> ---
>  **Master Summoner:** Now also reduces the cooldown of **Ritual of Doom** by 25/50%.
>
> ---
>  **Master Demonologist:** Greater Demons' healing reduction removed from its effect.
>
> ---
>  **Unleashed Potential:** Now also provides the Warlock with a tracking buff.
>
> ---
>  **Soul Link:** Damage transfer reduced from 25% to 20%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Due to removal of the healing reduction from the warlock with Greater demons and because the recently introduced PvP dampening has been more beneficial for classes focusing on survivability, we're balancing out demonology warlock's durability.*
>
>  **Tier Bonus Changes**
>
> - **Affliction Warlock Tier 3 (4 Set):** Effect changed to the following: "Your Curse of Agony does 100% increased damage for the first 4 ticks.".
>
> ---
>
> - **Affliction Warlock Tier 3.5 (3 Set):** Amount of mana gained from health drained by Siphon Life reduced from 50% to 25%.
>
>  **WARRIOR**
>
>  **General**
> ---
>  Removed cooldown from **Hamstring**.
>
>  *Developer Comment: ![💀](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f480.svg).*
>
>
>  **Fury**
> ---
>  **Improved Whirlwind:** Renamed to **Ravager** and now has an additional effect:
>  "Reduces the cooldown of **Whirlwind** by 1/1.5/2 seconds and rage cost of **Cleave** by 1/2/3."
>
>  *Developer Comment: Talent points could previously be spent before Whirlwind was learned, which caused confusion for new players. We’ve added a small rage cost Reduction to cleave to fix this inconsistency without affecting balance in a significant way.*
>
> ---
>  Cast time reduction granted to **Slam** by **Flurry** has been corrected. For example, with 5 points spent in Flurry, Slam cast time will now properly be 1.92 seconds instead of 1.75 seconds.
>
>  *Developer Comment: In the previous patch, Flurry was updated to reduce Slam cast time, but an incorrect formula resulted in more reduction than intended.*
>
>
>  **Arms**
> ---
>  Swapped position of **Boundless Anger** and **Precision Cut** talents.
>
> ---
>  **Precision Cut:** Changed to the following:
>  "Increases the damage done per extra rage point spent on **Execute** by 25/50/75%."
>
>  *Developer Comment: The previous redesign of Precision Cut did not deliver satisfying Execute gameplay and made the ability feel underwhelming. Restoring increased damage per Rage spent allows Execute to better fulfill its role as a high-impact finisher for Arms Warriors.*
>
>
>  **Protection**
> ---
>  **Defiance:** Changed to:
>  "Increases the threat generated while in Defensive Stance by an additional 4/8/12/15/20%."
>
> ---
>  **Shield Slam:** Attack Power scaling increased from 15% to 20% and its additonal threat modifier is increased from 50% to 75%.
>
>  *Developer Comment: Protection Warriors have been falling behind other tanks. These changes provide targeted improvements, while a more comprehensive review of the Protection talent tree and overall kit is planned for the future.*
>
>  **Tier Bonus Changes**
>
> - **Arms/Fury Warrior Tier 1 (3 Set):** Effect changed to the following: "Whenever you hit with an ability, you have 10% chance to gain 15 rage.".
>
> ---
>
> - **Arms/Fury Warrior Tier 3 (4 Set):** Effect changed to the following: "Increases the critical strike damage bonus of your abilities by 4%.".

Nerfing Fire was necessary and I think you have done a good job doing that with the changes to Elemental weapons.
But the unresolved issue remains; Nature is still lagging behind.
The pushback is great, primarily for leveling as Elemental (for example most bosses in Kara40 dont have a mechanic where this is usefull). Cooldown reduction on Earthquake is also good bringing it in line with other cooldowns.

Improvements need to be made to Lightning bolt and Chain lightning, especially now that you have eliminated the changing of equipable totems.

It is a shame the "Small Close-knit Community of Shamans" did not include any Nature Elemental players.

My perspective on rogue changes, from an actively raiding rogue:

There are still a major flaws with assassination that these changes do not address. Basically what is proposed here is a flat damage nerf and doesn't address the underlying causes of why the spec is OP to begin with.

 **The main issue with assassin:**
The power scaling of assassin is nonexistent and gear does very little to progress the spec. Most of the damage comes from poisons and because of that you're seeing assassin rogues using 1.3 speed blues over epic weapons. You're seeing fresh 60s able to outperform combat rogues in tier 2.

 **The Solution:**
Poisons need to scale with attack power AND be normalized with weapon speed (similar to pally seal of righteousness)

Otherwise you're going to have fresh level 60s pumping super hard, and the spec invalidating most raiding weapons.

The weapon issue completely ruins the power progression and fantasy of the game. It feels terrible to be sticking with underleveled blue items simply because of weapon speed, passing up using all kinds of great weapons from raid that you should be excited to be able to use.

Fix this one issues and you fix so many issue with the class. Combat catches up and surpasses assassin by t3.

## Post 167011 by Huihuibuhuifei — 2026-01-31T04:43:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=167011#p167011 | page 52 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

In an environment where overall PvP damage is being nerfed, further reducing the Demonology Warlock's survivability (by cutting another 5% from Soul Link) is completely unreasonable. I truly wish the developers would step into the Arena or Battlegrounds and play a few matches as a Warlock to understand the reality: we aren't as 'tanky' as you imagine.
We are already dealing with an extra 1-second cast time on Fel Domination/Instant Summons and a previous 5% Soul Link nerf. Continuing to gut this 31-point capstone talent strips away the Demonology Warlock’s core identity: a caster capable of holding their ground against relentless melee pressure. If the concern is that we are too hard to burst down, there should be compensatory buffs—such as moving Soul Link higher up the tree, increasing base armor, or reverting the instant summon cast time back to 0.5s—rather than a lazy 'one-size-fits-all' defensive nerf.
Furthermore, increasing Searing Pain’s cast time to 2 seconds is a massive blow. Forcing a 2-second cast without a significant base damage increase makes the spell feel terrible in PvP. By losing our only 1.5s Destruction filler, Warlocks have zero response when locked out of the Shadow school.
Please remember: removing the viability of such a unique spec as Demonology ruins the entire PvP ecosystem. Without the Warlock’s Curse of Tongues and high resistances to keep other casters in check, casters will run wild, kiting and blowing up slow-moving melee classes like Shamans and Paladins. Melee players can only close the gap because Warlocks suppress the backline. This game is an ecosystem; driving Demonology Warlocks out of the meta won't make the game 'happier'—it will only make the environment more toxic.

## Post 167426 by Heretic1987 — 2026-02-04T14:39:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=167426#p167426 | page 53 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

A few thoughts on the changes to Rogue in 1.18. As i see it rogues overall have unlike all other classes only one strength - single target dps (aside from small exceptions like Suppression room in BWL, or an interrupt which other classes can do as well). All other classes have different utilities, buffs, AoE and so on but rogues only purpose most of the time is single target dps and therefor they are and should remain best at it.

There may be an argument for a small nerf to Assassination dmg but the nerf as it is outlined now is a bit too much. First of all, Assassination is not the best performing spec. Combat daggers perform better once you have AQ40/Naxx gear. Assassination is just a very good stepping stone. Its a reliable way for a rogue to earn a place in the raid by the only way we can - single target dps. Rogues dps being so much higher then other classes is a way to compensate for their lack of other utility in most cases making them worth including into the raid. Subtelty support spec is indeed viable regarding overall utility in raid but the dmg nerf could force every rogue to go Subtelty and make other specs less usefull.

Second point is that the nerf alters the gameplay and makes it less engaging. A 5% nerf to Noxious assault and 1% per combo point to Taste for blood is fair and doesnt affect the gameplay. What does affect the gameplay is the change to Taste for blood, making it no longer affect Dissolvent poison.
It both nerfs the overall dmg too much (i would argue the % to Noxx and TfB is enough as it is) but also makes Taste for blood much less useful. Big part of what made the Assassination spec so engaging is the need to keep up Slice&Dice, Envenom and as high Taste for Blood as you can. How good you where at it decided your overall DPS as rogue. I myself was often able to edge out better geared rogues by paying attention to this rotation and it is both engaging and rewarding to do so. If you change Taste for blood to no longer affect Dissolvent poison at all you loose a big part of that aspect of gameplay. Keeping up Taste for blood as one of the 3 skills will have much less of an impact to overall dmg and could cause many ppl to skip it altogether, reducing gameplay rotation and engagement with combat.

By reducing the scaling of Noxious assault from 35% to 30% and the physical dmg buff of Taste for blood from 3% to 2% per combo point you already reduce the overall dmg of rogues quite significantly. I would argue that changing Taste for blood to no longer affect dissolvent poison will reduce the damage far enough so that other dps classes will be more preferable to bring into raids instead of rogues (why bring a rogue if a mage has same dps or close enough + can AoE, sheep and so on) and also make the gameplay less engaging and rewarding.

P.S. And with coming buffs to BWL we will need all the dmg we can get :)

## Post 167565 by Polak6868 — 2026-02-06T06:30:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=167565#p167565 | page 53 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Many of the the 1.18.1 preliminary changes are interesting, yet there are many potential changes that seem missing entirely or lacking. Respectfully, some folks and I have come up with a list - this is hardly the entire thing - of some 1.18.1 changes that could greatly benefit the game. Please note that all numbers and values can be altered.

 **Professions:**
 *Enchanting* - Higher tier runed rods now count for the requirements of lower tier wands.

 1) Runed Arcanite Rod counts for Runed Truesilver Rod, Rune Golden Rod, Runed Silver Rod, and Rune Copper Rod.
 2) Runed Truesilver Rod counts for Runed Golden Rod, Runed Silver Rod, and Rune Copper.
 3) Runed Golden Rod counts for Runed Silver Rod and Rune Copper.
 4) Runed Silver Rod counts for Rune Copper.

_.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'

 **Tanks:**
Earthshaker Slam (Shaman), Growl (Druid), Hand of Reckoning (Paladin), and Taunt no longer require Hit.

Talent remake required for Improved **Hand of Reckoning** in the Paladin Protection tree.
 **Improved Hand of Reckoning** (REWORK):  Increases the range of your Hand of Reckoning spell by 10/20 yards and your next Crusader Strike or Holy Strike costs 50/100% less mana.

 ***Having a taunt ability miss due to RNG doesn’t add challenge or skill; it only creates frustration.***

_.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'

 **Hunter:**

 **1) Alone Against the World** (REMOVE): This effect should be moved into the baseline of Dismiss Pet. When the player makes the active choice to dismiss their pet they gain this buff.

 ***The developer notes are good, but it would be more accessible as a baseline feature of the already existing Dismiss Pet.***

 **2) Experimental Ammunition** (SUGGESTION): Allow for the players to have agency and control over which ammunition they will fire.

 ***Players appreciate control, choices and options.***

 **3) Freezing Trap** (REWORK): A target frozen by this trap is immune to all damage for 1.25 seconds and remains immune to all damage over time effects until broken out. The duration of the trap can be reduced if needed.

 ***I believe this will be a welcome change in both PVE and PVP to avoid unwanted breaks and allow hunter talents like Piercing Shots and Endless Quiver to be a determent.***

 **4a) Scorpid Sting** (REWORK): Sting the target, reducing their armor by 300. Lasts 50 charges (consumed by physical attacks or abilities) or 30 seconds.

Level 22: 300 armor reduction
Level 32: 420 armor reduction
Level 42: 560 armor reduction
Level 52: 700 armor reduction

 ***Granting a party/raid a different source of armor reduction, or helping PVP hunters versus heavily armored players could be a good addition. This also would be something slotted into a rotation, thus could feel natural to play with.***

 **4b) Improved Stings** (CHANGE): Increases the damage done by your Serpent Sting by 6/12/18/24/30%, increases the mana drained by Viper Sting by 1/2/3/4/5% and Scorpid Sting reduces the targets armor by an additional 10/20/30/40/50%.

_.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'

 **Priest:**

 **1) Divinity** (REWORK): Increases the critical effect chance of your Priest (Disc, Holy, Shadow) spells by 1/2/3/4/5%.

 ***Not all things divine are of light and holy. Additionally, in later progression Shadow Priest tends to go 0/20/31 and the 15 points spent in Holy to get the final 5 in Spiritual Guidance are very underwhelming; aka they feel like a tax. Additionally with suggested Mindblast crits triggering Spirit Tap, this provides even more synergy.***

 **2) Holy Focus** (REWORK): Gives you 35/70% chance to avoid interruption caused by damage while casting any Holy spell, and increases your Healing (Power) by 50/100% of your spell damage from Inner Fire.

 ***Leans into the changes in 1.17 to have Inner Fire no longer grant Attack Power but Spell Damage. This gives it a little more use for Healers, however, with the suggested rescaling on many of our Heal spells this might be too much.***

 **3) Improved Shadow Word: Pain** (RENAME/REMAKE): Catechism of Pain: Increases the duration of your Shadow Word: Pain spell by 3/6 seconds, and the target of your Painspike spreads your Shadow Word: Pain to all enemies within X/Y yards.

 ****SWP multi-dotting is incredibly mana heavy and slow. This would give Painspike some more use and give Shadow an AOE cooldown. As for the 0/20/31 shadow build that gains Holy Nova, the spell does not benefit from your shadow power. This provides an AOE option that uses your accumulated shadow spell power.****

 **4a) Lightwell** (OVERHAUL). Rather than reducing its cooldown to 5 minutes, I would suggest making it 90 seconds to allow it to be a tool we use often. Remove the charges, and reduce the well’s up time to 25 seconds. You can keep that ‘players cannot benefit from this effect more than once every 5 seconds.’ If needed, increase the mana cost of light well and allow the Improved Healing talent to reduce its mana cost.

 ***First, thank you for reworking this clunky mechanic in the first place. It’s fairly clear to anyone watching TWoW that the developers want Lightwell to be relevant, likely because it’s such an iconic concept—even if it has historically been poorly designed. Your suggested changes effectively turn it into a smart healing totem, which is a genuinely neat direction.***

 **4b) Lightwell** (CONCEPT). To put a cap on how much Lightwell can actually heal, if it is possible to provide it with a Pool of Splendor on summoning. The formula would need to be figured out, but it could be <{(Flat Amount) + (Healing Power) + (Spirit * Coefficient)}>. Once the pool of healing is used, or the duration ends, the Lightwell despawns.

 ***The healing pool for Lightwell’s Splendor would need to be a flat amount at lower levels to ensure viability. However, at level 60 and with appropriate gear, this pool would scale significantly, making it a powerful and valuable tool in the priest’s kit.***

_.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'

 **Warlock:**

 **1) Demon Change:**
 - All Demons would benefit greatly from in dungeon and especially in raid zone buffs to their AOE damage reduction, and additional resource (mana) regeneration. This can be none present in open world, and PVP settings.

 - Succubus’ Seduce has a similar secondary as Paladin’s Repentance on creatures immune to charm. If the target is immune to the effect, they take X Shadow damage for Y seconds.

 **2) Demonic Aegis** (REWORK): Increase the effectiveness of your Demon Armor spell by 20/40/60%, and while you benefit from your Demon Armor spell your demon’s critical strikes increase the heal restored every 5 seconds by 100/200/300% for 10 seconds.

 ***Healing per 5 seconds is a largely underutilized stat. This change gives demon-using warlocks a reliable, self-sustaining benefit that is provided through their demonic companion.***

 **3) Fel Cascade** (NEW DEMONOLOGY TALENT - Row 3 / 3 Points): Certain warlock spells empower your demons.

 - Imp: Your Immolate grants the demon haste <{equal to your Warlock Level}> for X/Y/Z seconds.

 - Voidwalker: Your Shadowbolt empowers the demon by reducing all damage it takes and increasing its threat by X/Y/Z%.

 - Succubus: Your Searing Pain increases the damage of your demons' next 3 swings or abilities by X/Y/Z%.

 - Felhunter: While channeling your Drain Soul, Drain Life or Drain Mana your demon’s abilities cooldown by 0.X/0.Y/0.Z per tick.

 ***Using the already accepted demon list format, this talent is designed to further strengthen synergy between demonology warlocks and their companions. This synergy goes beyond increased damage, introducing thematic spell interactions that add flavor while giving the listed abilities meaningful, practical use.***

 **4) Fel Stamina** (REWORK -  3 Points): Increases your demon’s total Stamina by 17%/33%/50% and reduces its chance to be critically struck by 2.0/3.5/5.0%.

 ***This should help streamline the talent tree.***

 **5) Infernal Beneficiary** (NEW DEMONOLOGY TALENT - Row 1 / 5 Points): Your demons gain 1/2/3/4/5% increased chance to hit, and deal 3/6/9/12/15% bonus damage against the target of your Curse.

 ***Designing row 1 talents can be tricky, as they should not feel mandatory for every specialization. Demonology naturally avoids this issue by requiring an active demon, and some warlocks still choose to run without one. This talent increases damage and hit chance across a broad selection of warlock curses, providing strong value while leveling and remaining relevant in later PvE and PvP content.***

 **6) Master Summoner** (ADDITIONAL EFFECT): Reduces the casting time of your Imp, Voidwalker, Succubus and Felhunter summoning spells by 2/4 seconds, and the casting time of your Enslave Demon spell by 1/2 seconds. In addition , reduces the cooldown of your Inferno and Demon Gate spells by 25/50%.

 ***Demonology is currently more chaotic to play than intended. While Enslave weaving is engaging and enjoyable, it would greatly benefit from a reduced cast time, bringing it more in line with the pacing and thematic identity of the specialization.***

 **7) Otherworldly Ichor** (NEW DEMONOLOGY TALENT - Row 5 / 3 Points / Requires Power Overwhelming talent): When you take damage, including from your Life Tap, your demon gains the benefits of Power Overwhelming for X/Y/Z seconds. This cannot occur more than once every # seconds.

 ***The two-point talent Power Overwhelming (a great nod to Archons) is highly impactful. Requiring this talent enables both PvE and PvP warlocks to benefit from its effect in controlled and uncontrolled situations. Since warlocks are one of the few classes that can reliably damage themselves, this talent effectively weaponizes that unique niche. The remaining question is whether triggering this effect should also drain the demon’s health, mirroring the behavior of Power Overwhelming.***

 **8) Unholy Power** (ADDITIONAL EFFECT): The penalty to the time between the an Enslaved Demon's attacks is reduced by 5/10/15% and its casting speed penalty is reduced by 5/10/15%.

 ***This reductions the attack speed and casting speed penalties applied to enslaved demons thematically shows that the Demonology warlock exerts more control over their enslaved demon. This  further emphasizes the mastery of a skilled demonologist, allowing an iconic ability to stand out more clearly within the specialization.***

_.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'

 **Warrior:**

 **1) Anticipation** (REWORK): Increases your Defense skill by 7/14/20, and your blocks, parries and dodges have a 10/15/20% chance to reset the cooldown of your Thunderclap ability.

 ***Protection focused warriors desperately need assistance with AOE tanking.***

 **2) Defiance** (REWORK): Increases the threat generated while in Defensive Stance by an additional 4/8/12/15/20%, and reduces magic damage taken by 2/4/6/8/10%.

 ***Magic damage can be overly punishing to protection tanks.***

 **3) Improved Bloodrage** (REWORK): Increases the Instant Rage generated by your Bloodrage by 5/10, and reduces all damage taken by 1.5/3% while Bloodrage is active.

 ***Provides the warrior with a minor reduction boon and additional use for Bloodrage.***

 **4) Versatile Arms** (NEW ARMS TALENT - Row 1 / 3 Points): While wielding a two-handed weapon 33/66/100% of your block chance is converted into parry chance, and successful parries (with a two-handed weapon) generate 2/4/6 rage. Additionally, your Heroic Strike, Cleave and Masterful Strike generates a barrier based on your Defense score <{insert Forumula - could use Block Value as well}>. The barrier cannot exceed 5/10/15% of your maximum hit points.

 ***This would introduce the fantasy of the great weapon fighting tank into classic+. Arms is overall underwhelming in many aspects of the game. This should allow a fresh option to allow warriors to become more durable both in PVE and PVP if they chose to do so. The additional rage on successful parry might be overkill, but it is an attempt to smooth out the rage curve as most 2 handed weapons are slow. Lastly, if there is not a means to convert block chance from gear and talents and defense into parry; then a <{Formula}> that increases parry based on STR is an acceptable bandaid to this.***

 **5) Warclad** (NEW PROTECTION TALENT - Row 2 / 2 Points): While wielding a two-handed weapon or a weapon in each hand; increase your parry chance by <{Insert Formula}> X/Y of your damage dealt your Cleave and Heroic Strike for up to A/B seconds.

 ***This provides none-shield Prot warriors some mitigation options outside of having an equip shield macro.***

_.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'~-._.-~'

Thank you for taking the time to read this.  We have more suggestions, but wanted to highlight a few that meshed with the current suggested changes, as well as ones that address massive gaps in the current game.

Cheers!

## Post 167577 by Splitsec — 2026-02-06T10:58:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=167577#p167577 | page 53 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

**ALL**

Swapping **Librams**, **Totems** and **Idols** in combat now properly incurs a GCD.

 *Developer Comment: This was an ongoing quirk that was being (ab)used. Normally we would fix these in our weekly changelogs but because of the gravity of this change we've moved this to a Class Changes cycle.*

 - This change feels a bit misguided. Dancing with Idols, totems and librams offer some interesting depth to each of the classes. These items are already designed to sacrifice a lot of stats to provide very specific minor bonuses, allowing players to experiment and master their class. Forcing the GCD on them will bottleneck the gameplay into slotting a single relic and then forgetting about it. This was the exact same issue back in classic, namely boring and static design.

If you intend to go ahead with this, I would strongly argue that you also revise how each relic work, or simply bring up each relic's numbers. If we are to pick a single relic to use, make the choice harder and more meaningful.

 --------------------------------------------------------------
 **SHAMAN**

Physical DPS Enhancement will see some small tweaks in patch 1.18.1. Tank Enhancement and spell-power–focused Enhancement, however, are getting more meaningful updates to their core talents. These changes are aimed at strengthening each playstyle’s identity and reducing overlap with similar mechanics found in other classes.

 **General**

 **Lightning Shield:** Mana cost reduced across the board by roughly 25%
 **Rank 1 (Level 8):** 45 -> 40
 **Rank 2 (Level 16):** 80 -> 70
 **Rank 3 (Level 24):** 125 -> 105
 **Rank 4 (Level 32):** 180 -> 150
 **Rank 5 (Level 40):** 240 -> 200
 **Rank 6 (Level 48):** 305 -> 255
 **Rank 7 (Level 56):** 370 -> 310

 - **Welcome change. Always felt the mana cost of Lightning Shield was far too high compared to its usefulness.**
 --------------------------------------------------------------
 **Enhancement**

 **Stormstrike:** Can no-longer roll and trigger **Windfury Weapon**'s effect twice.

 - **Never seen this happen anyway, so I hardly think it will affect the class.**
 --------------------------------------------------------------
---
 **Windfury Weapon:** Each hit now has a 25% chance (was 20%).

 - Thank you! Finally. Physical enhance was just far too inconsistent in all content. I get that WF is a roulette spell, but you could go entire fights without seeing a single proc. That's just not fun gameplay.

IMPORTANT:
We have asked for a fix to the windfury threat generation for a long time now. You must increase the Calming Winds talent to at least 40% if shamans are going to be able to make any use of this buff. The spike-like threat is a massively annoying issue. I cannot stress this enough. Please, either increase the talent or put a baseline threat reduction on WF attacks.
 --------------------------------------------------------------
---
All of the following changes are to affect **Elemental Weapons** and its sub-effects:

 **Windfury:** Reworked to the following effect: “Gaining extra attacks increases your attack speed by 1% for 5 sec. Stacks up to 2/4/6 times.”

 - **I'm glad you finally are going in the right direction with this, but this is going to feel extremely bad to use in any fight where you have to stop attacking for even 5 seconds(which happens a lot). Increase the effect's uptime to 10 seconds and this will be far more useful.**
 --------------------------------------------------------------
 **Flametongue:** Reworked to the following effect: “Hitting enemies with your attacks increases the damage done by your Fire Totems and spells by 10/20/30% for 5 sec.”

 *Developer Comment: Requiring the Shaman to actively engage in melee combat to keep the Fire damage increase active should make this effect lean more towards spell oriented Enhancement Shaman gameplay while requiring pure Fire damage Elemental Shamans to stay in melee range to utilize its full power.*

 - I have a serious grudge against Flametongue in its current state, and this change will make it even worse. As per your own design direction, you want it to be the PvE(Spellhance) option to Frostbrand, but it is by far the weakest option of the 4 weapon imbues. And due to the incredibly low scaling, the only way to make it somewhat useful is to run 5/8 tier 1. It really screws with the whole idea of playing something like 2-Handed Spellhance at higher levels, because you get hard-locked out of a lot of gear slots. Shamans already have issues finding individual pieces of gear that match the stats needed for Spellhancing.

Solution:
 1. Buff Flametongue by 50% baseline, remove the bonus from the T1 set. Slap some random stats there instead.
 2. Introduce more shaman hybrid gear.

 *Who puts a fire-based bonus on a tier set that is designed to be used in 3 raids that are all either immune or resistant to fire? Seems a bit silly to me.*
 --------------------------------------------------------------
 **Rockbiter:** Reworked to the following effect: “Your physical damage builds up an earthen bulwark for 20% of the damage dealt, tripled while you're wearing a shield. The earthen bulwark absorbs 5/10/15% of incoming damage for 8 seconds or until the bulwark mitigates enough damage. The bulwark's durability cannot exceed 20% of your maximum health.”

 *Developer Comment: Changing the Rockbiter Weapon effect from a passive damage reduction into an active component that's kept up by attacking should feel make it feel more active in active usage while deterring non-Enhancement specializations from using the effect as a passive benefit which led to them being more durable, especially in Player vs Player environments.*

 - **I'm not sure having the shield proc only on physical damage will be enough, but I suppose it remains to be seen.**
 --------------------------------------------------------------
---
 **Flurry:** Reworked to the following effect “Increases your attack speed by 8/11/14/17/20% for your next 3 swings after dealing a critical strike.”

 *Developer Comment: This change should increase the uptime of Flurry especially for spell oriented Enhancement Shaman gameplay, making it less punishing to have less physical critical strike chance compared to their physical oriented counterpart.*

 - **Got nothing to say about this, other than thank you. We needed this.**
 --------------------------------------------------------------
---
 **Lightning Strike:** Water Shield's Attack Power-to-Mana ratio changed from 20:1 to 18:1.

 *Developer Comment: Shields are central to our vision of Enhancement, they are the specialization's biggest sink of mana, expecially in contexts where AOE damage is involved. This should improve the dependability of the specialization's mana bar.*

 - **A welcome change, but I don't understand your reasoning. I personally rarely have to use Water Shield as enhance in raids. The reality is that it is just far easier to chug runes or potions.**
 --------------------------------------------------------------
 **Elemental**

 **Eye of the Storm:** Renamed to **Call of Earth:**

"Earth Shield gains 1/2 additional charges and grants an additional 35/70% chance to avoid interruption while casting a spell."

 - **Finally Nature will be playable. Not even joking.**
 --------------------------------------------------------------
---
 **Elemental Fury:** Now also affects Frost spells.

 - **Why this was not included from the beginning baffles me. Thank you for finally fixing this.**
 --------------------------------------------------------------
---
 **Earthquake:** Base damage values increased by 15%, cooldown reduced from 20 seconds to 18 seconds.
New Damage Values:
 **Rank 1 (Level 40):** 227-253 -> 262-291
 **Rank 2 (Level 50):** 343-387 -> 395-446
 **Rank 3 (Level 60):** 510-551 -> 587-634

 - **Maybe it's possible to get a cast off in time now that we will have some pushback resistance.**

**Developer, please pay attention :)**

New spell: Rupture swipe (cat form)

Description: Fast amplitude attack with claw that hits up to 3 targets and causes minor bleeding wounds.

Lvl 28: Rupture swipe (Rank 1) - Deals 75% damage plus 24 to each target and causes bleeding that lasts for 6 seconds and deals 36 damage every 3 seconds.
Lvl 36: Rupture swipe (Rank 2) - Deals 75% damage plus 33 to each target and causes bleeding that lasts for 6 seconds and deals 48 damage every 3 seconds.
Lvl 44: Rupture swipe (Rank 3) - Deals 75% damage plus 48 to each target and causes bleeding that lasts for 6 seconds and deals 74 damage every 3 seconds.
Lvl 52: Rupture swipe (Rank 4) - Deals 75% damage plus 60 to each target and causes bleeding that lasts for 6 seconds and deals 104 damage every 3 seconds.
Lvl 60: Rupture swipe (Rank 5) - Deals 77% damage plus 80 to each target and causes bleeding that lasts for 6 seconds and deals 146 damage every 3 seconds.

Cost: 65 energy.
Cooldown: 6 second.

The idea is simple - we just took Shred and Rip (2 CP) of the corresponding levels and divided them by 3. We also took into account that the druid has Clearcasting and came up with a cooldown for this ability so that it does not introduce imbalance.
Warrior, by definition, cleavemachine. For rogues, mechanics from the subsequent WoW expansions - Blade Flurry - were added.
We ask the developers to consider adding a simple ability like the one described above.
Most cat players will agree that our spec's AoE damage is simply laughable.
