## Post 168128 by Outed — 2026-02-13T12:58:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=168128#p168128 | page 53 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Hello. I play a Demonology warlock and am a long time wow player and thought I write some stuff about the current state of Demonology and give some ideas or alternatives to the changes and so on.

First I would like to start with saying that Demonology plays very very fun, compared to how it was in both Vanilla and TBC (mainly talking PVE here) You guys did a great great job and I hope my observations bellow will not sound condescending in any way.

English is not my main language and this message might be scattered in a random way but I will try to explain as good as I can and provide decent arguments and examples.

First thing I would like to discus is the removal of the Master Conjuror talent and the change to Soul link (25% to 20% dmg reduction).

I Think that is a bad change backed up with very weak arguments from the developers. We need the extra survivability due to a few reasons:
 - Demo Locks have short range - no destructive reach and no grim reach, unless u play SL Nightfall, but almost no one plays that, as its a boring and RNG dependant build.
 - Bad mobility - If you do not preposition yourself well, your pet well, if you do not fanatically use LOS and so on. You are dead, simple. Any miniscule slow on a warlock is death. Frost shock from Shaman cuz you both have same range? good luck with the self devour, 50% of the time it fails. Got HoJ from a Pala cuz u got no range? Good luck with devour, 70% of the time it fails, funnily enough, the combat text says it devour successfully yet I'm still stunned. Got hamstring, crippling? I don't think I need to explain this, you dead, and with bad range, bad survivability, why bother fake casting, tricking and doing outplays if you just don't have the survivability?
 - Below average damage - No Shadow Mastery, no Emberstorm means we only got the 5% from Soul Link. Yeah we get 15% dmg for pets, but in PVP, the Fel Hunter dies in 2 or 3 right clicks from physical damage dealing classes and yet you are making the Fel hunter have 30% less armor now, i mean then what is the point in having the 15% dmg for pets if you barely send the dog out, you keep it just in range to devour or spell lock something.

The Demonology warlock in PVP is about using the environment, positioning to your advantage and the fact that you are a caster who can stand your ground for a while against insane dmg that physical dmg dealers can do, in Vanilla especially, now with all these changes there will be less of an incentive to PVP as Demo.

Don't get me wrong, Demo can still slap in PVP, get some good gear, know how to play, know how to capitalize the mistakes of other players and you will win the battles.

Lets say you guys are dead set on these nerfs for the Demo lock, fine. Lets call them Passive Survivability nerfs, that's fine, but then please consider giving some Active Survivability buffs, for example:

 - Demonic Aegis (3/3 you get 60% extra armor from the buff) perhaps consider buffing this talent to provide 90% or even 120%) why is this fair?  Because you take away 10% dmg reduction from Soul Link (reminder it was 30% in vanilla), you take away extra healing from Health Stone, you make the Fel Hunter more squishy and out of all casters, warlocks have the LEAST amount of armor on their gear, its not even funny how little we have... Now how would this affect the balance of PVP? Against casters, in no way, unless fighting shadow priests, because Demon Armor also gives you shadow res, but you could just alter the Talent to increase the armor gained, not the total effectives of all that the Demon Armor gives. Rogue or Warrior trying to kill you with the newly buffed Demon armor, you get a few extra seconds to survive, a shaman can purge it off, caster don't care about it. What you take away from Passive Overall dmg reduction you can bring some of it back in the form of active dmg reduction against physical dmg dealers that CAN be easily dispelled/purged.

 -----------------------------------------------------------------------

A Silly idea, but why not. In a perfect world, the talent Improved Stones should just have the health stone benefits included there, but yeah, I know it wont happen.

 - Experimental idea, food for thought. If you are so dead set on nerfing the armor of the Fel Hunter and the Infernal, then you could perhaps consider nerfing the armor of all our pets and either adding a new talent or updating some existing talent, that would allow your pets to benefit from an X amount of your active armor that you have. This would work very well with the improved Demon Armor and it would give more meaning to perhaps using a Scroll of Protection to give yourself some armor and maybe even a little elixir that increases armor. Those wont do much, but will be a more active way of giving your demon back some of the armor you took away.

 - The Searing pain change is interesting, Its in a way a slight buff, but I would like to point out, that with this change, most likely NO ONE will play SL into Nightfall for PVP. This does not bother me, but I know that this will hurt the one or two that do play SL Nightfall.

 - Fel Domination and Master summoner are, well strange. I don't fully understand it. You cant buff your pets, you cant summon them mega fast. Infernal has a 10min cd or 5min if u have Master Summoner, so basically in a away you have non stop upkeep of the infernal, the common demons become almost useless and now I see you will make ritual of doom also have a reduced cool down.
What I would say, and just for consideration, keep the nerf on the summoning part, keep it 1.5 sec, but perhaps, increase the default cooldown for the Infernal to 15min or even 20min, but make the initial dmg of the impact when summoning infernal a bit stronger, lets say 300 and perhaps a slight buff to the immolation aura the infernal has?
The Doom Guard is cool, I really like it, there are different ways to use him then you would with an infernal, but a small observation - the skill where he enchants his weapon for fire damage, the tooltip says it stacks, yet when i look at the buff, it never stacks? Do I understand this spell incorrectly? I look at the fire dmg of his auto attacks after using the spell a few times and it stays the same :/
Also about the thing with buffing pets. You made a change where you cant directly buff a warlock pet, but what about a small change where a warlock could at least use scrolls on pet? A little scroll of Agility or Stamina could help a lot.

 - Health funnel is great, i like how when the lower the HP the pet has, the more you heal, but perhaps consider making the talent be 3/3 not just 2/2 and that way its 30% more healing.

 ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A few observations about the Nether Studies talent, Power Overwhelming and the change to Unleashed Potential.

 - Nether Studies is fine for when you are leveling with the Voidwalker, but maybe a few little tweaks could make the talent be useful in more playstyles and scenarios:
 1. Would you consider that Suffering also gets its effectiveness increased or perhaps its cooldown reduced?
 2. Would you consider changing the Seduction part of the talent into Soothing Kiss? I really love what you guys did with Soothing Kiss, its brilliant, I use this ability a lot, but with Nether talents it could be even more useful.
 3. Experimental idea, but earlier I mentioned about giving the ability for warlocks to use scrolls on their pets, what if you include that ability within this talent? It would mean if u put just 1 point into Nether Studies, you can put scrolls on pets. I don't know how hard from a developing point of view that would be to make, but again, just an experimental silly idea.

Power Overwhelming:
 - I absolutely love this spell. The scream the demon makes, the way the demon becomes redder and bigger, that is awesome, also the fact that it removes all the movement impairing effects is very cool, this allows to be smart and perhaps not use it whenever its off CD if you know a boss or something will soon do like a massive CC of sorts.
But I do have a few things I'd like to share for you all to consider.
The 20% dmg increase is great, but the 40% base health lost is a bit too much, especially in PVP.
What I think would be perhaps kind of fair is to increase the cooldown to lets say 20 seconds or even 25 seconds, but reduce the base health loss to 30% or 25%.
 - Another experimental idea is to perhaps split the effectiveness of the ability to instead of giving 20% more damage, but to give 10% more damage and an balanced amount of faster attack speed so that this change would not feel like a nerf?

Unleashed Potential:

You guys are going to make a change that seems like a great buff to the talent, but here is my take on it and maybe it will make you reconsider:
 - When the talent works by activating while making a crit, it mixes up the gameplay when raiding or doing dungeons or even out in the world, because when you know you need stacks you get back to spamming searing pain just to get those stacks up faster and even maybe using Firestone to increase the crit chance of the searing pains to get the stacks up faster and in between fights you use Power Overwhelming to have the pet lose HP and then use Health funnel to replenish the health and keep up the stacks. (when pet is full HP, the health funnel does not replenish the duration of the buff btw)
That for me is a healthy, fun and active playstyle, now with this change, it seems like you just spam shadow bolt, like a turret and you will have an upkeep of the stacks all the time. Maybe I'm wrong, maybe I understood the change wrong, but this is how it looks like for me. I know it sounds stupid for me to say this, because why would anyone complain about a buff to a talent? Well I like fun too, not just having less buttons to press to do more dmg.
So, what about considering keeping the talent as it was, and if you really want to buff it, perhaps increase the benefit from 15% per stack to 20% per stack?

I love the gameplay of the Demonology warlock over here on Turtle WoW, even tho there are very few of us (locks in general) but yeah, you guys did a great job, and whatever the final changes will end up to be with the patch, I will still play for sure, but keep in mind, that guilds want locks, there is a shortage of locks and some more bad changes can make the lock population even worse.

Best of luck with further developing!

 - Outed

In all the changes to Demonogy for Warlocks, I see PVE bonuses and PVP penalties. It is not possible to summon a Greater Demon in PVP when it has started, when the Warlock is being attacked. Why is there a reduction in the time it takes to summon Greater Demons? Is this to prevent PVE players from wasting extra seconds on speedrunning? How can I ask another player to help me summon Doom Guard during PVP? Searing Pain ->2 sec is a penalty for affliction+Demonology for Warlocks. In general, the Demonology branch for pvp is 15% hp(DE), +60% Demon armor, Dispell CC for pet(power overwhelming), +60 resistance or -10% physical. damage (Master demonologist) and 20% (thanks a lot (no)) Soul link.
+10% crit bonus exclusively for PVE talent because: 1) in PVP the Warlock cannot cast freely, except after Death Coil. 2) the Demonogy Warlock  does not have an arsenal of instant spells to implement critical chances. 3) there is no critical chance on PVP equipment to make its improvement effective(it goes without saying that there is stamina and SPD) - the same applies to Demonic Precision. Other talents are a mockery (a 1.5-second (fast?) summon). The  Demonogy Warlock is a defensive playstyle class with curses that requires playing two units as one, and weakening each of them individually under the guise of strengthening the other half.It's a mistake to force PvP players to play a style with unreliable Greater Demons due to these changes. Demons that have a CD on summoning will never be taken seriously by players. These demons leave control and attack the Warlock at the most inopportune moment during PvP, and they disappear after dying on BG's. These demons are perfect for the arena and some fun moments that end very quickly. If you want to enhance the role of a pet in a Warlock+pet combination, enhance basic pets or add a new basic pet with a permanent summon.
In terms of survivability, you've brought the Warlock closer to the Shadow Priest, with the difference that the SP has a much stronger burst and doesn't need to carry a stupid pet with 1-2 PvP skills that the Priest already has.

## Post 168190 by Auralys — 2026-02-14T13:23:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=168190#p168190 | page 53 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Hello Turtle Team,
Following the announced Balance changes (Moonfury adjustment and Balance of All Things rework), I would like to provide structured feedback before the patch goes live.
This is not about requesting additional damage, but about internal design coherence and gameplay identity.

Structural Concern – Eclipse Duality vs Talent Direction
Eclipse alternates between Arcane and Nature empowerment.
You never benefit from both simultaneously.

This system strongly implies duality and rotational balance between Wrath and Starfire.
However, the announced talent direction appears to reinforce Arcane (Starfire) more heavily than Nature (Wrath):

 -Balance of All Things is shifted toward Starfire.
 -Moonfury scaling benefits Starfire way more than Wrath in practical raid scenarios.
 -Crit scaling further amplifies Arcane potential.

If implemented as announced, this could create a directional imbalance inside a system meant to represent celestial opposition.

Potential outcome:

 -Arcane Eclipse becomes the preferred state. (already is, would make this even a bigger issue)
 -Nature Eclipse becomes transitional rather than equally desirable.
Wrath risks functioning primarily as a proc enabler rather than an equally powerful rotational choice.
That would weaken the intended duality.

If Eclipse alternates between two forces,then talent support should preserve parity between them.

Otherwise, the system encourages steering toward one element instead of embracing cyclical balance.

Suggested Adjustments
 1) Balance of All Things applies to both Wrath and Starfire and both can put you in Eclipse state (this one rotates from first procced element to other automatically)

Even with adjusted values, this would maintain symmetry and reinforce dual participation in the Eclipse cycle.

 2) Eclipse Smoothing

To prevent excessive proc fishing:

 - Add bad luck protection, or
 - Allow shared contribution from both spells, or
 - Slightly smooth proc reliability

This would reduce forced behavior without removing RNG identity.

 3) Optional: Controlled Eclipse Agency

Introduce a cooldown that:
Forces your next Wrath or Starfire to trigger its respective Eclipse, even if the opposing Eclipse debuff is active.

This would:
 -Add player agency,
 -Reduce RNG frustration,
 -Reinforce celestial alignment fantasy, preserve duality rather than create a preferred element.

With an appropriate cooldown, this would enhance gameplay depth without destabilizing balance.

Closing

The concern is not raw power.
The concern is preserving the identity of Balance as a cyclical, dual-element specialization rather than evolving toward a preferred-element scaling model Starfire Turret.

Providing feedback early may help maintain that design coherence before release.

— Auralys

## Post 169108 by Shayrindale — 2026-02-21T09:47:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=169108#p169108 | page 54 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jan 23, 2026 7:24 pm**
> **UPDATES | Dated: TBD (1.18.1) 2026**
>  **Balance**
> ---
>  **Balance of All Things:** Reduced from 5 points to 3 points and functionality reworked:
>  "Damaging a target affected by **Insect Swarm** with your **Wrath** spell returns 10/20/30% of its mana cost back to you.
>
>  **Starfire** has a 2/4/6% higher chance to critically strike against targets affected by **Moonfire**."

I would rework this differently and entire balance AoE also to not feel so incredibly clunky and slow compared to other casters.

Does anyone still remember the times where Hurricane was the final balance talent and not channeled, before Moonkin Form was added? I would love to see a throwback to those times with changes like this:

 **Hurricane:** No longer a channeled spell, instead has a base cast time of about 4 seconds, a very significant mana cost, no cooldown. Basically it "stays there" after cast time is completed like the version centaur Stormcallers use and has a limit of 1 (if you recast it, the first one despawns). Damage and tick rate heavily reduced.

 **Gale Winds:** Reduces cast time and mana cost of Hurricane significantly, but not so much for it to be worth casting against single targets.

Currently this talent is really bad where it's not worth taking and it's in pretty much the best place to give defining characteristics to balance druid (too deep for hybrid specs to reach)

 **Balance of All Things:** Removed entirely. Changes proposed in the quoted post rolled into "Improved Wrath" and "Improved Starfire" respectively instead.

This would improve early leveling as Balance nicely too.

 **Eclipse:** Changed from 1 point to 3 point, current functionality unchanged, "Mana cost of your balance spells reduced by %" from Moonkin Form moved here instead, so Moonkin Form doesn't feel so strictly mandatory. Placed where Balance of All Things is now.

New Final Balance Talent: **Starfall:** Mostly same functionality as "Hurricane" is now, only Arcane damage type and maybe 2-3s shorter cooldown, so it's not as painful to wait when some of the cast time is lost to interruption. Damage lowered/adjusted to be on the current level only when properly combined with reworked Hurricane.

Bonus points if you bring the wicked cool overhead moon animation while channeling.

Also I think it would be great to adjust "Glyph of the Moon" effect to not make you a ghost and another Shadowform, remove the translucency effect and leave only the blue wisps of smoke effect.

## Post 169176 by Splitsec — 2026-02-22T09:18:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=169176#p169176 | page 54 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

> **dioaffo1 wrote: Tue Feb 17, 2026 5:49 pm**
> The problem with the flametongue elemental weapons change is that MB resets the swing timers. It's not meant to be used with elemental weapons. Elemental weapons (flametongue) is meant to buff your flame shock and fire totems. Though giving Molten Blast the Slam treatment and allowing it to be woven in between swings would be great(read: necessary) if they want to lean into spellhance.

This! I've long thought about a version of this mechanic. It would obviously have to sit somewhere halfway/late into Enhancement, but it would be a great way to give shamans some options. This could be the "Maelstrom" of spellhance, but with no benefit unless you actually play with Flametongue. It would give some more flair and depth to the build.

Bake the 30% fire damage to totems and spells into the last 2 ranks of Flametongue by default, its not really a big change. It could look like this:

Flametongue Weapon(Rank 5 and 6):
Imbue the shaman's weapon with fire. Each swing(each hit) causes X to X additional Fire damage based on the speed of the weapon, and also causes your fire spells and totems to deal 30% increased damage for 8 seconds following a hit. Slower weapons cause substantially more fire damage per swing.

Then replace the Flametongue part of the Elemental Weapons talent with something like this:

Molten Blast no longer resets your swing timer while under the effects of Flametongue Weapon. Your attacks with Flametongue Weapon have a chance to grant a stack of Rising Flames. Each stack reduces the cast time of your next Molten Blast by 20(or 33)%. Slower weapons have a higher chance to trigger this effect. At 3(or 5) stacks, it also deals X%(say 10-20) increased damage.  *Note: The proc rate would obviously have to be high enough to be able to reach 3(or 5) stacks fairly comfortably within the duration of Flame Shock, which is 15 seconds. The idea here being having enough time to reset Flame Shock via Molten Blast.*

This gives you an incentive to play with a two-hander, fight in melee and actually cast MB at full Rising Flames stacks, instead of just using Flametongue as a buff. There is NO need to nerf the crap out of Flametongue when there are options like this.

I have a big question to this fabled melee fire shaman so many people seem to actually be fond of?
What about it is actually different from regular enhancer? Because to me you use exactly the same rotation and totems. The only difference being the occasional mb, which is at current not something that wants to be slotted in due to casttime. Heck even if you get instant casts, you will still be lacking spellhit to make the refreshing of flameshock consistent. Due to needing melee stats too.

Different imbues are not meant to be different speccs. All that changes is how you spice your auto attack. In fact in classic all 4 enchantments perform similar in dps while levelling with green weapons and no spellpower.

The things that are crooked here is that endgame is almost exclusively faught against enemy without armor, boosting wf and not the spellbased imbues. As well as windfury actually scaling with your gear and the others not.

Flametongue scales 10% with spellpower, regardless of your swingspeed. Its base damage with slow weapon does already scale linearly.

We dont need crappy talent that give bonus effects on ft, we need ft to be worth it on its own merrits.

The change to give us a lingering buff to firedmg when meleeing with flametongue has the potential to create a shaman whose rotation will be the following, thanks to using a 1.5 or faster swingspeed weapon.

>Auto attack>Flameshock>Molten blast>Molten Blast>Earth Shock>Auto attack>Molten blast>Molten blast>Molten blast>Earth Shock>Auto Attack

Because the payoff for rocking flametongue weapon isnt actually flametongue. It amplifies spells that are actually worth using instead.

>  What about it is actually different from regular enhancer? Because to me you use exactly the same rotation and totems. The only difference being the occasional mb, which is at current not something that wants to be slotted in due to casttime. Heck even if you get instant casts, you will still be lacking spellhit to make the refreshing of flameshock consistent. Due to needing melee stats too.
>
>  Different imbues are not meant to be different speccs. All that changes is how you spice your auto attack. In fact in classic all 4 enchantments perform similar in dps while levelling with green weapons and no spellpower.
>
>  The things that are crooked here is that endgame is almost exclusively faught against enemy without armor, boosting wf and not the spellbased imbues. As well as windfury actually scaling with your gear and the others not.
>
>  Flametongue scales 10% with spellpower, regardless of your swingspeed. Its base damage with slow weapon does already scale linearly.
>
>  We dont need crappy talent that give bonus effects on ft, we need ft to be worth it on its own merrits.
>
>  The change to give us a lingering buff to firedmg when meleeing with flametongue has the potential to create a shaman whose rotation will be the following, thanks to using a 1.5 or faster swingspeed weapon.
>
>  >Auto attack>Flameshock>Molten blast>Molten Blast>Earth Shock>Auto attack>Molten blast>Molten blast>Molten blast>Earth Shock>Auto Attack
>
>  Because the payoff for rocking flametongue weapon isnt actually flametongue. It amplifies spells that are actually worth using instead.

I'll split up my answer to your question(s), lots of info to break down here:
> What about it is actually different from regular enhancer?

It is a mixed build that uses the built in bonus to fire dmg for totems and Flame Shock. Currently, Flametongue -with the help of the T1 bonus- also deals quite a lot of damage. You still deal decent physical damage if you play with a two-hander like I do, but nowhere near the levels of a windfury shaman. The build deals more consistent damage instead of big random bursts. You know where and when the damage will happen at all times. This also applies to PvP situations. In essence: Less burst, much more consistency.

> you will still be lacking spellhit to make the refreshing of flameshock consistent. Due to needing melee stats too.

Not quite true. Due to our talent in the Elemental tree(Elemental Devastation), we gain a free 3% to both spectrums. Once we make our first crit in melee, that spell hit gets boosted to +12%, meaning you only need 3% spell hit rating from gear to reach the 15% soft cap. The final 1% is provided via the Emerald buff from druids while in raids.
As for melee hit, there are enough skill books, weapon skill items(i.e. the legs from ES), and hit on gear to easily reach melee hit cap.

> Different imbues are not meant to be different speccs. All that changes is how you spice your auto attack. In fact in classic all 4 enchantments perform similar in dps while levelling with green weapons and no spellpower.

Firstly, they already are. Secondly, this is not classic and has not been anything near a true classic server since the class reworks. The original changes Turtle made are here to stay, so we might as well improve and polish upon the existing design.

> The things that are crooked here is that endgame is almost exclusively faught against enemy without armor, boosting wf and not the spellbased imbues. As well as windfury actually scaling with your gear and the others not.

While this may be true for most top tier endgame raiding guilds that have great lineups of players, this is not always the case for the more casual ones. Windfury -like with all physical damage dealers- scales better, yes. But I'd say that is 40% itemization, and 60% legacy game mechanics(Windfury Totem being the big obvious one here for warrs, rogues and druids).

> Flametongue scales 10% with spellpower, regardless of your swingspeed. Its base damage with slow weapon does already scale linearly.

In my experience (as the guy who champions this build and plays it daily), slower weapons using Flametongue will deal more overall damage and win out over fast weapons in the end. I've tested this to kingdom come with all manner of weapons and different swing speeds, and the result usually leans towards slow, two-handed weapons for best result. Might of Menethil, Maul of the Redeemed Crusader, and Sulfuras are great examples of well performing weapons.
As for the scaling of Flametongue, you are correct about that. Though that doesn't necessarily have to stay that way. As of right now, you are generally better off with stacking spell crit over spell power. But spell power has its place, mainly to boost your shocks and totems.

> We dont need crappy talent that give bonus effects on ft, we need ft to be worth it on its own merrits.

Why not? Its about having choice. As for Flametongue being worth on its own merit, I have already brought this up in a separate thread where I requested a change to the T1 5-set bonus of Enhancement.
Currently, it provides a 45% increase to Flametongue when you attack targets affected by your Flameshock. My suggestion to the developers is to take that extra damage and simply put it into the imbue itself, and then replace the set bonus with something like 2-3% melee and spell crit combined. This would bring Flametongue to the same level as the other two. ***Especially when considering the upcoming patch, where Frostbrand is getting a 10% damage increase(due to Frost now being included in Elemental Fury), and where Windfury is getting a 5% increase to its trigger chance plus the increased haste from Elemental Weapons.***

> The change to give us a lingering buff to firedmg when meleeing with flametongue has the potential to create a shaman whose rotation will be the following, thanks to using a 1.5 or faster swingspeed weapon.
>
>  >Auto attack>Flameshock>Molten blast>Molten Blast>Earth Shock>Auto attack>Molten blast>Molten blast>Molten blast>Earth Shock>Auto Attack

Then they make sure the new design has this scenario taken into account. Fast weapons -> low proc rate. Slower weapons -> high proc rate. Its really not that hard.
Or just remove the part where I suggested that MB doesn't reset the swing timer, and only does so if you have full stacks of Rising Flames(the buff). And if you as the shaman want to play full on Elemental in melee, you're gonna have a bad time. Spellhance and Fire Elemental are NOT the same build.

> Because the payoff for rocking flametongue weapon isnt actually flametongue. It amplifies spells that are actually worth using instead.

Flametongue is 20% of all my damage in my current build, with auto swings coming in at 15% behind it. I can very comfortably hang out in the top 3 overall during Naxx. Most of the time I'm sitting in number 1 overall damage done throughout the raid.

This is not about trying out compete Windfury or make another Fire Elemental build. Windfury will always be the true "zug zug" of shamans to my eyes, and Fire Elemental was kind of a braindead 1 button build. Yes, I mained it too. It was ridiculous.

 **This is more about a hybrid build akin to that of Spellrets, but for shamans.**

The foundations for it are already there and is ready to be built upon. All that would need to change to make it work officially would be three things, and they are all connected:
- Take the damage from the T1 5-set bonus and bake it into Flametongue by default(around 50%). Replace the tier bonus with some melee/spell crit(2-3%). ***This removes the issue of being hard-locked into T1, and would bring Flametongue up the same baseline level as Frostbrand and Windfury.***

- Take the current Flametongue effect from Elemental Weapons and put it into the imbue by default.***This gives Flametongue more usefulness and depth, right from the moment you get both it and your first fire totem down at level 10.***

- Make some form of version of the above suggested talent(Rising Flames) as the Flametongue effect in Elemental Weapons.

IE - Cast Frostbolt (While Frostbolt travels) -> Cast Frost Nova (You get Flash Freeze) -> Your Frostbolt hits the target and also procs Flash Freeze. You just lost a proc.

If a new Hot Streak happens from a crit, it will start a new counter and both buffs can live together without wasting stacks.

IE. You cast Fireball (its flying) -> You begin casting Pyroblast (Hot Streak doesnt get consumed until the cast ends) -> Fireball crits target and awards an stack -> Fireball finishes casting (never recieved the extra reduction from the last stack) -> Pyroblast is casted and all stacks consumed.

## Post 170363 by Mao1989 — 2026-03-08T21:29:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=170363#p170363 | page 54 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

Retribution
Repentance: Repent effect applied on immune creatures now scales with 8% of your Attack Power per tick.
Seal of Command: Procs per minute increased from 7 to 9.
Crusader Strike: Rank 5's weapon damage percentage increased from 90% to 100%.

Developer Comment: Retribution paladins that leaned into attack power have been underperforming for the last few patches. These three changes should bring them closer in line to their hybrid counterparts.

Great changes. But, this will not solve the problem. Currently, the biggest problem for an AP Retribution Paladin is low mana and high mana costs. In Classic and TBC, every time a Paladin uses Judgement, the active Seal is consumed. This means you must immediately reapply the Seal afterward. For example, the mana cost of Seal of Command (SOC) is 178, and Judgement costs 76 mana. After casting Judgement, you must activate SOC again, which costs another 178 mana. This means one full damage cycle costs about 432 mana, and you need to repeat this every 8 seconds to maintain your DPS.

In addition, you may also use Exorcism (345 mana) and Consecration (505 mana) to add more DPS. While these costs may seem low compared to some ranged classes, the issue is that an AP Retribution Paladin typically only has about 3.5k to 3.9k total mana depending on gear. With just one damage cycle as described above, you already spend nearly one-third of your total mana.

The only ways to restore mana are BOW, Judgement of Wisdom (JOW) and mana potions, which have a 2-minute cooldown and can be expensive. Mana Totem? Maybe...JOW is also very inefficient for AP Paladins compared to SP Ret Paladins who rely on spell damage. As a result, AP Ret Paladins cannot sustain their mana during long fights or raids. In general, all Retribution Paladin gear sets suffer from mana problems. The best gear set for an AP Ret Paladin is the T3 set, but even then, mana remains the biggest issue.

To solve this problem and make the T3 Retribution set viable in raids, I believe the developers should rework the set bonuses. The current 6-piece and 8-piece bonuses for the T3 Ret Paladin set are extremely disappointing. The 6-piece bonus reduces the cooldown of Exorcism by 5 seconds. This might be useful for tanks, who need additional threat and often stack spell power, but it does not benefit AP Retribution Paladins. AP Paladins rarely use Exorcism for sustained DPS because the mana cost is too high. Dealing around 500 damage (or even less) for 345 mana makes this spell inefficient for AP builds.

The 8-piece bonus is even more questionable. The T3 Retribution set contains no spell power on any of its pieces, which suggests it was designed for an attack power playstyle. However, the 8-piece bonus gives 71 spell power. What is the purpose of this design? An AP Paladin can easily have over 1000 AP, so 71 spell power is practically useless. How are we supposed to benefit from such a small amount of spell power? In reality, both the 6-piece and 8-piece bonuses feel poorly designed and ineffective.

To make AP Paladins more playable, the key issue to address is mana sustainability. My suggestion is to revise the set bonuses as follows:

 6-piece bonus: Reduce the mana cost of Exorcism and Consecration by 25% or 30%.
 8-piece bonus: When Seal of Command procs and successfully hits an enemy, restore mana equal to 8% or 10% of the damage dealt.

With these changes, AP Paladins would have a more reliable way to manage mana and could sustain their DPS during long fights and raids.

Please consider this suggestion.

## Post 170756 by Tmot — 2026-03-13T15:16:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=170756#p170756 | page 55 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

> **Jamey wrote: Fri Jan 23, 2026 7:24 pm**
> **DRUID**
>
>  **Balance**
> ---
>  **Balance of All Things:** Reduced from 5 points to 3 points and functionality reworked:
>  "Damaging a target affected by **Insect Swarm** with your **Wrath** spell returns 10/20/30% of its mana cost back to you.
>
>  **Starfire** has a 2/4/6% higher chance to critically strike against targets affected by **Moonfire**."

Balance of All Things — Suggestion:

I welcome the talent change — reducing it to 3 points is well justified. However, I'd like to suggest an alternative wording that preserves the core concept of the talent — the cross-synergy between Nature and Arcane:

> "Damaging a target affected by Moonfire with your Wrath spell returns 10/20/30% of its mana cost back to you. Starfire has a 2/4/6% higher chance to critically strike against targets affected by Insect Swarm."

Why this matters:

The current version of the talent is built around cross-synergy: Moonfire (arcane) enhances Wrath (nature), Insect Swarm (nature) enhances Starfire (arcane). This thematically aligns with Eclipse — a talent also built on the mutual activation of Nature and Arcane effects.

In the version proposed by the developers, both bonuses link spells of the same magic school (nature+nature, arcane+arcane), which breaks this concept and makes Eclipse and BoAT thematically disconnected talents within the same tree.

This way, the proposed wording preserves the concept of cross-synergy between Nature and Arcane abilities.

Thank you!

I am interested in seeing the ranger (no pet) build made viable, but I don't think Alone Against the World is the correct way. Having it be an early talent makes it useless for leveling, as the majority of your DPS comes from your pet, even without spec-ing in the BM tree. Having it also be part of the Survival tree gives the impression that Survival is supposed to bet pet-less, in which case you're just making Warrior 2.0.

I get why it's made this way. Give Marksman a reason to spend points in the Survival tree, instead of the BM tree. However, the damage bonus is still less than what a pet would do. Sure, it's for raids, where the pet can more easily die, but instead of having pet-less be a spec specific path, you're making it viable for 2 specs instead. And in turn, you're reducing BM-Survival builds. So please, reconsider this talent's row and spec placement.

 -----------------

As for Surefooted, I'm completely against duel wielding hunters. Thematically, it makes no sense. Up until lv40 Survival hunters look like rogues... The Survival tree is already overbloated and feels directionless. Having to facilitate duel wielding as an option only makes balancing of this spec harder, as you've probably already noticed

The Survival tree is already overbloated and feels directionless. Having to facilitate duel wielding as an option only makes balancing of this spec harder, as you've probably already noticed

Following your logic, a pet-less survival hunter with a two-handed weapon is a warrior/paladin/shaman clone, which is... actually true! Survival has no business getting Lone Wolf. Lone Wolf should be a deep MM talent only to fulfill the "archer fantasy" people ask often. However, this request actually comes from those who play *the* pet class not wanting to deal with the main mechanic, the pet, partially because TWoW keeps leaving key pet issues unfixed. Funnily enough you don't find this in other classes: where are the warriors that don't want to use rage? Or the mages that want to not cast damage spells?

While it's true that balancing DW vs 2H can be difficult (the devs can just keep thinking of ways to fix this), in TWOW there's only two classes in the game that can choose either play style, warrior and hunter, whereas the other physicals can only do one or the other.

If Lone Wolf makes sense to you thematically, then dual wield should also make sense. Otherwise, there's a contradiction here.

## Post 171323 by Lane13 (Barrens Chat Casualty) — 2026-03-19T15:15:00Z
<!-- url: https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=171323#p171323 | page 55 | era: 1.18.1-announced-pre-release -->

In the end, the BM tree releases as is but Coordinated Assault is nerfed and now says that it uses the hunter's "attack power" (not clear if it's melee or ranged) while Kill Command is buffed but the effect remains as dull as before. I also assume this means that the attack will still come from the hunter but considered melee even if attacking at ranged, thus not benefiting from BM talents or pet modifiers, making it harder for pets to keep aggro and transferring melee debuffs such as Magmadar's skin or Frost Armor.

Alright, we can deal with that until you decide to make changes again. However, why is BM the only talent spec in the game with **NINE** (9) points on the second to last row? Ranged hunters need 20 points in the MM tree for Mortal Shots and Frenzy is a talent that is never filled and only gets 2-3 points in every version of WoW, official or otherwise, it's in until the Cata rework.

So why exactly don't you just lower the maximum point requirement of the different 5-point talents deeper in the tree? There's *zero* wiggle room once you start the third row and what ranged BM hunters will end up doing is skip talents such as Bestial Discipline and put only 2 or even 1 point in Frenzy in order to have at least 4 points in Mortal Shots. In fact, considering the current numbers and scaling, a 5th point in Mortal Shots likely provides more damage than anything else in the BM tree.

Another solution would be moving Mortal Shots up the MM tree so it's easier to access or lower its maximum point requirement, like what happens with Assassination rogue and Arms warrior respectively.

Still, the BM talent tree is bloated and needs trimming when it comes to the maximum amount of points required for a talent node. Ferocity should be a 3/3 talent giving 5% crit per point (or better yet, make pet crit scaling baseline and have Ferocity do something else), Frenzy should be a 1/1 or 2/2 talent, Bestial Discipline should be buffed, and other talents such as Unleashed Fury should probably also be a 3/3 talent giving 7, 14, and 20% damage respectively.

Changes such as these are necessary to make BM, and especially the ranged version, flow better when it comes to talents.

Some changes feel weird.

Regarding prot pala:
I agree that their power curve was too strong early, push needed at lategame. But your solution made them absolutely broken at leveling, decent at lategame. Current prot tanks during dungeons are tiers above the other options, because they buff you up, pull 3 packs, kill all with perfect threat and survive.
I don't hate on the build, just saying that a better solution would have been lowering the power curve early and making it better late instead of a straight up push.

Prot warrior:
The changes definitely help with lategame but the overall design still feels weird. Why are there so many spendable talent points on revenge if the ability, which sounds like a core prot ability just becomes useless due to almost 0 scaling?

Hunter changes seem awesome but way too much for me to fully underand. Hopefully works out.
But as someone pointed out, hunter mana problems don't start at lategame and in this version of WoW, leveling is an important segment. Let them have the mana aspect much earlier.
